这就是在大家日经CRPG排名中经常莫名其妙钻出来的ELEX了，我刚好对德游感兴趣，又听闻老玩家说本作味正，于是我慕名入坑。
结论是虽然我没有体验到让粉丝狂热的独特点（鉴于目前游戏机制的融合性），但单从RPG本身来说，这是一款相当扎实的游戏。
[h1] 难度 [/h1]
我开着中等玩的，在被反复强调过本作没有新手期比较难之后，开头小心翼翼，过了十几分钟就发现。
1.本作AI相当蠢，除了人形之外只要你站在敌人可以接触到的地方他一定会冲过来近战，且冲过来的时候不会闪避。
2.主角的机动性相当高，本作没有任何AI移动速度超过主角的奔跑速度，主角不仅可以闪避（类黑魂用耐力条），也可以直接用喷气背包飞行（喷气背包是独有的飞行条），不死人看了想删号。
3.AI的仇恨机制有范围，超出范围不会追逐，但也可以一直拉怪脏守卫的钱。
由于以上原因我在前几个钟头就没战斗过，纯跑腿，又去贴吧找了个前期攻略，直接往北润到穹顶城开圣城传送，往东跑到转换站买配方。然后传到圣城买了把激光，开启简单难度。
建议入坑玩家去贴吧找份攻略即可，虽然我是反对没有新手期这玩意的，不过都说是德游特色，行吧。
注意两点：前期摸风力发电机上的物品显蓝框太阳镜（这东西不应该和无限负重一样开始就给吗？），中期关转换站拿毕业智敏电浆，之后想怎么打怎么打，无聊可以把力量点上去拿毕业激光。远程能武都算是很好拿的也算是制作组给新人的怜悯了。
最后，本作最无难度的地方是：
[b] 技能点是能喝药喝出来的 [/b]，只要你有钱买奥能直接毕业，人人都是水桶号。
真受不了的建议直接改钱，这不比别的还要改属性点方便？不过不推荐，本作来钱方式偷也好，拉怪也好，打猎也好方式多样。

[h1] 武器 [/h1]
单拉出来说，本作由于手感糟糕到有和没有一样的近战系统，建议新手转远程，但远程武器除了弓箭全员（喷子鱼叉都这样）半自动换皮我是遭不住了，我电浆一发发扣算了，我捡了激光害一发发扣，那我激光不白捡了？至于其他的什么切个武器自动上弹啊这类小问题就不说了。

[h1] 探索 [/h1]
如同刺客信条枭雄加了个钩爪一下好玩了一样，本作加了个喷气背包一下就上天入地了，探索流程十分自由和流畅，正好我上个玩的CRPG开放世界是龙腾审判，爬高上低找碎片给我恶心个够呛。缺点就是没有在一些高处设置回报（不过也无所谓了），和没有载具。

[h1] 剧情 [/h1]（含剧透）
[list]
    [*][b] 人物 [/b]：主角不可选先给我一个开幕雷击，后来意识到主角是个对外面世界几乎一无所知的肉体机器人也算勉强接受（虽然有一段主角科普智械架构），其余人物全员导游，拉着你先念一段世界观——给任务——再念一段世界观，还好这个世界观还行，托他们的福我都可以写个小科普了，代价是任务剧情我全忘光了，给人印象最好的还是狂鼠（给和一些土匪任务），因为这位终于考虑到他不是异世界导游，而是自己的利益优先。
    [*][b] 任务结构 [/b]：好评，绝大多数任务都有第二种解法，且大多数任务都会给出属性判定（虽然人人水桶号没啥意义）和事后回访（虽然有的没给），而其中又有不少能影响接下来的游戏进程，主角也能通过冷酷值来个反水。虽然有的比较刻意（比如狂战士的任务第二种解法大多数直接把东西卖了，官方剧透有多少任务了），但已经能干掉一些给重复任务，跑腿垃圾任务，选了跟没选一样任务，属性判定丢失任务的CRPG了
    [*][b] 世界观 [/b]：马格兰（就是地球）旧世界科技类似现代，有大堆悍马和M1残骸，其中有暗线是某公司发现陨石打算选人润到太空轨道，有点黑料（由于旧世界毁灭是纯天灾观感比不上避难所科技）。接着被陨石撞了，旧世界毁灭，撞出个新能源奥能，过了很久产生了三阵营，开掐，掐到100年前，三方议和，没多久又掐（所以时间已经过去非常久了那堆旧世界的破砖烂瓦烂坦克还能留我是没料到）。设定算是说得通。游戏流程是目前最滥大街的：团结N个派系组团打大BOSS，超浓的bioware味，能接受，但我是快玩腻了。主角出自BOSS阵营智械，需要团结四个阵营：
[olist]
    [*] [b] 狂战士 [/b]：武德充沛，拒绝一切科技，刀耕火种，制作组给上了个魔法BUFF来平衡。将奥能转化为魔法。制度也跟着退化，采用等级身份制和氏族制。掌握生命之种可以把沙漠种成绿洲（很德鲁伊）。  教条式严刑峻法（不会魔法的狂战就真是中世纪），只要用科技设备直接流放（但特权阶层可以偷摸着用）。号称尊重耕种者（因为耕种者职责是种地和照料生命之种），但大家都硬着头皮往武士阶层挤（耕种者需要到危险的边疆种生命之种形同流放，而且基本没有补给直接荒野求生了）。
    [*][b] 牧师 [/b]：武德及其充沛，将奥能注入科技，科技树直接点到了能量武器，少见的废土超越旧世界（费拉实弹）的阵营。大工业化生产，拥有人形机器人和双足无人机甲。缺人，到处拉人同时直接把人工智能原型科技点了（让机器变成人更快）。然后这么个工业国没干过上面的农业国（有点钛了），狂战认为是魔法的胜利，牧师表示战斗机甲没能源趴窝（实际多半是芯片故障图了自己人）。莫名其妙信了个教，连教义都没有，有点硬塞。认为死后会进入无限虚空（点一下，就是旧世界的公司名）。实行有教无类（想学科技？我教），自神以下人人平等原则，首都缺粮点了食物包技术（营养均衡就是难吃），从一把手到矿工每人一天一份。同甘共苦了。塞了个洗脑大黑点（两边拼精神力，赢了就入教）。
    [*][b] 土匪 [/b]：即使是狂战的流放抵制科技和牧师的洗脑信火箭也显得费拉不堪的屑阵营，纯社会达尔文主义，你死了还不是因为你不努力。直接用奥能造毒品嗑药。别的阵营一个绿化恢复生态一个科技发展可能机飞。这位重量级纯躺平爱咋咋，开摆就完事了，甚至大决战磨洋工，通关第一时间图图（野外敌人掠夺者就是没进城的土匪）。
    [*][b] 独立分子 [/b]：牧师有一派偷摸往自己身上扎奥能，奥能除了能让人变白毛（冲国人特攻）还能让人失去感性变成纯逻辑的肉体机器人，分裂出来变成了智械，智械找到了BOSS要搞大计划，一部分智械认为这玩意搞大计划要奥能最后估计兔死狗烹，反了丫的，独立出来变成独立分子，认为肉体机飞也是机飞，属于人类的进化。
[/olist]
 [*][b] 结尾[/b]：差评，你都搞幻灯片了说明也不是不知道，就能不能好好弄弄，一大堆阵营人物载入介绍往上凑数，次要人物没后续，阵营没后续，影响一些人物的支线任务没后续，好在主要人物队友有后续，每个还就一行字，我玩CRPG起码三分之一的动力就是为了看结局去的，要不是制作组准备出2代填坑我直接差评了。
[/list]

总之，作为一个二线RPG确实在矛头位置，和一线RPG也能凭借自身优势战一把，有狂热粉丝也不难理解。

额外吐槽：
一个二线RPG全语音，你们日厂能不能学学？
我确实产生了玩哥特崛起的乐趣，不过考虑到本作流畅的游玩体验是喷气背包和激光枪给我的，不知道前作有没有这些便利玩意啊？

Elex is an immensely underrated & overlooked hidden gem amongst a saturated RPG market.
On the surface you might try it and immediately think it's another half-assed, empty mess filled with more EuroJank than even a CDPR studio, but you would be oh so wrong to make that assumption. 

Elex has a tightly written, engaging narrative that branches out vastly depending on every single thing you do in the game.
The amount of freedom you have in building your character and writing his story in the world is absolutely STAGGERING.
Without spoiling anything, there are 3 major factions and whichever you choose to join completely changes how your playstyle will evolve. Almost all of your dialogue responses have some kind of consequence, either directly or far-reaching.
There's a host of companions you can find throughout the world to join you, each has their own distinct personality and set of morals and will react to your choices in various ways. Let's just say that after finishing the game and soaking up most of the side quests & lore, I absolutely can't wait to see where Elex 2 goes in terms of the story.

Now I'll admit that the combat, while I personally grew to understand & enjoy it, is flawed and has a few inherent problems with its mechanics. The hit detection is odd, enemies can stun-lock you into oblivion, and your companions sometimes aren't as helpful as they should be. But once you settle into the rhythm of the game it's easy to flip the odds in your favour. There are a plethora of ways to take down your foes, and it's always fun to experiment with new weapons or abilities.

The graphics, while obviously not AAA quality, don't look horrible, and in fact are supplemented by fantastic world design & art direction. Different environments all have their own distinct style, and ooze with the passion the team have put into building the world of Magalan. Scenic overlooks stretch out over miles and showcase massive landmarks, sprawling deserts, icy peaks, lush forests, huge industrial installations, and futuristic tech-cities. The world is alive with colour, and everywhere you turn is filled to the brim with environmental details, which really help to make the game feel truly lived in. 

The sound design is very well done in my opinion. Exploring the world is made even more enjoyable with a smooth, calming soundtrack that helps the sense of wonder to everything going on. The voice acting is great as well. and sets the tone of conversations and emotion perfectly.

All in all if you're looking for a deep, rich, action RPG to sink your teeth into and don't mind a bit of jank with your combat and controls, then look no further than Elex.

[h1] Ein Sprung [/h1]
Elex. Der Nachfolger der Risen Serie, der einiges anders machen wollte und es auch tat. Ein neues Postapokalypsenszenario, eine grundlegend andere Spielwelt, die hauseigene weiterentwickelte Engine, welche eine schönere Grafik zulässt, neue Waffen, Fähigkeiten, Fraktionen, Mitstreiter und Gebiete. Elex macht einiges anders. Und nicht nur das offensichtliche hat sich geändert, denn ich werde das Gefühl nicht los, dass sich  auch unter der Haube in den Details und der Herangehensweise an das Spiel einiges getan hat. Viele dieser Änderungen finde ich wundervoll, bei einigen von ihnen werden die Meinungen aber wohl auseinander gehen. 

[b]Pro's[/b]: 
[list]
    [*]Der Einstieg in die Story ist wieder wie in Risen 3 simpel gehalten aber die Geschichte selber nimmt im Verlauf des Spiels fahrt auf und ist für Piranha Bytes Verhältnisse sehr gut gelungen. Der sonst immer Namenlose Held, bekommt plötzlich einen Namen, eine Heimat, eine Geschichte, die weit bis in seine Kindheit zurück reicht. Diese Geschichte ist natürlich eng mit der Spielwelt verknüpft und erklärt direkt Ziele und Fähigkeiten der Feinde. Im Verlaufe der Geschichte kommen wir dann ihren Motiven auf die Schliche. Die Story ist aber ähnlich wie in Horizon Zero Dawn, nicht nur durch Dialog erzählt, sondern auch durch Hints innerhalb der Spielwelt, weiter erklärt, sodass Spurensucher und Hobbydetektive voll auf ihre Kosten kommen. Und auch wer einfach eine gut erzählte Geschichte erleben möchte wird sich mit dieser Veränderung sicherlich schnell anfreunden.
    [*]Die Charaktere sind auch hier wunderbar gelungen. Und gerade die Gefährten decken eigentlich alles ab was man als Partner gerne haben möchte. Man muss sich also bloß entscheiden, mit wem man sympathisiert. 
    [*]Die Fraktionen könnten wirklich unterschiedlicher nicht sein. Das ist sehr gut gelungen. Philosophie, Lebenseinstellung und Alltag, der verschiedenen Fraktionen fällt völlig unterschiedlich aus. Das wirkt sich natürlich auch auf die Quests aus. Und bietet Variation die sich echt anfühlt. Außerdem lebt jede Fraktion (Feindesfraktion der Albs eingeschlossen) in ihrem eigenen Gebiet, was sich deutlich von den jeweiligen anderen abhebt und immer mal wieder kleine Hints für das Gesamtbild der Geschichte bereithält. Verlassene Häuser, verblasste Fotos, alte Briefe und weitere Überbleibsel der vergangenen Welt sorgen dafür, dass sich die Welt von Elex einfach real anfühlt. Außerdem hocken Fraktionsmitglieder nicht alle in ihrem Gebiet und machen nichts bis du sie ansprichst. Nein, sie sind auch in Gebieten anderer Fraktionen um dort Leute abzuwerben, Chaos zu stiften, zu handeln oder sogar um zu helfen. Sogar Abtrünnige der einzelnen Fraktionen gibt es.
    [*]Das Szenario des Elex ist eine der besten Verbindungen zwischen Spielwelt und Geschichte, die mir in den Kopf kommen würde. Elex ist technologisch einsetzbar in Maschinen, lässt sich als Droge konsumieren und kann in Mana umgesetzt und zur Regeneration der zerstörten Natur verwendet werden. Alle Menschen wissen was es ist und handelt damit. Authentisch und interessant.
    [*]Grafisch hat Elex einen ordentlichen Sprung hingelegt. Immer noch nicht AAA, aber sehr schön, gerade im Rückblick auf die Risen Serie, zeigt sich gerade in Gebäuden und dicht bevölkerten Gebieten wie viel besser Texturen und Vegetation aussehen.
    [*]Nicht nur bei der Grafik und den Fraktionen hat sich einiges getan. Auch das Movement hat sich deutlich verbessert. Nicht nur, dass wir kurz nach Start schon mit einem Jetpack fliegen können und das dem horizontalem aber vor allem vertikalem Map Design völlig neue Möglichkeiten eröffnet, sondern zusätzlich wurden wir auch mit einer Ausdauerleiste beschenkt. Unsere Kombos sind also nicht mehr generisch immer das selbe, sondern wir können sie je nach Stärke der Schläge unterschiedlich kombinieren und müssen zwischendurch immer wieder einen Blick auf die Ausdauerleiste werfen. Auch das Sprinten, was wir in diesem Spiel, Gott sei gepriesen, wieder dürfen sieht wahnsinnig gut aus. So würde ich mir vorstellen sieht das aus wenn ich nen Sprint ziehe, nur halt naja in langsam.
    [*]Leuchtturmwärter Jack
    [*]NPCs sind sterblich. Sehr wenige Charaktere lassen sich nicht töten aufgrund zu großér Relevanz für die Hauptstory. Alle anderen die irgendwie an Nebenquests beteiligt sind lassen sich nicht nur K.O. schlagen sondern auch töten und man muss mit den Konsequenzen leben.
    [*]Beziehungen zwischen Charakteren sind von der Sympathiefunktion beeinflusst. Das heißt anwesende Begleiter nehmen die Auswirkungen deiner Entscheidungen im Dialog war und machen sich ihre Gedanken dazu. Wenn es ihnen nicht passt, mögen sie dich nach ein zwei Ausrutschern vielleicht nicht mehr.
    [*]Es lohnt sich jetzt doppelt Gebiete zu erkunden aufgrund der vorhin erwähnten Clues zur Story und Spielwelt und natürlich aufgrund des Loots. Legendäre Waffen und Kartenbruchstücke sind ein extra Anreiz zweimal hinzugucken.
    [*]Monster sind nicht an dein Level angepasst, sondern zerfetzen dich gnadenlos, wenn du in ein Gebiet gehst, wo du als Low-Level nicht gerne gesehen wirst. So kann man den Spielerganz natürlich leiten und muss keine unsichtbaren Walls oder Plotblocks nutzen.
[/list]

[b]Kontra's[/b]: 
[list]
    [*]Das Inventar und Skillsystem ist nicht wirklich einfacher bloß anders. Das geht besser, wie der Nachfolger eindeutig bewiesen hat.
    [*]Die Outlaws sind nicht wirklich eine erstrebenswerte Fraktion, auch wenn es jetzt mehr eine Entscheidung nach Charaktersympathie und Weltanschauung ist, merkt man als Outlaw relativ schnell, dass man selbst mit dem Beitritt in die Fraktion über den Tisch gezogen wurde, da Waffen und gerade Fraktionsskills wirklich unterlegen sind.
[/list]

[b]Tipps für Anfänger[/b]:
[olist]
    [*]Stell die Auto-Speichern Funktion auf 3 Minuten. Du musst dir nie wieder Sorgen um den Spielstand machen. An wenigen Stellen solltest du trotzdem selber speichern.
    [*]Erkunde die Welt und loote aufmerksam. Also noch aufmerksamer als in der Risen Reihe. Man übersieht extrem schnell etwas, wenn man nur halbherzig lootet.
    [*]Überleg dir 2 mal ob Diebstahl oder Truhen knacken nötig bzw nützlich sind. Jetzt zahlst du Strafe beim Vorherscher des jeweiligen Ortes, solltest du bei einer Straftat erwischt werden.
[/olist]

Man kann also abschließend sagen, dass sich von Risen zu Elex einiges getan hat und, dass es technologisch betrachtet einen weiten Sprung von Risen 3 gemacht hat. Die Welt und Charaktere aus Elex sind weiterhin eine Stärke des Spiels, hinzukommt diesmal ein überlegenes Questdesign und eine Story die zum Mitdenken einlädt. Der Soundtrack ist sehr passend und vll sogar passender als der der letzten Teile, verliert dadurch aber die Nostalgie außerhalb der Spielwelt. Elex ist ein rumdum gelungenes Spiel und bereitet auf 60-80 Stunden vollen Spielspaß in seiner Welt und mit seinen Charakteren.

TLDR is that I regret not playing this much earlier. It has its issues but there's a lot here that pulls you into it's world. Also, playing this game eventually gets rewarding as you feel the growth of your Jax.

[b]Graphics and Audio[/b]
It's a here and there situation. Some parts of the game look good and some parts are just poorly textured. It's not a triple A game but you have to admit the developers did well where they could. The audio part of this game is  its weakest aspect. The sound design can feel flat and character/NPC voice overs can feel uneven.

[b]Story[/b]
Piranha Bytes has an awkward and familiar way of delivering the story. The main character basically has to find out what led him to the intro sequence of the game and win over the favor of factions. There are a lot of conversations in the game plus the developer also made an effort to give closure with a few additional lines of talk when quests are done. You aren't even prompted at times. Just like the Witcher 3, you have to find out for yourself if NPCs have additional information to give you.

[b]Gameplay[/b]
Oh man, it's rough at the start. As you work your way up, you easily drop with a few hits and you swing or shoot like a wet noodle. It's partially due to the awkwardness of controls in movement and combat but if you just keep at it, things become rewarding. You will get to a point where you will enjoy punishing those enemies that gave you such a hard time. Piranha balanced it out though where you still can be taken down even at end game so being cautious is still a thing.

The other mechanics are fairly standard for RPGs - attribute points, earning currencies, skill points..it's all there. The only thing is that while it may seem you get a lot of points when you gain levels or drink Elex pots, some gear requires a lot of a certain attribute. So you can't be careless when distributing attribute or skill points.

[h1]Słowem wstępu[/h1]
Elex jest grą upośledzoną. Ewidentnie widać w niej czerpanie pełnymi garściami z serii Gothic, przy jednoczesnym podejściu do (trudnego bądź co bądź) tematu połączenia magii i miecza oraz zaawansowanej technologii w jednym świecie. Na przykład podczas przebywania w wiosce Berserków - frakcji, która nie używa technologii, a wręcz jej zabrania, możecie odnieść silne wrażenie, że gracie w kolejnego Gothica. Ale wystarczy przejść do budynku zarządcy, żeby wybiło nas z tego odczucia, gdyż budynkiem tym jest postapokaliptyczny, mocno zniszczony hotel.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
Sam gameplay jest dyskusyjny. Wprowadzono plecak odrzutowy, który pozwala nam dostać się niemal w każde miejsce (oczywiście jego użycie jest ograniczone do kilku sekund, ale w wiele miejsc możemy polecieć „na raty”. Kolejnym babolem jest strzelanie z łuku, gdzie parabola strzał jest jakaś kosmiczna i ewidentnie grawitacja Magalana jest znacznie mocniejsza niż Ziemska ;-). System walki wręcz też pozostawia wiele do życzenia. Po wyciągnięciu broni postać automatycznie focusuje się na wrogu i trzeba klikać, żeby zmienić cel czy w ogóle obrócić się w innym kierunku (a podczas walki to raczej wątpliwa przyjemność). Kiedy walczymy z jednym przeciwnikiem, to nie ma on szans. Zupełnie jak w Arcanii, wystarczy spamować lewym przyciskiem myszy i przeciwnik nie może nam odpowiedzieć. Gorzej jest, kiedy przeciwników jest więcej, gdyż po zabiciu jednego, żeby obrócić się w ogóle do następnego, należy się zatrzymać i pozwolić postaci obrać kierunek (lub odskoczyć i wtedy „wycelować”). Mało tego, przeciwnicy też potrafią nas zasypać gradem ciosów, przed którym ciężko się obronić, więc więcej niż jedna maszkara oznacza ciężką walkę... Przynajmniej na początku. Kiedy zaopatrzymy się w broń palną, powyższy problem znika niemal całkowicie. Broń jest niezwykle celna, a lepsze modele dosyć szybko masakrują kolejnych przeciwników. W połowie gry w ogóle porzuciłem walkę wręcz, bo stała się bezsensowna...

[h1]Fabuła[/h1]
Historia przedstawiona w Elex jest... przeciętna. Motywacje naszego bohatera są proste (zemsta), a podczas dążenia do celu pozostawiamy za sobą masę trupów kasty, do której fabularnie początkowo należeliśmy. I to tylko po to, by w jednym z zakończeń prostym dialogiem przyłączyć się do antagonisty. Okej?

Bardzo boli mnie mała ilość rozwiązań questów. Nawet bardzo oczywiste kroki, które przychodzą nam do głowy na rozwiązanie jakiegoś zadania, nierzadko nie zostały przewidziane przez twórców i musimy wybrać bardzo niesatysfakcjonującą drogę, typu "zabić A, lub zabić B" bez możliwości ich pogodzenia, co powinno być możliwe, bo odkrywamy, że wrogość między A i B była wynikiem nieporozumienia.

Niestety polonizacja również nie pomaga. Mimo pełnego udźwiękowienia, część dialogów pisanych i mówionych się rozjeżdża, a sporo też jest sytuacji, w których teksty po prostu wariują i są zupełnie nie na temat. Tak jakby zostały tam wklejone z innych dialogów i zaczynasz się zastanawiać o czym w ogóle mówi twój rozmówca. Istnieją też sytuacje, w których wybieramy 3 słowną linię dialogową, która powinna prowadzić do określonego kierunku rozmowy, a podczas wymiany 10 dialogów, na które dalej nie mamy już wpływu, wychodzi zupełnie odwrotne rozwiązanie niż to, do którego dążyliśmy...

Hi my name is Jay and for a bit over a month I experienced an incredibly involved choice driven RPG that unlike many other RPG's kept me intrigued all the way to the end. That RPG of course is ELEX.

ELEX is a post apocalyptic sci-fi rpg with 3 different main factions to choose from that all dramatically effect the outcome of the story and how combat works. I went with a fairly difficult build but there are options to make the game easier although even if you do choose to make it as easy as possible it will still give you a challenge. I was on difficult the entire playthrough till the end where I reduced it but I was still glad I had been playing on a harder difficulty because it taught me how the combat worked. It's very flawed and unfortunately the worst part of the game however can be fun in combination with the jet pack.

Elex is a game about story first and there is a lot of it to cover. Many characters are interesting and there are many bomb shells dropped as you go along. But what is Elex actually about? Long ago a comet hit the planet and infected the world with a substance known as Elex. Those who used it for conquest became detached from emotion through dependency while also becoming stronger. These people are known as The Albs and they wish to gather all Elex on the planet killing anyone and anything that stands in their way. You (Jax) are executed for failing an unknown mission that has left you with no faction or gear after it failed.

I could go on and on about how incredible the story is and how dynamic the choices are but it would ruin the experience. If you can get past the poor combat it's certainly worth a playthrough even if you are not an RPG fan.


Note: After finishing I went and pre purchased Elex II. It's an incredible foundation what has been built here and I am excited to see where it goes.

How do I chain combos? Well, you must figure it out.
How do I reflect attacks? Well, you must figure it out.
What skills are useless and which useful? Well, you must figure it out.
How not to die all the time? Well, you must figure it out.
Why can't I win by spamming left click and potions? Because it's not Skyrim or Assassin Creed.
Why is the game so frustrating to play? Because you don't want to learn something new.
Where do I go make progress in the quest? Well, you must figure it out. (Hint: read what they say or press the Z button).
If you decide to play this game the same way you would a typical rpg, you will get killed all the time. Nothing scales to you, meaning most monster and people will one shot you. However, it is technically possible to kill the strongest monster in the begging of the game. It's all up to your personal skills. The equipment  can only help you so far. I found myself bullied all throughout the game, even with the best items, and always forced  to pick my fights. That's what I love about this game. It reminds you that you're just a single guy. You aren't meant to take on an army all by yourself and if you position yourself poorly, you will get overwhelmed even by the weaker enemies. Well, if you pick melee combat that is. It's fairly simple to cheese the hell out of this game, but I just consider it game knowledge and learning its mechanics rather than an oversight. Let me just say this, if you really spend time learning how to fight you will get rewarded with a lot of satisfaction. 
I don't want to spoil the story, but I find it unique and captivating. The lore of this game is done masterfully. You can find notes, books and recordings everywhere giving you a sense of a tragically destroyed world. The strongest aspect of this game has to be exploration. Jax can use his jet pack to fly absolutely everywhere, There are hundreds of hidden items to be found in every nook and cranny. It really is ridiculous how stuffed the world is, despite its size. Just don't forget to advance the main quest every now and then. It adds a lot to the world building.
My only gripes have to be with the bugs. Characters disappear just to appear out of nowhere. Glitchy movement animations and so on. Nothing game breaking really, but it did break the immersion for me every now and then.
If you've ever played a Piranha Bytes game and enjoyed it, it should be an insta buy for you.

Man, this game is so weird. I've played it for almost 80 hours altogether and am currently on a second playthrough. I've been finding it pretty enjoyable for the most part, but the eurojank is definitely there.

ELEX is a post-apocalyptic sci-fi action RPG that takes place on Magalan, a planet that was hit by a comet made of magic space rocks called elex. The world got totally screwed, but humanity is stubborn, so they survived and managed to limp on by forming together into different factions who each use elex for their own various purposes. 

You play as Jax, a commander among the Albs, a group of emotionless magic techno-fascists who consume elex in order to become mad stronk. Unfortunately, you are betrayed in the opening cutscene and left for dead in the mountains, have all your cool tech stolen, and end up in a week-long coma that purges all the elex from your system, making you super weak as you go through elex withdrawl and start to experience emotions for the first time. 

The best part of this game is definitely the setting. You've got this huge open world map with various biomes, each occupied by one of the main factions, three of which are playable (the Albs being the fourth). In the lush forests of Edan, you have the Berserkers, magical vikings who have sworn off technology and have discovered how to use elex to create mana and use magic to restore nature. In the ruin-filled deserts of Tavar, you have the Outlaws, a Mad Max/Fallout-style gang/crime syndicate with chainswords, elex-enhanced drugs, and lots of leather. In the volcanic wastes of Ignadon, you have the Clerics, psionic techno-fascist religious zealots with elex-based technology on par with the Albs. And of course, in the frozen north of Xacor, you have the aforementioned Albs, the main enemies of the game. See, the Albs work for a creature called the Hybrid who has been directing them to gather ALL of the elex, which includes the elex inside of people. Naturally, people do not like this very much, so conflict is pretty much the constant. 

Over the course of the game, Jax is forced to side with one of the factions in order to get stronger and find out what the hell is going on back in Xacor. Each faction has its own draws, unique abilities and equipment, and effects on the story depending on which one you side with. Personally, I usually go with the Clerics, because I like their shooty energy guns and psionic powers, and I've always wanted to try out being in a cult. They also may or may not have mind-controlled me into joining, but whatever.

Combat in ELEX is very souls-like; you have stamina for your strikes, dodges, blocks and can do timed parries (and once you unlock the skill for it, you can even do melee attacks from the air with your jetpack, which is awesome). There's also a combo system, so the more successive hits you make on an enemy, the more damage you'll do with each strike, and then you can unleash a special attack once you land enough hits. There's ranged combat as well, which plays like a pretty standard third person over-the-shoulder shooter, and you can even hover midair with your jetpack while shooting things. Unfortunately, combat is where a lot of the eurojank is apparent. Sometimes your attacks just don't hit because reasons, or an enemy's attack will track you when it shouldn't, or you'll get stunlocked by a heavy weapon until you die, or a bunch of other shenanigans that are escaping me right now.

The progression system is pretty weird. As you level up, you gain points to put in attributes, but iirc, these actually do nothing on their own; they simply serve as requirements for equipment as well as skills you buy from trainers. The way looting works makes it really hard to find better gear too; enemies almost never drop weapons or armor (even though you had all your weapons and armor looted in the opening), so gear improvements are restricted to things you can buy in shops and occasionally stuff that has been manually placed in the world. 

You also start the game off really weak, like basically unable to defeat anything in direct combat outside the tutorial weak, so a lot of the early game is trying to get XP from doing fetch quests and running away from things with skulls in their healthbars. However, after about a third of the way into the game (level 15 or so) you'll actually to be able to stand and fight a decent portion of the enemies you'll encounter, especially if you keep a companion with you. In the endgame, you'll be the one with the skulls in your health bar (not literally), destroying nearly everything you encounter with just a few hits from your Giga-Chad Sword of Lightning +3 or whatever. 

Overall, I think I really enjoyed the game, even with the jankiness, and am actually pretty hyped for the sequel coming out in about a month. This game isn't everyone's cup of tea, but if you like action RPGs with really interesting settings and are willing to stomach the eurojank, you'll probably enjoy ELEX.

What a hopeless feedback loop: in order to be strong enough to do anything in the game you need to finish quests. To finish quests you need to kill enemies. But you are so weak that you can't kill the enemies needed to finish the quests. So you have to explore every mountain top and valley in hopes of finding something that can kill enemies so you can finish quests. But most of the good weapons you find during exploration can't be used because your base stats are too weak to use them. But the only way to increase your stats is to level up your character by finish quests by killing things. It took me a long time to figure a way out of this loop. Many hours were spent wandering around looking for easy quests or easy kills. Dozens of hours.

The easiest solution to the problem of the loop is to join a faction. With three main factions you have a few choices. The Berserkers use magic and have a strict code against technology. Clerics use technology and psionic powers. Outlaws use drugs and regular weapons. All three factions will give you powers or weapons that will make it possible to kill. They will make it possible for you to become stronger. 

The Berserkers are the easiest to join because you are literally led to them within the first few minutes of the game. Their fire spell will deal with all early enemies and most mid game enemies. Naturally they won't let you just walk into their town and join. You have to earn your place in their society by doing them favors. Quests. Sounds easy. Should be easy. Wasn't. Because of their code, you have to do the quests a certain way. I did them another way so they wouldn't let me join their group. 

That left two more groups, but they are a bit harder to find. The clerics are on the far north east of the map, while the outlaws are on the far south. Since I had no choice, I made the journey. I accepted another group of quests. Unfortunately these groups are located in a far more dangerous part of the world. Which means the enemies are even harder to kill. I slammed up against a wall. 

There was another way. Without magic, psi powers, or drugs you have to find a good killing weapon. A flame thrower can be bought fairly cheap and is as effective as the Berserker fire spell, but requires much higher stats than you can gain by simple kills. Fortunately there is this substance called natural Elex. It can be used to make potions that will give you points to add to your stats so you can use the flame thrower. Natural Elex can be found. More importantly it can be bought. It can be bought almost everywhere. With my new stats and my new flamethrower I could finally kill instead of be killed. I could finally be strong. The loop was broken.

Why am I telling you this? So you will know that this game is hard. It has some really punishing game mechanics. Melee combat involves stamina and timed hits. Lose stamina and you become helpless. If you pick the wrong perk you won't get enough loot to sell or be able to brew potions. Level up the wrong stat and you won't be able to use a good weapon. If you make the wrong choice in dialogue or quests you may get killed or be cut off from story options.

But it is a satisfying journey if you can overlook these flaws. There are dozens of companions with their own quests. Your actions affect how the story unfolds, who dies, and how the story ends. Most of the game mechanics are solid: save anytime except during boss battles and cut scenes, fast travel via teleporters, a jet pack that allows you to explore the top of just about any mountain, unique perks, interesting companions with their own quests. Explore deserts, jungles, mountains, forests, ruined towns. Kill dozens of unique creatures.


conclusion

a very frustrating but satisfying journey of exploration with an interesting branching story that changes according to your actions.

One of the absolute worst games I have ever played. I am a massive fan of Gothic 1 and 2, but this game is garbage. 

Note: I set all settings to default difficulty and mechanics, and had maxed graphics.

Hitboxes are inconsistent in every way, with some having active damage frames and some having a system where the time the attack is started is what determines when the damage is done, not if the weapon hit you or not. The world building is nonsensical, and Jax is a boring, unlikable character. The cold system makes very little sense, and has the worst faith interpretation of the players intention with responses. The enemy design is lazy, with something around 6 or 7 enemy types that at just re-skinned in different areas of the map. The leveling is retarded, with all stat levels above 30 costing two points instead of one, effectively stunting the leveling from even the early game. The AI seems like it was lobotomized prenatally, and are unbalanced in every way, with enemy stamina not being an active system. I also have an itching suspicion that NPCs ignore armor when attacking other NPCs. The art style is fine, even very interesting and engaging in some locations, but the graphical fidelity is horrid. The NPCs have much more in common with DND miniatures than with something resembling a person, and the draw distance is shamefully small for a game in 2017. The user interface, again, is significantly worse than that of Gothic 2. All items are in long lists that don't let you look at the item in your inventory, and the map and quest log are ugly to look at. Another issue with the quest design in this game is that there are quest markers. After about the 5 hour mark, I got bored of listening to the character voices and annoying dialog, and skipped through every line of dialog that I could. This would allow me to get a little quest arrow on my map, and I could go to the place, maybe check my journal once, and know exactly what I needed to do without turning my brain on for a second. Gothic 2's strength has a lot to do with it's world, it is logical historically and easy to navigate, whereas Magalan is nonsensical, with rediculous jutts of earth randomly placed around the land and biomes that change in an instant. This makes navigation to a single location that is marked instantly on your map tedious, and bored me out of my mind. The combo system is interesting, being that you increase your damage per swing as the combo meter fills, but if you use your special, the meter is reset. This has a clear better option to it, to never use your special. It takes between 3 and 4 swings to activate the special attack, but closer to 6 to fill the combo bar and max your damage. This is impossible in the early game, due to the incredibly small stamina pool that Jax has without skill point investment and/or rings that increase stamina, fooling the player into thinking the special is a good option later in the game. The companions are flat and uninteresting, with stories attached to them by scotch tape, but no character traits themselves. The crime system is retarded, with every NPC in the area going on a rampage if you accidentally pick up the wrong item, with no option to just return the item. There was even an odd situation where I was attacked by an NPC mid-conversation, I defended myself, and it was reported as a crime. Again, somehow 2002's Gothic 2 is vastly superior.

The only positive that I can give this game at the time of playing is that bugs are minimal. I only remember 1 instance of falling through the floor when I died, and ragdolls flying through the air when being walked over by mechs is more entertaining than annoying.

Please do not play this game. I understand this is late in the game's play-cycle, but please make Pirahna Bytes learn something from this game. They were amazing 20 years ago, and I kept asking myself as I was playing: how did they forget everything that made them great?

I will start with the good first, Elex is like a mix of fallout meets skyrim with a difficulty of a souls game. The open world is pretty large and has some really pretty areas if you can get past the dated graphics. There is heaps of lore in this game and almost everything can be looted. The story is pretty good for what i have been through so far, there is a good amount of armor/weapons. Elex has a fairly nice level/point system to it. Like skyrim you make choices in this game that affect you and the story. The voice acting is actually not bad for the most part. Elex has a pretty nice reputation function to the game that can really help you out or penalize you. The one thing i really like about Elex is you are not locked out of content by level restrictions or story progression, that is huge to me since a lot of games now a days seem to do this. In Elex it seems as you can pretty much do what ever you want when you want,you are not forced to do 1 thing before another. 



Okay now for the bad. As Elex is a good game it does come with it's negatives, the combat system is there as far as basic moves blocking dodging/parrying goes along with some other things,but it is VERY clunky!!!!! the best way i can describe this is think of the witcher 1 fighting, not to good as it is really annoying to control as it seems to be a bit delayed and sluggish. The movement in Elex is not much better, it to is not very responsive and is also hard to control. but with that said you can get use to it and adapt. you can loot just about anything in Elex but for some reason you can only loot things if you holster your weapon, as this is not anything to serious it just gets annoying. Elex has a good amount of enemies in it's world but unfortunately low level enemies can be mixed in with high level enemies, so what i mean is there is not areas with level limits, this means that you can be running around in the starting area and come across a enemy with a skull above it, this is not a game breaking thing it is just a bit rough is all. Obviously since this game is a bit dated the graphics are not the best. Elex has a LOT of talking in it and can get a little boring. There are some visual glitches that you will see when playing Elex like things clipping through stuff or just bad placement of things along with flickering lighting ect.. You will die A LOT when first starting out as it takes time to get use to the clunky fighting and movement. The way the lock picking system works is kinda janky and will take a min to figure it out. When fighting and killing things you would think like in most games you would get xp from it,well not in Elex, for some reason you only get xp when completing quests. When entering any building from outside it takes a moment for it to go from pitch black to where you can see, as i understand this to be a mechanic that is mimicking eye adjustment it just gets very annoying quickly as it just takes to long. Sometimes when fighting a enemy you will notice that you can become stun locked sorta speak, so what i mean is for some stupid reason enemies do not seem to have a stamina feature to them like you do, so what this means is they can just spam attack you with out ever having to stop,so you can become stuck in an endless stun as you are just being repeatedly attacked and there is not much you can do to get out of it once this happens, the best thing i found to avoid this from happening is to just use range attacks for when there is more than 1 enemy.



Overall Elex is not a bad game it just is a bit dated and has it's flaws for sure. I bought this game on sale for 10$ so i can not really wine to much lol, but i can say i do not think id pay the whole asking price for the game, i would say 20-30$ would seem fair. At the end of the day if you enjoy a game like skyrim/fallout with a dark souls game difficulty to it, then this is the game for you, if not then i would keep looking else where.

O jogo é excelente no que ele se propõem a fazer, o mapa, as quests, a história, a progressão do personagem, o sistema que divide o personagem em frio ou emocional e principalmente o jeito de recompensar o jogador pelos esforços são todos muito bem feitos e originais.
Entretanto, tem pessoas  que pensam que o jogo é como qualquer outro rpg da atualidade e acabam não gostando, então vou tentar explicar pra quem viu as análises da steam dessas pessoas e ficou com dúvidas do porque o jogo divide tantas opiniões.

O jogo realmente tem alguns bugs e problemas técnicos sendo esse o maior problema do jogo, várias vezes o boneco vai mirar no personagem errado, rolar sem querer pra um lado, no final do jogo alguns loadings vão ser muito grandes, sem falar que o jogo pode crashar algumas vezes
Só que a dificuldade e a progressão que muitos criticam não é um erro, o jogo foi feito para que no começo você seja extremamente fraco de forma proposital, ele força o jogador evitar combates no inicio do game e a fazer missões mais simples, não é como muitos jogos que te permitem vencer o boss final já no nível 1, e aos poucos você vai ficando extremamente forte de uma forma muito recompensadora, os inimigos que antes não matava mesmo no 2x1 você passa a vencer grupos pequenos. Quem entra no jogo pensando que é um hack in slash que vai deixar entrar no meio de 3 inimigos e sair com a vida cheia vai se dar mal, pode ser o inimigo mais fraco do jogo, no começo, vai ser um desafio grande se estiver sozinho.

PRO: 
- Story line has lots of options, and even after you join a faction you still have a whole world to explore and quests you can complete even if they are from an opposing faction
-Openworld - huge map, lots to explore. fun fun fun!
-Companions: Interesting enough story-lines, semi-useful in battle (and that can be improved) which is a huge help in the beginning
Factions - All the factions, even the Separatists, have good and bad qualities. There is no purely evil faction (that you can join) and that gives Elex a nice balance. I was really torn over which faction to join! And now I def want to replay with a new faction
CON:
-There are no tutorials, to the point where I was level 20 and only just discovered a command that made things 50% easier.
-Looting/shops are everywhere (good) - BUT there is no explanation on what you should keep v sell. And that will vary a lot based on your faction, and that is frustrating esp. in the beginning when you need cash
-Fighting is clunky. I died so many times because of the delay in switching between weapons.
-Skill Tree: Some of the skills A)require too high stats (by the time you get to that point you really don't even need  the skill or B) are not relevant or effect such a minor part of the game you are just throwing away your money (pick-pocketing, hacking)

As a gothic and RPG fan, this game turned out to be a real gem. I originally tried this game for a half an hour and then never touched it again for 4 years. As a fan of medieval setting, the fact you can get guns and stuff totally ruined it for me, or so i thought. Now, at 2022, i gave it another chance, having no other good rpg games to play and seeing this game on sale on christmas. 

I played 14 hours on my first day. That says a lot as i am a 37  year old with wife and kids. My saturday just went by like nothing. I got so immersed into it. I literally had to drag myself away from my pc at 2 hours after midnight.

It is tough at the beginning for sure and you have to do a lot of running away and sleeping to get the health back up again  but slowly you get stronger, you get familiar with the enemies, you learn how and how fast stuff attacks you, who you can beat, you learn to do combos and use jetback to get edge in battles. You get friends, companions, you do quests, you steal from bad people and step by step you get better gear, you get better at game and your character gets stronger.

All of the small jumps in your skill and power feel so rewarding. I love i can now 3 hit those damn oversized chickens that i had to run away from on the first 10 hours of the game. Just like those damn chickens in gothic games.

Overall, this game is totally a must have for me and i cant wait for the sequel.

[h1] Предисловие [/h1]
Ну чтож, начну с того что ELEX довольно странный проект, но при этом он необходимый для самих пираней, после тех же Risen, серия которой почему-то ушла от ламповой тематики средневековья к пиратской стилистике. Зачем? Кто этого ожидал? Я уж точно нет. И между тем первая Risen мне очень заходила, чего не скажешь о продолжениях, которых мне хватило на 1 раз. И я очень надеюсь что пираньи не будут тут на столько заигрывать с сюжетом.

[h1] ELEX [/h1]
Но обзор сейчас не об этом, а о ELEX. 
Итак, ELEX. ELEX- очень странная игра, текстурки мыльные, сцены в катсценах образца 2012 года. Сразу видно что издатель в лице THQ выделил довольно маленькую сумму на разработку, возможно скептически смотря на данную затею.
Но несмотря на старый движок, берущий начало с готики и Risen, несмотря на свою несуразносить, игра стоящая. Стоящая именно своей атмосферой и ламповостью, коими и славятся пираньи. 
Раз за разом пираньи пытаются сделать идеальную готику, ну чтож... в плане сюжетца и атмосферы у них есть успехи. Каждая фракция имеет чуть ли не тройное дно если её изучать, у каждой есть своя серая мораль в том или ином вопросе. И это не плохо! Лично я не ощутил такого же тройного дна во фракциях Risen. И тем более готики.

[h1] Минусы [/h1]
Огромным минусом ELEX является конечно гейм дизайн врагов. А точнее их расстановка, из-за чего создаётся странный искуственный барьер уровня сложности. Когда первые несколько часов игры ты просто огребаешь от любого зверька который только взглянет в твою сторону. Огрибаешь смачно, и с пары тычек. Даже спустя 10 часов геимплея ты продолжаешь огребать, всё так же смачно, но уже можешь убивать мелких врагов и даже... людей. 
А огребать с боёвкой, чьё начало идёт от Risen и готики - не очень, учитывая деревянность некоторых боевых механик в плане их устаревания. 
И ведь забавно что опыт дающийся за врагов фиксированный на игру. Т.е. ты с голой попой можешь побежать на условного огра, бья его по ляхам минут 30, и получить супер мизерное количество опыта! Да за миссии дают больше! От чего не стыдно агрить разбойников на диких зверей. Особенно забавно выглядит когда агришь штук 20 разбойников на 1 троля, который их выносит за пару минут.

А потом ты находишь в попе мира пушку-огнестрел, которая станет врагов, качаешь условную ловкость чтобы её держать, и игра резко становится очень лёгкой.

Зачем это было сделано? Не понятно. Но агрить противников на зверей можно было и в предыдущих играх, учитывая специфику игр пираней... но блин, там это не имело смысл, т.к. опыта больше давали, и он был важнее! А тут жлобить условные 10 exp - такое себе, учитывая размер мира. 

Ну и плюс ИИ не поумнел со времён готики, что я не считаю минусом для игр пираней, тут соль не в этом. Хотя... тут не однозначно. Задатки прогресса есть у некоторых врагов. К примеру когда убегаешь от альбов, отойдя от них на метров 10, они всё же достают пушки, начиная в тебя откровенно шмалять... чего не скажешь о бандитах, которые имея мушкеты будут бежать за тобой аки волки, и мушкеты достанут только если высоко залезть, либо взлететь. 

[h1] Плюсы [/h1]
И вот если вы пересилите этот треш в плане такой сложности, перейдя этот порог вхождения, то вам откроется волшебный мир ламповости и сюжетца тех самых пираней. Мир который таки интересно изучать. Сюжет сложным не назвать, он лежит на поверхности, но он интересен в своём изучении, как и изучение самих фракций игры. 
Боёвка тоже играет новыми красками когда учишься использовать джетпаком как способом уклонения и так врага. 

Даже вариативность квестов встречается. Позволю себе микро спойлер для описания. 
К примеру, в одном задании нужно помочь с поставками еды охотникам. И вот тут можно поговорить с охотниками, и помочь им собирая овощи для долгого пропитания до возможных поставок еды, а можно найти за амбаром плеснёвый хлеб, и принести им со словами "ну вы держитесь". И ведь они примут, т.к. мало ели в последние дни, а тот же хлеб уже забыли как выглядит. 
Что забавно, глава фракции потом вас отчитает, ибо в место чтобы нести вахту, охотники теперь дежурят очередью у туалета. 

И вот за такую ламповость мини квестов я и люблю пираней! 

[h1] Вывод [/h1]
В общем повторюсь, что если вам нравятся ламповые миры, то это игра для вас... Если конечно осилите порог вхождения, перейдя через эти "волшебные" геймдизайнерские решения в плане баланса врагов. И входить в эту игру действительно довольно сложно. И ради этого придётся пострадать, и довольно много. Но того стоит как по мне, игра не плоха несмотря на всё это.

[h1] Постскриптум [/h1]
Русской озвучки тут скорей всего нет из-за низкого бюджета на разработку игры, ровно как и мыло в катсценах.
Но вот уже по игровому трейлеру второй части видно подросший бюджет + там будет русская озвучка, что радует.

Combat is very tough at the beginning, but after you gain enough experience to get better equipment and after joining a faction, the fun begins. Overall, I really enjoyed playing Elex and can't wait to play the sequel.

8/10 - wish I played this rough gem earlier
+ Phenomenal environmental story telling. Hand crafted exquisite post apocalyptic ruins - eye candy galore
+ Strong mature story and competent narrative driving the plot along well
+ Excellent gameplay mechanics and that Dark Souls/DBZ feelz of going from zero to hero
+ Distinct upgrade systems offering something new from your usual AAA copy paste garbage
+ Great trichotomy of factions set to flesh out the world day to day life and themes. All well done with engaging storylines, characters with twists and turns with much humor
+ A bounty of side characters almost all engaging and some you want to stick with on and on
+ Combat, skills, upgrades and enemies provide much variety to tactical approaches once you're past a certain power level
+ Strong art direction with all world corners and cities shining in different lights

- Silly difficulty. First third of the game you run away. Second third you kite and fight. Last act you demolish everything with ease. Makes the game play very different and provides a very high barrier of entry due to the first 10-15 hours being so rough where you are the prey.
- This is a single A/double AA title. Polish is limited
- Screen tearing bugs. Stuck in textures. Rough controls.
- Limited upgrades & enemy variety
- Story drags in third act. Silly chapter titles where I spent 90% of my time in Chapter 1; seeing chapter 2, 3, 4 titles was strange.

For any Skyrim/Fallout/Witcher/Gothic fans this game is a wonderful experience that requires patience at first and then really opens up. Leaves you wanting more content.

Плюсы: 
1. Отличные ветвистые квесты, могущие выстрелить там, где вообще не ждешь.
2. Хорошее ощущение прогрессии: начинаешь обоссаным бомжем, потихоньку продвигаешься в выбранной фракции, зарабатываешь первую броню, апгрейдишь пушечки ну и т.д. Всё как вы любите в готике, только сложнее.
3. Прекрасный проработанный мир (любители horizon zero dawn будут ловить флешбеки), который интересно исследовать.
4. Интересные боевые механики (со своими недостатками о которых ниже): куча всяких интересных способностей (у каждой фракции свои), враги не будут вставать в ступоре практически никогда, если вы летаете вокруг них на джетпаке или забрались на горку, ведь почти у всех врагов есть дальнобойные атаки.
5. Как и в готике, эта игра не поощряет собирательство: всякие расходники типа заклинаний альбов лучше действительно использовать, а не складировать "на-потом-который-никогда-не-настанет".
6. Как и в готике, эта игра поощряет смекалку.

Минусы: 
1. Всоснейшее передвижение и корявые механики боев. В третьей готике передвижение персонажа было практически эталонным, крайне отзывчивым и плавным. Тут же всё какое-то дерганое, неотзывчивое. Половина монстров - эталонные безхитбоксовые мрази, ведь ты не попадешь в них из лука-ружья-плазмогана, если прицел при прицеливании не стал красным (натурально стрела может пролететь через [strike] колено [/strike] бочину, не нанеся урона). Выживать в ближнем бою я даже не пробовал.

2. Всоснейшие синематики (в плане постановки).

3. Некоторые системы работают через козий анус, типа того же хладнокровия. Вам периодически в диалогах будут писать, что ваше хладнокровие повышается или понижается, но при этом точных цифр вы не найдете.

4. Всосный кислотно-неоновый интерфейс инвентаря. Я понимаю, что сюжетно он обусловлен, но какая разница.

5. Невероятно скучный саундтрек. После третьей готики слушать прям больно.

В общем, начинал перепроходить несколько раз ради того, чтобы разные фракции пощупать. На фоне херовых игр по свиткам, игры пираний - прям отдушина.

Fun RPG. A lot of choices, a lot of consequences. Pretty nice graphics, good performance (doesn't stutter on 1080Ti, which I consider "good performance"), all (or almost all) dialog lines are voiced by actual voice actors, which is very nice.

The main issue I had with this game is fighting system. It takes a while to get used to (it is quite clunky). Starting hero is extremely weak and you won't be able to fight well for a very, VERY long time. So I swallowed my pride and dropped to easy difficulty. And that... didn't change anything, literally. I could perform more swings but, considering I was doing like 1% damage per hit and getting killed in 1-2 attacks by the weakest creatures, difficulty drop didn't help.

So what I did with the difficulty was just run around doing quests, run from *ANY* enemy I could see, get a companion to make running away easier (they get up if you move far enough and can tank like 3 hits) and grow my stats till I could use a bow (because growing stats alone doesn't affect damage, or health, or armor, or anything, really). And at some point the difficulty drop from "insanity!" to "trivial" - I could kill almost anything in 2-3 hits from the bow. At this point I was playing more for the story than fighting system.

The story was decent. Sadly, many pieces of the story remain disconnected, it doesn't all come together in one grand world where everything depends on everything, everyone's story is connected in some way. No, most characters are just plain generic characters with a bit of a story and that's about it. The main hero's story had a few twists and turns, which was fun.

Overall I'd recommend trying if you're into storytelling / RPG games, but be ready to play in "adventure mode" (running away from any enemy) for at least 15 levels (meaning, about 20 hours or so). The game evolves after that point, and opens up more options and opportunities.

My main issue with the game is, as I said, combat system. It feels extremely unrefined, the movement is very clunky, attack animations are very simple and there are like 3 sets of moves for three styles in melee fighting. AOE attacks with knockback are completely out of sync with the game, they can keep you (or groups of enemies) knocked out permanently over extended periods of time (I played with a bow to avoid exploiting this nonsense). The main issue with arrows is that they don't fly straight, they fly in an arc (slowly), easily miss your target, and your character aims at the point you're looking at, not the point where the enemy is. I'd prefer older Gothic arrow style - when the projectile flies straight for a while, then starts arcing after a while (and starts losing its power after some distance). I didn't use other weapons much because they were usually weaker than bows and required me to join a faction to upgrade weapons (which I didn't want to do till I did all the quests).

Another issue with difficulty - there is ZERO scaling. All enemies have fixed levels, fixed power, fixed damage, fixed health, fixed armor. They start as "impossibly hard" enemies, but later you wipe the floor with them. You can increase difficulty as you progress to compensate: enemies will take more hits to die, you will take fewer hits to die, enemies will attack more frequently, you'll be able to swing fewer times before running out of stamina... but overall it won't change much - you'll just need to swing a few more times.

Personally, I'd prefer a more fluid fighting system: closer to hack and slash, fewer animation lockups, faster swings, more mobility, less damage, ability to actually dodge attacks, skills (moves that perform some action to change the flow of battle or weaken enemies or make you stronger or crowd control). Or a slower, more predictable system - dodging evades or decreases damage, blocking decreases damage etc, slow swings that do not leave you or enemy stun locked, parrying, riposte, whatever - a system where you can react to opponent's action and take over the flow of combat. Like dark souls, witcher and many others.

TL;DR version:
Fun RPG with decent story, good graphics, nice voice acting (I've seen better, I've seen worse, I'd say this is pretty decent level to be at). Combat system leaves some things to be desired (you'll need more than a couple of hours to grow strong enough), although you can work with it (I completed the game on "easy" and don't regret it, usually I play on maxed out difficulty).

Чувствуется рука наших любимых мастеров. Потрясающая своими аспектами игра для тех, кто проводил детство/юношество в Готике.

Я довольно долго обходил стороной эту игру лишь по той причине, что мне никогда не нравилось смешение фентези и технологий. Мне всегда казалось, что это абсолютно несовместимые вещи, как сгущенка и копченая колбаса. Каждое хорошо по отдельности, но вместе они способны испортить вам экспириенс. Однако как же сильно я ошибался.

Посмотрев первые ролики по данной игре я подумал, что это Готика с пушками. Мне показалось, что создателям уже нечего придумать, кроме как намешать дикое хрючево из разных вселенных и жанров, и дать попробовать тем, кто ностальгирует по их былым проектам. 
Купил игру, потому что порядком насытился тем, что есть на рынке, повторяя про себя "а вдруг зайдет". И таки зашло. Зашло с такой силой, что я невольно впадаю в воспоминания, как я терпеливо по полтора часа ждал, пока установится любимая Готика 2 (которую я проходил около 20 раз, постоянно удаляя ее после очередного прохождения, ибо на винте у меня было всего 40гб, освобождая место для знакомства с новыми играми), как я наизусть знал каждый текст каждого персонажа, как дороги и милы мне были голоса Диего, Лестера, Ксардаса, Мильтена. Как стыдно мне было, что я использую единственный чит на воскрешение спутника в миссиях, где это было необходимо, потому что я любил их и не желал, чтобы они умирали. 
Играя в Elex я заново окунулся в эту прекрасную атмосферу, которую кропотливо создали Пираньи. Каждый диалог, каждая сцена, каждая локация, каждое событие здесь создано для того, чтобы мы с вами кайфовали как раньше. Я давно не помню такого, чтобы я прям вчитывался в то, что говорят персонажи, вникал в историю вселенной, пытался понять их мотивы, решения, религию, настроение. В этой игре невероятно интересно исследовать мир, проникаться сюжетом, делать выбор, который потом отразится на игре, принимать стороны тех или иных персонажей. У меня иногда создается впечатление, что я книгу читаю - настолько интересно Пираньи тут всё замутили. Прекрасно озвученные персонажи только дополняют эти ощущения. Я уверен, что если бы не знал, кто разработчик и издатель этой игры, то все равно поиграв понял бы, чей это шедевр. В нем есть что-то такое родное и приятное.

Для многих спорным моментом будет являться боевка и не совсем поначалу понятная прокачка. Однако когда вы постигните их, вы начнете наслаждаться и понимать, что тупое закликивание врага, присущее в других проектах - это просто скучный и однобокий процесс.

В большинстве современных игр есть графоний, но нет души. Собственно творения Пираний никогда и не были про графику, зато всегда были про душу. 
Это потрясающий и очень ламповый проект от талантливых мастеров. Ознакомиться с которым я крайне рекомендую. После неспешных 35 часов тут, я не изучил и 20% того, что предлагает игра. Спешить тут не хочется, а наоборот, хочется подробнее вникнуться и ничего не упускать. 
Я абсолютно точно приобрету вторую часть, когда она выйдет - эта серия должна и будет жить.

I usually wait till either my game is completed or more hours than 10 here, but there's an exception to this game. Not surprising though being on a console. Now here on PC? Its even better, graphics are way better and the game isn't laggy by any means. A flawed diamond of a game with a little different gameplay philosophy. It took a minute to adjust to the utter weakness of your initial character. Normally in these kind of RPGs you are a match for about 2-3 low level enemies. In Elex, you are easily killed by anything. You spend the first 5-10 hours running from enemies and doing story/side quests to get stronger to where you can fight back. That leads to the next strange mechanic, the combat. It feels like a combination of realtime souls-esque hit and dodge style with a queued-up hit combo mechanic. It makes the combat feel clunky, laggy and unresponsive initially. Once you start to watch enemy patterns and don't spam attacks it gets better.

On the other hand, the setting and story is amazing. A well thought out combination of sci-fi and fantasy, faith and tech. The morality system is not good vs evil, but human vs robotic, heart vs logic. The companions were well thought out and varied, well voiced, but not very long.

All in all, a good foundation for a franchise that I look forward to playing more of.

如何在残酷的ELEX世界内提高生还几率：
前期遇到怪就跑吧，刮痧不值得。先去做杜拉斯的伙伴任务，做一半就能拉他入伙。之后每次打架都让小伙伴上，你只需在一旁左右横跳耐心等待敌人的死亡即可。
前期商店能买的衣服性价比不高，还不如快速入一个派系，会送一件比商店里都牛逼的衣服。派系任务不用每个都完美达成，我的是狂战，做崩了好几个任务把牧师放跑了什么的，但是只要有钱（买赎罪券）就一切皆有可能，所以做任务随心就好了。
前期缺钱，所以第一个技能学偷窃，caps-lock键潜行然后你就知道了什么叫遍地是黄金，每个npc随身携带30~100+钱，等天黑他们都睡了再去偷，真正的一夜暴富。
开锁技能没什么用，需要开锁的箱子少，好多都只能用钥匙开，要不就是需要2、3级开锁才能开，顺带讲一下怎么开锁，只能用鼠标操作，左右移动，直到所有锁都被撬起变蓝。
讲一下目前遇到的前期非常好用的近战武器，商店里买的锯齿剑，配一块盾牌，战斗只用轻击，速度快伤害很可观。
顺带讲一下土匪女伙伴任务第二个任务里巨型boss怎么快速打，把商店全部手榴弹买光（大概二三十个），一开场就狂丢手榴弹等丢完boss就只剩一点血了，然后近身用前期捡到的那几个智械科技什么冲击波什么的轰几下boss就归西了。前期其他的武器打这个boss都是刮痧，它打你跟开挂一样，丢出来的石头会自动跟踪根本躲不开，只能靠手榴弹把它炸出硬直。

Ну и самая главная претензия - геймплей. Обошёл первый город, выполнил все задания, которые нашёл и смог сделать, и прокачался... на целых 3 уровня. И всё. Для всех остальных заданий в самом городе нужны определённые характеристики (или навыки, или ещё что - я хз, по вариантам ответов даже не понятно чего мне не хватает) или элексит. Если идти на задания за городом, то тебя завалит первый же попавшийся бандит, отступник или какая живность, а если попытаешься куда-нибудь забраться или улететь от них - они сразу же начинают стрелять из лука/пушки, или чем-то плеваться (выглядит странно, так как это единственный случай, когда они этим пользуются). Даже убегать от них неудобно, так как камера в бою направляется на противника и не поворачивается. Сама боёвка топорная. С оружием и одеждой видимо тоже будут проблемы, причём как с их поиском, так и с прокачкой персонажа, чтобы их использовать. И сразу становится понятно, что игра будет какой-то дрочильней, где нужно набивать опыт на всяких тараканах да крысах, чтобы как-то выжить.

Elex  is apparently an incredibly well thought out rpg with some great design leading to choices really impacting your playthroughs, it is everything you'd want from a storytelling perspective.

I didn't get that far, as you might have guessed from the negative review. 

Elex might have fantastic world building, but what it lacks is enjoyable gameplay. The combat is genuinely infuriating. To start there's a glass wall which prevents you from even dealing damage to higher level enemies as their armour or damage resistance nullifies all of yours. That wouldn't be a problem if enemies werent spread out randomly throughout the map, for example there's a troll which will oneshot you (and anything else for that matter) right next to where your "base" is (or what I'm assuming the base is). Either of these gameplay elements would be fine, on their own.  In fact I would actively endorse game developers spreading out high level enemies through their maps because it makes the game more exciting. Together here it just serves to create said glass walls barring your passage at certain intersections. It is artificial and more annoying.

Onto the combat though? 

In theory you've got a dodge, parry strike system with stamina. Enemies are auto locked on and you can switch between them. In practice, because enemies are often lunging at you whenever there's more than one enemy fighting you you get the oh so fun mechanic of "guess when the off screen enemy is going to attack you from behind and stagger you". The lock on mechanic is incredibly short range and often lets enemies cheese some damage at the start of combat if you aren't properly ready and it is both sluggish and unresponsive when you want to switch between enemies to hopefully get a chance of predicting their charge.  Quite frankly I have never wanted to throttle the devs of a game before but here I am. 

Honestly it would be a simple fix. Either have a warning system to show when offscreen enemies are going to attack you, or have the AI work so only one or two enemies can attack at once, or at least make it so they attack more sparingly when they aren't the primary target. That first suggestion would make the game actually playable.

I also got bundled with this game the demo for Gothic, which has a very similar but also more complicated fight system which after a taste of what Elex offers I want no part in. 

Story and rpg elements 4/5, albeit this is based more on the potential I've seen and other reviews than anything else because I didn't get far enough into the game to appreciate the wider world (I did make ti half way across the map to the Cleric's base though, which was at least entertaining to attempt at level 3).

Gameplay? 1/5, hair pullingly unplayable. I almost want to give it a 0/5, but the potential is there.

Hire someone to do the gameplay design, keep your writing and design teams.

Checks most of the boxes for a stellar scifi-fantasy RPG. The combat is unforgiving and clunky specifically in the early game until you get the hang of it. Melee combat can be a bit daunting but using range weaponry works just as well if you don't like the stamina system. The world is massive, filled with unique landmarks and vistas. its beautifully done, and they give you a jetpack to explore it ALL with. Meaning you're not restricted by verticallity, if there's a mountain in your way climb it. They give you a good cast of companions to go adventuring with, all with they're own side quests and faction affiliations. Speaking of which, the factions are all tastefully done and interesting in their own rights with distinct ideologies that effect the dynamic of the story. The overarching story is nothing to write home about, but does leave you satisfied for the most part. All in all its a true rags to riches game that starts off brutally hard until you build your power up overtime.

Коротко и по делу про седьмую Готику (аддон к третьей и четвёртая Готиками не являются).
Как известно, за что Пираньи не берутся — Готика получается. И Элекс не исключение.

Так-с, что мы имеем?

Элекс переплюнул даже третьего ведьмака по качеству [b]анимации[/b] движений. Однако все анимации в диалогах остались на уровне первой Готики — разве что лица стали немного эмоциональнее. К сожалению, это особенность движка игры. Всё тот же "геном", но совершенно новая версия.

[b]Графика[/b] просто девять с чем-то без десяти. Точнее, десять без чего-то. Идеал без прозрачной воды в реках. Это немного странно, учитывая невероятную проработку течений во всех водоёмах. Но и ладно, обстановка пост-апокалипсиса позволяет содержать мутную воду.
Всё крутое снаряжение имеет святящиеся элементы, которые в темноте дают плюс сорок к крутости персонажа.

О, цифры. Вот за это разработчики получают по жопе: [b]цифр нет[/b]. Игра почти никаких точных характеристик персонажа не показывает. Наверное, только уровень. И количество предметов. Это совсем плохо. Даже прочность главного героя можно уточнить, только подставившись под удар! 

Насчёт подставления под удар. В мире игры есть много областей, [b]исследование[/b] которых усложнено разными негативными эффектами — холод, жара, яд и радиация. Это справедливо, ведь обычное такие области либо являются границами мира, либо скрывают в себе много сокровищ. Однако игра позволяет упороться зельями и получить временную неуязвимость ко всем эффектам и пройти куда угодно. Разумеется, если хватит этих самых зелий.

А что можно сказать о мире игры? Много интересного. Очень много. [b]Огромный открытый мир[/b], в каждом уголке которого можно найти что-то интересное, охраняемое кем-то страшным и сильным. 
И просто очаровательные пейзажи.

К слову о сокровищах. В мире можно найти [b]уникальное оружие[/b] — это типа крутые версии обычного оружия с заоблачными требованиями к характеристикам персонажа. Такое оружие обычно имеет какие-то уникальные эффекты. К сожалению, улучшить его нельзя; и поэтому зачастую оно получается слабее полностью улушенного самого мощного неуникального оружия. 

В том числе и поэтому напрочь [b]убитый баланс[/b]. Для уже ознакомившихся с игрой тут и без объяснений всё ясно. 
Слишком усложнился ближний бой и упростился дальний. Экономика тоже не в лучшем состоянии.

[strike]Самое важное[/strike] — [b]сюжет[/b]. Ну тут как обычно — брутальный [strike]безымянный[/strike] герой без снаряжения появляется в огромном открытом мире, где должен навести порядок и прекратить войну, поддержав одну из сторон. Любую из семи (уже скоро восьми) Готик можно описать этим предложением. 

Кстати, насчёт [strike]восьмой Готики[/strike] второго Элекса. В нём планируется официальная русская озвучка. Очень этому рад. Первому Элексу не повезло в этом плане — локализаторы даже в строчки не вчитывались, вышло сомнительно. Передайте им мои негодования.
Кажется, представитель команды Games Voice недавно рассказывал, что планирует изучить группу актёров озвучки нового Элекса, чтобы в будущем связаться с ними для организации озвучки первого Элекса. Это, скорее всего, будет совсем в будущем, но имейте в виду.

Lohnt sich Elex in 2021 ? Kurze Antwort: Ja, trotz allem steckt viel Liebe in dem Spiel drin.

In den letzten Jahren habe ich einige Spiele gespielt aber seit Gothic III und Morrowind vor mehr als 10 Jahren und seit dem kein Rollenspiel. Gothic III fand ich damals nicht so toll aber Gothic II war eines meiner Lieblingsspiele.

Ich fing das Spiel an und hatte gleich das legendäre Gothic-Gefühl. Ich habe es bis zur ersten Stadt geschafft und es hätte tatsächlich Gothic sein können, wenn ich nicht das Jet-Pack gehabt hätte. Allerdings ist mir auch gleich das veraltete Kampfsystem aufgefallen, welches sich seit Gothic auch nicht viel weiterentwickelt zu sein schien. Warum da die Entwickler sich von andereren Spielen wie "For Honor" nicht inspirieren lassen, ist mir ein Rätsel.
Allerdings haben mich die Dialoge, die Welt und die Story gleich gepackt und ich habe mehr als 300 Missionen abgeschlossen, die End-Sequenz gesehen und es nicht bereut. 
Ich will jedoch auf ein paar Sachen eingehen, mir gefallen und welche mir nicht gefallen haben.

Negativ: 
- Das Kampfsystem mit den Nahkampf-Waffen. Ich fand es ziemlich umständlich mit dem Blocken, der Rolle und dem speziellen Angriff, dass ich den Nahkampf gleich aufgegeben habe und nur noch mit dem Bogen und später mit der Schrotflinte unterwegs war. 
- Die KI von den Begleitern ist unter aller Sau. Nicht nur, dass sie einfach anfangen Mitten im Kampf herumzuspazieren als ob nichts wäre, sie machen auch kaum schaden  
- Die Hauptstory allgemein ist interessant aber hin und wieder gab es da Sprünge und es fühlte sich abgehackt an. Manchmal kriegen die Charaktere nicht mit, dass viele Missionen schon erledigt sind und das macht natürlich die Atmosphäre kaputt. 
- Der Jet-Pack ist praktisch für höhere Sprünge und dem Kampf aber nicht wirklich zum fliegen da. Über eine Schlucht damit zu kommen ist wirklich umständlich. Da wurde viel Potenzial verschenkt, wird aber wohl in Elex 2 besser.

Neutral:
- Ich fand es gut, dass die Marker für die Quests Optional sind. Man kann jedoch aus vielen Dialogen nicht darauf schließen, wo man sich hinbewegen muss und dann muss man die Marker doch einschalten. Ich hätte mir einen Mix gewünscht. Bei Hauptmissionen sollten die Dialoge so sein, dass man auch genug hinweise bekommt um ohne den optionalen Marker dahin zu kommen. Die Entwickler haben sich aber wohl auf die Funkion verlassen und die Dialoge gekürzt. 

Positiv: 
- Der Schwierigkeitsgrad ist alles in allem knackig
- Viele Nebenmissionen sind spannend 
- Viel Auswahl an Fernkampfwaffen, z.B. Raketenerfer, Granatenwerfer, usw. Die Waffen fühlen sich gut an und die Projektile fliegen tatsächlch die Strecke, so das man auch die Beweg-Richtung des Gegners mitbeachten muss.
- Die Freiheit in der Welt überall hin zu gehen
- Das man Elex-Getränke brauen kann um so an die Erfahrungspunkte, Attributpunkte oder Lernpunkte zu kommen

Alles in allem fand ich das Spiel ziemlich gut. Der MIttelteil des Spiels fand ich am spannendsten, die Geschichte wird gut aufgebaut und es gibt viele Geschichtsstränge die man zusammenbekommen muss. Manchmal wirds Tiefgründig und ab und zu witzig (vorallem bei den Outlaws). Die Auflösung der Geschichte fand ich etwas enttäuschend und den Endgegner auch. Man hat die Geschichte richtig gut aufgebaut und man erwartet was bombastisches aber dann ist weder der Endgegner beeindruckend noch seine Motivation.

Sure glad gameplay took a backseat in an Action RPG.
While the general world space and setting seems genuinely quite interesting and unique, considering the core aspect of the game barely even functions, I refuse to subject myself to the torment necessary to overpower the inherent jank of the game to find out when it gets good, if it ever does.
While it's not even worth it to go super in-depth, let me just describe my limited experience that forced me make up my mind.
During some of my first combat encounters, where dodging and parrying become relevant, the game would do that thing most games do while they tutorialize you. Which is to slow or stop time, tell you to do the thing they're trying to teach you (RMB to Block/Parry, Double tap a direction to dodge, etc). So I follow the tutorial, double tap to dodge or block/parry, aaaand I still get hit and lose 90% of my health or instantly die anyway.
So what the game is telling me is that even if I do everything right, even with the game quite literally freezing time to allow me to input at the right time, I still take damage and or die. So core combat mechanics straight up do not work, period.
On a related note of Jank ruining the gameplay experience, so by default, double tapping a direction forces you to dodge-roll. Fair enough, and to my surprise there's even an option to toggle that function in case you don't want that to happen. Awesome! Or so I thought. Because for some ungodly reason this option can not be disabled. Why even include it in the options menu at that point? It's basically just a "♥♥♥♥ You". And maybe you get some skill or ability or something stupid later, or maybe it's tied to difficulty for some reason, but again I ask, why?
So suffice to say, for any experienced action platformer, dodge-rolling every time you go to slightly adjust your position is insanely infuriating. Especially when the movement itself is already fairly janky so trying to perfectly position yourself is hard enough already.
If all this rambling is to say anything, that is that this might be one of those games where if you can put up with the horrible game design and jank long enough, you might be able to find an autisitcally pleasurable experience somewhere in this dumpster fire. But if you care even the slightest bit about having a game that's actually enjoyable to play, this ain't it chief.
