WAY better than Cyberpunk 2077.  Get this instead.

"Clunky combat"
Arkham style 360 parry fests arn't "Good combat".  You have to commit to your attacks...  There's nothing "clunky" about a game having mechanics of movement, and you having to work within them.  I find playing this like Ninja Gaiden easier than playing this like Zelda; locking on is only useful if you can actually win a head-to-head fight.  If you're outmatched, which you usually are, don't lock on, that way you can bob and weave around a group of enemies easier without having to waste stamina rolling.  

"Too hard"
This game has no level scaling.  Start off doing quests around town, and visit at least two faction camps and do the easier interpersonal intrigue type quests until you reach level 10-12, then you can start taking on harder quests.  It's so much fun getting new equipment when you know that it will allow you to go complete a quest you couldn't complete before.

Because there is no level scaling, and there are no achievements for playing on harder difficulty settings, the difficutly setting is more there for you to keep the game from becoming too easy, or too hard, if you make really smart, or dumb, decisions with your character.  Coming from a guy who plays most games on the hardest, or second hardest, setting on his first try...  Start off on normal, for God's sake...  Starting off a non-scaled game on hard is Halo 2 Legendy type stuff.

"Bad graphics"
This one I don't even understand.  This game has like a million different types of plants, more than I've ever seen in any video game before.  There is so much detail in every inch.  There are way less big empty open fields than Breath of the Wild or Skyrim, it's just FULL of little details and landmarks EVERYWHERE.  Texture resolutions are fine, models are high poly.  Has modern material based shading like most modern games.  View distance is SUPER far and the LOD system is WAY better than Fallout 4, in that you don't even notice pop-in on medium, and on ultra, it's impossible to notice any.  I would say the world looks better than The Witcher 3 in a lot of respects, as far as non-repeating assets goes, but the people don't.  Only complaint on graphics is that there arn't enough NPC clothing options, so some quest givers can look too much like some nameless NPC background characters, which is distracting.

For having a fraction of the budget of The Witcher 3, this game sure isn't THAT much worse than it.  This is way better than anything Bethesda has been putting out for the past decade, that's for sure.

This game feels like it was made by people who kept asking themselves "What type of game would I want to play", rather than "What type of game would appeal to the most amount of people".

I managed to pick this up on sale, and still remember Gothic 3 fondly, which is why I gave another Piranha Bytes game a shot even after the drivel of the few previous titles.


Short version:

I really don't think I could recommend this to anyone but a person familiar with Piranha Bytes games and is therefore someone who knows what they're getting themselves into. It's *FAR* better than the garbage fires that were Risen 2/3, but this game just isn't quite polished enough. To their credit, they know this, which is why it was released at 50 bucks instead of 60.

If you've played basically all the other open world RPGs from the last 12 years, why not, give this one a go--you will probably like it since you played all those other games and it has its definite strong points. Else, maybe spend your time elsewhere.


Long version:

Controls: -
The controls feel sloppy and loose. The reactions of the character on the different slopes of surfaces and the animations played when stumbling forward are clunky and hard to predict, while the ability to boost up into the air is, in contrast, instantaneous. You have a jetpack giving you some of the verticality like you would have in something like Breath of the Wild, but unlike BotW's comparatively masterfully tight controls, you find yourself frustrated as often as pleased. In a game like Witcher 3, where the animations and delays are part of the play, these things coalesce into a system that requires a bit of learning (I'd even call it fun) and eventually you can really get in there and feel like you're driving Geralt around murdering faces. In contrast, this game's often-sluggish and stubborn controls are inconsistent and never feel like you've gotten a firm grasp on them, but merely that you've learned how to tolerate or mitigate them.

Combat: --
Combat, as you might imagine after reading the above, is also quite clunky. This has been a Piranha Bytes thing since as far back as I remember (Gothic 2 onward). Against most level-appropriate enemies in the game, whoever can start stun locking the other party first is the winner. It's not as ridiculous as O.G. Gothic 3's boars, but it's not too much better, either. Fighting multiple enemies simultaneously in the open pretty much requires save-scumming, but then again, it would be a perfectly valid point to say fighting multiple enemies should be very difficult. Trying to fight in melee in groups along with non-enemy or even friendly NPCs is an exercise in consistent low-level frustration. Ranged combat is far more bearable, though still generally weak gameplay.

Enemy/Friendly AI: -
The AI is at times serviceable and at other times terri-bad. PB games have always had places where the enemy gets stuck on a ledge, walking into it for 90 seconds while you pelt it with projectiles, and it's been a sour point in every single one of them. Luckily most alien animals can hork up nasty goo balls and spit them at you or lob rocks/dirt at you or fling spikes at you or whatever else, so "cliffing" things isn't totally one-sided.

Story/Quests: +
Quests don't hold your hand. You make choices, and they matter. People die (all but an extreme few NPCs can die) and that might and probably will change a large part of how you interact with other NPCs, or what quests do what. There's some replayability here for sure; by a few hours in I was already wondering how things would have gone differently if I had made other choices and was considering what I'd do on a second playthrough.

Story/Worldbuilding: +
To avoid spoilers, I'll just say that the game's general story line is pretty good. Let's talk about the factions instead. It might be because the last big open-world game I played was Fallout 4 where the factions had no semblance of what could be called coherent writing, but I actually liked how the factions in this game are handled. Again, avoiding specifics to avoid spoilers, each faction you encounter seems like it has a place in the world. The different factions' interpretations of one another is a coherent, driving force behind the plot of the game, and the whole thing really comes together better than most any other open world title I've played in the previous 15 years that relied on faction-based storylines or mechanics.

Voice Acting: ++/-
Some of the NPCs are voiced very well (the potty-mouthed outlaw hiding outside the berserker city being my favorite so far) and some others sound like they came straight out of a middling-to-high quality fan-made Skyrim mod. Some people may remark on the main character being the most dully-voiced character they've ever heard, especially compared to something like female Shep in Mass Effect, and while there is an ingame reason for some of this, even then, yeah, he's bland. Still, for every stinker, there're two gems, and the rest are totally passable.

Map/Worldbuilding: +
The map is good. The cities are large and full of people to talk to and things to learn about and get mixed up with. The explorable map might be more compact than in some other open world games (though still substantial), but there's also a distinct lack of filler and padding in the world that you'd see in some other games.

Character Progression: +
Progression feels meaningful. I adored how starved you are for skill points in the early game, and how each few you gain open up what seems like a large expansion on your capabilities. That being said, despite a general positive feeling, there is a clear down side: the whole system feels woefully underpolished.

UI: -
The UI is for consoles, plain and simple. It's serviceable, but far, far, far from ideal for a PC experience. Yeah, most other games like this in the previous decade have had the same issues, basically all of them that I can think of actually, but that doesn't mean we have to accept it without bitching about it. Furthermore, some of the descriptions of what you can invest in are just meaningless. What the hell is the difference between "attack strength" and "melee damage", you might ask? Well ♥♥♥♥ you, the game doesn't tell you, anywhere. There are several more examples. The internet is your friend here, but it shouldn't have to be. (Answer: the first is how much your melee attacks might stagger an enemy, and the second is just what you'd think it is.)

Graphics: +/-
I am running it on High everything. For a game released in 2017... meh? I can't complain too much. Textures are fine, faces are fine. There are the odd few trees I've noticed floating in the air and shit like that, the strange draw distance quirks, the torrential rain all around you as far as the eye can see that immediately starts/stops if you walk forward or backward a single millimeter, and so on, but it's totally playable and immersive enough, even if it's definitely not going to win any awards.

No ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Micro-transactions/Content Packs: +
I hate that this is a positive point for a game these days, but that's the world we live in.

Stability/Performance: +/-
Somewhat unexpectedly for me at least, this game ran rock-solid on my machine. I left it running for days between suspending my computer or just leaving it minimized for an hours+ several times while doing other stuff or sleeping the whole damn night. Not one crash, and hardly ever a hiccup. I've had two instances in my time so far of having a weird delay of ~10 seconds when opening a workbench, but it eventually passed. On the flip side, loading times seem to extend themselves substantially the longer you keep the game running, and go back to nearly-instant if you close and restart the game. It might not be so bad if dying wasn't such a regular occurrence due to the combat system...


Update after game completion:
Everything above held true through the end, with the note that your character's strength continues to satisfyingly increase as you level up. I finished the game at level 42, chugging that sweet, sweet soul-killing elex every chance I got. Total actual playtime of ~70 hours.

My unbiased opinions of the game, despite liking it, it has its faults. So if you're fine with what's written below you'll enjoy the game. 

The pros

-Lots of things to do
-Lots of choices
-Quests are interesting
-Good amount of combat variety
-Tons of dialog and information about the world as well as written information
-Lot of custom options and you can modify your weapons and character to your liking. Though this may be more limited than I would have liked. You have Gem slots, upgrades, and you can change the damage type of your weapon
-A few easter eggs
-Large variety of weapons
-You have a jet pack
-You can have a companion
-Hours of content, and I mean hours of it. especially if you do all of the side quests
-Romance options
-Decent replayability 
-Interesting story and concept. Story brought together in an interesting way. 



The Cons

-Too many bugs, thankfully not game breaking
-Game will crash but not often
-Badly done story clips, almost lazy if you ask me. They must have run out of funding and had to rush the game and make due.
-No sense of where my decisions lead me after the end of the story, other than certain factions and people not liking me. An attempt at closure was done through text after the last quest but that didn't cover everyone for some reason.
-Some of the dialog doesn't make sense because it was intended for the other character talking. 
-Combat is not ideal. Can be challenging at the start but there are several ways to cheat the system and it becomes more of a quest to grab all the money you can, then boost yourself until you become overpowered
-Weapon stat system is crap and it'll take you hours to get enough stats for a good weapon
-Ai is dumb and easily fooled, even companions are retarded sometimes and wont attack in certain situations. Companions are the worst AI in game. If you attack with range, your companion will too. This causes problems because the enemy AI will refuse to target your companions unless your companion is in their face, and they wont get in their face because all they do is mimic you until an enemy gets closer. Could have had options to edit battle preferences or something. 
-The companion affection system as well as the cold system are badly implemented and often don't make sense. They also aren't clearly explained. Took me a while to realize like was above respect.

Let me preface this by saying:  This game is like an addictive drug.

It's hard to believe it's been like 20 years since Gothic.   The word was that "Gothic" was the game Ultima IX should have been...and I agree.  I was blown away by the big open world and the seemingly endless exploration.  Gothic II continued this tradition by an order of magnitude.

I've had Elex on my wishlist for a while but only picked it up now, on the Xmas sale.  What on earth was I waiting for?  This game is like Gothic on...well, Elex.   The world is HUUUUGE.   You can spend hours just wandering around and exploring...and trying to not get killed.  This is not an easy game to play at all, death comes quickly..just like Gothic.  You have to earn your way to power.

The story is quite engaging.   I like the Almost-like-Earth feel to the world...kind of like Fallout in that sense.

Flaws?  Well I don't know I would call it a flaw per se...the combat takes some getting used to.  But then again the combat was quite complex in Gothic as well...but it grows on you, fast.   Becomes natural quite quickly.  It's almost like a Pirhana Bytes signature.   I'm sure it will turn people away at first but do stick with it.

And the jet pack!  If you've ever wanted to be Boba Fett here is your chance.  The jet pack just adds so much to this game in terms of exploration...AND combat.

One other detail:  This is a Windows game but I am playing it just fine on Ubuntu Linux 18.04, using Proton 4.11, NVidia 1060.  It works GREAT.    Do I recommend this game?  HELL YES.

If you liked the Gothic series, you will enjoy this one. It has an interesting mood to it, the world is pretty and fun to explore, and there's some curious history for you to discover. 

I have to warn you though - there are some aspects that are super clunky. I didn't mind overall, as this game is different enough from the others and so it was refreshing, but it's fair to point these flaws out:

[list]
    [*]Main character is clearly made by dudes for dudes. Not only is he one dimensional, he's also an archetypical dense walking pile of muscle. I found it hard to relate to him.
    [*]Some quests are buggy, although none of them game breaking (at least I didn't encounter those).
    [*]Storyline feels a bit rushed towards the end, that was a bit of a downer.
    [*]This game really wants you to play melee. I'm stubborn and tried to make psi + ranged work, and looking back, I just made things unnecessarily difficult for myself.
    [*]Character progression is a little weird. There's some sort of cliff function that means once you reach a specific threshold, all fights suddenly become very easy. I didn't mind this, it actually gave me a real sense that my character got stronger. Probably because I didn't go melee, it took most of the game to get to that point, and that may be the reason I didn't mind (most of my game was pretty difficult).
[/list]

Un peu hésitante au début , je décide de cliquer fébrilement sur le bouton " jouer " . J'ai vite compris sur quoi je venais de tomber : un petit bijoux ! Quelle belle surprise ! 

*Une belle histoire avec des personnages aussi différents qu'attachants . ( De plus , il s'agit d'une histoire qui n'est en rien tracée puisqu'en fonction de vos choix , celle-ci change . )
*Une évolution du personnage logique autant physiquement que psychologiquement ( A vous de décider qui vous voulez être ,  avec qui vous voulez continuer votre chemin ou à qui arracher la tête ! ) 
* Des quêtes variées et assez longues pour vous permettre de jouer pendant des heures . ( Les quêtes seront parfois touchantes et d'autres fois elles seront simplement de bons défouloirs ...   ces quêtes ne feront peut-être de vous qu'un esclave ou un barbare ou même qui sait , peut-être un bon amant ou un bon citoyen de Magalan ! )

En petit plus , je dirais :
* que le graphisme est plaisant 
* que les interactions sont vraiment idéales , surtout lorsqu'on est vraiment plongé dans l'histoire . 
* les combats sont interessants ( N'oubliez pas d'utiliser votre tête et beaucoup , beaucoup d'Elex : les grenades sont mes amis ;) 
* Une totale liberté ( baladez vous : sans vous faire tuer hein ! Allez commettre des délits ! Sauvez la veuve et l'orphelin ! Allez vous battre dans une arène ! Chassez du monstre ! Detendez vous au bord d'une falaise ! bref , lachez-vous ! ) 

et surtout que j'aimerais ENORMEMENT avoir la suite des aventures de Jax !

 L'immersion a été totale pour ma part et il fait parti de ces petites perles qui se font rares : avec un réèl contenu , une véritable personnalité , assumée du début à la fin . Il y a beaucoup de travail et d'imagination ... et ça fonctionne ! Il réuni tout ce que l'on peut désirer dans un jeu .

Dieses Spiel
Nun es ist ein Spiel welches von Piranha Bytes ist, was es schon mal von Anfang an besser macht.
Das Spiel spielt sich wirklich extrem flüssig und angenehm weshalb man über die paar Hindernisse mit komischer hitbox im Spiel hinweg sehen kann. Die Athmosphäre im Spiel ist einfach nur genial, es ist ja auch von Piranha Bytes und sie haben an der unfassbar gut Athmosphäre ihrer vorherigen Spiele wie Gothic 1, 2 und 3 gut anknüpfen können. Es ist eine ganz andere Handlung als in Gothic doch man merkt schnell, dass auch Elex von Piranha Bytes kommt, denn man wird einfach rein geworfen und muss schauen wie man zurecht kommt. Abschließend ich nur noch sagen, dass das Spiel wirklich extrem schwer anfängt und man einen Großteil der Missionen am Anfang nur durch kiten und wegrennen schafft. An alle die es spielen wollen: wählt eure Fraktion gut aus denn ihr könnt sie nie wieder verlassen es sei denn, ihr startet ein neues Spiel. 
Als alles in allem ein wirklich sehr gut gelungenes Spiel das keine Buggs hat und es wert ist, viele Stunden zu investieren.

А тут у нас, значит, RPG нового поколения от легендарных создателей серий Готики и Risen с открытым миром и возможностями перемещения по этому открытому миру как по горизонтальной плоскости, так и по вертикальной (за спиной всегда джет-пак!), хардкорными, как всегда у Пираний, локациями, в которых никогда не знаешь наверняка, что тебя ждёт (чаще всего ничего хорошего, уверяю; но ведь в трудностях и весь интерес, не так ли?) и увлекательным сюжетом про безэмоционального солдата, подсевшего некогда в своём легионе на инопланетную наркоту, у которого есть ВЫБОР, быть ли таким безэмоциональным и дальше, руководствуясь только логикой и собственными целями, или научиться понимать странных глупых живых существ с эмоциональными привязками к любым событиям. Люблю этого издателя за постоянное качество и внимание к мельчайшим деталям мира. Графон кстати тоже ничего такой, на пейзажи полюбоваться можно достаточно, звуковое сопровождение тоже задаёт атмосферу. В общем 13 из 10.

ELEX jsem jiz dohral pri jejim uvedeni. Po dvou letech jsem se k ni konecne vratil a musim rict, ze neztratila nic ze sveho puvodniho kouzla. Duch piranha bytes je ze hry citit a doslova jsem byl uneseny. To vsak rikam jako velky fanda Pirani. Gothic 3, vsechny 3 dily Risen, me neskutecne bavily a osobne mi cela jejich tvorba prijde z pohledu mainstreamu dost nedocennena. Na druhou stranu je pravda, ze se vzdy radila spise k narocnejsim RPG hram danneho zanru.

K samotne hre:
Pekny svet. Spojeni Sci-fi, Fantasy a Post-apo zde prekvapive dobre funguje, obcas jsou sice prechody mezi lokacemi prilis bijici do oci, ale jinak je svet zivy, uveritelny, graficky i hudebne velmi dobre zpracovany. Zde az na vyjimky - napr. lod a jeji animace hned na zacatku hry, dale pak Hort - zde se zub casu na graficke strance podepsal asi nejvice.
Hlavni pribehova linka je fajn, ale vetsi sila je dle meho nazoru ve vedlejsich ukolech. Ukoly lze zpravidla plnit nekolika zpusoby a dilci rozhodnuti ma vliv na dalsi postup. Toto plati zejmena v interakci s postavami. Dialogy jsou vtipne, maji hlavu a patu a nestava se, ze by cloveka zacaly nudit a chtel je klikanim preskocit. Hra je vyvedena kompletne v cestine a az na nekolik vyjimek je preklad zdarily.
Je treba podotknout, ze hra je ze zacatku mozna az prilis tezka a prvnich 10 hodin vas zabije temer kazda vetsi potvora. Nicmene zde je k pomoci JetPack, ktery lze efektivne pouzit k uteku prip. vyhnuti se nepriteli. Pomoci ke zkusenostem a vyssimu levelu lze pomoci "behacich" ukolu prip. "sebrat a utect". Soubojovy system je podareny, zadna akce typu For Honor (zde narazim na uvolneny Gothic Teaser), plne v duchu soubojoveho systemu prvniho Risen. V pripade, ze mate v nastaveni zapnutou asistenci zamereni nepratel, je souboj misty dost krkolomny.
Umela inteligence vasich spolecniku obcas pokulhava, ale i presto prijdou v soubojich vhod, hlavne ze zacatku jako tank.
Crafting je take na slusne urovni, ale bodu dovednosti neni moc a je potreba si dopredu velmi rozmyslet, jakym smerem se chce clovek dale ubirat.

Zaverem: Je to RPG ze stare skoly, ktere cili hlavne na fanousky zanru a tvorbu Piranha Bytes. Koho bavila serie Gothic a Risen, bude zde jako doma.

I've played pretty much every game that Piranha Bytes has produced and enjoyed them all. This one is an exception.
The normal difficulty setting on this game is equivalent to hardcore on anything other game from this studio.
I'm almost 28 hours into the game and have spent more time reloading than playing.
Everything in the game kills you. Even the ground you walk on and your own companions.
The combat system is very clunky. Target lock was a good idea but doesn't come off very well. It tends to lock onto whatever is closest to you, even allies and companions, and is difficult to break lock without putting away your weapon and then  trying again. Not good when you've got a monster trying to tear you apart. Once target lock is engaged, you can't even run away without disarming and hoping that you live long enough to even turn around to to flee.
The stamina bar depletes quickly (meaning you can't do anything until it reloads) even when you're in defensive mode since hits from a creature also drain stamina. I found myself stuck numerous times with an enemy beating me to death, unable to dodge, defend, run away or fight back because the stamina level was at zero and couldn't fill while I was getting hammered.
Many of the scripted dialogues are much too long. Once an NPC starts talking you'd just as well go get a cup of coffee . . . they'll still be talking when you get back and you won't have missed anything important.
I've never written a bad review on a game, even ones that I didn't think were worth the money; but, this one is a real stinker.

Elex ist ein absolutes Muss für alle Fans der Gothic- und Risen-Reihe.
Aber auch sonst ist es ein wirklich gelungenes Rollenspiel.

Positives:
Vor allem überzeugt Elex durch seine recht tiefgründigen Entscheidungsmöglichkeiten.
Ob ich nun den Dieb töte, ihm vorspiele, ihn nicht zu verraten, dies dann aber doch tue oder mir die Beute mit ihm teile, bei nahezu allen Quests hat man die Qual der Wahl. Das fühl sich zunächst sehr angenehm an, kann aber auf Dauer zu Problemen führen, worauf ich später noch eingehen werde.
Dieses System führt vor allem dazu, dass man in der Welt merklich etwas verändert. Von dem einen wird man plötzlich geschätzt, von dem anderen angegriffen. Seine Entscheidungen beeinflussen also aktiv das Spielgeschehen.
Auch die Charakterentwicklung überzeugt. Wenn man am Anfang noch von jedem noch so kleinen Monster ordentlich aufgerieben wurde, so kann man nach und nach stärkere Gegner bezwingen. Das ganze liegt nicht nur an den Punkten, die man auf die einzelnen Werte verteilen kann, sondern auch an dem Kampfsystem, welches man tatsächlich üben muss, um wirklich besser zu werden.
Es gibt auch sonst noch viele positive Aspekte, die ich nur kurz nennen möchte:
- eine Vielzahl unterschiedlicher Waffen und Waffentypen
- interessantes Verbesserungssystem von Waffen
- schöne, offene Spielwelt, die zum Erkunden einlädt

Negatives:
Wie in jedem anderen Spiel auch, gibt es auch bei Elex einiges auszusetzen. Wie sehr das für den einzelnen ins Gewicht fällt, muss jeder für sich selbst entscheiden.
Als aller erstes wäre zu sagen, dass Elex grade am Anfang recht schwer ausfällt, selbst für geübte Gothic-Spieler.
Das liegt nicht zuletzt an dem recht steifen Kampfsystem, das im Grunde recht simpel ist, aber deutliche Schwächen hat. So kann man Kombos nicht abbrechen, die Ausdauerleiste ist ständig leer und alles in allem wirkt es alles andere als rund. Das verbessert sich im Laufe des Spiels zwar deutlich, aber frustriert zu Beginn sehr. Dazu kommt noch, dass wenn man versucht, die Fraktionsquests zu machen, man sehr schnell auf unmachbare Aufgaben stößt, wie auf Level 5 einen übermenschlich starken Gegner zu töten. Das gibt einem das Gefühl, viel zu schwach oder zu doof zu sein.
Weitere Schwachpunkte des Spieles wären:
- Begleiter-KI ist wirklich unterirdisch (Gegner attackieren mich, während mein Begleiter nichts tut)
- Ob das Lösen einer Quest der jeweiligen Fraktion gefällt oder nicht, ist oft schwer einzuschätzen
- da die Teleporter im Spiel oft in der Botanik versteckt liegen, arten viele Quests in Lauferei aus

Fazit.
Auch wenn Elex so seine Schwächen hat, ist es doch ein wirklich fesselndes Spiel mit hohem Wiederspielwert. Die große Welt lädt zum erkunden ein und die Questreihen haben ihren ganz eigenen Stil, den ansonsten kaum ein RPG vorweisen kann.
Ich kann Elex jedem, der Lust auf ein anspruchsvolles und gleichzeitig entschleunigendes Rollenspiel Lust hat, nur empfehlen.

Meine Beziehung mit Elex ist etwas speziell. Ich habe mich damals beim Release sehr auf das Spiel gefreut und habe es sofort gekauft. Nach kurzem Anspielen, fiel mir jedoch auf, was vielen, vor allem in Negativen Rezensionen, aufgefallen ist. Die Grafik war für seine Zeit nicht wirklich überragend, fast enttäuschend, und die Steuerung, geschweige denn das Kämpfen waren eine Qual. Inputs werden erst super spät ausgeführt, Hitboxen sind phänomenal groß und den Gegnern werden meiner Sicht nach unfaire Vorteile im Kampf geschaffen, aber dazu später mehr.  

Ich habe das Spiel also erstmal Ruhen lassen und bin erst neulich aus purer Langeweile wieder nach Magalan zurückgekehrt. Diesmal wollte Ich mich intensiver mit dem Spiel auseinandersetzen (und statt mir "Ultra" anzutun habe Ich auf "Schwer" gespielt).

Bei diesem Durchlauf ist mir klar geworden, dass das Spiel vom Spieler eine gewisse Anpassung verlangt. 

Viele Negative Rezensionen sagen: 

1.  "unbalanced weil überall mal super starke und mal super schwache Gegner rumlaufen".

2.  "Leveling ist nicht ""Rewarding genug und zu langsam""".

3.  Combat System ist eine Qual.

4.  Generell nicht mein Fall.

Zu Fall 4 kann Ich nur sagen, "Ja das ist persönliches Empfinden", Zu 3 komme Ich gleich noch, bei 1 und 2 muss Ich aber hier ganz deutlich mal sagen, Ihr habt nicht ganz verstanden, wie das Spiel gespielt werden "möchte".

Elex ist nicht wie unsere Standard-RPG's, wo man beispielsweise klare Map-technische abgegrenzte Gebiete hat, wo man sagt: "Vom Anfangsgebiet 5Km auswärts sind schwache Monster, 5Km weiter sind dann die etwas stärkeren etc. Elex will eine etwas realistische Spielewelt kreieren. Elex möchte, dass sich der Spieler zu beginn denkt: "Hm da ist ein starker Gegner, Ich weiche dem besser aus und nehme einen Pfad durch die Wildnis, weil dort ein etwas schwächerer Gegner ist. Es möchte das sich der Spieler durch seine Spielwelt "schlängelt" und seinen eigenen, seiner Stärker entsprechenden, Weg findet. Es soll kein stures Geradeauslaufen von Golieth nach Albessa sein, der Spieler soll sich bewusst sein, dass er schwach ist und die Bestien, die Magalan bewohnen eine ernstzunehmende Bedrohung sind, die man nicht ,wie in vielen anderen Spielen, gleich nach einer Stunde Gameplay alle besiegen kann. 

Das selbe sei zum Progression-System (2) gesagt. An alle die sagen: "Ich hab das Spiel jetzt 3 Stunden gespielt und kann immernoch kaum stärkere Monster bezwingen als Junge Hornwölfe", oder "Man braucht 3 Level bis man eine bessere Axt benutzen kann, die kaum mehr schaden bringt" -> Ja, genau so will es das Spiel. Das Spiel baut (Gott sei Dank) nicht auf Combat auf (jedenfalls nicht zu Anfang). Seht es doch mal so, Ihr seit ehemaliger Commander der Albs, jemand der aber durch seinen Elexentzug alle Kräfte des Elex einbüßen musste, zudem wird eure komplette Ausrüstung gestohlen. Jetzt steht dort ein Mann, welcher überhaupt keine Kräfte und keinerlei Erfahrung mit seiner derzeitigen Situation hat. Jemand der nicht stärker, wenn nicht schwächer , als ein ganz normaler Durchschnitts-Mensch ist. Die Welt soll gefährlich sein, Ihr sollt lange dafür arbeiten müssen um euch in der Wildnis behaupten zu können. Man kann ohne Probleme locker bis Level 12 ohne jeglichen Kampf auskommen. Das Spiel bietet einen Startquestst in Hülle und Fülle, sodass ihr alles andere als gezwungen seid Mobs zu verkloppen (was ohnehin nicht viel Erfahrung bringt).

Was Ich damit sagen will ist, dass, wenn ihr an den Punkt gelangt,  wo ihr eine gewisse Stärke erreicht habt, auf jeden Fall sagen könnt: "Wow, Ich hab einiges erreicht um das jetzt machen zu können" und nicht: "Ja super, Starterrüstung sofort wenn man durchs Stadttor kommt, los geht's Monster kloppen!".

Das Spiel legt den Fokus ganz klar darauf, dass der Spieler die Spielewelt kennenlernt, mit den Mechaniken des Spiels vertraut wird, und es sich vor allem 2 mal überlegt anfangs einen Kampf einzugehen. Somit ist man gezwungen friedliche Lösungen zu finden und kann nicht bei jeder Quest die einfache "Ich hau dir aufs Maul, dann krieg Ich was Ich will" Methode wählen.

Ich habe es so gemacht:
Anfang: Alle Monster meiden, nur Questen, Jägerrüstung und Hose besorgt und weiter mit Rostiger Axt gespielt, bis Ich das "Hornschwert" ausrüsten konnte. Ab da sind kleiner Mobs kein Problem mehr und man kann sich etwas "freier" in der Welt Bewegen. Ab da mit Begleiter die anderen Fraktionen aufgesucht und weiter gelevelt, bis Ich "Schlangenbiss" ausrüsten konnte. Ab hier sollte es um einiges einfacher werden, da die Waffe sehr stark war (verhältnismäßig). Dann noch ein paar Level für den Kriegerbogen und alles war erstmal gut. 

Alles in Allem will Ich nur sagen, dass das zähe Levelsystem und die willkürliche Verteilung der Gegner dir einen gewissen Respekt einflößen soll und es ein riesen Erfolgserlebnis für dich sein soll, wenn du es endlich schaffst, dir eine gewisse Stärke anzueignen. Wem das aber nicht gefällt mache Ich trotzdem keinen Vorwurf, aber man möge bitte nicht behaupten es wäre "unspielbar".

Zu Punkt (3):
Das Combat-System ist der größte Müll, mit dem Ich seit langem fertig werden musste. Das soll nicht heißen, dass das Spiel unspielbar wäre, es wurde einfach nur sehr, sehr schlecht umgesetzt. Inputs hängen meistens 1-1,5 Sekunden hinterher, Hitboxen der Gegner sind gigantisch und dazu kommen noch allerlei Bugs und Unreinheiten wie: 

1. Bogen müssen manchmal manuell "nachgeladen werden", wenn man in der halben Sekunde in der der Spieler automatisch "nachläd" rollt oder unterbrochen wird.

2. Gegner straucheln bei Kettenangriffen des Spieler, können jedoch mitten in dessen Angriff selbst eine Angriffsanimation starten, die daraufhin einfach durchgeht, da man diese nicht unterbrechen kann, der GEGNER aber, kann das immer bei dir und dich so "Tot-spammen". Dies dient nur dem Zweck Kämpfe künstlich zu erschweren.

3. Der Bogen schießt manchmal über den Gegner hinweg, da das Zielsystem absoluter Müll ist. Die Entwickler entschieden sich für: "Das Zielkreuz ist absolut". Aber wenn ein Gegner sich bewegt und man aus Versehen mal in die Lücke zwischen z.B Arm und Körper kommt, denkt das Spiel statt "Pfeil geradeaus" -> "Pfeil in den Hintergrund auf den Stein da!". In jedem anderen Spiel hätte der Pfeil trotzdem getroffen. Frustrierend!

4.Hitboxen sind riesig. Beispiel: Ein Alb Commander mit Hammer trifft euch auch dann noch, wenn ihr schon weggerollt seid und zwischen dem ausgestreckten Hammer und euch 2m Platz sind. Es gibt viele andere Möglichkeiten Spiele schwerer zu machen.

Mir würde locker noch mehr einfallen, aber belassen wir es dabei. Ich kann nicht verstehen, wie man sowas testet und sagt: "Das ist gut so, lassen wir durchgehen". Und andere die das Combat-System verteidigen und meinen: "Ja das soll so sein wegen Gothic oder Whatever", schön und gut, aber absichtlich produzierter Müll ist immer noch Müll. Ich kann das zwar nachvollziehen, aber letzten Endes ist das auch nur eine Ausrede und macht das Endprodukt keinen deut besser.

Und was soll diese furchtbare Interaktion von Ausrüstung und Rüstungen. Das fiel mir damals schon auf, aber beim Spieler und bei vielen NPC's Glitcht die Waffe, oder das Schild, oder irgendwas, durch die "wehende" (oder auch nicht) Rüstung. Super unprofessionell und ruiniert das eintauchen ins Spiel. Niemand will ein Kriegerschild ausrüsten, was zwar gut aussieht, aber den Nachteil hat, das die Ellenbogen beim sprinten hinten "durchgehen".

Kann man über das mal hinwegsehen, ist es immer noch ein klasse Spiel, das mit abwechslungsreichen Dialogen erfrischt und mit seiner Entscheidungsvielfalt begeistert.
Gewöhnt man sich an die Grafik und das Kampfsystem, ist es ein schönes RPG mit einer wunderschönen Geschichte und vielen Charackteren die man liebgewinnen kann. 
Dem Spieler wird nichts auf dem Silbertablett serviert, er muss selber viel Zeit und Mühe aufbringen um das Spiel zu beherrschen, aber am Ende lohnt es sich allemal.
Für Gothic Liebhaber wird dieses Spiel viele Erinnerungen erwecken vor allem die Steuerung. Die fesselnde Storyline sorgt für viel Spielspaß.

I played only 1 playthrough in ultra difficulty that took me 72 hours to beat the game with every possible side quest and this is my opinion:

The lore is fantastic and the dialog choices matter a lot (it would be far more interesting if the player couldnt control when to save). The world and set up is amazing, the mix up of scify and fantasy is done beautifully and completely credible (you will realize why at the intro cutscene). The soundtracks didnt feel epic or immersing, but they arent bad. The physics of the game are kinda bad, and it takes a few hours of getting use to the way the character moves and does stuff. Combat didnt feel fun, it was repetitive and not very rewarding (specially since playing in ultra because its very tedious to kill anything during the first 10-20 hours). The character progression is pretty much gear based, once you start gearing up everything becomes easy, specially towards the end. The world is beautiful and full of places to visit, but exploration didnt feel rewarding, the weapons/armor were extremely limted and the city vendor always sold the best in slot gear. The plot was fun and interesting, i would totally love to play the sequel.. The skills were unimpressive, as well as ranged combat. The personality of every faction is very unique, but the game is not flexible enough to allow a second playthrough in my opinion. The music was too loud and didnt change during dialogs, so it was annoying in some way.

Overall is a good 70+ hour snack for RPG lovers but it feels 10 years all. As of 2019 i didnt enounter any kind of bugs or technicall issues. 

I strongly recommend to get during sales, not worth the full price.

"Elex" is an open-world action role-playing game developed by Piranha Bytes and published by THQ Nordic, released in 2017. The game is set in a post-apocalyptic world where players take on the role of Jax, a former member of the Albs, a faction of technologically advanced humans who use a powerful substance called Elex to enhance their abilities.

Gameplay:
The gameplay in "Elex" is a mix of melee combat, ranged combat, and role-playing elements. Players can choose from a range of character classes, each with their own set of skills and abilities, and can customize their character's appearance and equipment. The game's open-world design allows players to explore the game's world at their leisure, with plenty of side quests and activities to discover. The game's combat can be challenging, with enemies that are quick to react and can quickly overpower players who are not careful.

Graphics and Sound:
The game's graphics are impressive, with detailed environments and character models that showcase the game's post-apocalyptic setting. The game's use of lighting and visual effects also adds to the overall atmosphere of the game. The sound design is also well-done, with great voice acting and a soundtrack that captures the game's tone.

Storyline:
The game's storyline is intriguing, with a complex narrative that explores themes such as the ethics of technology, the nature of humanity, and the consequences of greed. The game's writing is generally strong, with interesting characters and dialogue that help to bring the game's world to life. However, some players have criticized the game's pacing and execution, with certain story beats feeling rushed or underdeveloped.

Technical Issues:
One of the most notable aspects of "Elex" is the technical issues that can impact the game's performance. Players have reported bugs, glitches, and other issues that can impact the game's stability and playability. These issues can be frustrating for players and may detract from the overall experience.

Overall:
"Elex" is a game with a lot of potential, but its technical issues and uneven execution have led to a mixed reception. The game's open-world design, combat, and customization options are all impressive, but the game's narrative can feel rushed at times, and the technical issues may detract from the overall experience. Despite its flaws, "Elex" is still worth playing for fans of the action role-playing genre and those interested in exploring its post-apocalyptic world.

1) В игре все завязано не на чистом уроне, а на чем-то вроде брони. Поэтому разница в реальном уроне между оружием в 70 единиц и в 90 может легко отличаться вдвое, а то и втрое. After two mediocre letdowns - Risen 2 and Risen 3 - Piranha Bytes finally prove that they still have it in them: ELEX is a great game in the style of the classic Gothics, with a huge world to explore, player choices within questlines, and a cool scifi-fantasy-mashup setting that I haven't seen done this way in a computer game before.

The game's greatest strength is its exploration. The world is completely open to you as soon as you exit the tutorial area (which is just one small dungeon), after which you get a jetpack that lets you ascend to roofs of buildings and steep cliffs. The jetpack is one of the best additions to the classic Piranha Bytes exploration formula that ELEX introduces. It allows you to go up almost any place, be it a tall building or a mountain. And for some places, using it is pretty much required: a lot of the game's landscapes and structures are vertical as heck. There are plenty of structures with multiple levels, where you ascend ladders and stairs (and then jump back down from the top to land safely at the bottom thanks to your jetpack slowing down the fall).

But don't expect the game to be easy: the world is completely open from the start, but most creatures will be tough to deal with at first. Even low level enemies offer a challenge to your character when you start the game, but with time you will grow stronger and become able to deal with them more easily. The power curve of ELEX is great. You start out as a weakling but feel like a demigod at the end, when you're all leveled up and equipped with devastating weapons. The placement of enemies is great, too: rather than every region being within a narrow level range, there are some creatures in the first region of the game that will still be difficult to defeat even when you're level 10 to 15. There's always a reason to return to a place, so progression from region to region is not linear. Later regions also contain some weaker creatures that will be a pushover once you make it to that region, but that just contributes to the feeling of a coherent world. Rather than arbitrarily being divided into level zones, creatures appear where it makes sense for them to appear from an ecological perspective.

The sheer variety of creatures, landscapes and structures is also worth mentioning. There are dozens of different monsters (although most have similar attack patterns and behaviors: rottmolch, rottboar, jackal, spine hound, ice beast for example all share the same attack behavior; there are maybe about half a dozen different enemy types, but for each of these types there are at least 3 to 5 subtypes), and on your journey through the world of ELEX you will wander through fertile river valleys, lush mountainsides, an arid desert, a volcanic wasteland, and a snowy region where rivers turned to ice. You will explore dilapidated industrial ruins, high tech bases, and even one or two medieval castles and towers. Wherever you go, there's always something new to discover.

Combat is not great, but decent. Melee combat has combos and forces you to manage your stamina. I found melee to be enjoyable and primarily played a melee character throughout the game. Towards the end, I switched to mainly using an overpowered unique plasma rifle that downed even the strongest enemies in three shots. Shooting is kinda wonky, especially when it comes to hit detection, but it's alright, too. Overall the combat is decent enough to be enjoyable, but this is no Dark Souls.

Quest design ranges from meh (simple fetch quests we've seen a hundred times before) to great. The best quests allow you to make various different choices, and during the course of the main quest you have to join one of three factions, all of which have good sides and bad sides to them. None of them are perfect, so there's no obvious "good guys" choice, but they all have advantages and disadvantages, both gameplay-wise (different factions allow access to different armors and different special skills) and story-wise. If I were to describe the three factions by their ideologies, I would (humorously) say: the berserkers are essentially nature-worshipping ecofascists, the outlaws are lawless anarcho-capitalists, and the clerics are techno-catholics.

Overall, ELEX is a great game that scratches the Gothic itch, and a huge improvement upon Piranha Bytes latest games (Risen 2 and Risen 3). A definite return to old form for the developer, and I'm looking forward to what they'll do with ELEX 2.

Having spent more than 50 hours playing this game, I decided to write a review in which I definitely recommend the game. In this review, I will attempt to give the overview of the game by trying to refrain from all the more common advantages/disadvantages and simply describing different aspects of the game as objectively as I can. So, let's go.

Quests
The system of quests in this game has been appraised not for the sake of it - the game boasts an intricate network of nonlinear quests (most of which can be completed in AT LEAST two different ways). To be clear here, I'm not talking about the main quests now, but about all of them! Yes, you read that right - the system of quests is superior to that in almost any other game (and I've played hundreds).

Story
I am yet to complete the game, but from what I have seen thus far, the game has an interesting plot that involves rediscovering who you are, waging war, wreaking vengeance on your enemies, and deciding the fate of (not necessarily saving) the world. Coupled with the way questing in the game is organized, it promises to be time well-spent.

The world
The developers of the game are renowned for their way of scrupulously creating locations, and the game is the manifestation of the skill. No location is similar; no place is dull. True, the world is not that big (which is often the subject of constant boasting of various developers), but it is alive and truly interesting to explore.

Controls 
Now, let me turn to the part of the game that was widely criticized. I have to admit that it is indeed tough to get to grips with the way you control the movements  of your character. Even more so with the fighting system (the fixed target system can be a real bummer at times). But all that fades away once you have put 5-10 hours into the game - it all starts feeling natural. Many people also complained about how difficult the game is, and I do agree that for a non-hardcore gamer the game is rather an ordeal than a walk in a park. For those, however, who are willing to experience a throwback to the tames of Gothic I&II, this will be just the right experience!

Gameplay
What I loved about the aspect (and the way it is different from many other games of the genre) is how much lack of skill/attribute points is felt! What happens in every other RPG is you have plenty of skill points to distribute and getting the skills you need is usually child's play. In this game, you constantly have skills that you want to acquire, but there is simply not enough point, so you have to do a lot of thinking as regards what to improve.

Graphics
The game looks beautiful. I wish I could say stunning, but let's face it, there are more beautiful games out there. However, taking into account the fact that the game is 2 years old, it looks amazing (and the fact that I play on the highest settings on my ASUS Zenbook laptop should tell you how non-demanding the game is hardware-wise).

Bugs
The only bug I found is if you don't talk to Nasty right after you complete the 2nd quest for her, she fill go back to her place and the next time you see her she will be in a combat mode until she gets to the entrance to the city. But that is a minor thing, although a bit annoying.

Overall, the game is one of the best RPG I've played, and I do recommend it to everyone who's looking for an interesting story set in a handcraft world accompanied by a challenging gameplay.

The worst game by Piranha Bytes and the worst of all RPGs I've played in the last 10 years.
First of all, loot. For me, it's the most important gameplay point in Piranha Bytes' games. Unlimited inventory allows to pick up every item in such a big world. So what do we got here? Tonns of toilet paper and cutlery, over than a thousand mugs and fine cups, a couple of toys, lots of scrap, old coins and bundles of ♂Three hundred bucks♂. All of these items are worth almost nothing, and it's so damn boring to find another pack of trash instead of something useful. You can't loot any weapons from defeated enemies, even if you are killing them. Maybe developers didn't want to break game economics yet they allowed to abuse crafting system wich damages economics even more than selling picked-up weapons. By the way, there are almost no good equipment in this damn game. The strongest meele weapon is not the legendary but some random axe upgraded to lvl 3. You can't upgrade legendary items even if they're much weaker than common. You can't upgrade modified weapons (though you can but they lose their modification). I've never used legendary or modified weapons in this game (except The Mortal Beam in the end of the game) just because they're weaker than common. I've never met any weapon that stops stamina regeneration on enemies, though enemies had such swords and axes. The only good thing here are sunglasses that allow you to see any loot in a short distance. BUT they cannot be equipped with helmet and they reveal damn frustraring items that are stuck in textures (guess I was lucky that there were no stuck quest items). I could've written a lot more text about loot, but there are more things to tell of.

Secondly, the combat system. I guess guys on game jams can create more logical and balanced fights than we can see in this game. Tell me, what will happen to strong man if you beat him with 10+ kg axe (just imagine, I do not call up to do it)? At least, he will step back. What happens to almost every enemy in this game if you hit them that way? Nothing, They just finish their move or strike you if they began backswinging before your hit. And the funniest thing is that you WILL be stunned if an enemy hits you. Just because. The most disgusting thing here is stamina. I know that consumption of it is varied due to difficulty level, but it's hard to find more crooked and useless mechanics than this one. I passed the game on ultra level and every fight till the middle of the game was like save/load every 20 seconds (or even less). And it's not about reaction. You just hit and enemy (or an air: hitboxes here are beyond any understanding) three or four times and... you can do nothing but walk around. You can't run, you can't EVADE ATTACKS just cause you have to wait for stamina regeneration. It could've been okay if not what I've written above. Btw, it all works only for a player. Animals don't suppose to have stamina here and human enemies can strike even if they have no stamina. Yeah, every hit here stops stamina regeneration and decreases its level. Aggro also is non-understandable for me, sometimes a whole bunch of beasts can run a half of the map to fight you even though you only ran pass them in 15+ meters away. Some human enemies (Zardom, for example) have much more HP and damage than Mountain troll, and fighting them is even harder than fighting the final boss.

Thirdly, personal progress. I won't say much about it, it's just broken. You can learn 3 spells that increase the amount of exp you are getting for: killing beasts (not every enemy, just beasts, not humans), completing quests and reading books. Before learning them you need to upgrade about 10 lvl and reach 50 points of intelligence. And what do you think the percentage of added exp is? 5. FIVE DAMN PERCENTS. Or even less. It's almost nothing compare to how many exp you need to reach the next level. You get 10 attribute points with every level (11 with corresponding spell), but after 30 points of any attribute you need 2 instead of 1 and after 60 points you need 5 to upgrade it. Btw, if you are travelling with the companion (wich is almost inevitable on ultra difficulty if you don't wanna spent 20+ minutes fighting one dog and an eternity if there are 2+ enemies), you need to last hit every enemy or you just don't get additional exp. For the whole game (even after the epilogue!!!) you companion's damage is much higher than yours. Reading mechanics is bugged and usually you just don't get any experience for it. FFS.

Paragraph 4. Story.
While previous games by Piranha Bytes at least had interesting and logical plot (for average RPG), this one has none. The only story that is more or less interesting to know is the story of Clerics' god Calaan and old world Scientists (almost all information is located in one place that takes 30 minutes to fully discover it). All the rest is annoying, common and doesn't make any sense. All quests are monotonous and boring. There could've been much more interesting stories but we have lots of empty places as instead.

There were much more things to discuss how awful they are but if you aren't convinced by my words that this game is not worth of your attention, you can buy it and test by yourself. The only reason I've played 170+ hours in this piece of junk is that I hoped there will be something interesting in the end, but the only thing waited me here was disappointment. I'm happy I didn't pay the full price for this (it was on Steam sale) and if I could turn time back, I wouldn't even add this 'game' to my wishlist.

Начнем, пожалуй, с начала

1 - Начало: я понимаю, малый бюджет, не лучшее положение, но можно было
сделать нормальную заставку и сюжет! Правда - я ожидал чего-то явно другого.

2 - Геймплей: Я скучнее и нуднее фарма редко где вообще встречал, для примера:
Я в начале игры попытался победить огромного тролля (это огромные чубрики, которых в начале победить почти невозможно), долбил 3 часа и наконец-то победил, получил 100 XP. Думаю, норм! Но скоро нахожу буханку хлеба, которая дает с только же, блн! Я хз кто делал систему прокачки и систему получения опыта, но я ему бы лично сказал, что эта система мучения игрока просто ужасна!(плюс, да некоторые квесты построены интеренно и дают за них прилично, но дальше я напишу про это побольше)

3 - Сюжет: Ну да в начале я написал, что это слабость игры, но иногда может удивить поворотами и разветвлениями.

Плюс, есть фракции квесты, проходить которые может быть реально интересно, но в основе своей это банальное - принеси похлебку из барана и не сдохни по пути, или убей этих ужасных монстров и спаси наших друзей. И да, это очень надоедает
после 5, 7 квеста, а их надо выполнить как минимум 30, чтобы более-менее прокачаться.

Сам сюжет это вообще нечто - постоянное убей альбов, найди кого-то, ну и так далее превращается из удовольствия в рутину. Ну и да, конечно,обязательно, сами персонажи, диалоги, все как обычно, условно во время диалога иногда собеседник может чесать то место, которое я не хочу называть, или вообще рука через текстуру проваливается.
Вообщем да,  сюжет и правда проходить интересно только из-за концовки.

4 - Баги: Оооо, на этом разделе я и вправду оттянусь по полной! В этой игре, если ты прошел квест без проблем, то это уже не Елекс! Каждое задание ты должен лезть в интернет, чтобы найти решение проблемы, из-за которой может возникнуть еще одна. 
Помните, я говорил про похлебку, так вот я должен был отдать похлебку кое-какому персонажу, но из-за ошибки в другом квесте он не хотел со мной говорить! Гениально, Пираньи, я аплодирую вам стоя. И удивительно, но через какое-то время (16 часов) он внезапно заговорил со мной! Я никогда в своей жизни еще так не орал... иногда персонажы проваливаються... умирают... это временами похоже на Вьетнам. Вообщем, если я буду рассказывать про все баги, то это затянется как минимум на обзоров 10, поэтому просто скажу, что тут багов очень, очень и очень много, привыкай!

5 - Детали: Я искренне не хотел делать это, но придется... Если кратко, то тут будет много всего. 
Начнем, пожалуй, с халатности, нет, холотности, неа - а холодность, во! Если кратко, то она, как по мне, в корне не нужна, ибо играет роль она только в концовке или иногда в диалогах. Так если вы не хотите гриндить 35 часов нон стоп, тогда у нас есть способ! Если быстро - есть такие вещи, как преобрезователи. Рекомендую не идти туда в начале игры, но рекомдую на лвл так 14! Где-то в пустыне есть один преобрезователь. Если правильно пробежать и отключить его, то там можно будет найти пушку "Отпускатель грехов". Для нее нужен интеллект и ловкость. Если сделать один баг с деньгами, то можно получить кучу элексита и спустить его на элексовое питье. Распределив очки вы получите доступ к этой пушке. И НАЧИНАЙТЕ РАЗНОСИТЬ ВСЕХ НАПРАВО И НАЛЕВО ВЕДЬ ТЕПЕРЬ ТЫ ПОВЕЛИТЕЛЬ ИГРЫ! Да, некоторые баги и вправду могут очень сильно помочь. 

КОНЕЦ АБЗОРА, СПАСИПКИ ЧТО ПАСМАТРЕЛИ ЭТОТ АБЗОР НА ЕЛЕКС!

Ich hatte erstaunlicherweisen jede Menge Spass mit dem Spiel.  Elex schaffte es auch mich wieder mit dem Piranha Bytes Studio zu versöhnen, von welchem zwei meiner absoluten Lieblings Spiele Gothic 1 und Gothic 2 stammen (beide zwischen 20 und 25 Mal gespielt), dass mich aber auch mit Gothic 3 und Risen 1 ziemlich verärgert hatte.  Zur Erklärung: Gothic 3 war zum Release kaum spielbar. Risen 1 hingegen fand ich grossartig, bis ich zu dem seltsamen "Super Mario Brothers" Endkampf kam. Danach deinstallierte ich das Spiel und warf es in eine Ecke, wo es für immer Verschwand. Zurück zu Elex. Ich hatte mir schon einige Let's Plays angeschaut und war deshalb im Bilde über die Dinge die viele Spieler geärgert hatten. Trotzdem hatte mich das gesehene irgendwie "angemacht".  Also kaufte ich es mir und legte los. Ich liebe diese neue Welt. Sie ist so atmosphärisch und wunderschön, dass ich, als ich hätte zum Endkampf aufbrechen können stundenlang einfach nur durch die Welt gestromert war, um jagt auf die grösseren "Viecher" der Welt zu machen. Die Story finde ich besser als viele Kritiker des Spiels. Mir gefällt wie sie in Audio Logs und Ingame Texten erzählt wird. Klar dadurch werden Spieler, die wie ich, jede Ecke der schönen Welt erkunden und sich alles anhören und alles lesen, besser mit der Story bedient, als Spieler die sich gerne eng an eine Hauptstory halten und diese schnell durchspielen. Die Idee ein Jet Pack einzuführen fand ich ebenfalls sehr gut (der Jet Pack Angriff, war meine liebste Nahkampf Attacke). Weniger interessant fand ich die Fraktionen, die waren aber auch nicht mehr annähernd so wichtig, wie zu Gothic Zeiten. Die Kämpfe können zu Anfang des Spiels recht hart sein, zumal das Kampfsystem, wie meist in den Spielen des Studios nicht besonders gut ist. Später wird das Spiel jedoch leichter (besonders wenn man sich die Waffen Todesstrahl und Witwenmacher besorgt hat).  Letztlich hatte ich über 370 Stunden in das Spiel investiert, und mir aufgrund des Spielspasses den ich hatte, sogar Risen 2 und Risen 3 besorgt und gespielt. Ich bin absolut zufrieden mit den Kauf des Spiels.

Elex je zjevení. Nečekal jsem, že ještě někdy vyjde hra, kterou budu hltat jako 17 letej kluk Gothica. Ta atmosféra, kdy procházíte s hořčíkovou loučí temné podzemí továrny, obydlené fakt zlými potvorami mě uchvátila. Celkově atmosféra sci-fi a fantasy světa do sebe zapadá a dává to smysl.

Elex je lepší než Fallout 4, po objevení Calaana jsem si připadal jako hrdinové z knihy Chvalozpěv na Leibowitze (geniální sci-fi jež bylo inspirací Falloutům). Jsou tam ledový záporňáci jako ve Hře o trůny. Důležité vztahy s vašimi parťáky, které mi připomněly Sons of Anarchy. A je to i takové Dark souls, umíral jsem hodně. Třeba když jsem byl líný zapálit louč a spadnul jsem do výtahové šachty. Hudba, byť není od Rosenkranze se mi líbila. A je to snad první hra, kde na konci nemám plný batoh zlaťáků a není za co je utratit, tady se pořád dá něco kupovat a vylepšovat, i když ukradnu co vidím.

Nejvíc bych vyzdvihl příběh a atmosféru světa. Vůbec nechápu, že jsem se k té hře dostal až teď. Pořád jsem čekal na Gothic 4 a mezitím přišlo něco lepšího :-)

So this game was hella jank. There were tons of little obnoxious bugs and inconsistencies. The voice acting was pretty butt, the animations were pretty weak, there were only like 2 or 3 different faces for female characters, and the combat was pretty easy to cheese.

But I had a blast. This game was sick as AF. I didn't play this game with the goal of min/maxxing my power level and doing every quest to maximize my reward. I chose a play-style at the beginning and decided 'this is how I'm going to play this' and it definitely didn't make things easy. I entirely avoided a mechanic that is borderline necessary to become powerful to stay true to my chosen path, and honestly, it totally paid off. I was not the all-mighty god-killer I am by the end of most RPGs but I had a very significant sense of satisfaction. 

There are a TON of things to complain about in this game - but they were overshadowed by the positive elements. 

While I feel somewhat compelled to play it again because there are basically 3 distinct ways you can play it - I probably won't, for the foreseeable future, but I got about a hundred hours out of it, and I came nowhere close to 'hunnerd percentin' this beast.

ELEX not a game you will say would draw your attention when you look at how ugly the character models looks in the game yet that doesnt take away from how brilliant the game looks when it comes to the world or even the game play. Now as a fan of piranha bites for years thanks to masterpieces like Gothic 1,2 & 3, I was rather letdown when they allowed JoWood & Spellbound to release that appalling excuse for a game called Gothic 4 so when they announced ELEX, I was sceptical, I thought to my self can they reinvigorate my love for them with this game and the answer was yes, yes they did. ELEX is a true rpg with a level of difficulty that I enjoyed. You cant just out of the gates just start maiming and butchering every npc and creature you see, you would get your but handed to you in a second flat. Instead this game relies on you to gear and level your character up and gain allies to help you along the way. ELEX as its predecessors it relies on you to figure out how you want to spend your skill points as you don't have a skill window as so many other rpgs does to destribute them, instead you need to find the correct trainers to teach you the skill you want. And with the factions of the game comes certain talents that's only available to you if you join that faction. Over all ELEX is a game that shows what an rpg could and should be like.

Despite a handful of flaws, my time with Elex was fairly enjoyable. Anybody who has ever played a Gothic game will feel right at home. There's a little discrepancy in this being a sci-fi game, fighting against mechs with swords and arrows feels a little odd and might take some time to get used to for some people. PB should've probably stuck to a fantasy setting. However, it's a beautifully handcrafted open gameworld with something new to discover anywhere you go. Dialogue is plentiful and your choices really matter, right up until the end. Gameplay is fine. Melee combat is a little broken, the autolock and "combo" system work as long as it is a 1 on 1 fight, but as soon as you fight more than one enemy who isn't a complete pushover, you'll be in trouble. You'll find yourself relying on ranged combat more often than you would like just to avoid having to put up with being stunlocked by a horde of enemies. Of course, this might be a dealbreaker for the scrubs who would rather play the game their way and then complain about the game being too difficult. I've encountered no bugs in my playthrough. Picked the game up on sale for 15$ and it was worth every penny. Solid 7/10.

Many of the other reviews for this game are right.  It will be  love or hate for this game.  The start of the game is very difficult. I advise avoiding quests that require combat early on. The way I played was to just run to all 4 major cities and do non-combat quests there. Avoid enemies that have a skull on their health bar. Get the hunting trophies perk to max level as soon as possible for extra stuff from enemies you can sell for cash.  The game is also very bad at telling you have to play early on, and you will probably have to consult the internet how to do things.

Pro-tip: press "f" to cycle through alternate fire modes on weapons. In particular grenades have a default time-fuse mode which is useless or just use the fire mode where they blow up on impact. Grenades are a great way to make short work of difficult enemies early game.



I will say that while the middle of the game is fine since you can  against enemies you can kill in a reasonable time frame, while at the same time being vulnerable.

Late game starts to get a bit one-sided. Experiences may differ based on which of the three factions you join, but I have a powered up flamethrower that stun locks the most powerful enemies, and plasma rifles that can emp stun lock the more dangerous mechanical enemies.  Groups of certain enemies can still be a challenge, but overall the game hits an acceptable, but not outstanding place torwards the end.

Exploration is important for a game like this and I would say it never gets to the level of Skyrim, but it does the job.   Many of the ruins appear to be copy-pasted structures. 

I have rambled enough. If you can get the game on sale, and you are on the fence go ahead and buy it.  If you can plow through the early game you will enjoy yourself if you found games like Skyrim fun.

Элекс - это игра, которую встречают по одёжке. Но, наиграв в ней 80 часов (именно столько ушло на прохождение за клирика), провожал я её с восхищением. 
 Это самая настоящая олдскульная РПГ, которая обязательно зайдет фанатам жанра. В Элексе не ведут игрока за ручку, он во многом неинтуитивен и неудобен, но, вопреки всем своим недостаткам, это прекрасная игра.
 В современной игре для меня было неожиданностью встретить такое количество диалогов, причем диалогов разветвленных, и имеющих реальное влияние на дальнейшее развитие сюжета. Разговоры в этой игре прописывались явно не для "галочки". Обилие квестов и их разнообразие тоже впечатляют.
 Система прокачки заставляет дважды подумать, прежде чем ввалить экспу в умения, и лучше заранее определиться, на каком типе оружия будет специализироваться ГГ, т.к. выкачать статы, достаточные для топовых образцов, в течение сюжета получится скорее всего только для одного, максимум двух классов - слишком много очков придется потратить. Хотя, конечно, никто не отменял прием элекса в промышленных масштабах, но там уже компромисс между статами и холодностью.
 Элекс отлично держит жанровую марку постапокалиптической РПГ, и для меня является бОльшим фолаутом, чем, допустим, тот же четвертый фолаут, на поверку оказавшийся обычным шутаном с символической РПГ-составляющей. 
 Из неочевидных плюсов - возможность сохраняться в любой момент, даже в бою. После убогой консольной системы сохранений по чекпоинтам, которая подпортила мне впечатление от многих хороших игр, возможность засейвиться где угодно - это очень приятный момент. Раньше, в старых играх, это было само собой разумеющимся, а сейчас вот за счастье.

 При всём позитиве, который игра мне подарила за 80 часов, всё же считаю нужным пройтись и по недостаткам.
 Самое первое и явное, что бросается в глаза - явно не соответствующая 2017г графика. Году эдак в 2010 она была бы топовой. Хотя, проработка лиц персонажей довольно уныла даже по меркам 2010г. Но для игры 2017г графическая составляющая откровенно слабая. При этом, требования к системе не сказать что совсем уж скромные - на уровне третьего Ведьмака (сужу по тому, как обе игры на максималках ведут себя на моем компе), который по части графики уделывает Элекс как Бог черепаху, хотя и вышел на 2 с половиной года раньше.
 Второй момент, наверняка отпугнувший добрую часть игроков, принявшихся играть в Элекс - абсолютно несбалансированное начало игры. Надо смириться с фактом, что первые 10 уровней ГГ - просто мясо, которое может легко загнуться даже от самого чахлого моба, а сильных вообще дальней дорогой обходить должно. Учитывая, что опыта на первых порах отваливают мало, а на убийствах его не нагриндишь (т.к. никого убить не можешь), то начало игры - это, скажем так, испытание для сильных духом. Однако, после присоединения к фракции, все меняется. Открывается доступ к фракционным способностям, броне и вооружению, и ГГ ступает на путь терминатора. Только вот до этого момента, судя по всему, терпения хватает далеко не у всех - и в этом явный косяк разрабов. Слишком уж у Элекса хардкорное начало, и через 5-6 часов игры начинает казаться, что беготня от всякой мелюзги типа кусак или гнильцов никогда не закончится. Поэтому, если кто вдруг после прочтения отзыва решит упороться в Элекс, знайте: боль заканчивается при вступлении во фракцию. 
 Также игра имеет очень неудобный по современным меркам инвентарь. Быструю кнопку прочтения только что найденного документа уж можно б было добавить, чтоб не ковыряться в длиннющем списке бумажек и не выискивать какую из них ты только что залутал. С другой стороны, инвентарь в игре это и плюс - он безразмерен, и не ограничен ни количеством вещей, ни их размером, ни массой.

 Из собственного опыта прохождения за клирика могу дать несколько советов тем, кто будет проходить игру.
 Первое. ОБЯЗАТЕЛЬНО вкачивайте на максимум умение сбора трофеев у любого учителя выживания - это залог хорошего фарма, т.к. с трупов будет лутаться куча всякой дорогостоящей лабуды, которую можно продать за нормальные деньги. А деньги (элексит) в игре крайне важны - на них вы будет покупать не только броню и боеприпасы, но и качать перса, и улучшать оружие. Да, для изучения навыка у профильного учителя нужны не только свободные очки умений, но и деньги - бесплатно вас учить никто не будет.
 Второе. Обязательно качайте "фракционный" оружейный навык. В случае с клириками - это псионические способности, берсерками - магия. Потому что имба и не контрится.
 Третье. На ранних стадиях игры получите умение "Химия" - это позволит вам иметь фактически неограниченный боезапас к магическому/псионическому оружию в виде маны или ментальной энергии.
 В принципе, это основы, которые позволят комфортно играть, остальное на свой вкус. Кому помогать, кого убивать, кого обворовывать - Элекс тем и хорош, что в нем можно творить что угодно.

 Подведу итог. Элекс - игра противоречивая. Но лично для меня она стала откровением, вернувшим меня в начало 2000х, когда я проходил Плейнскейп:Тормент, Арканум, первые два Фолаута, и прочие культовые игрухи. Она далека от современных стандартов "красоты" и удобства, во многих моментах хардкорна, но при всем при этом невероятно крута и интересна. Для любителей старых РПГ - однозначный маст хэв.

ELEX
- Vásárlás előtti vélemény -
Már elég régóta vágytam arra, hogy megvehessem. Hiszen a kedvenc számítógépes játék készítő cég alkotta meg ezt a játékvilágot is. Risen is jó volt, de annyira nem fogott meg, hogy játsszak a második és harmadik részével. A Gothic az más, számomra még mindig az a legjobb alkotás amit összehoztak, Gothic egy természetesen az első helyen szerepel, és a második helyen a Gothic 3, aminek szintén fergeteges a hangulata bármiféle erőltetés nélkül.
Olvastam róla véleményeket a kívánságlistára adása előtt, s kíváncsi leszek milyen nehéz is. Path of Exile ota az-az érzésem, hogy nem sok olyan akció játék van ami nehezebb lenne annál.
Kivételes árengedménnyel vettem meg, 60% os leértékeléssel , azonnal rávetettem magam :D. Jól fog jönni a Fallout 76 os csalódás után.
- Játszás utáni vélemény - 
Már egy ideje nem játszottam, a játékkal, és úgy gondoltam akkor írom meg mindezt ha kijátszottam az egészet, de végül abbamaradt.
A játék maga nagyon szép, pár hanghatás ugyan az mint a Gothic 1 ben :D ( PL: víz hangja, úszáskor, tapicskoláskor )
Kíváncsi voltam hogyan oldották meg a lőfegyverek használatát egy olyan játékban mint ez, de kicsit másabb mint amire számítottam, de legalább nem olyan eszetlen mint pár Fantasy játéknál.
Nagyon érdekes, hogy választhatjuk azt hogy megint erősek leszünk az Elex szedésétől de érzelmileg hidegekké válunk, de a válaszaink is lehetnek érzelmesek és érzelem mentesek.
Úgy is dönthetünk, hogy nem szedjük, és tiszták maradunk, de nem kapunk plusz pontokat, amik valljuk meg lvl 20 után is nagyon kevés van.
Vannak nagyon durva fegyverek, amik azonnal megölnek.
Difficult nehézségen kezdtem, és később igencsak meglátszott a nehézsége. Szerencsére akkor kezdtem el játszani vele amikor lehetett változtatni a nehézségen. Félreértés ne essék difficulton is ki lehet játszani, csak 3x annyi időbe telik, és a rá szánt 3x annyi idő kezdett frusztrálni. A Szintezés jó dolog, minél magasabb a szinted és a tudásod annál könnyebben győzöd le az ellenfeleket ( megszokott Piranha Bites játék mechanika ).
A három frakció közül a Raidereket választottam, de sajnos itt sem azt kaptam amit vártam. Nagyon kevés olyan küldetés van ami tényleg Raider jellegű. Inkább kisstílű utcai gettó hierarchiája van, mintsem megfogó hangulata. Majd később megpróbálom a Clericet. A Nomád életet folytatók is hangulatosak, de ott pár dolog nem tetszik.
Mindenesetre bárhogyan is nézem, 40+ óra után is érdekes, fordulatos volt az egész. Minőségi játékot adott ki a cég, érződik, nem csak a táj szépségén.

Röviden-
A pozitívumok:
+Hangulat
+Környezet ( romossága ellenére csodálatos helyek vannak benne )
+Kalandozás élvezete
+Harcrendszer logikus
+Változtatható nehézségek
+Rengeteg választási lehetőség
+Elex befolyása - ha szeded ha nem -
+Szemelyiség fejlődés - romlás
+Csapattársak ( sokszor jól jönnek, főleg az elején )
+Megannyi fegyver lehetőség
+Érdekes küldetések
+Gyors utazás lehetősége
+Jetpack
+Effektek
+Zene
+Effektes tárgyak ( pl ellenséget mutató napszemüveg. )

Negatívumok:
-Orientáció problémák előfordulnak
- Ki lehet hagyni jó pár npc - quest szálat - beszélgetés úgy, hogy egy későbbi végső beszélgetést elkezdesz, és utána fogalmad sincs hogy jutott el odáig.
- Kevés pontok, és rengeteget igénylő alap fegyverek.
- Ha elértél egy rangot, megcsappannak a frakció küldetések, aminek eredménye, hogy szegény leszel, mert a jó kis páncélt valamiből kifizetted, és utána is költeni kell de nincs miből mert nincs normálisan, vagy egyáltalán fizető küldetés.
- Néha nem lehet tudni hogy hülye a karakter, vagy csak pár kérdése az.
- Akkor elfogadható a karakter arca ha napszemüveget vesz fől, különben eléggé kellemetlen pár pillantása de gondolom szándékosan. ( talán ezért nem szeretem Wichert )
- Szívatós események ( nem spoilerezem )
- Néha bevakító fény, vagy sötét effektek.
- Sokaknak Easy módon is nehéz lehet.
- Némely ellenfelet akkor esélyes legyőzni ha gránáttal agyon dobom, mert kardforgatást használva ellene azonnal letarol és megöl, de vannak ilyen tulajdonsággal rendelkező lőfegyverek is, amik elől érdemesebb elmenekülni és rajtaütni hogy azonnal váltson fegyvert az ellenfél.

Nagyjából ennyi, lehet van még és akadnak profik akik részletesen tudják felvázolni milyen búgok s egyebek vannak, de én így távlatba visszaemlékezve ennyi ragadt meg.
Jó játék szerintem, és megéri a pénzét, főleg ha kedvezményesen vehető meg :D Hamarosan itt a karácsony, lehet ez a játék is akciós lesz :).
Jó kalandozást mindenkinek, és sok csillogó kék Elexet kívánok. ( kellene egy olyan otthonra, nagyon szép, és bevilágítaná a helyiségeket esténként.

Look, this is a Piranha Bytes game and that means a few things:
- the voice acting will be painfully bad
- the controls will be awful and not fluid
- the animations will be terrible
- the UI will be a joke
- graphics and performance are likely to suck
- difficulty curve will be brutal and unbalanced
- story writing and quests will sometimes be confusing and flat out broken

On the positive side, the story will likely be unique and interesting.  

True to a PB game, ELEX hits the mark for the cons and the pros. Great RPG game which doesn't hold your hand. Familiar play style for Gothic players.

Took me a little while to get into it, as the game presents really lot of characters and places and names and my brain couldn't really soak it up immediately, but I really started to enjoy the world as soon as I started to orient in it. So, just be patient. This is not Diablo, you cannot just run in and kill everything right of the bat. It's a slow burner.

Addressing some negative reviews:
Game is difficult in the beginning - and that means it takes 10 or 20 hours to get your character to a power level on which you can fight without fear. That was also typical for Gothic games.
It forces you to be creative with solving different quests. If I couldn't kill it with a sword, I killed it with grenade, kited it around, or used jetpack to get to advantageous position.
If I needed to take object I could sneak to take it, or just run in, pick it up and jetpack away from enemies.

I didn't have problems with combat controls. It is also connected to power level of character. Takes a while to get used to, but I had no real problems. Just don't button mash, know how much stamina you need for attack and defense and you'll be fine.
Use target locking and unlocking (or hiding a weapon) when fighting multiple enemies. It will help you not faceplant nearest pillar or wall when you are trying to disengage from a fight to heal up or run away.

Also, I finished the game without any faction abilities (spells and enchantments). After that I read a review saying: "Without faction ablities, you will die so often and so quickly that you have to force yourself to continue."
Horsecock.

I didn't experience whole lot of bugs either. Game crashed about 4 times in 50 hours, once my frames dropped but restarting game helped, once I couldn't hack something, dialog options disappeared - restarting game helped.
I am really OK with all of that, it literaly took 3 minutes out of my gameplay. Other than that I had stable and high frame rate, no issues.

If you like Piranha Bytes' other games you're probably going to like this one as well. Like others have said it takes quite a while to get going, but I think that's a design decision aimed at making you feel like you're actually growing stronger. Sure, there are bugs, and the combat could definitely be improved. but the world is absolutely fantastic (something PB have always excelled at) and I actually did quite enjoy the combat once I learned how to use it.

Even with all the negatives I mention below, I still enjoyed the game and the story. You will enjoy the game if you lower expectations a bit and read a few guides on how to avoid the pitfalls. Under the unpolished mechanics is a gem of a story in a compelling world.

Bad stuff to ignore (if you can):
-can't remap some keys
-some useless skills not worth the cost
-uneven progression
-fighting is clunky but workable when you understand it
-graphics are serviceable but you get used to it

Could be bad to some, but I liked:
=no quest giver markers. You have to exhaust most dialog to get quests.
=quests give the most XP. Killing mobs to advance is possible but not efficient. Forces you out into the world to grow.
=mix of easy and difficult mobs. Early game is dangerous to explore
=lots of dialog. Some main NPCs are chatty, but it helps flesh out the complex world. (You can fast-forward most dialog)
=you have to pay attention during the dialog. They give hints and clues.

Good stuff:
+world building is good. The setting is solid. The map world is decent size with varied biomes and lore behind each area.
+four main factions. Each have their own lore and reason for survival. They clash against each other and build the story.
+you join one of three factions and get their perks. Each are unique and powerful, but think carefully before joining.
+most quests have multiple options for completion
+your choices do matter. Completing a quest a certain way will make some happy and others not so much.

If you like to explore an interesting world with secrets and lore, just ignore the bad bits and play the game. It is a fun journey.

Edit: I bought the game on sale. I felt I got my $20 worth of fun. I wouldn't recommend paying much more.
