I should have taken the "mixed" reviews more seriously. Terrible combat, and occasionally too buggy to finish quests. Found the in-game karma system very poorly executed. Parts of the main quest can be entirely gated off if your "Cold" stat is too high or too low, regardless of things you might have otherwise said or done, with no options to use your character's skills or stats to convince people otherwise. In other RPG's with karma, like Fallout NV, you have the option to sweet talk people, or use your massive brain to convince them with science. 

Other than those downsides, the setting is neat, and a lot of the side quests don't suffer from the same faults as the main quests do. 

Definitely a mixed bag. I would wait for a reasonably good sale, and be prepared to rely on cheap stupid tactics and save spamming to make any headway.

Very good. I was on the fence about this game because of the mixed reviews, so I waited for a sale. Throughout the game, for about a quarter of it, I wasn't really sure what I thought of it. By halfway though, I was thoroughly enjoying it overall.

It's important to go into this game with the right expectations, which you can get easily from other reviews. The difficulty is enjoyable once you know to expect it, and that you're expected to wander around a lot in this game to find where you're going. The only reason it feels tedious or hard is because it's abnormal for RPGs to be like this. I kind of wish it were more normal. I died a lot in the first ~10 hours of gameplay. By the last 1/3 of my game time though, I almost never died. It's also important to know that, even when dying frequently, the game doesn't punish you for it. You just have to save frequently, but there's even an autosave every 3min. The game reloads very quickly (a few seconds on my SSD), so dying never felt tedious.

Don't feel bad about looking things up for this game. A lot of it goes unexplained, such as what the skills actually do (the descriptions are vague at best, and misleading at worst). The game could get better at this, or at least give you a way of resetting your skills.

For all of this game's lack of polish, one funny thing I noticed is that you can pause the game during dialogue. I don't think I've ever seen a game support this! It's a very useful feature when life interrupts your gaming and you don't want to miss anything.

Overall, if you're a fan of RPGs in general, you should be open to this game. It's a change of pace and a much-appreciated addition to the modern genre.

Elex is an action RPG that takes upon the daunting task of combining sci-fi with medieval fantasy and surprisingly manage to pull it off. As long as you can get over the very high amount of AA jank, this an ambitious title worth experiencing. 

[b]Positives:[/b] 
[list]
    [*]Quest design is excellent. Almost always there are multiple ways to complete a quest that help in roleplaying and I don't remember there being any uninteresting fetch quest. There are 3 main factions to choose to from and they provide very different abilities, so lots of room for replayability. 
    [*]The exploration is rewarding and has enough unique locations & loot. This is the closest you'll come to Bethesda's level and damn impressive for a AA game. Despite some low poly areas, the world is beautiful with perfect use of lighting to bring out the atmosphere. The verticality of the map design is really well done and the jetpack allows for fun traversal. 
    [*]Player progression is one the best I've seen. You start as a complete weakling and the world feels genuinely dangerous as you try to avoid almost every enemy. 1st time you get companion feels like huge rewards mechanically. You take your sweet time to level up and can get frustrating and it indirectly hinders your exploration but keep at and you'll be rewarded.
   [*]The world building and story can feel a bit silly in the beginning but as more of the game opens up, you see the genuine effort the devs have put in to make a believable immersive world. 
[/list]

[b]Negatives:[/b] 
[list]
   [*]Combat. Don't let fanboys fool you, it's terrible, at least for 2/3rd of the game. Hitboxes are some of the worst I've seen in past decade. Melee combat plays like a poor man's Witcher 3 so get a gun as soon as possible or join a faction to get magic/tech abilities. A game the prioritizes stamina management, the devs made an inexplicable decision to give only bipedal enemies stamina but 70% of the enemies you fight are monsters with no stamina requirement. 
  [*]Companion AI is trash. A significant portion of the time they stand around while you get mauled by beasts. Do yourself a favor and stick to the companion Duras, he has the most aggresive AI and thus the least bad. 
  [*]Although enemy visual designs are very good, most are actually just reskins of earlier enemies with more damage. This wouldn't have been a problem if not for the fact that you fight enemies by learning they attack pattern and when newer enemies have the exact same pattern as earlier ones, it sucks out the joy of discovering something new. 
[/list]

Overall Elex is an ambitious game that stumbles in almost every area. Despite that if you can look past the AA jank, it's a very enjoyable experience. Certainly a much better roleplaying experience than Bethesda titles. Here's hoping that Piranha Bytes will actually improve for a change since Gothic in the inevitable Elex sequel.

Взять топовую пушку клириков "Отпускатель грехов" в середине игры и идти в соло зачищать весь Магалан от альбов и прочей нечисти - изи. Штраф на повышение холодности от элексового питья не работает. Холодность повышается только при выборе определенных вариантов ответов в диалогах и употреблении чистого элекса. Цифровых значений холодности у нас нет, что означает то или иное состояние не объясняют, и как это влияет на игру вы тоже поймете не сразу. Я проходил игру за эмоционального персонажа, снизил холодность почти до нуля и в финале понял, что не могу получить лучшую концовку. Загрузил сохранение перед битвой с Гибридом, сожрал весь чистый элекс из инвентаря, повысил холодность до "нейтрального" и получил лучшую концовку. Сколько еще раз нам нужно будет получать пропуск, чтобы войти в город? В игре 4 города, в 2 из них нужен пропуск! Сколько еще раз нужно будет убить X штук Y монстров? Это не "готический" шарм и не тру РПГ для олдов, это лень и самокопирование, которое уже откровенно надоело. Ярких харизматичных персонажей как и квестов в игре тоже почти нет? Могу вспомнить разве что Бестию - сестру Герцога из Тавора с её заносчивым характером и одного из спутников - клирика Фалька с его довольно необычной историей.

ELEX is a fun little game that sat on my virtual shelf for far too long before I felt like delving in to an RPG. It scratched the old Bethesda itch, feeling a little like Fallout, in that the world is post-apocalyptic and features radiation, mutants, and people, especially Outlaws, living in and off of the ruins of the past, while the Berserker faction, magic, and melee combat were more reminiscent of The Elder Scrolls. ELEX, however, manages to feel smooth by comparison, and looks far better in third person (which is good, because that's the only way you can play the game).

The story has three paths that overlap somewhat, aligned with each of three factions, none of which are at all appealing, but one of which you must join. The Berserkers are raging technophobes, shouting at you for actions as innocuous as opening the menu within their line of sight, the Outlaws are ludicrous pastiche of anarcho-capitalists, and the Clerics worship [spoiler]a space program that never got off the ground[/spoiler] and aren't above using literal Jedi mind control to grow their ranks. Despite these flaws, each faction offers some solid companions with their own personality, combat style, and missions, and none of them are faction-exclusive. The main character is set in stone, and while you may guide his choices to an extent, you're not going to get any sort of character creator to play around with. Jax is Jax, and he can be passionate or icy, but he won't be silly.

It's not just the style and theme that evoke images of Bethesda's major franchises, unfortunately. There are a few bugs that never got hammered out, but for a studio a tenth the size of Big B, that can be overlooked. I certainly didn't encounter anything game-breaking, just a few segments of dialogue out of place here and there, some self-unlocking chests, and the occasional AI glitch that left enemies and allies in permanent hover, unable to choose a direction to travel.

Back to positives, there's no annoying morality system in-game that boils down to "angel" and "churlish brute". Instead, the balance is between emotion and logic, with both "good" and "evil" options in each category at times. The "Thieves Guild" is a particular stand-out, in that it's actually inconspicuous and easy to miss, unlike in TES games where every third person will talk about it in radiant dialogue.

As for technical specs, it ran well on High settings on a machine slightly older than the game itself without complaint. Load times were minimal, and a seamless map helped keep them even more rare - if you never teleport, you might never see a loading screen.

[h1]In Conclusion[/h1]
If Fallout 76 left a bad taste in your mouth, the release of Skyrim VR for the AppleWatch didn't catch your interest, and you missed ELEX the first time around, it's worth your time to watch some gameplay footage to see if it catches your interest.

ELEX is a single-player game in which you play a character who gets expelled by his people. You start with pretty much nothing, but can equip yourself by solving quests [i](of which there really are a lot in this game)[/i] until you're strong enough to challenge your former leader and guide your people into a better [i](or worse)[/i] future.
On the way, you get to choose between 3 factions which you can join to get better equipment and support for your mission. You also gain friends that help you in fights, you can learn skills and abilities and you can explore the really wide and rich open world.
Your decisions affect your "personality" and determine whether you're successful in fulfilling your mission or not.
Apart from the story, there is stuff waiting around every corner and if you like looting as if there's no tomorrow, then the game is perfect for you. Even if you don't find enough material to craft and trade for better equipment, you might as well play thief and loot houses of your fellow human beings.
The game can be played at least 3 times as you can choose to join a different faction or make decisions that lead to a [b]different ending[/b] with every new run.

I did not see a lot of bugs, apart from companions doing some weird stuff from time to time. 
Also, the game does not require high-end PC components [i](GTX 1050 Ti, I play on highest settings, 40fps)[/i], but that is the result of the not very overwhelming visual experience. It uses an older engine and textures often have a "good enough" resolution or quality. To me, this was not a problem though. I assume that the time and money saved on graphic design was probably invested in story and open-world development. In fact, those two things are really, really great.

All in all, ELEX is a content-packed game that satisfied my will to explore and told a nice story at the same time.
Recommended!

Nach über 44 Stunden des Spielens bin ich zwischen Hass und Liebe hin und hergerissen. Leider überwiegte zu lange der Frust, als dass ich das Spiel klar empfehlen kann.

Was fand ich positiv und warum habe ich weitergespielt?

So genau kann ich das nicht sagen. Mir gefällt das Set mit einer Mischung aus Witcher und Fallout recht gut, sodass ich es doch durchgespielt habe. Außerdem war die eine oder andere Quest doch ganz lustig und mit ein wenig frischen Sarkasmus garniert. Insgesamt war es ok, auch wenn ich 45 Stunden für ein angeblich umfangreiches Rollenspiel eher dürftig empfinde und lange Etappen mit Frust gesegnet waren.

Was fand ich negativ?

Das ist eine ganze Menge und ich möchte nur die wesentlichen Aspekte benennen:

1. Kampfsystem
Das Spiel sorgt für Frust und lernt einem das Dauerspeichern von der ersten Minute an. Nein, nicht weil es schwer ist oder die Herausforderungen besonders kniffelig sind, nein, es liegt an diesem total miesen Kampfsystem. Die Steuerung ist derart mies, dass man öfters (und auch noch gegen Ende des Spiels) einfach in die Luft haut oder der Held nicht in der Lage ist den gewünschten Gegner zu fokussieren oder das Jetpack reagiert nicht, und man kann bei Erschöpfung nicht Abstand zum Gegner aufbauen. Das ist frustrierend hoch 3 zumal man später sehr stark ist und jeden Gegner in Sekunden zu Brei schlägt aber man dennoch stirbt, wenn die "buggy" Steuerung mal wieder zuschlägt und der Gegner den Helden nach 3 Kombos zerstört

2. Unendlich dumme Mitstreiter
Sowas habe ich selten in einem Spiel erlebt. Der Mitstreiter schaut in der Regel zu wie mich Gegner angreifen und im schlimmsten Fall fängt er erst an zu kämpfen, wenn man selbst schon fast am Boden liegt. Des Öfteren greifen die unfassbar dummen Mitstreiter dann zu einem Raketen- oder Flammenwerfer während man selbst im Nahkampf den Gegner bestreitet. Natürlich ist das eine dumme Idee, wie sich hier jeder vorstellen kann. Häufig rennt der Partner über jede Mine die im Feld liegt, was einem auf Grund der Nähe selbst mit in die Luft reist.

3. Unsympathische Fraktionen und ein noch unsympathischerer Held
Bei vielen Dialogen würde ich am Liebsten gar nicht antworten, weil jeder Vorschlag derart dreist oder einfach nur stumpfsinnig ist. Der Held muss einen IQ von 70 haben, anders können die gebotenen Antworten und dieser archaische Rachedurst nicht erklärt werden. In vielen Situationen ist der Held dem NPC gegenüber völlig unterlegen und dennoch macht er das Maul auf so groß wie Mich Jagger. Am Liebsten würde ich einen anderen Helden wählen können. Die Dialoge nerven meisten...
Bei den Fraktionen ist es ähnlich. Alle sind geprägt von einem totalitären und faschistoiden Führungsstil. Letztlich habe ich mich für die Kleriker entschieden, was noch das geringere Übel war. Warm bin ich mit keiner Fraktion geworden. Die Sympathie, die man in anderen Rollenspielen für die "Mitmenschen" und den Helden entwickelt, fehlt hier, zumindest bei mir, völlig.

4. Wenige Quests
Anfangs bei den Beserkern noch recht umfangreich, aber gegen Ende des Spiels doch eher dünn: Die Anzahl und der Umfang der Quests. Man könnte meinen, die Entwickler hatten gegen Ende hin immer weniger Lust sich noch was auszudenken. Alleine die Quests, um bei der 3. Fraktion (Kleriker) aufgenommen zu werden, waren vom Umfang her gut 1/3 von den der Beserker. Im Feld findet man noch ein paar Quests aber im Vergleich zu anderen Spielen doch eher unterdurchschnittlich.

5. Bugs in Quests, beim Kämpfen und beim Klettern über Hindernisse und Berge
Hier ist echt nahezu alles vertreten. Gegner bleiben in der Wand hängen, Quests können nicht beendet werden bzw. Mobs tauchen nicht auf. Manche Quests können nicht abgegeben werden weil man von der Hauptstory noch nicht soweit ist. Leider gibt es da kein Hinweis nach dem Motto "Komme doch später noch einmal wieder". Nur durch die Berichte anderer Spieler bei der Internetrecherche wurde ich darauf hingewiesen, dass ich erst im zweiten Passus sein muss, um als Kleriker im Rang aufzusteigen. Der "Quest-Mob" hingegen sagt "alles erledigt" und statt dem Aufstieg im Rang sagt er danach "du musst dich noch beweisen". Natürlich denkt man dann als erstes an einen Bug. Beim Klettern in den Bergen und über Hindernisse ist ebenfalls häufiges Speichern angesagt. Festsitzen in einer Ritze oder Hängen in der Wand, ja, dies passiert doch öfters mal...

6. Loot
Eigentlich gibt es bis auf wenige Ausnahmen nur Schrott in dieser Welt. Die 25. Klopapierrolle, Elektroschrott oder eine weitere inhaltsleere Notiz machen es nicht besser. Die vielen Notizen hätten der Anfang einer interessanten Questreihe sein können, aber nein, meistens haben diese gar keinen Einfluss auf das Spiel.
Theoretisch gibt es keine Gründe unbekannte Regionen zu besuchen, die man nicht über die regulären Quests erreicht. In der Regel findet man auch in gut bewachten Ecken nur Mist. Immerhin hat man gegen Ende hin so viel Elex, dass man gar nicht mehr weiß was man davon kaufen soll, womit wir schon beim nächsten Punkt wären..

7. Handel, "Crafting"
Beides nutzlos. Im Endeffekt habe ich lediglich Heiltränke oder Nahrungsmittel in diesem Spiel gekauft. Alles andere ist nutzloser Müll, den man angeboten bekommt. Das Spiel beinhaltet auch eine Art "Crafting", wobei diese "lite Version" schon fast gar nicht so bezeichnet werden kann. Ich bin jedenfalls gut ohne ausgekommen. Die Anleitungen die ich gefunden habe, haben bei mir keinen Drang ausgelöst den jeweiligen Gegenstand herzustellen. Auch hier war es meist unnützer Mist. Die einzigen Gegenstände, die ich hergestellt habe waren auch hier Lebensmittel und Tränke. Ansonsten kann man seine Skillpunkte getrost auf Schadensreduzierung/Schutz und Angriffsschaden vergeben (in dieser Reihenfolge!). Alles andere (auch Intelligenz und Gerissenheit) haben im Vergleich zu anderen Rollenspielen so gut wie keinen Einfluss auf den Verlauf des Spieles aus inhaltlicher Sicht und sind daher bei diesem grottigen Kampfsystem verschenkte Skillpunkte. Intelligenz und Gerissenheit machen die Dialoge von dem unfassbar dummen Helden auch nicht besser.

Insgesamt echt schade.. Hier wurde echt eine Chance vertan aus den guten Ansätzen ein klasse Rollenspiel zu bauen.
Immerhin hat es mich 45 Stunden beschäftigt wovon jedoch leider gut 1/3 Frust war.

Very broken and unbalanced game, just as I love open world RPGs.

Beginning is very challenging, but you can either play smart, avoid enemies, progress with quests instead of fighting until you're strong enough, or just cheese the game using some of the many ways to abuse combat.

Faction choice is also basically another difficulty system. Some are OP, some are poop.

Quick note: I have closer to 40h played (mostly offline hence wrong hour count), and finished the game. Also, first PB game, so no baggage carried over from Gothic etc. 

ELEX is one of those 'greater than the sum of its parts' things. There was a point in the first two hours of playing where I seriously considered refunding ELEX, which would have been a mistake. Yes combat is jank, no it's not difficult. Progression is iffy at best. Writing, dialogue, voice over... is there.  And yet I found myself always ready to go back... cause there is just one more hill to crest, or one more troll to kill. There is nothing funnier than juggling mutants or mechs with explosive plasma rounds. Conversely Alb flame troops can die in the fiery pits of that damned volcano. 

The world is really the star of the show with soooo daaaang muuuuuch to explore, and verticality that is fantastic. There are quite a few 'Throat of the World' moments in ELEX, just with jetpacks and pulse rifles (again, so good), and a lived in design to everything that they just nail. I spent more time hopping around than actually chasing quests. 

Quest design varies, with some being a bit better than others. It's more in how the game allows you to use your toolbox that elevate the quest system to an extent. Clerics 4 life! 

It's not as bad as some more critical opinions suggest, but it is also not as good as others tend to proclaim. Ultimately it's just fun. Rough, weirdly paced, oddly written fun. And we can all do with more fun.

After very much enjoying Greedfall despite its non-AAA implementations (such as copy-paste some buildings, mostly poor facial graphics, etc.) I figured I would try out Elex since it was on sale.  Risen 1 was so-so in my view but I liked Risen 2 and Risen 3.

I could not get into Elex.  The world and story seem okay but its non-AAA implementations make Greedfall look slick by comparison, and ultimately it didn't do anything for me, in contrast to Risen's pirate themes.  I remember Risen 2 and 3 having that non-AAA type of feel and I was fine with that, but Elex seems to have a whole lot more of that lack of polish, unless it's just my memory of Risen 2 and 3 being off.

I played Elex for 8 hours and there is a huge amount of dialog which would be fine if it was more than just okay and if there weren't so many discontinuities in dialogs so that dialogs simply don't make sense.  For me immersion can be broken when a dialog response is not in my view close to realistic to what someone would say in that situation, and this occurred very frequently in Elex in my view.

Combat would have been functional but in those 8 hours I was not able to obtain any decent weapon or armor (the story was progressing to that point, later) so I had to just run from most enemies, which is not fun gameplay to me.  I often had to get from A to B but simply couldn't compete with most of the enemies on the way there (I had it on normal difficulty).  Git good may seem like a valid response to me, but I have been playing many dozens of these types of RPGs and other similar games for decades and I don't think that git good is the issue here.

In my view the game is poorly designed in several areas including dialog and combat.

I very much doubt that I will ever purchase another Piranha Bytes game again, unless they git good in a future game (maybe Elex will be to their next game what Technomancer was to the ones who made Greedfall).  Their heart is in the right place, I think, but the designs are not.  I rarely write Steam reviews but this was a very disappointing game to me considering that I enjoyed Risen 2 and Risen 3.

This is just a very meh kind of game. Personally I don't like RPG's that force you to play as a certain character they create, I like to be able to create my own character to start out personally. So when a game forces you to play as a certain character I expect the character to be interesting and the character's story to be interesting to make up for this. This is very much not the case here, the story doesn't make much sense starting out and seems a bit too tropey to me. Though to be fair, someone might not have experienced these tropes I myself saw in the story, so it might be fresh for a few people there. The voice acting is like nails on a chalk board also. Like if you can't get get good voice acting for an RPG, it's fine to just have text for dialogue so not sure why it's done here. Visually it doesn't look too great and the people look a bit chunky faced, but it's also not the worst in this area. I just very much get the sense like I'm playing a game from 10-15 year ago myself.  I'll likely come back to this game later myself and try again as it's not too bad but just generally not great in a lot of areas. Got the sense I can probably chug my way through as I like RPG's. I would say this is the kind of game you only get if you run out of games of the genre to play, and probably best to only get it on deal.

Я начал прохождение ELEX, практически в момент его выхода, упоролся с нереального уровня сложности боёв, и забил.
Потом превозмог себя, и дошел аж до 2 главы, дико горя жопой, и затирая F5 и F9 до дыр (эти кнопки понадобятся вам больше, чем кнопка достать/убрать оружее, серьезно) После этого, я на игру снова забил. Персонаж остался воином (2 ранг берсерков) С говнолуком. На 21 уровне развития. 

Спустя еще какое-то время, от безделья, я решил зайти в игру снова, и начать с нуля, проходить игру за фракцию Клириков (слава Каалану вся фигня). Сразу понял, что нужно как можно быстрее получить топ оружее и броню, и полез в вики, смотреть, где что лежит. В итоге нашел подходящие пушки, и пошел их собирать. Первую, самую крутую, получить очень легко, подбежал, взял, убежал. Но есть маленькое НО. У неё такие требования, что мой персонаж не может ей пользоваться до сих пор (26 уровень, и куча элекс запоев примерно на 30к местных денег, только для того чтобы ходить в топ броне Клириков, и использовать ВТОРУЮ по крутости пушку в игре). Вторая пушка добывается с боем, и как я написал в скобочках, тоже требует нехилого кача, и отличается от первой, только уроном (разница в 6 едениц урона) и типом припасов (плазма вместо энергоячеек), ну еще и режимами стрельбы. В общем и целом после получения этой пушки, игра [b]СРАЗУ[/b] утратила смысл. Самые жесткие мобы, ложатся как дети, подойти к герою, не может никто. Даже рэйндж атаки гуманоидов с оружием, не представляют угрозы. Стало скучно. Инвентарь стал больше похож на портовый склад, деревня прокачана на весь возможный максимум. В общем стремиться стало не к чему. Но я решил закончить сюжет, как бы наградить себя за мучения, узнать, что да как в этом мире, откуда в нем такое количество туалетной бумаги, как она сохранилась за это время? В общем, получить ответы, на фундаментальные вопросы бытия. И вот, спустя 1 час после того, как я получил броню МК3, сдавая один сюжетный квест, я получил х*й в лицо. В конце очередного "флэшбэка" главного героя, случилось ничего. То есть совсем НИЧЕГО. Тёмный экран. И всё. Хотя можно было вызвать меню, ничего не происходило. Перезагрузка не помогла. Вторая тоже. Загруски с ранних сэйвов, тоже не помогли. В общем, всё, я пытался. Но эта игра САМА не хочет чтобы я её проходил. И я не буду. Да ну её. Может вам больше повезёт.

A large open world RPG, in a strange post-apocalyptic world caused by a comet with a strange substance in it (ELEX) crashing into the planet.

This was a hard one to rate as there is both good and bad, in the end I have to give it a pass as I don't think most people will like it and I didn't find it that rewarding.  The combat is very clunky, the dialog is pretty bad and the game is very hard in the beginning.  The biggest problem is the "difficulty".  It is by design, you are a weakling in the beginning and it takes a long time to become competent.  On top of that, once the story opens up a bit, there are creatures way above your level all over the place that will kill you with one hit.  I don't mind this design, but it would have felt better if there were fewer high level creatures around and there was some way to kind of know when you are somewhere out of your league (almost everywhere early).  Also quests give you no indication as to how hard they are, only trial and error will tell you if you can do one or not.  This makes the long beginning of the game (maybe up to level 10-20 depending on how you built your character) an un-fun slog.  Constantly running or sneaking by nearly everything you meet.  Just not fun and only those with very good patience will make it through.  If you persist though, you will eventually find the game actually ends up kind of easy in the late game.  The final boss was a joke and died in about 5 attacks, for instance.  So balance is also an issue here.

If that were the only issue, I would have rated it a "recommend" but the combat tries to be realistic with stamina requirements for melee attacks and dodging, limited quick slots, slower movement, weird under the hood rules for staggering and limitations on when you can switch weapons (i.e. not when jumping or using your jump pack).  You will get used to it, but it always feels unsatisfying and feels like you are fighting the controls more than just fluidly combating enemies ,especially when something unexpected happens.

Also the dialog / voice acting is just mostly horrible.  Stilted, dry and the actual choice of words used is sometimes very awkward.  I think this game was not native English, so maybe that is why.  I can't speak for the other languages, maybe the native language (German maybe?) is better.  Not the end of the world though, I've seen worse.

If you can get by those issues, the game has a unique setting, if maybe a bit too unique, some good character development, interesting quests and a slow developing but actually somewhat interesting story.  Graphics and sound are nothing to write home about but are good enough to not give you a headache or anything.

In the end, it was a game I finished but it was honestly a struggle up until I got to about level 20.  I had much more fun later in the game though.  It's rough, it's not pretty and everything just feels a bit off.  But like an ugly dog, it can still be something that some people will love.  Most should probably avoid it though.

Например можно толпу бандитов натравить на подобие тролля и он их красиво укладывает, подбегаем шмонаем их трупы и дальше шаримся по их лагерю, а можно найти гранаты и закидать всю толпу, это на 3 уровне, где даже крыса может отправить спать за несколько тычков. Даже при встречи с первым бандитом, рядом с мостом где лежит топор, можно его просто заманить на минное поле, а потом добить. Как и в первых Готиках тут можно страдать, а можно нагибать если умеючи. Gleich zu Beginn: Mir hat das Spiel sehr gut gefallen. Auf Piranha Bytes kann man sich einfach verlassen. Und selbst unter den durchweg starken Spielen sticht Elex hervor, auch wenn es meiner Meinung nach nicht ganz an die Klassiker Gothic I und II rankommt passt einfach vieles:
+ gute Spielmechanik (Bewegung, Kampf; teilweise einstellbar beim Schwierigkeitsgrad!)
+ ähnliches System zur Charakterentwicklung aber sehr gut angepasst. (Man ist Anfangs vielleicht ein bischen lange viel zu schwach)
+ fesselnde Story, interessante Dialoge
+ vielfältige Ausrüstungsmöglichkeiten
+ Fraktionensystem
+ nahezug Bugfrei (hat quasi keinen Einfluss auf das Spielerlebnis)
+ open World

Schade finde ich:
- es fehlen ein paar Daten zu den Charakterwerten (Leben, Schaden usw.), denn manchmal ist es etwas undurchsichtig, warum man jetzt wieviel Schaden macht. Das mag Absicht sein, aber es hätte mir viel googlen ersparrt.
- Das Zeitmanagement für die Spielphasen (Kapitel) ist nicht ausgewogen (sehr Earlygamelastig; vlt. ein bischen ZU "open World")
- einige Fähigkeiten sind quasi unbrauchbar und andere fast schon notwendig. (hier ein bischen balancen)
- zu wenig interessante Fraktionsfähigkeiten
- Nahkampf und Fernkampf müssen nach meiner Meinung gebalanced werden (in vielerlei Hinsicht)
- Auto-Fokus hat mich anfangs häufiger das Leben gekostet; es nimmt was vom freien Spielerlebnis und es als Anfänger-Modus zu verkaufen finde ich fragwürdig. Vlt, wenn man mit der Konsole spielt.

Fazit: Das Spiel macht echt Laune. Habs gerade erst gespielt und bin jetzt schon auf Elex-Entzug. Ein Story-Addon oder Nachfolger mit gleicher/ähnlicher Grafik und leicht angepassten/erweiterten Charaktermöglichkeiten würde wahrscheinlich nochmal einschlagen. Die genannten negativen Punkte sind absolut vernachlässigbar und/oder umspielbar.

Elex is a classic RPG similar to Bethesda games, but with a different engine and new ideas.

Pros:

- The graphics are quite good and fluid, the game seems to run at 60 FPS on my GTX 1050 Ti.

- Despite taking a lot from Fallout and Gothic (by the same dev) Elex still manages to be interesting due to the somewhat odd combo of Fantasy and Sci Fi

- The game is very difficult and has a lot of complexity, with a refreshingly simple UI.

- The lore is kind of empty, although I've only played for about 1 and 1/2 hour so it could be expanded upon later in the game. 

Cons:

- The game's combat is hard to use and locked on targets are easy to miss, just like in Gothic.

- Some of the factions are derived from Fallout, in particular the Clerics who want to preserve all technology (Brotherhood Of Steel) and the Outlaws (Raiders).

- The developers hardly used the vibration feature, so even when its turned on its not used in most instances where it should be and is weak on the few occasions it is.

Overall, I feel like Elex is a breath of fresh air for me and I will continue to play it

I wanted to write a review for this game because it's got Mixed currently, and I don't think it deserves a large amount of the negative reviews. First of all, you have to have patience to play this game. If you have played Risen, Gothic, Kingdoms of Amalur or maybe Divinity II you get the idea. This is a kinda-janky slow burn game that you simply have to sink a lot of time into if you really want to enjoy what it offers. What I liked about this game compared to some other similar 3d RPGs is that it has a sci fi setting. 

The only really negative thing I can say is I don't think anyone enjoys being a plain bald grunt guy, and I wish this game had character creation, but I didn't expect it to since Risen and Gothic did not. 

Overall this game is a timesink, and a pretty slow RPG in general... but it's also pretty difficult. So, if you buy it expecting something short and easy you will be disappointed. If not, I think this is a pretty entertaining alternative to something like Mass Effect or Fallout.

Насыпали в Готику роботов и Mad Max, перемешали, получилась ELEX  с топорной анимацией, подергиванием персонажа, женщинами на одно лицо, никакой вариативностью персонажа (тебе дают стокового мужика, и ничего не изменить, хотя в игре есть романтические отношения).

Ich kann jeden Verstehen, der das Spiel nicht mag. Es hat ne Menge Macken, aber wenn man Gothic/Risen mochte, kennt man diese Macken schon und weiß was man im Gegenzug dafür geboten bekommt. An sich ist Elex eine klassische Piranha Bytes-Erfahrung, aber 2 neu Facetten haben mich mehr als Überzeugt. Zum einen haben sie eine open World geschaffen, die zu erkunden mehr Spaß macht als die Exploration in Skyrim. Ich bin stundenlang durch die Welt gezogen und hab jeden einzelnen Winkel abgesucht, weil es überall was zu entdecken gibt. Es gibt wirklich atemberaubende Locations. Auch haben sie sich sehr viel Mühe gegeben die Welt mit mehr Lore zu füllen als ihre Vorgänger. Das alles macht die Open World zu einem wahren Genuss.
Und zum anderen haben die Entwickler sich dieses mal mehr mit Entscheidungen und Konsequenzen beschäftigt und das gibt diesem Game eine unheimliche Tiefe. Zwar hätten es etwas drastischere Konsequenzen an manchen Stellen schon seien können, aber trotzdem saß ich manchmal vorm PC und musste Minuten lang grübeln wie ich mich entscheide. Hinzukommen Skillchecks, die eine mehr als willkommene Erweiterung zum alten Formular der Piranha Bytes Games darstellt. Alleine mit diesen 2 Aspekten hatte mich das Game schon überzeugt. 

Aber das ist ja noch nicht alles was es zum Game zu sagen gibt. Charackterprogression ist in diesem Game wirklich arbeit, aber zahlt sich aus mit einem Characktersystem, das im Laufe des Spiels seine Tiefe erst preisgibt. Seinen Charackter weiter zu entwickeln macht in wenigen Spiel so viel Spaß wie hier und man hat ne Menge Freiheiten. 
Die Story war wirklich sehr spannend, auch wenn der ganzen Sache etwas mehr Komplexität gut getan hätte. Etwas mehr Hintergrundinformationen, ein paar mehr spannende Akteure innerhalb der Story hätten aus dieser wirklich guten Story eine fantastische gemacht. Auch die Albs hätten etwas mehr Vielschichtigkeit vertragen. Aber wie gesagt, beschweren kann man sich in dem Punkt nicht wirklich. Was aber wirklich ein Höhepunkt des Games ist, sind seine Fraktionen. Die sind so genial gestaltet und durchdacht. Alle Fraktionen sind auf ihre Weise bekloppt, haben auf der anderen Seite aber eine nachvollziehbare Agenda. Es ist wirklich schwer sich für eine Fraktion zu entscheiden weil jede davon auf ihre eigene Weise was cooles hat.

Jetzt zum Hauptmanko der meisten Kritiker: Das Kampfsystem. Ich muss sagen ich hatte eine Menge Spaß damit, aber ich hab nach ein paar Versuchen mit dem Nahkampf aufgegeben  und mich für Fernkampf entschieden. In Kombi mit Jetpack, Dodge und Spezialfähigkeiten meiner Fraktion war das eine klasse Mischung aus Action, Taktik und Reaktion. Bis zum Ende hat es einfach Spaß gemacht. Wie gesagt, ich hab mich mit dem Nahkampf nicht lange auseinander gesetzt weil es mir einfach keinen Spaß gemacht hat, deshalb kann ich dazu nichts sagen, aber der Fernkampf war klasse. Warum sich bei diesem Game so viele über das Kampfsystem aufregen aber Skyrim mit seinem mehr als langweiligen System das nur aus blocken und zuschlagen besteht, ohne Taktik, ohne Reaktion und ohne dass etwas Skill vom Spieler verlangt wird, in den Himmel gelobt wird muss mir erst mal einer erklären. 
Die einzige wirkliche Kritik die ich am Game hab sind die Bugs. Eine Quest konnte ich nicht abschließen und immer wieder muss ich im Kampf meine Waffe wegstecken und wieder ziehen damit ich weiter schießen kann. Aber einem Open World Game das von 30 Menschen entwickelt wurde kann ich das verzeihen. 

Fazit: Ich habe es geliebt. Ein mit Herzblut entwickeltes RPG das seine Macken hat, aber wenn man über diese hinweg sieht offenbart sich ein geheimer Juwel der Rollenspielgeschichte. Es hat die Qualitäten eines Gothics und mehr muss man nicht sagen. Klare Kaufempfehlung wenn man Gothic mochte.

Hab das Spiel nach Lesen der negativen Kommentare gekauft, denn es ist von der Mechanik ähnlich Gothic 2, was ich liebe weil: 

Du nicht gleich der Große mächtige Held bist der SOO toll ist,
und der sich einfach nur doof durchklicken oder die richtigen Skillkombis mithilfe von Lösungen aus dem Internet beschaft um alle 10.000 Gegner die einem permanent in den Weg laufen niedermetztelt. 
Nein, hier muss man erst mal lernen welcher Gegner wie angreift, muss auch etwas Feinmechanik und Hirn beim Klicken und Tasten drücken an den Tag legen, wenn man denn schon stark genug ist, was mich zum nächsten Punkt bringt:
In einer bösen gefährlichen Welt gibt es doch tatsächlich viele böse gefährliche Gegner, die einen schlecht Ausgestatteten verwirrten Typen ohne Plan, also Mich, ganz schnell töten können. Ich kann nicht einfach wie ein kleiner Junge jeden bösen Typen der mit mir redet nur weil er mir nicht gefällt und wahrscheinlich "böse" ist mal eben töten und linear mit metzteln weitermachen. 

Es plopt nicht irgendwo gleich ein Questfenster auf und sagt mir in großen Lettern was ich tun soll wenn ich nicht weiter weiß. 

Auf der virtuellen Karte sehe ich nicht gleich alle Gegner oder NPC's weil ich GPS Spionagefähigkeiten wie die CIA habe. 

Quests werden einem nicht mundgerecht verabreicht so dass jeder idiot weiß was zu tun ist und der nötige IQ damit um das Spieß zu spielen nicht höher als ein Stein sein muss. Ich muss hier doch tatsächlich nachdenken was zu tun ist. 

Die Orientierung ist manchmal schwer, es macht also tatsächlich sinn zuzuhören was NPCs sagen und zu veruchen ihre Beschreibungen zu verwenden. 

All das und noch mehr, macht das Spiel schwer, es macht es umständlich, es macht es mühsam, und am Ende so unendlich befriedigend wenn man endlich ein gute Rüstung hat, eine gute Waffe, ein toller Diebstahl gelungen ist, man Anerkennung und Presitge hart und geistreich erkämpft hat, etc. Die andern Charaktere fühlen sich gleichwertiger an, und man selbst sich nicht so abgehoben und losgelöst davon, weil man ohne sie zu attakieren nicht weiß wie stark sie sind, und oft sind sie unerwartet stark. Das macht sie ernst zu nehmend, man fühlt sich nicht wie der überhebliche Held der über alles hinwegfegt sondern wie ein Teil einer Welt in der man selbst Grenzen hat, die man langsam erweitern kann. Das alles macht Elix für gamer wie mich zu einem genialen Spiel von deren Sorte ich mehr haben will, während es für andere nichts ist.

Hab ich gekauft und direkt wieder zurück gegeben.
Die Texturen sind einfach nur gruselig.

A tentative recommendation from me.
The Risen games are better so I'd recommend you play them instead if you haven't already.  Experiencing them will also give you an insight into how much jank these games have and prepare you for this one as the jank is very heavy with this one..
A solid 40+ hour adventure awaits you if you want to do pretty much everything and every quest at the difficult setting (2nd hardest out of 4).  The story is good if not always conveyed through well written dialogue, but the story beats roll out at a steady clip that keeps you interested.  Voice acting for most part is fine.  Graphics also are fine.
The RPG elements regarding shaping your character are so-so.  You level up through gaining experience.  This lets you level up your stats, and this in turn allows you then to buy training in different abilities from trainers with gold provided you meet the stat requirements.  That's it.  Most abilities were pretty much useless however and I didn't realise notice a tangible difference as I leveled up my stats.
The biggest issue this game has is combat.  It is beyond woeful.  I avoided it as much as possible and just ran away from enemies wherever I could.  I think the developers knew it was rubbish, so they've made it so combat gives you very little experience compared to quests, to emphasise that combat is not why you're here for.
The saving grace was the interesting world and nonstop swirl of quests that kept me going.  Worthwhile picking up on sale if you fancy a sci-fi fantasy romp in an original universe, just don't expect it to be the best game ever.

I hate to bash on this game, because i *do* enjoy it, but the initial difficulty is far too great when you're learning how to play a new game.  Starting equipment and skills are far inferior to the enemies you'll encounter and missions often require you to cover great distances to avoid conflict to reach your destination.  Any fight that's not 1-on-1 it's basically hopeless and even then it'll take 4 times the hits for you to fell an enemy than it will for them to best you (roughly 20 strikes for, 4-5 against).  I've logged more than 40 hours (just now reaching level 17!?) and I'm finally getting to the point where my attributes are high enough to use the decent equipment I acquired 10 levels ago.

If you have the patience to cope, then you'll probably enjoy the game, too.  There is a lot of area to explore, plenty of which offers some rewards, often small, for your efforts.  

Now that I can hold my own in a greater variety of situations, I'm looking forward to continuing the adventure.  But if I hadn't read other reviews before picking this game up, I would have been greatly disappointed, and likely would have given up long before now.  If you're up for a challenge, give it a go, but I can't rightly say I recommend this game to everyone.

PS, If you decide to put in your time, get a shield as soon as you can.  You don't have the stamina to dodge every enemy attack.

Всё таки на дворе 2019ый, а мы продолжаем делать продукт для своих. Ну такое себе..
Короче, после Ведьмаков и Тёмных Душ пришлось вспоминать, каково это - быть игроком в готик-лайк.

Впрочем, общие приёмы остались без изменений. Пираньи крайне консервативны в этом плане.
Формула успеха проста и неизменна от игры к игре:
1.) Любыми способами подсосать первые 8-10 уровней, попутно вытирая зудящую задницу и больной рот. Напоминаю, умирать ГГ будет много, часто, крайне быстро и с удовольствием;
2.) До 2 главы обирать все дома на планете до последней кружки, продавать весь мусор торговцам, шантажировать и канючить у NPC максимально возможное кол-во денег;
3.) Как можно быстрее раздобыть снаряжение: броню, бижутерию, оружие и базовые расходники. По возможности опробовать все типы оружия и выбрать свой;
4.) Т.к. в стороне остаться всё равно не получится, крайне желательно сразу определиться с группировкой, с которой будет пройдена игра - это позволит сильно облегчить себе первые 3 пункта;
5.) Очень, ОЧЕНЬ хорошо драться.
Или прятаться за спинами напарников, пока они танчат и попутно режут мобов;

Выполнив хотя бы 2-3 пункта, игра пойдёт гораздо легче и вы сможете уже адекватно воспринимать происходящее вокруг.
Сюжет неплох, очень порадовали отсылки на мой любимый Масс Эффект на протяжении всей игры. Даже миссии на лояльность напарников завезли :)
Больше всего понравилось поэтапное погружение в мир Магалана.
ГГ предстоит побывать во всех ключевых городах и регионах планеты. Познакомиться с десятками самых известных и значимых (и не очень) личностей. Выполнить 300+ квестов. Собрать команду из максимально разноплановых персонажей со своими убеждениями и загонами. Стать губернатором мирной деревеньки. Построить семью и посадить 
свой Элекс. Ну и познать себя, разумеется.

Диалоги прекрасны, и чем дальше заходит сюжет, тем интереснее в них вникать.
Ничего выдающегося, они просто качественно прописаны и весьма неплохо озвучены. Чувствуется, что актёры выкладывались как могли. Увы, сказывается небольшой бюджет, поэтому актёры озвучки иногда дублируют роли.

Эта игра НЕ понравится:
а.) любителям качественной боёвки;
Здесь она такая же кривая, как и в любой игре студии. Даже стрельба далека от идеала, и это действительно печально.
б.) любителям крафта;
Он скучен и не логичен, инвентарь через пару-тройку десятков часов будет нещадно загажен. Можно (и нужно) было сохранить крафт из Risen и Г1-Г2.
Запредельное кол-во ресурсов игроку просто не понадобится, учитывая чёткое деление фракций по приоритету оружия, которое грейдится строго по своим чертежам и материалам.
в.) любителям билдов;
Резета в игре нет. Неправильно прокачали хар-ки - начинаем заново. Вложились в бесполезные навыки (а их тут достаточно) - начинаем заново. Не подумали о последствиях своего базара, профукав важного NPC - начинаем заново.
Хардкор, как в старые добрые.
г.) манчкинам;
Т.к. Elex это не TES, то стать главой всех гильдий, фракций и поселений не получится - РеализмЪ.
Зато можно прокачать все навыки, если знатно упороться по гринду. Благо мобы научились респиться.
д.) любителям фентези от Пираний;
Микс стилей в Elex ещё на стадии анонса наделал шуму похлеще пиратской тематики в Risen 2-3. Что уж говорить, я и сам был весьма скептично настроен - никто в здравом уме не представлял, как вместе будут смотреться высокотехнологичные гаджеты и средневековые щиты, лазерные (плазменные) стволы и луки с арбалетами, керамические и железные доспехи.
Мне понравился получившийся компот и я до сих пор не понимаю, почему никто не пытался сделать так раньше - как по мне, получился просто великолепный стиль и весьма гармоничный геймдизайн.
Заходя в деревни Берсерков можно словить неиллюзорные флешбеки с прошлых игр студии. Оказавшись в столице Клириков можно надолго залипнуть на футуристичный дизайн их домов, неоновые вывески, стильную униформу членов фракции и патрулирующих улицы роботов. Родина Изгоев - типичный Безумный Макс, только без корчей и бензака. Атмосфера в каждом регионе, от душистых лесов до знойных пустынь - запредельная.

К своему удивлению, я довольно быстро проникся игрой как только решил проблемы со снарягой и деньгами. Чем дальше, тем интереснее и легче становилось играть.
Лично я считаю Elex достойным стартом для новой вселенной и искренне надеюсь на увеличение бюжета для будущих проектов студии.

Тем не менее, это определённо последний проект грехи которого можно, так или иначе, простить разработчикам - ещё раз подобная продукция на фоне конкурентов будет смотреться нишевым и невзрачным инди, не более того.

P.S. Брал по скидке за ~500 рублей, полностью отбил по эмоциям. Чего и Вам желаю :)

I'd give it a "mixed" if that was possible... The game's movement, combat and damage system are terribly "rough" - but nevertheless I find the game charming in the end.

The first 10-ish hours of the game are quite painful and it feels like they wanted you to dislike the game. I enjoyed the gothic series and the "fair" difficulty in gothic2 NOTR, but ELEX takes it too far combined with an extremely annoying movement system and extremely bugged hitboxes: I got hit THROUGH A WALL by a melee monster and died in one hit. WTF. At least quick save/load is fast. You can "dodge" roll, but you will still be hit as the character's hitbox is WAY too big, unless you factor the faulty hitbox in and stay at ridiculous ranges from enemies.

The first few hours are extremely painful as you have to run from pretty much any enemy. After several hours combat changes to kiting around enemies while your companion takes them out (he and you still get one shot by medium sized stuff but he "revives" after a few seconds...so...yay). After a while you go from pathetically weak to pretty overpowered all of a sudden, because of the way damage is computed (final damage = incoming damage - armor, or 0), which causes your effective damage to suddenly spike in a big way if you find a better weapon and upgrade it.

If you found this review, you are one step closer to discovering a hidden gem of a game. I was just like you when I stumbled into ELEX and looked for reviews to figure what this game was about. 

If you not a sci-fi fan, this game may not be for you. It takes place in a post apocalyptic environment on the planet of Magalan after a comet destroyed civilization as we now know it.

The remains of the human race scattered across the planet, each surviving utilizing different means. Four factions were created and they all fought over one resource, Elex. The limited resource was left by the comet. It empowered technology and allowed for advanced weapons, it could be refined and turned into mana to use for spell casting, or it could be consumed raw to gain strength but at the cost of emotion, the definition of what it means to be human. 

In a third person single player adventure you take on the role of Jax, an Alb survivor whose glider was shot out of the sky to discover who attempted to kill him and how it all comes together in a grand scheme of things.

Similar to Skyrim and many other RPG games, you travel the world to discover new factions and quests and start to piece everything together little by little. You interact with the world and the NPCs in it. There is a lot to discover. A lot to learn. Your character is customizable with weapons, armor, perks, attributes, etc. 

As you seek to survive in the harsh world infested with a million things that help you die you must make decisions on which factions to back and where to invest your trust and faith. The berserkers are a group of individuals who banned technology. They are attempting to heal the planet after the comet strike. Their lands are filled with green leafy jungles and life. They hope to bring back the planet as it was before the cataclysm. Berserkers utilize medieval style weaponry and leather armors to defend themselves.

The outlaws are a group of western cowboys residing in the desert. They steal, salvage, and kill to turn a profit. They don't make good friends, but can make good business partners if you like a little profit. One rule. No rules. Just don't ♥♥♥♥ with their big boss. Outlaws use various drugs (chems) to enhance their abilities and prefer to use standard ballistic weapons and grenades to get the job done.

The clerics are a group of advanced religious zealots who believe in the God Calaan and hoard all the technology they can get their hands on. They have an army of advanced robots and AI to assist them. They are all fancy with their advanced armors and laser and plasma weaponry. Out of the three joinable factions they are by far the strongest. Perk of joining, mind control.

The final faction and unfortunately not joinable are Albs. They used to be Clerics who consumed raw Elex and lost all emotion. They serve the one they call the Hybrid and gather Elex from the remnants of the comet to feed it to him. Needless to say, they are super strong, cunning, and technologically savvy. 

Your character, Jax, is actually an Alb who is wanted dead by his own people. Being alone and cut off from his Elex supply he must overcome getting to experience emotions again as you make player decisions that will shape what kind of a character he will be. Do you stay the cold and rational Alb? Do you become a trigger happy junkie who is consumed by his own agenda? Up to you.

Good story line. Good characters. Good world to explore. Good times.

There are some negatives however. The combat feels a bit clunky. Ranged combat is easier with melee combat being a bit hit or miss. The lock-on system is not the best and brightest and it may be a bit getting used to. Personally, I did not much care for it. Even hated it starting out until I figured it out and it grew on me a little bit. You have to figure out rolling away from attacks and timing parries and knowing when to utilize your handy jet pack to be successful. 

Another good mention, the leveling may seem a bit off in the mid-game. Enemies feel like they scale quicker than the player and may become difficult to handle. The response to that is grinding out better weapons, gear, perks, etc to handle them. There are some enemies in areas that are best avoided until later in the game. Not all areas are safe to explore. Watch for those predators until you are truly prepared to venture fourth. 

Other than the melee combat this game is easy to get into and fun to continue playing. Give it a spin. It may surprise you.

Despite the negative reviews about mechanics, and my own technical issues (detailed below), I found this game to be quite enjoyable.  It certainly has its flaws in AI, particularly as it relates to companions, but the combat system itself is fine if you don't button-mash. You'll need to manage stamina, study your enemies, and time your attacks.  

Jax feels incredibly slow in combat for a while, but eventually you'll be able to dodge almost every attack thrown at you.  Maybe every attack, if you're better than me.  More importantly, Jax feels incredibly weak when you first start the game.  Many player complaints stem from this fact:  Jax IS weak.  He's supposed to be.  That's kinda the whole idea of the game; to start from nothing and evolve until you're basically unstoppable. The first enemies you encounter can actually kill you. Just don't let them.

The early hours of the game will involve far more running than combat. Non-violent quests and exploration are your friends.  Maybe some light thieving, if you're into that sort of thing. You should have no trouble outrunning most enemies even with the meager starting stamina, so feel free to rack up easy xp by exploring some of the map.  There are only a few locations I can think of where quest outcomes are automatically decided if you aren't prepared for combat, but they're pretty far from the starting zone. 

Companions are incredibly powerful early on, and will give quite a boost when you unlock them. Unfortunately, they do drop off pretty dramatically regardless of which weapon set they randomly generate.  Which is another strange choice.  Companions generate a random weapon set when you encounter them, and that's what they will use for the entire game.  It is possible to end up with a severely gimped sidekick, and subsequently bench them for the entire game.  Other players have reported being able to reload just before meeting until they get the set they want, but I didn't read that until after I'd met all of mine.  Still, companions can sometimes offer interesting or humorous input during quests or even when just exploring.  

 It feels like some things in the game may have been lost in translation, but that isn't so bad if you go into the experience with the mindset that things have literally been translated in order for non-German-speaking folk like me to enjoy it.  The different factions, though somewhat oddly named (See 'translated'), have very distinct personalities.  I had a difficult time deciding which faction to join, because all of them have some pretty compelling pros and cons. There will probably be things you like about each faction, things you can tolerate, and things you absolutely can't stand.  For me, that made them feel a bit more real.  Absolutely no one in this game is perfect, and that's kinda perfect.  

  Unfortunately, many players run into the issue of the game randomly deciding to crash and never reopen.  For me, it was after around 30 hours of gameplay, when I was well invested in the story and looking forward to building my character juust right.  Some players managed to get it working again with an exhaustive list of troubleshooting tips. Here's what I tried:

Verifying game files
Removing steam overlay
Removing windows overlay
Unplugging any irrelevant devices
Updating drivers
Regressing drivers
Re-downloading Visual C++ Redistributable
Uninstalling and reinstalling ELEX
Praying to every deity I could think of
Looking up new deities to pray to

Nothing worked. Until...

Edit:  I don't know what changed, but I decided to try loading the game again today after work, thinking "Wouldn't it be funny if, after two days of trying without success, it just suddenly worked without any further effort or explanation?"  And it actually was kinda funny.  

Edit 2:  After completing nearly every available quest, I've decided to give this game a positive review.  While it did have some very frustrating technical difficulties, the end result was still well worth the price point (particularly if purchased on sale). I've added a few more details to the original review to help people make a decision.

Normally I don't like to review a product before having at least 50% of the game completed, but this one is something special. I'm usually cold and unbiased in reviews, but I don't even have to be for this one since the good and bad are so clear:

Just to be clear, I'm looking solely at the playability of the game as an RPG in general. This game apparently fits perfectly into the little cult following the developer has but I don't understand what that's about so I'm not going to open my mouth about it.

Combat - 1/10
Exploration - 7/10
Character Development - 4/10
Plot - 8/10
Voice Acting - 5/10

The developers are clearly designers and not engineers, this is one of the most beautiful games I've ever played. The scenery and characters and even most of the items are maticulously crafted and everything is perfect. But then there's the gameplay. 

This game has some of the absolute worst gameplay mechanics (on the coding side) that I've ever seen. Everything is stable, but during combat it feels like the game simply ignores commands because it has to finish the previous action first. Exploring is a nightmare because the fall height is stupidly low for a game. Interactions and character developement are disgraceful. 

But the plot and storyline are inspired. This one truly has me torn. 

Overall I'm going to recommend everyone give it a chance. I'll explain each point in greater detail now:

******SPOILERS****** Nothing plot related, but some of the points I'll touch on do give away a lot of the feel of the game.

1. Combat - At low levels you should just run away. There are maybe 2 zones with creatures you can beat and even then it's tough. These developers pretty much said **** it when it came to level balancing. And while that lends to the immersion, it costs massive points as far as playability. When you do find something at your own level you still have to contend with the worst mechanics I've ever seen implemented in a full price game. We're talking 3 attack choices, blocky animations that have to finish before the next command can be recognized (Unless you trigger a combo, then they stack without you realizing), commands that get ignored entirely, and a health regen system that requires you to escape your foe to heal. And what do you gain for all of this frustration and constant save/load? Not much. Combat is a terrible source of exp and the items are useless. Total shit on combat score. 1/10

2. This is a gorgeous game to explore, which really sucks because it's the most frustrating part of the game. Fall damage is rediculously high and starts at far too realistic of a height for a video game. Maybe that's what you're looking for, then you're fine. But then you have the completely unbalanced encounter system out there to deal with. Level 3? Cool, heres a level 11 Troll that'll one shot you before you even learned to dodge. Finally get that item/goal/kill you were working on so hard? Hope you were saving every 10 seconds because Velociraptor eating your face!!! Btw, they should change the name of quick save to just as f****** long save as normal save cuz it's total B***s*** and why won't the B button exit that stupid menu? On that note we'll leave exploration with a 7/10 because as frustrating as it is, it's f****** beautiful and insanely detailed. 

3. Character developement is deceptive here. At first you're like "Oh s***, I get 10 points to put wherever I want each level? Heck yeah!". But you quickly realize that levels are tough to gain and then past 32 (not 30, 32 for some reason) each stat starts taking 2 points. Now there are some really useful skills available too.... later. You won't get any of them until at least level 5. Not because they unlock then, but because they require such stupidly high stats (many require 2 stats to be above 40 something for the first level) to aquire. Now for the real kick in the little boys, you NEED these skills to succesfully complete certain quests you already have. Without them you can technically proceed, but it's highly railroaded and not at all desirable outcomes. This all lends challenge to the game, that much is sure, but it also makes you feel hopeless in the beginning. I only stuck around to see if it picks up speed and to continue exploring the world. So far I haven't gotten far enough to comment on whether it does ever pick up speed or not. This section gets an abysmal 4/10, and only so high because you can still adapt to it and play the game.

4. The plot is fantastic so far. So far it's coherent, deep, and well implemented. The characters are deep and they invite you into the world. The immersion is there, it's just not polished. What I mean is the script they gave to the voice actors. The actors must've been locked in a booth with no interaction between each other, the inflections are wrong in so many sentences it makes you wonder if they knew what was going on. Also, several of the lines feel like run on sentences, stating the same thing over and over just in different ways. Especially the first guy you get to talk to... great first impression to the game guys. As far as the review goes this is really two sections, with plot so far getting a solid 8/10 but voice acting getting a generous 5/10.

Do you enjoy getting legitimately "1-hit" on easy mode? Perhaps getting attacked by a small horde of wild animals that run at you like Amy Schumer runs towards a dessert buffet? Feeling like you're re-enacting a scene out of 28 Days Later because the moment one of them reaches you, you die. 

ELEX is a great running simulator if you're willing to put the hours into holding W and praying nothing reaches you. Your trusty and clunky jetpack flies in the face of danger directly up with no real forward movement. Ensuring your death to the animals you've just let catch up to you, waiting for you to fall and instantly kill you.

How do you fight? You may ask. Simple. You legitimately cannot fight monsters until you reach a high enough level.
How do you get a higher level? You may ask. Simple. Run and complete quests. 
What if the quest makes you need to kill monsters? You may ask. Simple. Find a new quest.
The game cant be that hard. You might say. I have fired 20 arrows in a single creature. ON EASY. and it wasn't even close to dying. Instead all I managed to do, was create a pissed off hedgehog.
Whats the point of getting an axe at the start of the game if you cant use it? You might have the absurdity to ask. Simple. Its to openly laugh at you while you try to think this game is fair. The secret is, The game isn't fair. Its broken. And the only people enjoying the game are the ones who are experiencing stockholm syndrome due to the sheer hours they put in before they got to even think they can play the game and have fun.

Seriously do not buy this if you have High Blood Pressure or you're trying to reduce stress in your life. Its not worth the 15 hours of running to maybe think about actually fighting monsters on EASY.

Update 17-10-19: после прохождения игры несколько поменял свое мнение.
+ вручную созданный открытый мир;
+ встречаются интересные задания и персонажи, некоторые решения имеют неожиданные последствия;
+достаточно интересный сеттинг;
+приемлемая графика без тормозов.
- самый главный для меня минус, убивший все удовольствие от игры - просто убогая боевая система вкупе с весьма высокой сложностью даже на Easy. В Готике 3 и Risen 2-3 по крайней мере не приходилось страдать из-за высокой сложности, а в Готике 1,2 и Risen 1 боевка была намного лучше.
-новая ролевая система. Я просто ее не понимаю - почему нет экрана статистики персонажа, почему любой из профильных учителей может обучать сразу все навыкам группы, зачем требовать такие высокие статы, что достичь их можно только упившись элексовых зелий и др.
-скучный лут. В большинстве локаций вы будете находить металлический и электронный хлам, сигареты и элекс. Даже обычное оружие встречается очень редко. Уникальные же экземпляры часто проигрывают обычным улучшенным "пушкам".
-непроработаный мир. Почему спустя много лет после падения кометы все еще работает старая техника и не испортились сигареты? Как клирики так развили свои технологии, учитывая намного более низкий уровень развития цивилизации до катастрофы и свою малочисленность? Зачем у клириков обучают воздействию на разум, если это используется буквально в паре квестов? И многие другие вопросы...

В итоге: если вам понравится/устроит боевая система и высокая сложность, то можете попробовать эту игру. Я же лично все равно ее не рекомендую.

To say Elex has blown away my expectations is a severe understatement. I've had it on my wishlist since it came out. Negative reviews seemed to be valid at the time so I stayed away from it, a massive backlog of games I still haven't beat didn't help, but when Elex went on sale it was too tempting...I bought it after watching one of my favorite youtuber's review on it, even though the review initially still left me on the fence. I'm glad I took the plunge because Elex has been VERY good, and the price I paid for it is borderline criminal. 

I played Elex for almost 7 hours straight. which I haven't done in years. It's a mix of Fallout, Gothic/Risen (same devs), Skyrim, and reminds me of Mass Effect because there's a lot of NPC conversation that often has more than one response to choose from and those actions and responses can sometimes have an effect on the quest or the entire storyline. I have had to remind myself more than once that this is a sci-fi, post apocalpytic game, not medieval fantasy, but the first area of the game and the NPCs that belong to it, have you second guessing, which was cool to see. The devs have done a terrific job mixing sci-fi with fantasy unlike I've seen in any other game that I can think of.

I haven't experienced any major bugs, only a few minor ones, mostly related to grass texture pop in, nothing that has really bothered me. For those who aren't fans of the combat, I didn't think I was going to be either but it's really grown on me. Anyone who hasn't played Gothic or Risen games, the combat is slower making it more strategic than your average ARPG. You really have to think about each input selection instead of wild button mashing. It's not input lag, it's intended, and you'll see that when your moves are timed successfully, the combat flows very well. Do not button mash, or it will confuse you and it will look like input lag, but it's not, think of it as the game punishing you for mashing buttons. I'm not huge on the combat but it's enjoyable and works when you know what you're doing.

For melee, you press either the quick or strong attack button, the animation will perform, you wait until the animation is done before pressing another attack button. If your timing is successful, you'll quickly fill the combo gauge, once full you can unleash a special attack. Quick attack almost performs as fast as other ARPGs, the strong is a bit slower/the animation a bit more drawn out. The combat is all about timing, combos, blocking, rolling/dodging, all while managing your Dark Souls-esque stamina gauge. Range combat plays just like any other game, ranged combat is not slowed down by any means. I can actually fire arrows very quickly with my bow. I haven't obtained guns nor crossbow yet.

So far I rrrreeeaaaaallllllyy like Elex, i've had a lot of fun exploring, talking to the quest givers who keep me engaged, instead of skipping what they say like I do in most games, combat is challenging and I appreciate it not being another button masher, very refreshing, the map is massive with some serious verticality, which most open worlds lack. You have a jetpack which makes traversing the world fun as hell. I even use it to run away from tougher enemies. Jump on top of a building instead of getting gang banged by 5+ mutants. There are some mighty hefty TROLLS in this game, need I say more? 

There's different factions you can belong too as well with all of them at odds with each other. I also love that you distribute attribute points when you level up., because I've been craving that old school type of progression. Weapons and learning skills have attribute requirements besides that skills cost money and require finding a trainer (there's several). There's crafting but in my 11 hours so far, I haven't unlocked that skill as I'm investing my attribute points in making a melee/tank build, but I've been putting a few points in Dex as well, because a lot of melee weapons require it alongside strength, but there's tons of guns in this game so I'm anticipating getting one of those soon. There's also magic in this game that I haven't unlocked yet.

I'd pay near full price for this game based on what I've experienced so far, at it's current sale price, no question, I recommend it! Just know that you're getting an old school type of rpg with slower, thoughtful combat, not a button mashing loot-a-thon and you'll be doing easier quests for quite some time before you can handle most enemies, there's a grind but just like with any other game, grind is not a bad thing in a game that you're having fun with. 

If you're not digging the melee combat you can invest skill points that increase stamina, which improves it a great deal, or just go ranged, you get a bow pretty much right off the bat. A lot of the negative reviews did not give this game enough time, 1 or 2 hours is nothing in this game, you don't get past the first town's dialog in that time. Of course being open world you can go where you want, but you're weak as a piss-ant starting out.

Absolutes muss für alle Fans der alten Gothic teile, die Grafik entspricht natürlich nicht dem "Witcher Standart" den man kennt, aber der Charme der Gothic und Risen Reihe kommt hier definitiv durch, das Gameplay ist sehr ähnlich aufgebaut. Probiere was du willst und mache es dir wie es dir gefällt. Alles ist erlaubt und man kann die Welt nutzbar machen wie man sie braucht.

Besonders gut gefällt mir das Element, dass das Spiel scheinbar sehr schwer erscheint am Anfang, man läuft los und begegnet direkt Gegnern, die man nicht mal eben mit einem Schlag töten kann. Sondern man muss sich eine Taktik überlegen oder eventuell einfach später wieder kommen, wenn man sich verbessert hat, ob mit Fähigkeiten oder Items.

Pro:
- Gothic/Risen Elemente wiedererkennbar
- Gute Story
- Schönes Setting

Хотя, должен признать, поначалу я оставил ей даже отрицательный отзыв: уж очень она похожа на предыдущие игры этой компании (Готику и Risen). К тому же примерно до 15 уровня персонажа игру была для меня довольно нудной/занудной: однообразные побеги от монстров (потому что ты их просто не можешь убить или это займёт уйму времени) и забеги между заданиями (тем, что ты можешь выполнить). Als Jax machst du dich nicht ganz freiwillig auf die Suche nach dem jenigen der dich tot sehen will. Dazu stehen dir zum Anfang nur wenige Möglichkeiten offen in dieser sehr schönen aber feindseligen Umwelt. Damit du nicht gleich zu Beginn spielentscheidene Fehler machst, hier ein paar wichtige Tipps: Nimm restlos alles mit was du findest und verkaufe es zunächst mal auch nicht, behalte immer etwas von allem. Erlerne möglichst schell erlegtes Wild fachgerecht auszunehmen der Verkauf dessen ist deine Haupteinnahme Quelle aber behalte von allem etwas übrig. Lerne alsbald deine Waffen zu verbessern aber konzentriere dich auf ein bestimmten Waffentyp. Vergesse nicht das du auch einiges Wissen erlernen mußt das rein gar nix mit Kampf zu tun hat, aber dennoch sehr wichtig ist.
Das erlernen von Magie, Fernkampf und Alchemie ist nur dann wichtig für dich wenn du kein Nahkämpfer sein willst. Ich habe das gesamte Spiel als Axtkämpfer durch gespielt. Was mich nicht davon abgehalten hat kurzfristich auch mal ein Schwert zu nutzen. Im gesamten Spiel gibt es nur 1 Monster und 2 Gruppen von Gegnern wo ich eine Fernkampfwaffe einsetzen musste. Magie habe ich überhaupt nicht gebraucht. Ich habe auch keine Drogen genutzt sie sind völlig unnötig mit Ausnahme von Heiltränke die du aber eigentlich auch nicht brauchst da es genügend Kräuter und Fleisch gibt das du essen kannst. Das Jetpack ist für vieles sinnvoll einsetzbar aber es bedarf einige Übung damit richtig umzugehen, also nutze sich bietende Gelegenheiten zum üben dies wird dir oft das Leben retten und dich an Orte führen wo du sonnst nicht hinkommst.

Ihr solltet den Fraktionsbeitritt erst machen wenn ihr alle anderen Aufträge abgeschlossen habt, so könnt ihr euer Abenteuerleben voll ausnutzen und fast alles machen das es gibt in Elex. Noch ein letzter Hinweis, nutzt nicht den Teleportzauber da euch sonnst der größte Teil des spielspaßes entgeht aber schaltet dennoch alle Teleporter ein, da ihr ganz am Ende des Spieles sie wohl doch nutzen werdet.

[h1]Elex[/h1]
This post-apocalyptic SF Action RPG from 2017 takes you into a lovingly designed, open world full of dangers.
In Magalan, you'll find mutated creatures, mentally disturbed religious theorists, crazy environmentalists, soul-numbing separatists and end time outsiders. Then fight bandits, dealers, brainless Albs and much more.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1867069437

As Jax, you're not quite willing to go looking for the one who wants to see you dead. At the beginning there are only a few possibilities open to you in this very beautiful but hostile environment. So that you do not start making game-critical mistakes right at the beginning, here are some important tips: Take everything with you and do not sell it, always keep something of everything. Learn to exclude as quickly as possible caught wild game the sale of which is your main source of income but keep something of everything. Immediately learn to improve your weapons but concentrate on a specific weapon type. Do not forget that you also have to learn some knowledge that has nothing to do with combat, but is very important.
Learning magic, ranged, and alchemy is important to you only if you do not want to be a melee. I played the entire game as an ax fighter. That did not stop me from using a sword at short notice. There are only 1 monster and 2 groups of enemies in the entire game where I had to use a ranged weapon. I did not need magic at all. I have not used any drugs they are completely unnecessary with the exception of healing potions but you do not actually need it because there are enough herbs and meat that you can eat. The jetpack is useful for a lot of things, but it takes some practice to handle it properly, so take advantage of opportunities to practice this will often save your life and take you to places where you can not get there.
I played with normal difficulty and joined the outlaws. This is also my recommendation for you, as it is very varied and has many surprises in store during the game. You should not join the faction until you have completed all other assignments, so you can fully exploit your adventure life and do everything that exists in Elex. One last clue, do not use the teleport magic because you miss most of the fun of the game, but still activates all teleporters, because you will use them at the end of the game.

Hallo zusammen,

für mich ist ELEX Nostalgie pur. Seitdem Gothic 1, 2 und 3 mich als Kind in die Welt der RPG's eingeführt haben, konnte kaum ein Spiel mich so in seinen bann reißen wie ELEX. Wie jedes Spiel hat auch Elex Stärken und Schwächen. Und wie für ein PB Spiel üblich, sind es auch bei ELEX die üblichen Verdächtigen. 

- Die Grafik ist schlicht und einfach nicht auf dem Stand, auf dem sie sein könnte. (3/10)
- Das Kampfsystem ist, wie formuliere ich es am besten, gewöhnungsbedürftig. (5/10 da man sich schnell dran gewöhnt hat)

Trotzdem überwiegen für mich vor allem die Stärken. 

+ Die Story ist fesselnd! (9/10)
+ Die Map ist mit Liebe zum Detail entwickelt worden, wirklich überall findet man einzigartige Ort und Items! (10/10)
+ Tolle Charakterentwicklung (Kälte, Persönlichkeit, Handwerk, Kampf, Überleben) (8/10)
+ Entscheidungen haben einen Einfluss auf die Story ( mal mehr, mal weniger durchsichtig) (7/10)
+ gänzlich unterschiedliche (gewollt unsympathische?) Fraktionen, die durch einzigartige Fähigkeiten hervorstechen (8/10)

Was viele als Kritikpunkt auflisten, ist die Schwere des Spiels. Vor allem in den ersten 10 Spielstunden. Das kann ich tatsächlich nicht verstehen. Ich habe es satt von Anfang an der über krasse Zerstörer zu sein und einfach durch die Welt zu laufen als ob mir niemand was anhaben könnte. Lieber habe ich bei jedem Kampf eine Herausforderung, und lerne aus meinen Fehlern. Wobei man auch in ELEX am Ende einfach alles Zerstören kann! Wer darauf keine Lust hat kann das Spiel auch auf "Einfach" Spielen. 

Trotzdem muss ich gestehen das ich ELEX beim ersten mal anzocken direkt wieder abgebrochen habe. Für Leute die wenig Zeit haben, ist das Spiel einfach ungeeignet! Gerade am Anfang sollte man sich 1-2 Tage Zeit nehmen um in das Spiel zu finden. Anschließend kann man auch Abends mal in ruhe 1-2 Stündchen zocken. 

Alles in einem würde ich das Spiel jedem empfehlen der RPG's liebt! Nehmt euch etwas Zeit. Seit die ersten Stunden nicht zu streng mit dem Spiel und ich versichere euch das ihr Spaß haben werdet!

Anfangs sau schwer. Man weicht eigentlich nur alles und jedem aus und erfüllt vorerst lieber Botengänge. Mit den ersten Kampfskills geht es dann allmählich los. Dennoch sollte man immer auf der Hut sein. Später mit den entsprechenden Skills und Waffen wird es dann einfacher und so werden auch die großen Kampfbots mit Leichtigkeit vernichtend geschlagen.

Die Kampfmechanik ist nicht mehr ganz auf dem Stand der heutigen Technik und ist demnach etwas gewöhnungsbedürftig. Aber wann war diese bei Piranha Bytes Spielen jemals wirklich gut? xD

Dennoch wer Spiele wie Gothic oder Risen kennt und liebt (so wie ich), wird sich freuen dürfen. Der Charme von Piranha Bytes ist auch hier klar zu spüren.
