С Готикой познакомился начиная со второй части и для меня именно она стала примером качественной бродилки. В свое время её считали прорывом в жанре РПГ и прямым конкурентом Элде скролс Мороуинта. Она брала компактностью, ненавязчивым и простым лором, неписями с распорядком дня,  неповторимыми локациями и большим количеством событий на 1 кв.м карты. Игра затягивала и заставляла возвращаться к ней вновь и вновь. После нее поклонники ждали грандиозного дополнения, достойного легенд у камина и прославляющих песен, однако все закончилось с выходом в свет сыроватой, с запахом попытки наживиться на фанах 3 части и громким провалом с гневными окриками. Лишь с приходом ризена ситуация изменилась, хотя по факту эта была та же готика на тех же рельсах и даже с теми же звуками и бородатыми мобами. Но и она зашла и получила место в моем сердце. Что не скажешь про ее братьев поменьше ризена второго и ризена младшего, третьего.

Gemischte Gefühle bei dem Spiel. Zwischen Wut, Verzweiflung, Freude, Spaß, war alles dabei. Zu Anfang das Spiels, ich glaube nach den ersten 10 Stunden, hatte ich erst Mal keinen Bock mehr. Die Wut und die Verzweiflung (Frustration) war einfach zu hoch. Also der Einstieg in das Spiel ist schon ziemlich knüppel-hart und man bekommt eigentlich nur und ich meine wirklich nur aufs Maul. Es dauert gefühlt eine Ewigkeit (gut und gern 20 Std.) Spielzeit, bis man nicht an jeder Ecke krepiert. Die Steuerung, die etwas "klobig" daher kommt und wenig dynamisch, macht es dabei einem nicht unbedingt einfacher. Aber nach einer kleinen Pause von der Frustration, hieß es wieder ran an den Speck.
Tja was soll ich sagen, mit der Zeit wurde es immer besser und besser. Ich kam immer besser mit der klobigen Steuerung zurecht, wusste worauf ich achten musste, wem und was ich aus dem Weg gehen musste und letzten Endes war man so OP, das es fast egal war, was da einem entgegen kam und wie viel davon. Heißt das Spiel hat einen heftigen Kontrast von Start bis ungefähr die Mitte/Ende des Spiels, wobei ich sagen muss, das ich viel, sehr viel gelevelt hatte und am Ende des Spiels Stufe 54 war. 
[spoiler]Das Spiel nimmt langsam fahrt auf, ab ca. Stufe 20, davor bist du fast nur Futter für die Säue (Viehcher).[/spoiler] Was mir wirklich weitergeholfen hat (findet man relativ früh ist die "Hightech Brille", Achtung kleiner Spoiler: [spoiler]Dieses Item hat den "Sechsten Sinn" als Fähigkeit. Sie bietet dir zwar keine Rüstung, zeigt dir aber auf der Minimap alle Gegner in deiner Umgebung an. Das hat mir weit öfter den Arsch gerettet als jede Rüstung. Zu wissen was in der Umgebung lauert, hilft enorm um erstmal zu checken, was da an der nächsten Ecke lauert. Denn oft, ist das was dort lauert viel zu stark und nur all zu oft läuft man ohne diesen 6. Sinn, einfach Blindwegs rein und man darf das Spiel wieder neue laden..[/spoiler]
Oft wird kritisiert, das sich Leveln (Grinding) nicht belohnend anfühlt, und das ist zu Beginn des Spiels wirklich so. Ich dachte mir jedes Mal, warum soll ich mir den Stress antun hier Monster versuchen zu töten (wo ich evtl 1-3x neu laden muss), wenn eine wehrlose Ratte oder Assel mir fast genau so viele XP gibt. Aber ich denke es ist bewusst so, das zu Beginn des Spiels es einfach eine weile dauern soll bis man endlich mal selber bisschen austeilen darf. Bis dahin heißt es Kopf einziehen und Ärger weites-gehend aus dem Weg gehen.

Letzten Endes hat mir das Spiel trotzdem viel Spaß gemacht, in einer Manier wie man es von PB gewohnt ist. Daher kann ich das Spiel bedenkenlos weiterempfehlen. Am meisten Spaß hat mir dabei tatsächlich gefallen, die Welt zu erkunden, da sich wirklich hinter fast jedem Stein etwas verbergen kann, entdeckt zu werden. 

Hier und da gab's paar Bugs, aber keine die meine Story beeinträchtigt haben.

[u]Dislike Facts:[/u][list]

[/list]

The good and a REALLY bad 5.5/10

The Good
I have been playing RPG's for 35 years. This is definitely a true RPG in the sense where your actions shape many subtle aspects of the game world. Conversations are incredibly meaningful in this regard. The range of character builds and customization skill wise is great. You can certainly play in your style of choosing. If you ever played Arcanum a lot of the ideas will feel familiar in regard to Technology vs. Magic.

The REALLY bad
The enemy AI is both impossibly good at aiming, and less adapt at path finding than a toddler in a mine field. Combat difficulty is so unpredictable you will die dozens of times just to figure out you shouldn't have gone down a particular quest path. You will die a lot and encounter combat and quest lines without knowing it that can easily trap you in an incredibly difficult or near impossible situation to get out of if you save while in them. On the other hand, I killed a giant monster that could easily one shot me after I got stuck fighting him due to a bad save decision. The only reason I killed him was due to a glitch in the path AI getting him stuck against a rock and running towards me forever frozen in the same spot. 

The verdict
If you are a die hard fan of RPGs and loved Arcanum like I did back in the day, this just might be your game. The Technology vs. Magic trope is well played and feels considerably consequential. My best advice is to save as often as you can when moving through unknown areas. I definitely recommend having several saves so you can back track if you save in impossible situation.

Ich weiß nicht wieso die Entwickler sich nicht weiterentwicklen wollen. Das Spielprinzip ist immer das gleiche, seit Gothic schon. Das ist prinzipiel nichts falsches. Gothic und Gothic II sowie Risen waren großartige Spiele. Allerdings waren es entsprechend alle anderen nicht mehr. Gothic 3 spielte sich furchtbar, Risen 2 war noch ok, aber Risen 3 war bzw. ist eine einzige Katastrophe und nur schwer spielbar. 
Wo reiht sich Elex in diese Auflistung ein? Sicherlich nicht zu den erfolgreichen Spielen. 
Die Atmosphäre soll sicherlich isolierend sein, ok. Vielleicht wurde es auch ein wenig übertrieben.
Der Schwierigskeitsgrad ist lächerich. Wenn man nicht direkt den Questverlauf folgt, hat man gerade am Anfang keine große Chance beim erkunden zu überleben. Es gibt keinerlei Hinweise, wo man hingehen kann und wo nicht - außer es anhand von diversen Toden herauszufinden. 
Dann komm ich gleich zum Balancing. Weil mir der Schwierigkeitsgrad nicht gefällt hab ich mich relativ früh hochgecheatet. Trotz bester Werte und vergleichsweiser bester Ausrüstung haben die Gegner mich immernoch teilweise mit 2 Schlägen besiegt. Nahkampf ist also absoluter blödsinn. Fernkampf war ok, wenn man bei den Bersekern den Kampfbogen mit 200 Angriff kauft. Die gefühlt stärkste Waffe im Spiel, von Anfang an verfügbar.
Das Storytelling fühlt sich eher gequält an, es fehlt meiner Meinung nach an Hingabe. Vielleicht liegt es an den sehr monotonen Hauptcharakter, welcher zwar geschichtlich eben so korrekt dargestellt wird, aber spielerisch trotzdem keinen großen Spaß macht.

Wäre das Spiel 10 Jahre eher rausgekommen, wäre es vielleicht noch brauchbar gewesen. Aber 2017 damit anzukommen... Es ist erschreckend, wenn man eben sieht wie gut Piranhy Bytes eigentlich Spiele machen KONNTE.
Ich kann damit keine Kaufempfehlung abgeben, außer das Spiel ist für unter 15 oder weniger € zu kaufen.

I had previously rated this game as positive, but talking to a friend I could not say anything positive about it. To be fair, I could never say anything positive about any similar games, although I had hopes for this one. The game starts very well, good quests, dialogues, consequences to your actions and, best of all, a challenging difficulty. And the first 15 hours of the game are the hardest ones, you struggle to get experience and money. After that you are strong enough to farm, and after some farming you can steamroll anything you find and your character gets overpowered, just another Skyrim hammer swing fest.

The combat has a very strange characteristic, it’s hard because enemies hit very hard, but once you start a combo you can just combo the enemy to death with melee attacks, so you basically only have to hit an enemy once and then keep hitting them (the more times you hit, the more the enemies take damage per new hit, so it's all about big buttom mashing combos). This is true for some other weapons also, with which you can just stunlock enemies, namely the flame thrower, which behaves more like a missile launcher, but that does less damage and has a lot of ammunition.

The quests, that at the beginning are so interesting, after a while you finish them all and only the main quest is left. And although there are some interesting points in this main quest, the plot as whole is quite weak, with some cringing dialogues. A positive point I have to highlight is that the game really try to portray the factions as having a good reason to act the way they act, they didn’t try to trace a clear line between good and evil, and as such they avoided many cliches. I also hated the aesthetics of the game, the clothes, the characters... All that cyberpunk mixed with medieval fantasy didn't really mix well.

Is it a bad game? Not at all, I had more fun than playing Skyrim, for example. Although Skyrim has superior aesthetics and lore, the combat was so poor it really bored me. In this game I had to use some strategy for quite a while, use the correct weapons... But I got disappointed that before half of the game you can achieve maximum upgrades and you already know nothing will be able to stop you from that point on. Enemies hit hard, you die a lot, but constant auto-saving and quick saves at any place make it really not matter.

If you are different than me and really loved games like Skyrim and Fallout, probably this game will meet what you want. Ich fand es ziemlich gut.

Also ich spiele dieses Spiel schon 40 Stunden und es macht echt Spaß. Wie Welt ist groß, die Quests mannigfaltig und die Geschichte fesselnd. Aber das Kampfsystem is echt schlecht :) Manchmal reagiert der NPC gar nicht auf Richtungswechsel oder weglaufen, oder es ist 2-3 Sekunden verzögert! Das ist echt nervig. Kämpfen macht hier keinen Spass. Die Grafik ist insgesamt schön, bis auf die...Wasserfälle. Oh man, die sieht furchtbar aus ;) 

Alles in allem trotzdem sehr empfehlenswert.

Na bitte, ein weiteres PB-Spiel durchgespielt – langsam waren es nicht wenige. Nachdem ich alle Gothic-Teile gespielt und gemocht habe, und auch alle Risen-Teile sehr gut fand (ja, mit all ihren Macken), hatte Elex schon mal gute Karten. Besonders auf das neue „Endzeit“-Szenario war ich gespannt, mich persönlich spricht das sehr an, deutlich mehr als das Piraten-Setting aus Risen 2+3. 

Und siehe da, das neue Setting ist super! Die kaputte Welt, die Relikte aus alter Zeit, die daraus entstandenen neuen Fraktionen – all das passt perfekt zu der Art, wie Piranha Bytes ihre Spiele machen. Und ja, man darf sich nichts vormachen, oft ist das auch eine klischeehafte, eigenartige Mischung. Wenn die Mad Max-Outlaws auf die Gothic-Berserker treffen, und die Mass-Effect Kleriker auch noch mitmischen, ist das sicher nicht jedermanns Sache. Aber gerade wenn all diese Fraktionen unter einem Dach stecken, wie zb. in der Kuppelstadt, dann entsteht ein ganz eigenes Feeling, das wenige Spiele so rüberbringen. Sowas kann PB, und es macht immer wieder Spaß.

Ich hab das Spiel mit Controller gespielt, das klappt ganz hervorragend. Positiv zu erwähnen wären die, wie auch schon in Risen, kurzen Ladezeiten, das geht ruckzuck. 

Der Schwierigkeitsgrad ist am Anfang recht happig, auch das ist etwas das ich gerne mag. Wenn man am Anfang oft „aufs Maul“ bekommt, freut man sich später um so mehr, wenn man auch mal austeilt.

Das Kampfsystem ist leider etwas mühsam, so richtig gut von der Hand geht das nicht. Ehrlich gesagt hab ich aber nichts anderes erwartet, mich hat’s nicht gestört. Ganz großartig ist hingegen der Jetpack, eine der besten Neuerungen im Spiel, dadurch wird alles „freier“, und man hat noch größeren Spaß beim erkunden der Gegend.

Man bekommt hier übrigens wieder mal viel Spiel – wer sich darauf einlässt, kann hier locker seine 50 Stunden verbringen.

Also wenn’s nach mir geht, kann Elex 2 gerne kommen – ich werde es sicher wieder spielen. Daumen hoch, ich mag eure Spiele!

Ich bin frustriert und verärgert! Die Verärgerung und Enttäuschung über dieses nahezu unspielbare Spiel ist besonders deswegen so groß, weil ich ein großer Fan all der wundervollen Spiele von Piranha Bytes bin, die sie vorher herausgebracht haben. Die Spiele der Gothic- und Risen-Serie habe ich alle mit wachsender Begeisterung durchgespielt, und erhoffte mir mit ELEX wieder eine solche überragende Unterhaltung und Freude am Spiel. 
Daß gerade zu Beginn des Spiels die meisten Gegner unbesiegbar sind ist in Ordnung - und war bei Gothic und Risen auch nicht anders. Daß man auch schnell mal stirbt und den letzten Spielstand wieder einladen muß ist auch normal.
Daß es aber nicht der Sinn des Spiels sein kann, nur am ständigen Laden des Spielstandes zu sein und sich fast ausnahmslos fluchtartig durch jede Gegend fortzubewegen - auch bzw. gerade auf den angeblich "sichereren" Wegen - und von einer Gruppe unbesiegbarer Monster in die nächste Gruppe zu rennen.
Ich spiele ELEX jetzt 40 Stunden und bin auf Stufe 11 und kann selbst "leichte" Gegner nur besiegen, indem ich alle möglichen Einstellungen in der Schwierigkeit auf ganz leicht gestellt habe. Und selbst damit ist ein Kampf gegen Monstergruppen, die zu dritt oder viert auftreten - was fast immer der Fall ist ! - nicht zu gewinnen.
Nimmt man die schön gestalteten Gegenden, die unterhaltsamen Charaktere und Dialoge und die Geschichte und Handlung an sich, hätte ELEX wirklich große Klasse sein können - hätte.

I have a lot to say about ELEX but won’t. This is a very “Vector” game. I loved Risen and it’s first sequel made by the same developers. ELEX is Risen, and apparently Gothic, set in a true post-apocalyptic world. It’s harsh, unforgiving, confusing, poor-written and acted, fascinating, heavy in lore, and awkward. The world of Magalan is huge and dangerous. It is extremely fun to explore and gives the feeling that you’re scratching for every centimetre until you finally get a foothold. They don’t tell you anything and while this is frustrating it is also satisfying. This makes your early skill choices incredibly important and shape how you go about solving problems (quests, situations, and exploration). 

The downside is that, at a certain point, you become so overpowered that skills and abilities are useless. The end of the game feels superfluous and the leveling curve is irrelevant. I was left with a bunch of quests that offered no challenge and the presentation of the story just isn’t strong enough to make up for it. I was able to cheese the game by getting a particular gun that can perma-stun and stagger the strongest enemies in the game. While this was rewarding in that I worked very hard to get there (about 40 hours worth) it made the next 34 hours trivial. A big negative is that there are absolutely no people of colour in the game and women are just not as important as men. It’s a common problem I see in these style RPGs and is making me less and less willing to play the quirky European games. From a pure gameplay experience perspective, nothing offered what ELEX did in 2017.

[h1]Additional Info[/h1]

There are bugs already reported on day one that still have not been fixed now almost a year later. Like weapons stopping working mid-combat that need to be switched forward and backward to fix. Sometimes the protagonist doesn't wake up after sleeping or enemies are immortal till reloading. The alzheimer's syndrome with the weapon modes and armor is also somewhat annoying.

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]

If you like complex open world sci-fi-fantasy-fun RPGs and the mentioned bugs above don't bother you too much then I can still recommend this game. If however you can't stand such technical imperfections, it's perhaps better to stay away from it.

If you want to play a game that will fight against you at every turn, then this is for you. Whatever you do the game will always try to go against you, even the smallest thing like walking/running from point A to point B will be disturbed by clipping errors and input lag.

If you are willing to put in hours upon hours to find some fun in the game, then you will certainly find fun, world building and world design are incredible, one of the few open world games that don't have half the map copy pasted, you can find characters, all of them with their own personality and problems, though I have to say they could've used a few more unique character models. Also most of the quests feel unique and are woven into the world lore.

But that's it, a wonderful concept of a great game kept back by horrible game play and mechanics.
I will make a comparison with Dark Souls, not because the game play is comparable, but Dark Souls perfected the enemies that are always a threat, but even the hardest enemies can be dominated, in Elex it's exactly the other way around, enemies are either excruciatingly hard to kill or no threat at all.
Then to this problem you can add the broken controls, many minor clipping errors, surprisingly bland weapons and hit detection from hell, there you have your mix of disappointment.

There are some other problems whom I don't consider as fatal as the combat ones:
- From a world building perspective it doesn't really make sense that nearly all ppl are easily overwhelmed by one stronger monster, because if that is the case they should already be extinct
- It can take up to around 15 hours of gameplay before you're actually able to take on any enemy besides the weakest ones (it doesn't have to, but that's around the time it took me)
- If you don't take any combat skills at the beginning you leave yourself open for having to grind exp later because you can't do any quests anymore, since all enemies in these quests just destroy you, wich means you can't take the quality of life skills whom I chose (that's a common problem in RPGs having to decide between the skills that will make the game more fun or the skills that I need so I'm strong enough for what's to come)

The game is an enormous time sink because of all these problems wich could be alright if the time in the game wasn't a continuous struggle to press some fun out of the experience.

There is a good game burried somewhere under the garbage, but I can't find it, so I can't recommend this.

Quando ELEX foi anunciado, passei a acompanhar gameplays no YouTube e a ler as raras notícias publicadas sobre ele em sites brasileiros, mas por algum motivo acabei criando hype. Isso não é comum, ainda mais se tratando de uma franquia nova de uma empresa que nunca estimei.

Mas você deve estar se perguntando (provavelmente não está, mas finjamos que sim): então o que te chamou atenção? 

A resposta é muito simples: a temática, até então inédita para mim.

ELEX se passa num planeta devastado por um cometa que trouxe magia ao mundo. Nessa catástrofe os humanos sobreviveram, mas tiveram intrigas e formaram vários grupos. Bem, isso na verdade parece bem com a vida real. Mas tá, voltando ao assunto. Você já imaginou um mundo medieval, futurista e pós-apocalítico num jogo só? 

Pois é, ELEX fez isso muito bem de forma coesa e interessante. Assim sendo, há uma mistura muito bacana nas construções dos cenários, que variam das sobras do velho mundo, misturadas com as novas vilas medievais, futuristas e de bandidos.

Existem três facções, nas quais o jogador pode se afiliar a apenas uma (o que encoraja várias jogatinas). Todas as facções são muito distintas uma das outras em termos de visual, comportamento de NPCs, histórias e habilidades, tornando cada uma única. Elas também possuem seus próprios equipamentos, como armas brancas, a distância e armaduras - todos de acordo com o estilo visual e atributos de cada facção, portando existe uma grande variedade de itens utilizáveis encontrados no decorrer da campanha.

Berserkers: homens e mulheres anti-tecnologia, portanto se agarram a magia e um estilo medieval. Eles usam arcos e armas brancas. Esta é a classe que escolhi porque magia é magia, né? Brincadeira a parte, o motivo foi devido ao enredo, pois não concordei com os dogmas e posturas das outras. Não se preocupe, não tem spoiler nessa análise!

Outlaws: adivinhe qual é o estilo dessa! Adivinhou? Se disse "pós-apocalíptico", acertou mizerávi! Os caras são os badass, os sem lei, os párias. Lembram muito Fallout e Mad Max. Não é lá muito original, mas oras, funciona. Usam armas de fogo, óculos espelhados, jaquetas de couro, drogas e provavelmente não tomam banho. Hell yeah!

E por fim, os Clerics: esses são tecnológicos! E super estilosos também, diga-se de passagem! O problema é que... Espera, lembrei que essa análise não tem spoiler da história. Então, esses caras tem habilidade chamada "PSI", que é  similar a magia, mas não é magia. Com ela dá para usar ondas que jogam inimigos longe, se teletransportar a curtas distâncias e até criar hologramas. Parece legal, né? Quando jogar novamente vou escolher essa.

Ah, e tem os Albs. Inimigos, não aliados. Não queira contato a não ser que você esteja num level alto.

Falando nisso, os inimigos não acompanham o nível do personagem. Ou seja, você vai se ferrar muito nos combates, sendo muito conveniente apenas fazer missões e explorar sem entrar em conflito com os inimigos. Mas como ganhar XP? A esmagadora parte de XP é ganha completando missões, que são muitas, então quando estiver poderoso vai poder matar geral (com cuidado).

Vale alertar: o combate não é lá muito amigável. Dá pra domar, mas muitos se estressam e abandonam antes de se acostumarem. A dica é: pratique, pois não demora para pegar o jeito e se adaptar a jogabilidade. 

A forma com que se progride é penosa. Não é um sistema que dá pontos e mais pontos, dinheiros e mais dinheiros, explicações e mais explicações de como jogar. Comprar habilidades e PRINCIPALMENTE atributos requer muitos pontos. Ah, e só dá pra aprender habilidades PAGANDO os treinadores específicos, isso depois de cumprir certos requisitos! Viu, o capitalismo sobreviveu ao fim do mundo! Eba!

A parte mais gostosa de ELEX é a exploração. É um mundo grande e aberto para explorar como e na ordem que quiser, tendo um jetpack que deu um belo tchan ao game. A flora é bem variada, indo de deserto quente até deserto nevado, passando por florestas verdes e vermelhas com árvores altas... E pasme, uma área vulcânica! É super legal, sério.

Menções breves: a trilha sonora é ótima, sempre presente em momentos de combate e exploração. Os gráficos são muito belos, principalmente pelos cenários bem construídos.

Vale a pena? Sim. Se você curtir o game ao ponto de explorar e fazer tudo o que aparecer, vai ter pelo menos 75 horas de campanha. Se gostar ainda mais para zerar outra vez seguindo outra facção, que desbloqueia diferentes missões e habilidades, melhor ainda. No meu caso, a compra foi de 37 reais, num clássico desconto de promoção. Sem arrependimentos.

TLDR: It took me a while to get into this, it's slow to unfold due to its huge size and (for me at least) difficult combat learning curve. It really is a great RPG, something I sorely needed after the slow death of AAA single player RPGs with money grubbing tactics and MTX where plot and gameplay should be.

Pros:
+ An expansive, a diverse & truly beautiful and densely detailed world. There's nowhere you can go that isn't rewarding for both beauty and loot. 
+ Freedom. The choices are yours. 
+ A moral system based on your actions that affects the plot. If you're a cold son of a toaster or a gender studies snowflake, you'll get what you deserve. 
+ Distinct factions. Tree hugging Beserker barbarians with the D&D weapons to go with that, technophile Clerics that should have restraining orders from Alienware, the Outlaws with matching liver damage and bullet holes or none of the above because your weapons are the only friends you need. 
+ A full and true RPG. Think KotOR with fewer lightsabers but more wrecked civilisation. 
+ Rewarding mechanics and weapons. Everything you thought Fallout 4 & 76 would have but didn't. 
+ The story is, as far as I can recall, unique and compelling.
+ (I shouldn't be putting this as a pro as non-scumbag behaviour should be the standard.) No MTX, expansions, gimmicks etc, you just pay for the game and get the whole damn game.

Cons:
- Steep combat learning curve. I got a whooping more times than I'll admit. 
- A story that takes a long time to get going, you'll feel like you suffered through Twilight to get there. 
- Frequently doesn't let you say what you want, you'll find yourself saying "I want to shoot this guy in the access port, why won't you let me?!"
- The world is great but before you find the teleporters you will should learn to love background podcasts. 
- Large scale battles feel less than epic and more like you're herding a cats.

I really did love this game, despite my negatives I loved the world they built, it felt alive and the motivations felt realistic. It's just a good, old fashioned 3D RPG.

Here is how to evaluate if this game is for you. Ask yourself:

Did I have fun playing any of the Gothic series or the first Risen game from this dev?

If the answer is yes, then go ahead and make your purchase. You and I both know what you are getting into. 

If you have not played previous games from this dev then you may have to ponder a bit more. The game is slower than some RPGs, the combat can be wonky, the dialogue is bad enough to be funny...like...consistently. If you dig into it there are a ton of layers, hidden ones like a secret thief society and obvious things like different choices that impact (and often kill) different groups. The graphics are decent but again can go sideways...like when you start a convo with a dude who is pissing off of a bridge, and so he turns mid pee and starts pissing on you as you chat.

Your stoic voiced hero dude is going to be soft as spoiled fruit to start, with stupid frog things even having a chance to end your life. By the end you will be tossing skills around that crush...well...whoever you want to crush. I think that after around 30 hours of playtime I could probably kill everyone in the world if I had the time and attention span. Ranged seems to be EZ mode in this latest PB offering, so for a challenge go ahead and wield that sword.

It's fun for what it is and plenty broad in scope, just don't expect a perfected masterpiece and for the love of all things holy make sure you familiarize yourself with the quick save button. Save a lot. Seriously. Mistakes are made and they are not always even your own. It's part of the charm.

[b] 扮演賈克斯，一名智械指揮官在遭遇陷害後開始屬於自己的故事。[/b]

本作在體驗上類似上古卷軸、異塵餘生，但又更加硬派。

戰鬥、動畫和操作設計算是一大敗筆，但劇情的環環相扣和完整的世界觀依舊讓人十分沉浸。

由於遊戲設計初期對新手十分不善，導致在前期就勸退不少玩家。
(路上遇到看起來很弱的怪馬上被教做人，邊打邊跑開始思考外鄉人戰術)
(好不容易湊錢買好裝備，卻因為屬性不夠而無法裝備的情況屢見不鮮)
(任務沒提示建議等級，導致某些任務會遇到的怪一巴掌直接讓你上天)，
上述狀況直到中後期整體體驗才順暢許多。

探索方面由於無負重設定、再加上一開始就能拿到的噴氣背包讓整體過程流暢許多(對喜歡撿垃圾的玩家是一大福音?)，並且遊戲有數位NPC隨從可以伴玩家上山下海，但一次最多帶一名。每位隨從皆有專屬的故事劇情，並在跟隨玩家時依照玩家的對話提升或降低好感度

遊戲總共有三個派別供玩家加入，分別為狂戰士、牧師及匪徒，但須注意一旦加入其一派別則無法再加入其他勢力。狂戰士的代表為傳統及魔法、牧師崇尚科技和神，而匪徒則以藥物、自由及金錢為宗旨。

自由度可謂本作的賣點之一，在任務方面每個任務都有至少兩種以上的解法，並依解法不同導向完全不同的後續。
在城鎮內盜竊、殺人等等被發現則會被人通報，須親自向領主繳賠償金才能繼續在城鎮內自由活動。
在戰鬥上則可自由切換身上的武器，從冷兵器到科技武器(長劍及雷射槍)等，須注意大部分敵人及隊友也具備遠近攻擊能力。

在與NPC對話時有些對話需要靠社交技能來解鎖，而有些回覆甚至會提升或降低主角本身的冷酷值(人性)並將決定整個遊戲劇情走向。

整體而言若不在意戰鬥、設計平衡及過場動畫雞肋等等缺點的話，這仍然是一款十足的好遊戲。

Je vais essayer d'être le plus honnête et divertissant possible dans cette évaluation puisqu'il faudrait que vous la lisiez en entier... même si elle sera probablement un peu trop... "complète"...
(c'est le terme que l'on utilise pour qualifier la préparation culinaire imbouffable d'une personne que l'on apprécie).

Je vais commencer par faire court pour ceux qui n'ont pas de temps à m'accorder, et j'extrapolerai plus tard (dans tous les cas, je ne spoilerai rien).

ELEX est dur... nan, attendez, vous n'avez pas saisi... il est VRAIMENT DUR.
Alors que certains se masturbent devant leur skill sur Sekiro qu'ils considèrent comme l'apogée de la difficulté, les joueurs d'ELEX découvrent les nouvelle stratégies de combat du commandant à coup de fuites et de PLS derrière le décor.

Je ne déconne pas : les trois-quart de vos quêtes seront faites en grande partie de fuite. C'est bien simple : le moindre petit animal agressif qui fait la moitié de votre taille peut vous mettre une race.

Et je ne parle même pas d'affronter un groupe de 3 bandits... c'est le VIOL le plus complet.

Vous vous dites sûrement : "HA ! Mais mon ami, j'ai joué à RISEN et sais parfaitement comment berner les ennemis avec des mécaniques de jeu douteuses !" eh bien je te répond TANT MIEUX ! car sans mécaniques de jeu douteuses, tu vomirait ton sang... rassures-toi donc, tu ne feras que le cracher.

En fait, on dirait que les programmeurs ont été tellement frustrés par les "techniques" des joueurs pour se simplifier les combats sur les Gothics et autres Risens qu'ils ont tout fait pour rendre l'IA impossible à maroufler.
Vous ne me croyez pas ? Essayez de vous enfuir sur un rocher ou un bâtiment pour éviter le corps à corps, la TOTALITÉ des ennemis du jeu (à quelques rares exeptions, comme les poulets du début) ont des attaques à distance complètement fumées (petite mention aux boules de plasma des monstres). Même le dernier des pécors a un fusil d'assaut qui provoque des saignements dans son inventaire.
Au niveau corps à corps aussi, vous serez rapidement reçu par les petits bandits avec des épées tronçonneuses empoisonnées.

Alors vous vous dites "oui, d'accord, mais si tu en tues un, prends-lui ses armes et armures !"... non seulement toutes les armes nécessitent des stats pour les équiper (et pas de petites stats) mais en plus, la meilleure nouvelle c'est que vous ne POUVEZ PAS récupérer l'équipement de vos ennemis ! Et les acheter est le pire investissement possible vu que vous avez peu d'argent et qu'il part généralement dans l'apprentissage de compétences lié aux niveaux.

Au fur et à mesure du jeu, on en vient presque à se demander si ça vaut vraiment la peine d'essayer d'être le personnage principal... vu que malgré le fait que vous incarniez l'ancien COMMANDANT JAX, eh bah... le moindre poulet vous roule dessus sans difficulté. C'est à se demander si votre héros n'a pas récupéré son diplôme de commandant dans un Kinder.

Allez, arrêtons de blaguer. Retenez surtout que vous aller probablement passer plus de temps à regarder l'écran de chargement de partie qu'à combattre. Pensez aussi à comprendre les mécaniques de combats et les paterns des ennemis, sinon vous ne jouerez tout simplement pas... et évitez à tous prix d'affronter plus gros ou fort que vous... vous n'êtes pas dans Skyrim. (c'est mon meilleur exemple de jeu qui ouvre son anus face au joueur, désolé de le citer tout le temps).

Après toutes ces explications, je suis ravi de vous annoncez qu'au moins, vous pourrez vous vanter de vous être battu pendant 8 heures de jeu avec une hache comme seule arme ! (c'est vraiment le temps que j'ai passé avec juste une hache en main si on ne compte pas le trop peu de flèches pour tirer à l'arc).
D'ailleurs, oubliez le combat à distance, car outre le fait que les ennemis y soient formés depuis leur plus tendre enfance, ils ont une AIM d'enfoirés qui visionne vos déplacement dans l'espace-temps.


Alors pourquoi je recommande le jeu ?

Parce que c'est un bon jeu. c'est tout. Les graphismes sont beau, le personnage est cool le jet pack est pratique, l'univers est bien construit, les monstres sont assez variés, il y a plein de quêtes et de PNJ et même si la difficulté des combats est trop élevée, les quêtes en elles-même sont faisables, les marqueurs activables pour les localiser sont fidèles et c'est ce qui permet d'avancer.
En revanche, vraiment, si vous êtes du genre à abandonner face à la difficulté, oubliez l'idée d'acheter ce jeu. Un PNJ normalement armé vous butte en un seul combo bien placé. Alors vous allez recommencer souvent et abuser des sacs de couchage pour restaurer la santé.

Partez simplement du principe que le jeu sera méchant... genre... vraiment très méchant... il cherche à vous mettre la misère et ne s'en cache pas.

mon dernier petit conseil sera : si vous papillonnez comme moi parfois, évitez à tous prix les combats contre des trucs que vous ne connaissez pas. même au début du jeu, sauvegardez avant tout.


Sur ce ! paix à votre âme et n'allez pas voir à droite sur le pont en bois ! des bisous.

Da una parte mi dispiace per Piranha Bytes, lo sviluppatore. Costretti per quasi vent'anni (!) a creare sequel dopo sequel, sempre rimanendo sulle stesse strutture di gioco e di storia.

Dico che mi dispiace in parte, ma in effetti da loro non voglio altro. Gothic in eterno.

Per chi sa già cosa aspettarsi, Elex non delude. Mondo enorme, ed enormemente dettagliato. Si vede e si sente che è una cosa fatta a mano, che non si piega o fa concessioni al giocatore. Se giochi ad Elex, devi stare alle sue regole. Non ci sono nemici livellati automaticamente, che diventano più forti man mano che lo diventi tu. Se vogliono prenderti a legnate nei denti, ti prendi le legnate nei denti e impari in fretta chi è il capo.

Cosa che rende la vendetta ancora più dolce ore dopo, dopo aver sputato sangue e denti, ed essere tornato nei luoghi già visitati con qualche livello in più e la rabbia di chi le ha prese e sa che ora è il suo turno di distribuirle.

La storia e l'ambientazione mischiano fantasy e scifi, con un tocco di post-apocalisse. Come in tutti i suoi predecessori, Elex offre una storia che a un certo punto può divergere in tre rami differenti. A differenza dei suoi predecessori, il finale è più aperto e tiene molto conto delle varie scelte intraprese, con conseguenze dirette per personaggi e fazioni.

È sempre una gioia esplorare liberamente, scoprire i piccoli anfratti con i tesori, le missioni o in generale decidere che ti va di scalare quella montagna per vedere com'è la vista da lassù (il jetpack aiuta molto!).

Non è da ignorare il fatto che Piranha Bytes alla fine della giornata è composta da 30 persone o giù di lì, le ambizioni sono enormi, ma la realizzazione a volte manca qualche colpo. Nonostante tutto, dopo i primi dolori di crescita e le varie patch, il gioco è solido.

Per chi non ha mai toccato un gioco Piranha Bytes prima d'ora, il consiglio è di stringere i denti e sopravvivere alle prime ore, tutto diventerà più soddisfacente man mano che si gioca.
Per i veterani non ho bisogno di scrivere recensioni o raccomandazioni. Sanno già di volerci giocare, se non lo hanno già fatto.

Your Piranha Bytes expert here to give you another well rounded review of their terrible yet somehow addictive games. Piranha Bytes continue to be an enigma in the gaming world; their games are all great on paper and I've played each of them for hundreds if not over a thousand hours, more than my money's worth. Naturally it would be absurd for me to claim I disliked their games or thought they were bad but there are aspects of every single Piranha Bytes game from Gothic 1 to Risen 3 which make me scratch my head. Elex is not only no exception but it actually punctuates a lot of these problems because releasing a game of this poor quality in 2017 is unimaginable. I might even be willing to start believing that Piranha Bytes just aren't good game developers!

Let's start with the flaw that each and every Piranha Bytes game has: the combat. I don't know what it is about these guys but they just have not been able to nail down combat in any way, shape or form across their entire catalog. The basis of every fight in every game is this: mash the attack button and hope you get the first hit in or you'll be stun locked until you die. That's it. Because of this the only viable class to play in any of their games is the ranger until the player is so overpowered that they are killing enemies with one strike. Elex tried to change it up by adding combos and "heavy" strikes but to be frank the combat here is no different from Gothic 3 or Risen. I'd wager the games would actually be MORE fun if there was no combat. Wouldn't that be an interesting game?

The biggest thing that sticks out in the 2010's is the voice acting and dialog. Jesus F. Christ if English isn't your team's first language you can find a better translator for your story on Reddit than these guys manage. The quests are poorly detailed, the main plot points are a convoluted mess of broken grammar and words that don't make sense in the context used, and so on.  The voice acting is unsurprisingly poor, given the lack of detail to the script. Amazingly the worst voice actor in the game was used to voice the main character. His delivery is banal and trite, hitting every "disgruntled bad-ass" trope you can think of. Even minor characters deliver more of a performance than this guy. Which, again, is not out of the ordinary for these games. The main voice actor in Gothic 3 was apparently just some drunk they found at a pub who needed a few extra deutschmarks.

Modeling and animation are improved slightly over older games in the catalog but still far from great by most industry standards. Hands and arms clip through static clothing, weapons float mysteriously next to your character when holstered, mouths don't quite match the words being spoken, and so on. In the early to mid 2000's when Piranha Bytes first started producing RPGs these things were all standard and their games actually looked beautiful compared to their contemporaries. Unfortunately they've failed to change with the times and are still producing games in 2017 as they did in 2001. In fact if you look at character models from their earliest games they've really not changed anything aside from poly count and textures. At least they have a style, I suppose.

But all that aside, the game is fun. All of their games are fun. The world is immersive and interesting. The side quests are gripping and actually change the world around you which a lot of AAA RPGs still can't manage to get down. There's a lot to DO in the game even if doing it could be a lot better. The crafting system is far better than any of the companies' previous games (all you could really do in the past was make potions anyway) and there's a much more diverse range of weapons to choose from unlike other PB games where there was always just one weapon that was obviously better than the one you had.

In conclusion, Elex is like any PB game: you are either going to love it or hate it. There is absolutely no middle ground. Nobody ever thought Gothic 3 was just "OK". It was either a blast that they spent a hundred hours in or they played it once and regretted purchasing it. Elex is no different. You'll know in the first 15 minutes if it's something you're going to want to keep playing. Which is great because that's still inside the refund window.

Kurz gesagt: schönes Spiel, dass ich empfehlen kann, aber mit deutlichen Schwächen, über die man manchmal nur schwer hinwegsehen kann. 

Mein größter Kritikpunkt ist die Art, wie die Story präsentiert wird. Die Geschichte selbst wird sicher keinen Preis gewinnen, nicht mal einen ganz billigen. Aber wirklich schlimm ist der Pathos und das vollkommene Fehlen von Glaubwürdigkeit. Es gibt keine Möglichkeit, sich mit der Hauptperson zu identifizieren - dafür ist sie zu sehr Abziehbild. Und dann diese Monologe - schrecklich. Auch die Plattitüdendrückerei von einigen NPCs ist wirklich eher Qual als angenehm. Und trotzdem hatte ich viel Spaß mit Elex, weil die Welt Spaß macht. Gothic 2 bleibt unter den Spielen von Piranha Bytes weiterhin unangefochten bei mit auf Platz eins, aber etwas von der Stimmung und dem Flair der Welt von Gothic 2 findet sich in Elex wieder und rettet so das Spiel für mich. Wenn ich ein "neutral" vergeben könnte, würde ich es tun. Da ich es nicht kann, und meine Tendenz doch eher zum positiven geht, wird es also eine Empfehlung.

Nach dem ersten Durchzocken in 68 Stunden innerhalb nur einer Woche kann ich schonmal sagen: Ich konnte es nicht mehr weglegen, bis ich durch war!

Nun aber detaillierter:

Was mir gefiel: 
-Tolle Open-World mit unendlich viel zu entdecken (einfach mal 2 Stunden keine Quest machen, sondern nur auf Entdeckungstour gehen ist hier möglich)
-Man kann jede Quest so angehen und abschließen wie man möchte. Man kann sogar jeden einfach töten, wenn man will und es hat Konsequenzen.
-Tolle Atmosphäre wird hier vermittelt, vor allem in dem Drittel der Karte, wo es viel Natur gibt.
-Beziehungen zu den Menschen bzw. eigene Kälte/Menschlichkeit verändert sich durch Gesprächsoptionen, was letzten Endes zig verschiedene Enden und Beziehungen zulässt. 

Was mir nicht gefiel:
-Schlechte deutsche Synchro (Trotz deutschem Entwickler) mit oft total falschen Betonungen, die nicht zum Kontext passen. Man merkt, dass beim Sprechen wohl keiner so richtig wusste, warum wann was gesagt wird.
-Unlogische Gespräche, vor allem so Sachen, dass mir immer als Wildfremdem direkt die größten Geheimnisse anvertraut wurden.

Abschließend genoss ich aber eben total die spielerische Freiheit, die man hier hat. Wiederspielwert ist auch super, da man sich immer anderes entscheiden kann und einer anderen Fraktion beitreten kann und sich so eine ganz andere Geschichte entwickelt.

В общем то на один-два прохождения игра пойдёт, если хочешь залипнуть в тру рпг где тебя будут насиловать пока не подберёшь одно из орудий апокалипсиса, то заходи, не задерживайся.

Well.. I had high hopes for this game.

I'll start with the Pros:
-Great atmosphere, love the mix of middle ages and futuristic tech.
-Terrain is pretty lively, detailed areas, old ruins of civilization and new settlements ranging from metallic fortresses to shanty wooden shacks, makes exploring each place fresh.
-The equipment and skills looked fleshed out, made me want to aspire to get such weapons, and the game doesn't hold your hand and give you too much from the start, the feeling of starting out from nothing is true.

But, the big Cons:
-The combat, although not terrible, is clunky, dodging becomes life or death with most enemies, and there's no guideline to what you should or shouldn't fight. All the animals look pretty much the same whether they are too strong or not. Plus, all the equipment has absurd requirements just to use them, even something basic as a sword.
-Anything above animals pretty much bodies you in one or two hits, if you have the pure determination to kill anything, you really can; But it just becomes dark souls at that point, and not in the good way.
-There's not as much free choice as the game advertises. [spoiler] Early on, you're pretty much forced to side with the Berserkers after one of them practically saves you. [/spoiler] I haven't gotten that far into the story of the Berserkers, because I have absolutely no interest in them. I wanted to side with the Clerics from the start, and I wasn't even given that option, regardless of the Berserkers saying "You can leave whenever you want" and that's what I did, yet the game wasn't built for that kind of free choice. You're practically stuck there helping them until you're capable of taking on things yourself.
-The lack of balancing with the mobs is rather discouraging, because it pretty much restricts you from free roaming from the beginning. Either you're equipped and leveled to take them, or you're not.
-The ranged combat.. is pretty much useless. Aiming can't happen without spending precious ammo until you have the crosshairs over the enemy, and at that point the enemy is already either filling you with holes or slashing you to pieces. You can just use melee and the game would be (mostly) fine, but that is a core part of the combat, and it shouldn't be just useless to begin with. (Disclaimer, I never got far enough to get a proper gun, but I doubt it is much different)

To summarize: This game, with a lot of polish to the combat, would really make this game enjoyable. But when it is being advertised as an open world game, I wanna explore it, not muck around in a fort giving people beer just to spit in my face. I -wanted- to like this game, but that just want just kept getting stepped on by things I was forced to do, and replaced the things I wanted to do. Refunded, even on discount.

Do not even try. If you want to try this game, and like it, you probably have a lot different tastes to me. You're all obligated to your own opinions.

Un ottimo erede del capolavoro che è Gothic. Consigliato a chiunque voglia una vera esperienza action GDR. 
Un action GDR che non tiene la mano dell'utente, e che lo stimola a trovare soluzioni "organiche" ai problemi che gli si pongono davanti. 
La curva di evoluzione del personaggio è molto ripida all'inizio, e questo può spiazzare il giocatore che non conosce il modo in cui Piranha Bytes sviluppa i suoi giochi. Il segreto è immedesimarsi nel personaggio e comprendere che il mondo è molto più avanti di noi quando inizieremo i nostri passi. Col tempo riusciremo a metterci al suo passo e poi a superarlo, di gran lunga. 
Ed è qui che il gioco brilla veramente...quando lo sviluppatore mette nelle mani del giocatore il potere tanto ambito e sudato. Passeremo a sentirci degli inetti completi al diventare dei punti di riferimento per gli altri NPC del gioco. 
Questo, insieme ad una ambientazione altamente immersiva, fanno di ELEX un gioco da non mancare per gli appassionati del genere. 
Altamente consigliato.

Risen 1.2. Clunky controls and combat system. Gigantic, living open world and moderate grafics. For all those who were disappointed with Risen 2 and 3 because they weren't true successors of Risen 1, here you go. Four groups fighting against a common enemy, whose Commander you once were. Choices everywere, and be sure they will remember them all. No bag capacitiy holding back your urge to loot the entire world. And if you stray offroad, you better be prepared to find something interesting behind every corner (and thats were you will find new enemies as well, so better be prepard).

Vorab möchte ich sagen, dass ich ein großer Gothic Fan (1 & 2 selbstverständlich) bin, da vermutlich viele der Elex Interessierten ebenfalls über diese Schiene gekommen sind. Daher werde ich Elex auch öfter mit den Gothic Spielen vergleichen.

Nun aber los:

Das Spiel fängt gut an mit einer nachvollziehbaren Situation, warum man mal wieder der erinnerungslose schwache Typ ist. Die Spielwelt ist gefüllt mit Verstecken, Aufgaben und NPCs. Theoretisch könnte man auch direkt am Anfang überall hin, nur sehr starke Monster machen einem irgendwann das Vorkommen schwierig.
Insgesamt sind viele der Quests gut geschrieben, vor allem die um den Anschluss einer der Gilden. Die Gilden selbst fand ich deutlich schwächer als im Vergleich zu Gothic, ich habe mit keiner wirklich sympathiert.
Wo viele der NPCs gut geschrieben sind haben mich allerdings oft die Wahlmöglichkeiten die man hat sehr frustriert. Beispielsweise gibt es einen Charakter dich mal beklaut und man wurde zwangsweise so etwas wie Freunde, es gab nie die Gelegenheit ihm "volles Pfund aufs Maul zu hauen".
Am häufigsten geärgert hat mich das Kampfsystem. Phasenweise ist es wirklich ein sich "durchsterben", also so lange den Kampf versuchen bis es mal klappt. Dabei kamen mir die Hitboxen teilweise sehr skuril vor, man wurde noch getroffen obwohl man schon ausgewichen war. Auch gibt es mehrere Feinde mit knockback Effekten und gerade wenn es ein paar von denen sind gerät man relativ häufig in einen Stunlock.
Ich habe zwar keins von den Souls Spielen gespielt, bin also nicht gerade der beste Kämpfer, aber sowohl in den Gothic Spielen als auch in den Witcher Spielen kam mir das Kampfsystem runder und fairer vor.
Schaffen tut man viele der Kämpfe dennoch und wenn man weit genug gekommen ist gleicht man vieles durch gute Ausrüstung aus. Ich empfehle nur eine hohe Frusttoleranz.
Die Story hat zwar gut gestartet und auch viel Spaß gemacht als man die Gebiete und Gilden kennengelernt hat, aber die Haupt Story zum Ende hin fand ich immer schwächer und schwächer. Das Ende fand ich auch nicht befriedigend. Das ganze wirkte zu aufgesetzt.
Bugs sind mir wenige begegnet, es gab ein paar Abstürze und hin und wieder hatte ich das Gefühl, dass das Spiel sich nicht die richtigen Entscheidungen von mir bei einigen Quests gemerkt hatte, ein paar NPCs haben an ein paar Stellen gewisse Sachen gesagt, die so einfach keinen Sinn gemacht haben. Z. B. NPCs denen ich geholfen oder denen ich mich angeschlossen habe sagen mir auf einmal sie würden mich nicht unterstützen, da ich ihnen ja auch nicht geholfen hätte.

Daher kriegt das Spiel insgesamt von mir einen Daumen nach unten. Es ist zwar ok, aber es gab mehrere Stellen wo ich mich wirklich zwingen musste weiterzumachen, allen voran wegen dem Kampfsystem und der Story. Ich werde es wohl nicht nochmal spielen, da lieber nochmal Gothic.

This game is everything that's right with a Piranha Bytes game and wrong at the same time... A this one for me at least - went a bit too far into the wrong camp.

Good stuff - a massive, pretty world to explore with lots of variety, cool looking monsters etc. A decent combat system coupled with some nice RPG elements are here too, just like in the other PB games.

The bad stuff - it's so drawn out that it is simply huge...ly boring. Oh my - even this world I mentioned above - it's huge, but also - there's barely anything interesting here. It's all just "we have to make it big" but there never was any thought like "should we make it so big?". The first town you arrive in is massive - you can't find a single thing in it. That feeling persists throughout the game. Why not make it more compact? Think Skyrim and it's cities and towns - pretty much everyone who played that game can draw the layout of Whiterun or Riften from memory. Elex - nope... it's just some buildings here and there...

Then there's the conversations - why, oh why did someone thought it would be cool to record hours of conversations about essentially nothing. Early on - you get a choice of going to some ruins or not - this devolves into a 10 minute talk about such a simple task. And every single character in the game is designed this way. It's always blah blah blah, 10 minutes. You learn to love the skip button very quickly. 

Ultimately - there's fun to be had, but it's all blocked by boring dialog that you need to get through and way too much unnecessary level space that serves no purpose it seems. 

Also, the main character is essentially as interesting as a wooden board. He has nothing fun to say at all and his dialogue is just a bloated as everyone else's.

Spiele das Spiel nun zu zweiten mal. Das erste mal hab ich irgendwann keine lust mehr gehabt. Nun macht es aber richtig Spaß. Möchte deswegen paar Tipps geben, die man vielleicht beachten sollte.
1) Das Spiel hat völlig eigene Standards.  Man muss seine Entscheidungen immer mit bedacht wählen. Es gibt kein "man ist eh immer stark genug alles zu schaffen und hat immer viel Ressourcen"
2) Deswegen Anfangs nicht blind drauf los skillen, wenn ihr ne Stufe aufsteigt. Reiner Damage + Leben Build wie er in fast jedem Spiel super stark ist, wird nicht klappen. 
3) Bezieht auch Skills mitein, die nicht auf Schaden aus sind. Diebstahl, Tiere ausbeuten etc.  sind nicht umsonst da. Solche Skills bringen euch ne Menge Geld ein und das bekommt man in Elexnicht geschenkt. Bei meinem ersten Spielstand war das tatsächlich ein Problem. 
4) Soweit ich weiß ist eine gute Ausrüstung das wichtigste in Kämpfen. Schaden und Verteidigung über Skillpunkte soll nicht so Ausschlaggebend sein.
5) Deshalb wenn man eine coole Waffe hat, die man nutzen will, am besten gerade so Skillen, dass man die Stats dafür hat.
6) Vermeidet anfangs Kämpfe jeder Art. Ihr werdet, gewarnt dass ihr keine gute Ausrüstung habt, aber in jedem anderen Spiel würde das nichts bedeuten. In Elex sollte man sowas aber beim Wort nehmen. Anfangs schafft man echt nur die aller schwächsten Gegner. Ich empfele auch das Spiel auf leicht zu stellen. Nicht, weil man dann mehr aushält, sondern weil manche Gegner echt abnormal viel Leben haben und wohl kleiner Lust auf nen 5 Minuten Kampf gegen nen normalen Gegner zu haben. 
7) Aus diesem Grund. Quests sind das A und O. Man wird zwar später stärker und kann einige Gegner recht leicht besiegen, aber Quest lohnen sich in der Regel am meisten. Vermute, dass das bewusst so ist. Man möchte in dem Spiel möglichst viel Geschichte rüberbringen und das Kämpfen eher Nebensache sein lassen. 
8) Für Piranha Bytes üblich: Überlegt euch genau was ihr bei Gesprächen mit NPCs und in Quests von euch gebt. Die NPCs werden euch nicht einfach sagen: rennt von A nach B, dann bekommt ihr Geld. Manche werden euch beleidigen, andere sind super nett, aber behaltet im Hinterkopf, dass man nicht immer die friedliche Antwort wählen sollte. Ein Kochrezept habe ich dafürnicht gefunden. Wie gesagt, vermeidet Anfangs vielleicht den Kampf. Auch wenn ein NPC sehr provokant sein kann, oft bekommt man die Gelgenheit, sich später noch zu rächen. Aber genug davon, wollte nur erwähnen, dass man  immer Misstrauisch sein sollte. Genau das finde ich auch so gute an dem Spiel. 
9) Speichert möglichst oft. Überraschungen gibts genug und dann will man nicht die letzten 10 Minuten nochmal spielen.
Fazit: Ich finde es einfach nur gut.  Der Spielstil ist komplett einzigartig, auch wenn er anfangs als normal empfunden wird. Es gibt echt an jeder Ecke was zu entdecken. Sucht immer alles gründlich ab.  Die Karte ist wirklich gut gefüllt mit vielen kleinen Nieschen in denen sich Schätze verstecken. Grafik ist toll. Meine einzigen Kritikpunkte: Die Gesichter der NPCs sehen sehr oft sehr ähnlich oder gar gleich aus. Das Kampfsystem könnte noch ein paar Verbesserungen brauchen. Man kann es zwar in gewissermaßen beherrschen, aber  diese abnormal hohen Lebenspunkte bei manchen Gegnern ist schon nervig. Dennoch Top Spiel und würde es jederzeit empfehlen. Achja und Deutsch als Hauptsynchro sieht man heutzutage auch kaum noch. Jeder NPC wurde vertont, auch unwichtige Namenlose sagen ein paar Worte.

Overall, I like this game.

I was really annoyed by the game ending. This is a 'actions have consequences' type of game, but it was really unclear how my actions would turn out. I expected a certain outcome, and then out of nowhere the game ended in a completely different way. It really bothered me!

The strengths of this game are in its lore, and environment. It's a really nice-looking game world, and great fun to traverse on foot and with a jetpack. Except when a low-level beast one-shots you into next week after 5 paces out of a town (which is something I dislike about Piranha Bytes - the punishing level system, and having to pay for skills).

The factions are really diverse, and it was interesting trying to use the Adjutor (inventory implant) in Goliet, with the technology-hating Berserkers yelling at you.

The game is good, but I had to use hacks to enjoy it more (sorry, but that's how I roll - if you're more hardcore than me, by all means play the game how you like).

I had a good time with Elex. I liked its world, found its plot interesting (if not perfect), and enjoyed its characters. It's no Gothic II, but if you're looking for that Piranha Bytes vibe, you'll find it here.

I should note, however, that the game *can* be horribly frustrating. The combat system is clunky and the early game can be entirely too hard, and not in an enjoyable way. There are also big chunks of its upgrade/skill system that are basically useless. Sometimes it feels like the design was intended for an ever bigger, even longer game, and then it got cut down at the end. Who knows. But you might want to look up a few things in a wiki to improve your overall experience.

I should also note that the game is *way* better in the original German. This is generally true of all Piranha Bytes games, but it especially applies here, so if you happen to speak German, don't play it in English. The English translation is really lifeless.

This sounds negative, and I can imagine that some people will find the game's clunkier aspects too much to bear, but I would still rate my overall experience as quite positive. I liked the journey that Elex took me on and I look forward to the sequel.

Elex has a shopping list of substantial flaws that should all individually ruin the experience but somehow combine into an experience that kept me coming back for more.

 - The difficulty curve is awful; there's a sweet spot about eight hours in between being beaten up by all but the weakest mooks and dominating groups of the most powerful enemies that gives you about two hours of what I'd consider an enjoyable challenge.
- Most characters are flawed enough to be irritating but not enough to be interesting. There are a handful dotted throughout the game that don't fall into this category, but unfortunately the main character is not one of them.
- The gameplay mechanics are clunky and unrewarding. By the time you get good with them,  you are presented with new options that are far more effective and require less still to use.
- The world building is intriguing but sporadically delivered and holds back critical information for a potential sequel.

TLDR: I played through the game 3.5 times.  I like this game a lot.  If you like games like Mass Effect, Witcher, the newer Fallout outings, or Dragon Age this should be an easy sell.

This game has so many parallels to Mass Effect 1 that comparisons are inevitable.  For me though, the comparison goes deeper.  I bounced of ME 1 the first time I played it.  The beginning Citadel area can swallow you whole, become tedious, and become frustrating.  In the same way Elex has a hard push back at the beginning that can make the game frustrating.  This game has an actual learning curve and you will die constantly, especially when you first start playing.  Once I got beyond that I just kept coming back for more.

Pro tip: Play your first game (or first few hours) on easy.  It will give you a chance to feel out the systems because the game generally doesn't do a good job showing you how to play.

Positives-
Definitely replayable (You would need a minimum of three playthroughs to see everything this game has to offer)
Faction powers and armor give you a real sense of power progression
Fully Voiced
Unique world with memorable characters

Negatives-
Various bugs or glitches.  Including, if the power to your computer drops while the game is autosaving you will lose everything in that playthrough.  At least I did.
The starting Berzerker area will become stale. (Although that did push me to try other conversation options.)

Overall I would certainly recommend this game.

Saw the game and was fairly excited about the premise like a good number of people have been I am sure...

Where do I start...
The basic mechanics ARE NOT EXPLAINED IN ANY COHERENT MANNER. I know that tutorials can be tedious and boring, that is usually because the mechanics are intuitive and at the very least consistent.

Combat (Magic/Melee/ and Laser Rifles) should be the highlight of this game in particular is clunky, poorly tuned, and has the unfortunate side effect of aggravating the player. If a game is genuinely difficult, that is one thing, when you can get in your own way by hitting any button in combat, you have a serious problem. 

Progression is something most people take for granted in a fleshed out game. After doing some research, this game does qualify as fleshed out in the same way as the 2nd act of a game is fleshed out. There is no clear path of progression or even a hint towards one. Your initial quests are set at a difficulty that equate your equipment to that of a wet noodle (I tried it on easy/normal/hard for points of comparison). In short the game starts, random title screen, no tutorial or ease-in section, and then everything is mid-game or higher.

To sum up all my thoughts in a few words;
Good premise, bad game. VERY bad game. Spend your money on something that deserves it.

[h1]Un bijou imparfait qui ne plaira qu’aux RPGistes pures et durs, voilà ce qui correspond le mieux à ELEX.
Son gameplay si particulier propre à Piranha Bytes et sa difficulté extrême se rapprochant de Dark Souls vont décourager et tromper de nombreux joueurs tout comme il a trompé admirablement certains testeurs soi-disant « professionnels ».[/h1]

[b]Les + :[/b]
- Un scénario principal pas incroyable que je ne développerai pas mais dans un contexte par contre franchement sympa à la game of thrones en plus simplifié : [u]Sans spoil[/u], dans ce monde post-apocalyptique 3 factions au style bien opposé (Grosso modo les fanatiques religieux à la technologie avancée, les moyenâgeux à la puissante magie et les drogués sans aucune limite) sont embourbés dans une guerre plus ou moins ouverte entre eux, mais sont également menacé par une autre faction bien + puissante.
Tout cela sur un lit de magouilles et de traitrises et vous obtenez le monde d’ELEX.
- On retrouve des choix dans les quêtes qui vont quelques fois changer le cours de l’histoire mais surtout vos relations avec les factions et les pnj.
- Choisissez totalement vos alliés et vos ennemis, aucune faction ne vous est imposée et je pense même que vous pouvez vous en passer. Vous l’avez compris, niveau rejouabilité ça se pose bien.
- TOUS les pnj peuvent être tués sauf les compagnons (hmmpf…)
- Au niveau de la map on a connu plus grand mais avec une multitude de lieux se balader prend bien assez de temps comme cela haha
- Le paysage justement, il est magnifique ! De la neige, de la forêt, du désert, des ruines, des bases, des montagnes, des plaines… C’est un plaisir de se balader dans un monde si diversifié.
- Une multitudes d’armes au corps à corps, à une main, à deux mains, tranchant, contendant, armes à distance, à énergie, à plasma, à munitions, à gaz… qui peuvent être pimpées avec des effets, des améliorations…. Oui c’est un plaisir !
- Du craft, on a connu plus développé aussi mais il a le mérite d’être là.
- Un bestiaire pas énorme mais bien cool entre mutants en tous genres, animaux, humanoïdes, robots, il est très sympas.
- La difficulté en early, mid-game et mid-game + oh ouii on retrouve du Gothic là, vous allez spammer la touche de sauvegarde rapide et vous allez recommencer encore et encore certains combats, surtout si comme moi vous ne voulez pas vous balader en sneeky mais chasser tous ce que vous croisez !
- Le gameplay, du combat rigide mêlant esquives, parades, enchainements… très particulier qui ne va clairement pas plaire à tout le monde.
- TOUTES les options sont modifiables, la consommation d’endurance, les dégâts, la vie…etc… je pense, même si je ne comprends pas l’intérêt, que si vous souhaitez vous balader dans un monde de bisounours c’est possible.
Je pense avoir oublié certaines choses mais cela commence à être long, donc…

[b]Les moins :[/b]
- Graphiquement c’est pas ouf, les paysages sont beaux, le monde est beau, mais au détail c’est très vieillissant.
- Le gameplay : Oui les déplacements et le combat sont rigides, c’est rageant, c’est compliqué, mais c’est Piranha Bytes donc on connait et on apprend à aimer, MAIS…. Ou sont les attaques dirigées ??? On pare avec un clique, on esquive avec un autre et on attaque avec un troisième… et c’est tout ! Et certains testeurs osent dirent que les mécaniques des combats sont compliquées ! J’ai été extrêmement déçu sur ce point-là…
- L’approche RPG : Sur les stats (Force, endurance, intelligence…etc) rien à redire, mais sur les skills… déjà il n’y en a pas beaucoup et surtout, bien qu’ils soient divisés en branches différentes notamment entre les factions, ils sont finalement très ressemblant. La rejouablité ne se fera pas pour tester la magie à la place de la technologie par exemple, il n’y a que peu d’intérêt à cela.
- L’IA, mon dieu… ils sont aveugles déjà, vous pouvez pourfendre un type à 20 mètres d’un de ses potes, même en journée ensoleillé il ne le verra pas… et l’équilibrage ! Un exemple : j’allais attaquer une base avec des mecs armés, badasses et agressifs, puis je vois quoi, un marchand itinérant avec ses deux gardes du corps, ils prennent l’aggro et ripostent en lavant littéralement tout le monde…. Et des situations burlesques semblables on en croise de temps en temps malheureusement…
- Vos compagnons : Ils ne peuvent pas mourir mais ils peuvent s’évanouir, et je peux vous dire que cela va leur arriver souvent tellement ils sont nazes.
- Le EndGame : Déjà vous êtes pété de thunes assez rapidement, finalement le stuff ne sera jamais un problème c’est juste les stats qu’il faut pour pouvoir les porter qui complique la chose. Mais sur la fin voilà, vous faites masse de dégâts, esquiver les attaques devient un jeu d’enfant… Easy game =/
- Les armes à distance : Les trois quarts servent à rien, si cela ne stun ou ne fait pas trébucher, sont inutiles car 0 dégât sauf quelques exceptions et si vous faites un focus extrême sur la dextérité mais cela reste négligeable comparé aux dégâts au corps à corps.
- L’IU, le menu, l’interface quoi : C’est moche, pas pratique, il y a trop d’onglet, il n’y a même pas de système de « bazar », pour vendre il faut retrouver les objets inutiles dans l’inventaire… Ouais, c’est chiant.

[b]CONCLUSION personnelle :[/b]
	Je fais de belles sessions de jeu sans pour autant geeker h24 dessus. C’est un excellent jeu, je ne regrette absolument pas son achat, mais ses points négatifs font que je n’y passerai pas une grande partie de mon temps libre dessus comme j’ai pu le faire sur d’autres jeux auparavant.

怎么说呢，这是我买的第一个游戏，169元，当时犹豫了好久，印象特别深，里面的动作或许有一点僵硬，但是玩起来还可以，自由度很高。对话时，不知道怎么的就把某个NPC得罪了，然后任务进度就出现变化了，挺有意思的。另外，怪物有一点厉害，前期主要靠猥琐，有了伙伴，也只是可以欺负一下低等级的怪物，同等级都要两人一起上，而且怪物会招仇恨，一声嚎叫，附近的同类怪物就过来攻击了。怪物之间不同种类也有敌意，会出现两个怪物打得不可开交，你要是贸然冲上去，就会出现混合双打你。这个游戏没有职业，有派别，加入不同帮派，解锁不同的技能，也可以都不参加，有通用技能学习。升级有点慢，赚钱也慢，而且怪物没有等级区域划分，新手区没准旁边就是超高等级区域，然后就出现被撵得嗷嗷叫的场面。是一个可以长期肝的游戏，但是，游戏为啥更新这么慢呢，最新的更新是2017年年末的，敢问2018年都去干啥了，难道就打算把这个游戏当累赘一样打折打折处理了吗

Still have a very large chunk of the game left after 61 hours..... it has a few rough edges but I have greatly enjoyed my time with Elex.  Some nice twists in the main and side-quests, lots of player-agency in terms of making your own way in the world, lots of replay-value do to only being able to ally yourself with one of the major factions in a given play-through.... all-in-all just a really fun experience for those of us that enjoy deep, well-written RPGs with interesting world-building.  Combat is QUITE difficult early on until your stats are sufficient to use higher-level weapons but the point where you go from prey to predator is VERY satisfying as a result.  The combat is a step above typical RPG combat while being a step below what would be considered an "Action-RPG".  The graphics and music are above-average.... basically if you are someone who enjoys RPGs and is willing to endure a few rough edges- Elex could give you a ton of enjoyable hours.  61 hours into my first play-through I still have a LOT of side-quests and and I'm not too far into the main quest.  I expected the game to be good but it exceeded my expectations by quite a bit and I'm going to check out the rest of the games by Piranha Bytes.

Only played about an hour of the game before refunding due to the weird combat system.
This game seemed to be 25% really good and 75% really bad:

Cons:
HORRIBLE COMBAT SYSTEM! It makes it seem like a new indie developer made the combat system. For a newer game (at this price), the combat should be good and there are many games with good combat systems they could of just mostly copied and then added their combo system on-top. (This game did not have anything new to add to combat so copying/paraphrasing was all they did--they just did it horribly! Also, this isn't their first RPG game so they probably just imported the combat system from the old games, which I am sure was a criticism in their previous games as well.) If I'm going to have to play Dark Souls but with extremely large hit boxes... REFUND! This was the biggest reason for returning the game since the player would have to use it from beginning to end.
Generic alpha male protagonist with a scar on his eye who starts out more stupid and weaker than the rest of the world (even though he was the chosen one to do some sort of important mission?)
Too much lore that could of been easier to understand if the character explained a bit more when the lore comes up in conversations--as well him telling his own background on what his mission was to begin with and why the beginning scene happened (as I am supposed to be the character)
Speaking animations are weird and the surrounding NPCs will run into the conversations, which makes this whole game seem extremely silly
Have to spend lots of time finding people in the towns--the nameplates works wonderfully because I ain't got the time to unnecessarily check every NPC in the game!
Quest = Exp & Killing = Loot: this concept has never been logical to me and should more be the other way around where my reward for finishing a quest is loot or a perk such as a store discount and killing should give me more exp as that should be where the character gains... experience...

Pros:
Big open world
Many things to do--can tell that someone put a lot of thought into the environment. (Not so much thinking into the other parts of the game...)
Story seemed to have depth
Ability to choose a faction (which means 2x replay value)
Companions are very nice in these solo games so it not so boring when exploring and fighting

Overall:
If you have the patience to play Dark Souls, don't mind the indie-like combat system, can handle weird conversation scripts, and can ignore odd character animations (like with the jet pack) as well as odd controls, this game might actually be really good in terms to exploration, story, and rewarding gameplay hours.
For me--if the beginning can't entice me with anything worthy of $50, what's the point in making a game that can have many hours of gameplay?

This is a difficult game to love, visuals are great, music is good, game concept is interesting, but game mechanics are a bit too challenging.  Starting out, most everything you encounter can quickly shred you to pieces, so you learn allot of escape and evasion tactics.  If you do hone your skills with a wrench or a bow, you will find the XP gain for killing something is so minimal that it really wasn't worth the effort.   Your stat pool starts off with what you think are average numbers, (if you are expecting a D&D style game), but when you check the stats on a weapon you find and realize its minimum required strength is 50, you realize that 17 you thought was a good number means your character is still quite weak and hopeless.  Unlike some games where you can improve your skills by performing a related task, here you must find a trainer and pay him 500 in currency to learn the first level of the skill you are looking for.  Plus, just to add another layer of complexity, your Stat pool is not high enough to actually learn any of these skills, if you did have the money, (which you won't initially).  So you think, no problem, I'll just grind out a few levels, add points to the stat pool, then start really building out this character.   Well the only real way to level is to complete quests, since killing things offers no real XP, and the quests you get are not scaled to your difficulty level.  Plus, you can only track one quest at a time on the Map.  So you start off doing allot of exploring, which is fun in this post appocolyptic world, if you like the whole escape and evasion thing.  You can't tell if something is too strong enough to tackle until you actually hit it, and most things too strong for you can kill you with the first blow.  Plus human NPC's can be friendly or not, but you won't be able to tell from a distance until you get close enough for them to kill you.   F5 is your save game key, use it often.  Your progress towards the next level is shown as a bar, but without any numerical quantification you are left to guess how close you really are to getting 10 more points to increase your stat pool.  The one bright spot is you start off with a small jet pack, which lets you leap up for about 5 seconds to get over obstacles, or get away from something.  Learn to use this, and the game becomes much more enjoyable.  As you wander the map, you will discover portals that make traveling around much easier, you can jump to a portal from anywhere, so when you finally collect the last item a quest wants, you pop back close to the quest giver. 
While that is nice, it strangely doesn't seem to fit within the whole game concept.  For example the Beserker clan you start with hates technology with a passion, yet they don't seem to mind when you use a portal that is right in front of them, (that they themselves never use).  Overall on a 1 to 10 scale this game is a 6 for me.  It's not hopeless, but there are allot of other games out there that are more rewarding.

Tiene cosas muy positivas y cosas muy mejorables, empecemos por las segundas:

Encontré el sistema de combate muy frustrante no por su planteamiento, sino por su realización. Los hits no son realistas -esquivaba golpes que podía ver perfectamente cómo me golpeaban y a la inversa-, y hay ciertas cosas molestas, como que impactos con efecto de tumbar al enemigo al suelo no funcionen si el enemigo está reincorporándose. En otras palabras: te tumbo si estás de pie, si te estás levantando eres inmune a la caída -no al daño-. 

En general, el combate es lo más feo que le vi al juego.  

Otro aspecto negativo es que Piranha Bytes vuelve a caer en su Gothic. Parece que les cueste salir de ahí. No digo que no sea un juego maravilloso, sino que me falta mucha originalidad. Vuelven las tres facciones, vuelve el malvado boss final, vuelve el mineral mágico. En ese aspecto, es una llamada muy clara a la nostalgia. Ojo, esto no impide disfrutar y sumergirte en la historia (muy buena, por cierto), pero no esperéis jugar algo que no sea un Gothic -¡si hasta reciclan sonidos, por el amor de Xardas!

¡Y sin embargo es un juego que recomiendo enormemente!

La historia, como ya dije, es bastante atractiva. Tiene una campaña principal con una duración perfecta -ni te la pasas y se acaba el juego ni tienes que entregarle tu alma a nadie para pasarla-. El mundo es profundo, está muy bien desarrollado e invita a la inmersión más absoluta. Hay una variedad enorme de historias y personajes que puedes descubrir a través de las misiones secundarias o de la mera exploración -¡a ver si encuentras alguno de los easter eggs que escondieron!-.

El juego en sí no aburre ni se vuelve repetitivo en ningún momento. Estamos hablando de un rol muy bien implementado, notas los progresos de tu personaje, que te cuestan algo de esfuerzo pero saben recompensar muy bien. Además tus decisiones tienen consecuencias: el desarrollo de tu personaje te abre o cierra opciones de diálogo, cómo seas con los NPCs te puede facilitar o dificultar fases futuras, matar a X persona conlleva que Y se quiera vengar... Ains, el buen rol.

Confío en que la segunda entrega sepa mejorar la primera. Mientras, ¡a jugar ELEX!

Das Spiel von den Gothic- und Risenmachern ist ein RPG im Stiel eben dieses Entwicklers. Es gibt eine interessante Welt zu erkunden, eigentlich überall gibt es etwas zu entdecken und mit dem Jetpack hat man als Spieler ganz andere Möglichkeiten. 
Die Story ist dabei eher flach und es gibt drei Fraktionen, von denen man sich einer anschließen muss. Um in Gothic-Sprache diese zu benennen, es gibt die "Magier", die "Bürgerlichen" und die "Söldner". Magie ist hier zwar etwas anders, als bei Gothic aber die Fraktionen passen vom Aufbau her.
Das Spiel hat auch den einen oder anderen kleinen Logikfehler, so werden alle die sich nicht an die Regeln im Berserker-Lager halten in ein Tal "geworfen" (Gothic 1 lässt grüßen), dass sehr gefährlich sein soll und für das man einen Pass hat oder einen Aufzug (Jetzt ist das aber wirklich Khorinis).  Etwa 200 meter neben dem Aufgang zu diesem Pass gibt es aber noch einen zweiten, der ebenfalls aus dem Tal heraus führt und das Tal ist an den meisten Stellen nicht so schwer, wie die Landschaft direkt östlich von der Berserker-Siedlung.

I can deal with janky games as long as they are interesting, either because of the combat or the story or other gameplay gimmicks but this one is just dull and feels like it's gameplay ideas are outdated despite being released in 2017.

The setting of the gameworld seems interesting enough and the story on paper is pretty good, even if it's a bit generic. But the gameplay just drags it down. First of all, the voice acting is the dullest thing I've ever heard. For a commander, the main character has zero charisma, it would have been a lot better to just skip the voice acting altogheter and focus those resources into making it a more fun experience.

All the factions are annoyingly illogical, it's unbelievable that they were able to survive this long. The berserkers have this plant that's making the world livable again but for some reason none of the other factions thinks that "Hey being able to survive in the world is a pretty good cause". I want to join the bad guys just to destroy these idiots but I'm guessing you can't since there doesn't seem to be a skill tree for them.

The combat is unsatisfying and hard but not because it requires skill or good planning. You mostly fight against the camera and unresponsive controls. It's hard to get a decent weapon especially because you can't loot enemies. For some reason every enemy I encountered in the game has a ranged attack so you can't even use your jetpack to get a tactical advantage.
I played this for 13h and I'm not willing to put up with more to find out if it gets better, which I doubt. If the base game is this bland I don't care what they build on it.

This is a great example of a classic piranhabites game in the line of the Gothic series.

Pros: excellent storyline, really draws you in; very versatile choices and game play, you can be pretty much anything you want to be (within reason), yet at the same time you're limited by the number of levels you can possibly gain; combat is very similar to the Gothic series where it is very unforgiving and makes you think (challenging), yet once you figure it out, can be extremely rewarding and satisfying; smaller items of note: good map, good quest descriptions (typically), and good social interactions for your character.

Cons: if you aren't expecting it or aren't accustomed to it, combat can be absolutely deadly; not easy to disengage from an enemy if you get surrounded, except by jet pack; hacking can be a bit of a pain, same thing with lockpicking, but patience and clear thinking can help; did appear to have a few bugs in it, but nothing too difficult to manage.

All in all, a very fun and fascinating game.  The biggest thing to remember when playing, is save often, and use multiple save slots.  If you don't like how a conversation turned out, reload and try again.  Give it a chance to grow on you and you shouldn't be disappointed (unless you just don't like this kind of game, then oh well).
