An das Spiel Elex bin ich mit einigermaßen normalen Erwartungen rangegangen. In vielen Dingen weiß man bereits worauf man sich einstellen kann, da es die Piranha Bytes typischen Fehler etc. hat.

Also hier mal eine kleine Zusammenfassung:
Wie man es gewohnt ist startet man in Elex als ein Held der (so wie immer, aus irgendeinem Grund) keine Kräfte mehr hat. Diesmal ist es der Entzug des Elex, das man vorher immer eingenommen hat.
Anders als früher hat man diesmal allerdings einen Namen.
Die Welt wurde von einem Meteoriten zerstört, der Großteil der Menschheit ist tod. Allerdings hat der Meteorit auch ein neues Element auf die Erde gebracht. Das Elex. 

Nun ist es genau so wie früher in den ersten beiden Gothic Teilen oder in Risen, man kann sich drei Fraktionen anschließen.
Da gäbe es:
Die Berserker (ein Volk angelehnt an die alten Wikinger), die auf alle Technologie verzichten und nicht so begeistert sind wenn andere Leute sie nutzen.
Die Outlaws, ein Volk das sich in der Wüste niedergelassen hat und dort in "Freiheit" lebt. Sie basteln sich ihre Hütten, Waffen und Rüstungen aus Schrott zusammen.
Die Kleriker, ein hoch technologisiertes Volk, das eine eigene Religion befolgt.
Soviel dazu.

Zusätzlich gibt es noch die Albs:
Die Albs sind Menschen, die das Elex in großen Mengen und über einen großen Zeitraum zu sich genommen haben und somit immer mehr zu Maschinen wurden, da das Elex zwar die Kräfte steigert aber auch immer weiter die Emotionen unterdrückt.

Die Spielwelt:
Die Spielwelt von Elex ist, meiner Meinung nach, eine sehr schöne. Es gibt überall in den hintersten Ecken etwas zu entdecken und man merkt das die Welt liebevoll gestaltet wurde. Und das erste Item das man hier im Spiel entdeckt, was man dauerhaft benutzt, eröffnet einem völlig neue Möglichkeiten diese zu entdecken. Das Land ist in verschiedene Gebiete unterteilt. Da gäbe es einmal das Waldland von Edan, Heimat der Berserker. Dann die Wüste von Tavar wo die Outlaws zu finden sind, das Vulkanland von Ignadon wo die riesige Klerikerfestung zu finden ist, das Hügelland von Abessa und zu guter letzt das Reich der Albs, Xacor, das eine riesige Eiswüste ist. 

Die Grafik:
Wer bei Elex eine Grafische Neuheit erwartet, den muss ich enttäuschen. Die Grafik sieht zwar sehr hübsch aus aber man merkt, das sie nicht die aktuellste und auch nicht unbedingt die beste ist. Ich habe in meinem Rechner eine GTX 1080 und selbst die muss ziemlich arbeiten, trotz der älteren Grafikengine. Dennoch macht das Handgearbeitete und liebevoll gestaltete Land alles wieder wett. Mir macht es spaß stundenlang einfach nur durch die Gegend zu rennen und alles zu erkunden.

Die Mechanik:
Die Spielmechanik ist wie in den Gothic - und Risenspielen auch. Man fängt als kleines Würstchen an und wird am Anfang von alles und jedem erstmal aufs Maul bekommen. Das ändert sich aber relativ schnell und man wird sehr schnell stärker. 
Das Kampfsystem ist gewöhnungsbedürftig. Vor allem am Anfang ist es hakelig und schwer zu verstehen, aber man kommt relativ schnell auch rein und ich finde das System echt gut gemacht. Für den Anfang kann ich aber sehr eine Fernkampfwaffe empfehlen, da diese mehr Schaden machen zu Beginn.

Die Story:
Nun gut es ist ein Piranha Bytes Spiel. Man darf also keine Storytiefe wie z.B. bei einem Witcher - Spiel erwarten. 
Es gibt zwar jede Menge Quests und kleinere Geschichten aber diese sind meist beschränkt auf hole die oder töte das. Häufig halt Botengänge. Allerdings kann man in der Welt überall kleine Fitzel finden um die Geschichte der Welt nach und nach rauszufinden und es gibt auch einige Eastereggs zu entdecken. Dennoch ist die Hauptstory relativ spannend und durch das neue "Moralsystem" wirken sich entscheidungen stärker aus. Je nachdem wie ihr euch entscheidet bei Quests etc. verändert ihr euch. Handelt ihr Rational steigt euer Kältewert, handelt ihr emotional sinkt euer Kältewert. Dadurch bekommt ihr verschiedene Boni. Außerdem wirken sich viele Entscheidungen auf später aus. Aber das muss man selbst entdecken.

Fazit:
Ich kann jedem der die Gothic - oder Risenspiele (Gothic I + II) mochte nur empfehlen Elex zu kaufen und zu spielen. Allen anderen natürlich auch aber ich muss sagen das ihr keine Erwartungen wie bei Witcher z.B. haben solltet. Wenn ihr die nicht habt werdet ihr verdammt viel Spaß mit diesem Spiel haben :)

Ist ok, hat leider kein Levelsystem wie mans von Gothic gewohnt ist. Items/waffen im Shop sin wie immer zum größtenteils überflüssig, weil zu schwach und zu teuer.

Wenn man Geschäfte und Shops einbaut, warum kann man dann überhaupt soviele bessere Waffen finden ? Ergibt doch keinen Sinn.

Fürn Thumps down hats aber trotzdem nich gereicht, denn die open world is wirklich gelungen, viele Secrets und Easter Eggs zu finden. Also da haben sie sich echt mühe gegeben.

Я  пытался выделить на нее время, чтобы она мне понравилась и игре это не удалось.
Вообщем то, если сказать кратко, то хотите знать как чувствуется эта игра, махните мечом в начале и это чуство нелепости и убогости будет точным описанием сей игры. Она морально устарела, по механике похожа на серию райзн,  вас ничего не удивит в ней, разве что знакомые механики, которые либо вам нравятся и вы играете или нет. В остальном же все тут раздуто, карта конечно местами смотрится красиво, но какой толк в этой красоте, если на гектарах обитает пару кривых монстров, в целом похожих друг на друга, почти с одинаковой атакой?!  Диалоги написаны неплохо, но этого будет мало. Присуствует кое какая вариативность, но в основном это завязано на выборе фракций, исследовать карту скучно - гектары наполнены всяким хламом, монстры нужный для гринда, а от кучи заданий в начале разбегаются глаза, куда бы пойти, учитывая ваш уровень, не везде вы пройдете. Причем рядом с относительно хилыми мобами обитают до жути сильные, которые отправят вас в вальгалу раньше времени. Путешествие без союзника абсолютная глупость в этой игре. Причем механика стрельбы, что из лучевой пушки, что из лука одинаковая и  не отличается, увы, видимо движок на большее не способен. Я бросил играть, когда понял, что игра меня уже ничем не удивит и дальше врдяли мне будет интересно, а бегать минутами, даже несмотря на наличие телепортов меня как то утомляет, мало экшена, мало секретов, мало сюрпризов. Ради диалогов я не намере тут оставаться, даже несмотря на то что сюжет в принципе неплохой.

Итог: морально устарелая, раздутая и нудная игра. Неплохие диалоги присуствуют, но вся убогая (знакомая) механика не заставить Вас в ней задержаться надолго. Надо быть уопротым фанатом серии ризн и готики, чтобы в нее играть и чувствовать нотальгию по тем играм. Для совсем незнакомых может и покажется прикольным, но на мой взгляд, даже первая локация выполнена плохо, что не добавит энтузиазма заинтересованым. Проходняк. Она может Вас зацепить только сюжетом, увы.

Elex è il nuovo gioco dei creatori delle saghe di Gothic e Risen. 
L'ambientazione è molto particolare, ci sono zone tecnologiche e zone immerse nel verde, anche una zona che ricorda i film di Mad Max, ma in ogni caso possiamo definirla post-apocalittica.
E' il miglior gioco di ruolo che abbia giocato da anni a questa parte, la quest principale è molto bella da seguire ed il gioco è pieno di quest secondarie tutte di buon livello e senza troppi tratti da fattorino; io l'ho concluso dopo più di 70 ore facendo tutte le quest secondarie.
Graficamente si difende bene e le musiche sono variegate e ben eseguite, così come i sottotitoli italiani sono ottimi e senza errori ortografici.

Se posso fare un paragone, lo preferisco perfino a Fallout 4 e soprattutto non ci sono grossi bug, cosa molto apprezzabile in questo genere di giochi.
L'inizio è molto ostico, come ogni gioco di questo sviluppatore, però con il passare dei livelli avrete molte soddisfazioni sviluppando il vostro personaggio, in più aggiungo che il sistema di combattimento a me è piaciuto molto.

In definitiva consigliatissimo, in sconto a 20 euro è un acquisto obbligato !

5 main factions,  The Beserkers (viking hippies.  Nord Wood Elves?), the Clerics (brotherhood of steel basically), the Outlaws (if the Fiends from New Vegas were a playable faction) and some group i just encountered who are just some random people living on top of a mountain who want you to be leader.  And the evil Albs, who are very Enclave and High Elf like.  

The world and lore isn't as fun as the Fallout world, no nuclear apocolypse, just some magic comet that came and destroyed everything. No character creation but the main character is bland enough that you can still have emersion.

选择少，有时反而是一种幸福。

        这款游戏，还是熟悉的捡东西动作，熟悉的跑步方式，熟悉的镜头运作，希望能带来熟悉的游戏性。
        

        觉的这游戏，操作难，战斗系统烂的，你们完全可以换个方式来看嘛，不要看作老滚这种实时战斗的，而是看成回合制游戏，将战斗的每一招与闪避所花费的精力都量化成行动点，在砍怪的时候保证有闪避所需的行动点。

Wieso empfehle ich dieses Spiel?

Zu aller erst. Elex ist ein Pyraniabyts Spiel, das heißt alle Gothic und oder Risen Fans werden den Humor mögen. Es ist auch die typische Atmosphäre. Das heißt, die meisten sind Arschlöcher und von sich und dem was sie machen überzeugt, bis wir kommen. Es gibt wieder ein paar Fraktionen. 3 um genau zu sein. Berserker, Outtlaws und Kleriker. Die Welt sieht sehr schon aus. Über die Grafik kann ich nicht merken. Waffen und Rüstungen gibt es auch zu genüge. Ob Fern - oder Nahkämpfer beides ist wieder möglich. Auch als Magier kann man sich versuchen.

Doch obwohl ich dieses Spiel "Empfehle" musste ich ein bisschen wanken mit der Entscheidung. Den das Level System und das Kampfsystem sind beide echte Aufreger. Fangen wir mal mit dem Kampfsystem an. WARUM HABE ICH AUSDAUER? Ja ihr habt ab jetzt Ausdauer, die mit jeder Aktion, also Ausweichen oder Schlagen zuneige, geht. Die Ausdauer kosten sind auch sehr unrealistig. 2 Schläge Ausdauer weg. Und dann könnt ihr auch nicht mehr ausweichen.

Dann der Anfang in diesem Spiel ist so ABGEF'CKT, das ist der Wahnsinn. Man kann die Welt nicht wirklich erkunden, weil alle Gegner und Monster einfach stärker sind. IMMER. Das mit der Ausdauer macht es nicht einfacher. Man braucht locker 3 Stunden um überhaupt eine Chance zu haben durch die Anfangs Gegenden zu kommen. Und das wird im Spielverlauf auch nicht besser. Man muss wirklich so viele Quests wie möglich machen, um Erfahrung zu bekommen und stärker zu werden. Wie viel XP man braucht, um ein Lvl aufzusteigen, bekommt man nie gezeigt. Man kann kaum werte über den eigenen Spieler sehen. Und damit gehts auch schon zum Inventar. Das Inventar bzw. das ganze Interface wurde anscheinend montags gemacht. Unübersichtlich, Unspektakulär und lieblos hinge klatscht.

Mein Fazit es ist ein gutes Spiel, dass sich so anfühlt als wäre es nicht fertiggestellt worden. Wieso ich es trotzdem Empfehle.

Das Kampfsystem ist schwer und gewöhnungsbedürftig. Man kann es aber für sich selbst abändern. Man die Ausdauer ausschalten(super angenehm), den Schaden den die Gegner machen und den eigenen kann man erhöhen oder senken(unabhängig voneinander). So kann man das Spiel für sich selbst spielbarer machen. Und an das Interface gewöhnt man sich mit der Zeit.

Ich muss sagen, als ich das Spiel für mich angepasst hatte, wurde es besser. Denn unabhängig von dem Kampfsystem ist es ein sehr schönes Spiel.

ELEX is proof positive that you can spend enormous amounts of time and money building a RPG and get it all wrong anyhow.

It starts off bad, with no first-person view, a main character with laugh-out-loud voice-acting and terrible issues with texture resolutions unless you use obscure INI tweaks.

Ends with console-specific control schema, a combat system that forces you to stand around rather than giving you the freedom to run away, and a nonsensical damage system.  

I got through the first tutorial bits, got killed three times by a "Reaver" (right next to Mr. BlahBlahBlah after the Tutorial) whose armor magically ignored all hits, and basically, my Suspension of Disbelief was already exceeded; game uninstalled.

The problem here, I think, is that the developers wanted a magical world, but settled on an incoherent post-apocalypse, thought that the console crowd was their market, not the PC, and generally... the game just feels like it was a pretty lame port that wasn't well-thought-out.

I know that fans of this will say, "but you only played 1 hour".  It wasn't Fun in one hour; little things like "you cannot search for loot until you've put away your weapon", "enemies may be totally immune to your attacks", "welcome to the awful mess that is the character / inventory / etc. UI", long-winded dialogs, unskippable intro movies, etc., etc. got in the way.  Sorry, it's just not my cup of tea at all.  Next time, make a game where you don't hit level-walls immediately and where things make some kind of sense... and for goodness sakes, build better UIs that don't bog us down so much clicking on sub-menus.  

The whole felt like a weird combination of really ambitious world design and poorly-thought-out mechanical design, which, coupled with the complete disdain I felt for my alter ego, drove me to uninstall rapidly.

After a while playing this game, my thoughts on it slightly changed. I didn't get the similarities between it and the classic piranha bytes games (gothic/risen) at first glance. 

In fact, the main difference is that you are no longer a blank character with no name and past. Your name is Jax, and you must figure out why you've been betrayed by your own brother.

It is one of these games in which you start almost naked, lost, and you can go wherever you want, but no in a fake way like in most open world games in which you must wait to have the right character level to wander where you like. In fact, at the begining, almost every opponent you will encounter will shatter you, either they are human or beast-like. Combat is "dark souls-ish"; by that I mean it is based on quick/strong attack combos and dodging, with a short stamina bar. Ranged weapons are also avaliable. 
During your early adventures in the world of Elex, you will also notice that most  skill based dialog options are way above your range. You will feel like there is a lot of things to be done, but that you simply can't do anything yet.
But you eventually will be able to take part in the struggles of this world. I don't know yet if the choices you make are really meaningful on the course of the story, but that is what the game promises. Currently, I can only tell that there is definitely a lot to discover in this game.

The soundtrack is pretty good : music is almost only atmospheric but sounds fresh and not cliché. Dubbing is correct.
Graphics are even.

Be warned : The game is painfully difficult on the start. Quicksaves are your friends.

UPDATE : 
Be warned that the game is not perfectly polished. For exemple, your allies can stand in your way and will sometimes not do anything when you fight a NPC.

Tolles Spiel, für mich das beste Piranha Bytes Game seit Gothic 2.
Als großer Fan der Düsseldorfer Spieleschmiede trifft das Spiel völlig meinen Geschmack.
Sicher kein Spiel für jedermann, wie meist bei den Spielen von Piranha sind Grafik/Animationen zumindest teilweise nicht auf dem aktuellen Stand.
Das Kampfsystem wurde zwar teils erweitert zu den Vorgängern (Jetpack, Granaten, Lasergewehrte, Ausdauerbalken etc) aber ist wie gewohnt nicht gerade perfekt und fehlerbehaftet.
Ist für mich jedoch alles nicht so tragisch, ich finde die Spielwelt ist bisher nicht nur die größte sondern auch beste von PB!
Der rauhe Ruhrpottcharme ist erhalten geblieben, ja in Elex gibts sogar nur Fraktionen randvoll mit rauhen unsymphatischen Ärschen^^
Die Story ist für ein RPG OK, für PB-Verhältnisse sogar ziemlich gut.
Das Jetpack ist eine coole Ergänzung, mit der man leichter fliehen kann und die Spielwelt vertikal nutzbarer macht (bzw. ist die Spielwelt an sich vertikaler als in früheren Spielen), wenngleich auch das Handling noch optimiert werden sollte.
Der Mix aus Fantasy, Sci-Fi und Endzeit funktioniert überraschend gut, zumindest solange man nicht zu viel darüber nachdenkt^^ und bringt frischen Wind.
Alles in allem ein sehr gutes Spiel, auch wenns nicht für jedermann ist sollte zumindest jeder Rollenspieler einen Blick drauf werfen und PB Fans können bedenkenlos zugreifen.

This for me is the best PB game since Gothic 2. Beautiful (if a bit dated) setting, nice quests, large world and well thought-out factions. 
It mostly feels like a reimagined Gothic 2 in a new setting blending Sci-Fi and Fantasy elements. As is usual in this kind of games you need to pick your fights (and routes) carefully in the early game and the game world will gradually open up as you get more comfortable with the world and better equipment. Most of the high-tier equipment is locked away until you join a faction and climb their ranks, but it is possible to get to know and access to all of them before committing to a specific one. I can completely understand the caviats mantioned in other reviews, but for me (apart from the slightly dated visuals and sometimes clunky UI) those are based in the kind of game this is.

I recommend this game, but only barely.

Sollte man sich das Spiel kaufen? Wenn man ein Old school Gothic oder Risen erwartet, NEIN.
Pro:
Elex bietet eine abwechslungsreiche Spielwelt, mit in Game Questsystem (sprich zeigt an wo man hin muss), Schnellreise und Begleiterfeature. Die Quests sind abwechslungsreich und bieten die Möglichkeit auf mehrere Weise ein Problem zulösen. Ebenfalls finfinde ich es extrem GUT das einige Entscheidungen erst später Einfluss auf den Spielverlauf nehmen. So das man nicht eben mit einem schnellen Quickload eine zuvor getroffene Entscheidung rückgängig machen kann. Weil man einfach schon zuweit vorgeschritten ist und es teilweise bis zu einer Stunde dauern kann bis man seinen alten Spielstand wieder hergestellt hat. Das gibt den Spielentscheidungen eine Gewicht. Der Stilmix aus Scifi-Schwertschwingenden-Outlaw muss nicht jedem gefallen aber bringt eine angenehme Abwechslung zwischen den Settings.
Kontra:
Zu Spielbeginn ist es fast unmöglich die Starterquest solo zumachen. Es wird vorraus gesetzt das man sich schnellst möglich einen Begleiter zulegt und sich dann hinter ihm versteck. Um gelegentlich hervor zuspringen und einen Hieb auszuteilen oder man tank die ganze Zeit und hofft das es schnell vorbeit geht. Was bei Gruppen von Gegnern (2+) zu einem wahren Problem wird. Damit wird der Spielfluss unnötig zäh und beschwerlich. Gerade wenn man alle Quest der einzelnen Fraktionen machen will bevor man aufgenommen wird (wie z.B. in Gothic) damit man extra viel EXP bekommt. Ich habe mich dann geschlagen gegeben und anstatt alles mit zunehmen das Nötigste gemacht um mein Ziel zu erreichen. Das wirkte schon fast wie Arbeit und nicht wie Spass. Die Inventarnavigation, die Karte und Questverfolgung waren einfach nervig. Letzteres gerade weil man mit dem JETpackgürtel nicht mehr wirklich auf Hügel o.ä. achtet sondern einfach drüber fliegt. Bis es dann halt doch Orte gibt die nicht so einfach erreichbar sind und man sich aber schon so sehr an den Komfort gewöhnt hat. Und dann die technischen Makel, Eingaben werden nicht angenommen, Charakter rennt ohne anzuhalten ohne die Möglichkeit abzubrechen (musste neu laden) und Clipingfehler. Das Belohnungssystem ist auch kein Motivator, ich habe bereits die Vorraussetzungen für die 2. Stufe meiner Fraktion erreicht. Kann Sie jedoch nicht annehmen da ich nicht das nötige Level habe. Meine Rüstung ist auch noch die eines Anfängers da ich mir keine bessere leisten kann. Und meine Waffen sind auch noch größtenteils die von vor 17h.
Allgemein fand ich mich immer wieder in der Situation das ich einfach aus Frust das Spiel zur Seite gelegt habe und erst Tage später wieder anfing.

Fazit:

Ich habe bevor ich das Spiel gekauft habe schon gehört das es kein neues Gothic oder Risen ist. Auch die Bewertungen auf Steam lasen sich oftmals frustrierend. Dennoch ich dachte mir du das diese Reihe schon lange verfolgt du musst dem eine Chance geben. Und nach 24h in Game fühle ich mich als wäre ich über die Startfrustration hinweg. Die Quest sind sind mit vielen Folgequest verbunden und Entscheidungen nehmen wie gesagt Einfluss auf die Umgebung aber auch deine Questbelohnungen. Die Dialoge sind wie man Sie von Piraniabite kennt ruppig, nur das erkunden wird nicht mehr so sehr belohnt wie in den Vorgängern. Dennoch sollte man eine ordentliche Spule Gedultsfaden mitbringen wenn man sich für Elex entscheidet.

Not a bad little RPG but I don't think it's worth $50. I had Elex on my radar for a while and during a sale I picked it up for $20 and that seems about right. 

The game is your standard open world RPG where you're the "Chosen One" who has to save the world. The real standout though is the world you're trying top save. Elex has one of the most interesting settings and stories I've ever seen in a role playing game of this scope. Piranha Bytes basically took Skyrim, Fallout and Mass Effect and mashed them all together to make a super cool world for you to explore. Quests are fun, if a bit generic, and the enemies are varied and interesting for the most part. 

The only real down side to the game is the combat. It's extremely clunky and takes a lot of getting used to. In the end you realize that the most effective way to defeat enemies is to find a tower, hill or cliff that the enemy can't get up to and just spam ranged attacks. Fighting toe-to-toe is fun and rewarding but since the combat is extremely sluggish it's hard to judge your attacks and blocks against your opponents and 1 hit from even the lowliest creature will knock you down to half your hit points; even at higher character levels. And to top it all off you'll be wrestling with the camera if you're "locked on" an enemy. But after a while you start to ignore the fact that you're cheesing the combat and relying on exploits and just enjoying launching "nuke" attacks on groups of mobs a quarter mile away and watching the XP roll in and then walk on over to their bodies and strip them of their teeth and claws. I mean what's the difference in the fun you have between that and say Skyrim where you just stand and spam your main weapon/spell on an enemy who barely scratches you? No open world RPG has really deep combat mechanics to begin with and at least Elex makes you feel like you really are a low level character when you start out rather than just giving you shinier and shinier weapons to fight against bigger and bigger enemies while having basically the same experience.

Slightly crappy combat mechanics aside I recommend the game just for the setting which is easily one of the best worlds in any open world RPG's.

Новый тайтл от Пираний! Любителям Готики - брать обязательно!
Впечатления: В эту игру нужно погружаться. Как и в любую игру от Пираний. Больше чем в другие игры. Чем всегда и славились их игрульки - это живым и проработанным миром. 
На месте фракции и фирменный процесс вступления в какую-то одну из них. 
На месте и система "убери оружие, парень!" и "убирайся прочь из моего дома!".
На месте и "готично-ризеновская" прокачка с учителями, которые обучают перкам за монетки (здесь - элексит).
На месте жестокий и беспринципный мир, где с самого начала можно нарватьс на тролля, где обычные противники могут вынести тебя с одного-двух плевков на начальных уровнях, где до момента, когда ты можешь вольготно блудить по миру - тебе нужно попотеть и прокачаться. Эта игра достаточно хардкорна и напичкана различными тайниками и загадками. Желаете легкой прогулки и привыкли, что игра бережет вас и боится покалечить - тогда смело проходите мимо. Здесь все наоборот.
Графика: она есть. Художники поработали как всегда прекрасно. Пейзажи игра выдает, зачастую, очень приятные. Адепты просмотра пикселей в упор и просчитывания количества полигонов на пятке ГГ - тоже проходите мимо. С технической стороны тут графического пиршества нет.
Звук и музыка: Как и всегда у Пираний - на твердую "пятерку". Из пяти.
Сюжет и квесты: Сюжет клиширован и содержит массу отсылок к другим играм, книгам, фильмам, но...подается весьма оригинально. Квесты варьируются от "подай-принесы", но неплохих детективных расследований (но не уровень Геральта). 
Спорные моменты: 
1) боевая система. Перекаты-клик-клик-отошел. Полоска выносливости теперь иссякает быстрее и в целом (играл за боевого мага берсерков) выглядит лучше того, что было в 3м ризене, но все еще "не то"
2) инвентарь. Громоздкий. Неудобный. Куча вкладок. Нет нормальной сортировки предметов.
3) странное распределение опыта за разных врагов. Болотников валить тяжеловато до 15 лвл. Про ночеров вообще молчу. И сколько же за них опыта дают? 60 и 90... Разбойника или солдата альбов завалить проще, а там - 100-150... И есть еще пташки, которые дохнут от одного взгляда и за них дают около 40-70 экспы...хм.
4) ранги "холодности" можно было бы сделать и понятнее. А то "спонтанный" - и какой же это? Хотя отдельные перки увеличивают урон "если холодность ниже 20" и т.д. Как же считать, не залезая на сторонние ресурсы?
5) глючащий интеллект и багованные квесты (миссия невыполнима)
В общем и целом - прекрасная игра (не без недостатков). Надеюсь на скорое продолжение и желаю Пираниям не слушать ноющих про "устаревший геймплей" и продолжать делать свою идеальную игру. 
Моя оценка - 9/10 (холодность достаточна)

A post-post apocalyptic adventure in which you work to save Magdalan from the grips of its oppressors, only to find the world is much more complex than you first thought. If you are a fan of other big titles in the RPG Genre such as The Witcher: Wild Hunt and Fallout 4, you may enjoy this title as well. It takes much in terms of map style and sci-fi themes from the Witcher, with companions and building raport with characters via dialogue choices from Fallout. If you were to combine these two games and make the theme about the world after a meteor hit, this would be what you got. The other key difference is that both other titles, perhaps because they are from much larger studios, are much more refined all around. From gameplay to graphics, Elex cannot compete, but it is still a great an enjoyable game that will satisfy your RPG itch.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
[list]
[*] [b]Side quests[/b] follow the classic do 5 extra sub-side quests in order to solve this side quest kinda style
[*] [b]Melee combat[/b] is pretty wonky. Theres a lot of dodging and timing of attacks in order to have a decent battle. If you hit first at the right time, you can continue a chain of hits without the enemy being able to respond, likewise, if they hit you and you are mid-animation, you might get caught and they will chain hits against you and you will not be able to escape/dodge/block/etc.
[*] [b]Ranged combat[/b] is virtually useless. Weapons dont hit hard enough and energy weapons are easy for both you and the enemy to dodge because the projectiles are too slow
[*] [b]Lighting[/b]: the world is overall bright, but entering buildings is always very dark until your eyes "adjust" to the indoors, but it seems to take too long
[*] [b]Story Line[/b]: The factions make more sense the more you play through their side quests, but the first couple hours can be kinda disorienting. There a huge amount of narration and exposition from each character about their backstory and how their faction fits into the grand scheme of the world, which is both necessary and difficult to absorb all at once. I found that if you explore the map and unlock portals for later, it helps orient you
[/list]

[h1]Map & Environment[/h1]
[list]
[*] [b]Destroyed building[/b] from the "old world" exist for exploration and we are told no one understands how technology before "the event" worked. Lots of cars, computers and buildings just used as junk
[*] [b]Creatures[/b]: maybe 90% passive until provoked, not really explained, but kinda like Fallout's rad-animals - things poisoned, mutated, and generally supersized by "the event"
[*] [b]Graphics[/b]: they work. Not super high quality. It will still look great on a 4K, but it may be more geared for a 1080p. For being a 2017 game, it feels a lot older. like 2007/Halo 3 animaions era
[*] [b]Other Characters[/b]: the world is full of people to talk to about... stuff. sometimes it advances the plot, sometimes its just like.. *skip!*. one thing that does get kinda old is the conversation so frequently starting with "who are you.. youre not allowed through here"... like gtho my way. If you talk mean back to them, they often surrender and are like "oh man, dont need to be so rude"... geez, they dish but cant take
[/list]

[h1]Mechanics[/h1]
[list]
[*] [b]Controls[/b]: a bit rigid. Everything you do from jumping and climbing to fighting and pressing buttons must be very deliberate. thers not much forgiveness for bumping into objects, getting around things or clicking the right thing when two things are near each other
[*] [b]Fighting[/b]: blunt weapons, archery, laser/energy weapons, and magic - kinda a mix of medieval and futuristic stuff, with emphasis on the medieval. Ammo is hard to come by, and once you get an effective battle axe, it hits 2x as hard as most ranged weapons so theyre kinda pointless
[*] [b]Exploring[/b]: open world, hidden locations, curious sub plots, dicover notes that describe something that happened
[*] [b]Factions[/b]: by choosing a faction at the begining of the game, you unlock certain abilities that will go with you throughout the rest of the game
[*] [b]Day/Night cycles[/b]: nights are not very dark, which is nice, but the tools you have to light up dark environments (flares, lamps) are pretty much useless and have certain limitations (like only 5 flares can be activated on the groud at once)... good luck exploring dark areas (use your magic?)
[*] [b]Lockpicking/Code Hacking: not much to say here. its easy, just gotta unlock the skill
[*] [b]Discussions[/b]: choices during conversations enhance certain levels of your character which ultimately impact your gameplay style (to some degree)
[*] [b]Relationships[/b]: your choices impact how much characters like you, but as long as you dont get them to want to fight to the death, it does not seem to impact the story
[*] [b]Inventory[/b]: seem to be able to carry as much of whatever as you want with minimal impact to weight/carying capacity (yay)
[/list]

[h1]Things to Fix[/h1]
[list]
[*] [b]Character Models[/b]: the character model for the random bad guys or villagers are copy and pastes with few to no differences across villages - Different clothing, maybe different hair style, but even same voices.
[*] [b]Factions[/b]: They are heavily unbalanced, favoring something and pretty much ignoring everything else. Too much to go into here, just read up on the factions/YouTube before you choose one to see what best fits you.
[*] [b]Fall Damage[/b]: 2ft drop fine, 6ft drop ouch, 8 ft+ drop DEAD. Seriously messed up falling mechanics. you end up using your jetpack a ton for getting off stuff
[*] [b]Learning Skills[/b]: This whole mechanic needs some work. Its really annoying to have to google what character gives you lessons on crafting, which other on fighting, etc. Just need to be simplified and clarified up front
[*] [b]Trading[/b]: Only certain merchants have certain products, but I think Fallout's handling of this was much better.
[*] [b]Crafting[/b]: Its just clunky. Too much googling involved. Maybe adding the little map indicators like in Farcry for types of plants/animals would be nice
[*] [b]Map[/b]: Needs to be improved a lot. its glitchy and the icons are kinda too big. gotta constantly be zooming in and out to see details. Minimap on the HUD should have zoom settings and a partially opaque overlay of the actual environment and not be only what ammounts to a radar screen with no scale, just a North pointer.
[*] [b]Loot[/b]: There is a ton of garbage loot you can pick up - spoons, mugs, etc. They seem to have no use and an option to "sell junk" should be added to traders menus
[*] [b]Teleporting[/b]: When you tp, you always see the NPC's in the EXACT same locations and often talking about the same exact things. Not very dynamic environmentally speaking + kinda kills the mood
[*] [b]Overall Play-Through[/b]: Would like to have seen the game last a little longer. Certain parts of the map you dont ever visit unless you go out there yourself just to explore - seems like a lost opportunity. Other parts, the only reason you ever visit is to activate the portal, but thers not much to do.
[/list]

[h1]Rating: good (7/10)[/h1]

[b] Introduction [/b]
ELEX is a third person RPG set in a futuristic phantasy world where you play as Jax, an ex-commander of superior Alb forces who after losing his strength and skills has now to find out his role on the planet Magellan.

[b] Gameplay & Story: 8/10 [/b]
The story starts as in other Pirahna Bytes games, the only difference is that you are not a nameless hero, but actually your deeds as an Alb commander have made your name as Jax, the Best of Xacor, quite famous. Most of the main story is bound to your past and finding out what happened, that lead to your downfall and betrayal, and for that you have to join one of the three factions. Suprisingly, the factions are really different and offer great immersion level into the story of Magellan. The gameplay in ELEX consists mostly of doing the quests, collecting items in the world and killing some free walking monsters. As in other Gothic-like RPGs, it picks off really slow since your world knowledge and combat abilities limit you to a very margin area. The choices you do through out the main and side story quests matter for your attitude, that will decide the happiness of your companions and the ending. The story is quite well written with multiple far reaching choices, however there were few points that disappointed, like for example after reaching a faction the main faction quests have nothing to do with the global world story anymore and become simple "go fetch" or "go kill" quests.

[b] Combat & Challenge : 5/10 [/b]
It is actually hard to give a rating for combat in ELEX since it has some interesting elements, but on the other hand is watered down to very few choices if you want to have decent progress. Some points in combat were absolutely broken, like when you side-step but an enemy still hits you even though not being even close to you or shots flying through enemies. Some enemies could stun lock you till you are dead, especially if there are 2 or more of them (hello Albs with Flamethrower...). The combat against human enemies that supposed to be the hardest, especially endgame bosses, is actually one of the easiest since you can just circle them until they start hitting and simply give them a back massage with your hammer or axe. So the only challenge in the game is that at the start you are so weak, that almost any enemy almost anywhere on the world can one-shot you. The combat behaviour of monsters is very easy to learn, since there are only about 5 different types of enemies, which always do the same attacks no matter their colour or your progression into the game.

[b] Graphic & Interface : 6/10 [/b]
The interface in ELEX is fitting the theme of the game, but looking quite aged for a game released in 2017 (more like a 2010). The graphic is very diversified - on some places I thought that they actually put some work into it, some other places like snow/ice and the desert were so simple and contain tons of reused models and landscape. The berserker city is definetely the most detailed and cool place in the whole game, while the other both cities seemed to get a little bit less love. Tons of enemies are just re-coloured models and the main enemy in this game - the Albs are looking all the same. The only models that differ from each other are the weapons, however it does not matter that much as well since there are only few decent weapons in the game, so your choice of usage is very limited anyway.

[b] Progress & Mini-Games : 7/10 [/b]
The progress in ELEX is very simple to describe - gold2win. You simply skill as frist the ability to create so called Elex potions, which increase your stats and give skill points. After that you simply have to farm money either by quests, killing monsters and collecting their trophies or just gathering loot. After about level 10 you can explore most of the world, after 25 you become strong enough to kill the touphest enemies and after 35 you become God and have so much HP and power to kill even the hardest enemies in seconds without caring if they hit you on hardest difficulty.
ELEX contains mini-games for hacking and lock-picking chests, of which only the former introduces a new mechanic with small digit games, while the latter is as always picking locks in the right order.

[b] Audio & Immersion : 7/10 [/b]
As mentioned in the story section, the story and some places offered great level of immersion into this mix of sci-fiction and phantasy, while on the other hand some parts of the game, especially the bad combat and collecting hundreds of plants that seemed to be randomly placed all over the world, broke the immersion. The audio offered by the music designers actually lasted for me about 80 hours, so the hits felt impactful and the music was fitting the situations of discovery, battles and choices.

[b] Side-Notes [/b]
[list]
[*]This game offers a single player long campaign with 50+h if you finish all the side quests as well.
[*]This game contains steam achievements that are sometimes quite hard to get and require either replaying of re-saving.
[*]This game offers mediocre replayability since its heavily story based. but you might want to experience other factions or weapon choices.
[/list]

[b] Conclusion [/b]
ELEX is a good Gothic-like RPG set in an interesting and at some places beautiful world with an immersive story line and far reaching consequences of your choices made through out the game. The combat is lacking, but if you consider the game more of a walking and quest RPG with character progression, it will not bother you much. It contains some references to the old Gothic games and some other easter eggs, that make the world and some encounters more interesting. Overall, i can recommend it playing for the storyline and as an example of a successful combination of Sci-Fi and phantasy elements in one world.

I had heard both good and bad things about ELEX since its release last fall and had been kind of o the fence about getting it but got distracted by other games and sort of forgot about it. The 60% off Black Friday sale was just too good to pass up so I picked it up. And boy am I ever glad I did.

It's a very good 3rd person, open world RPG with a very engaging story and very competently voice acted. The combat difficulty take a bit of getting used to (especially for my 69 yr old reflexes :)) but it's very worthwhile persevering even if you have to run away quite frequently at the beginning. As you gear up and level it starts getting quite a bit easier and by the end of the game you do feel quite powerful. This is a very nice change of pace from many other RPGs the merely go from easy to easier so you never really get to feel your character's progression. You certainly feel that progression here.

The graphics are definitely good enough and some of the world is just gorgeous and contrary to what I had read in some places (probaby because it was patched a few times) it is actually quite technically tight with very few bugs or glitches.

It's a post apoc game with a twist in that one facion of tree-hugging technophobes has discovered magic and they play very much like a fantasy RPG medieval faction and a different faction are technophiles and make you feel like you're playing a Mass Effect game if you side with them. The 3rd faction, the outlaws, plays more like your typical Fallout game. 

That's right: think Skyrim meets Fallout meets Mass Effect and you have the gist of the game play possibilities. That they manage to pull this off with both a believable story and combat balance is almost a miracle but pull it off they do.

If you're on the fence about this one take the plunge - it's worth it.

Elex ist ein mehr oder weniger typisches Piranha Bytes Spiel.
Der Mix aus fantasy und sience fiction/post Apokalypse ist recht gut gelungen und auch gut in die Geschichte eingearbeitet.
Darüber hinaus können hier Entwickler wie z.B. Bethesda eine ganze menge über Questdesign lernen. Viele der Entscheidungen die man im laufe des Spiels trifft erzeugen eine gewisse Resonanz an anderen stellen des Spiels, die auch funktionell gut ineinandergreifen. Desweiteren bietet die Entscheidungsfreiheit bei vielen Quests auch die möglichkeit "böse" oder "destruktiv" zu spielen und so durch getroffene oder ausgelassene Entscheidungen die Spielwelt und Charaktere zu beeinflussen, was wie im klassischen Fallout Stil am Ende des Spiels für einen zusammengefasst wird.

Der jedoch größte Faktor bei diesem, wie bei älteren Piranha Bytes Spielen sind die Dialoge und  die hervorragende Vertonung der Charaktere.
Zwar ist die Art der Charaktere natürlich Geschmackssache und wird evtl. nich jedem so sehr gefallen wie mir, doch unabhängig davon weit über dem bakannten Niveau der neueren Fallout Spiele z.B..
Leider kommt an Dieser Stelle auch das große Kontra, denn dies ist leider bei der Übersetzung ins Englische verloren gegangen, was dem Spiel den größten Reiz nimmt, da die Qualität der Dialoge bereits im Detail der Wortwahl beginnt.

Zum Kampfsystem:
Beim ersten durchlauf habe ich das Spiel auf normal gestartet, was gut zum lernen der Steuerung war, jedoch schnell zu einfach für meinen Geschmack.
Als ich das zweite mal auf schwer gestartet habe kam dann noch eine ganz besonders nette Überraschung, da NSC's viel mehr Fernwaffen verwendeten als zuvor und Kämpfe viel anspruchsvoller wurden.
Es mag sein, dass die Kämpfe vor dem großem Patch nicht ganz so ausgewogen waren, ich für meinen Teil habe es auf jeden Fall genossen mal wieder ein Spiel zu spielen, das mir auf die Fresse gibt wenn ich zu blöd bin.

Beim Design der Karte sticht zwar doch mehr der fantasy Teil raus, doch ist auch hier wieder das von Piranha Bytes gewohnte Maß an Qualität und Detail zu finden. Durch die Einführung von Jetpacks ist jeder Winkel der Karte erreichbar. Dies macht schnell die absolute Sorgfalt klar mit der die Karte angelegt wurde.

Stabilität:
Ich habe keinerlei probleme mit dem Spiel gehabt, seien es nun Abstürze oder sonstige Bugs.


Für mich reiht sich dieses Spiel gut neben den alten Gothic Spielen ein und somit auch neben Spielen wie Fallout 1&2 und Borderlands


Aufgrund der schlechten Übersetzung kann ich das Spiel zwar nur auf deutsch empfehlen, aber für jeden oldshool gamer dürfte es ein Genuss sein.

I've played enough to get a feel for the game. 

1. Exploration is pretty fun. This is an open world game, and the player can run pretty much anywhere in the map. The main issue with that is some areas have very strong monsters that are hard to kill. But that's what the jetpack is for, right? Just jetpack to some very high location and run like hell. I tend to keep to the hills and go around the monsters to explore new areas and take a look at the land. My goal is mostly to find the teleporters, that will help you do fast-travel to interesting places and to give you short-cuts to the goal of a quest. 

2. Combat is wonky, and hard to avoid when exploring. It does not feel as fluid as other open world games, and it depends heavily on stamina. Low stamina? Forget about living, especially with packs of wild animals after you. Try to focus on either long-range at first, or luring each animal away from all the others and take that one down alone. Otherwise, you will die. I put it on easy initially, as I'm way more interested in story and exploration than combat, but even then it's hard. The power attacks you do when in combat depend directly on stamina, so watch that bar. 

3. Lore and worldbuilding is pretty darn good. The factions each have their own lore and history. Characters have backstories and motivations for their actions. Each faction has it's own infighting and quests to bring harmony to those within the faction. And each faction has its own motivations and goals for the world in general. There's different playstyles depending on which faction you join as well, so there's multiple ways to play the game. Want to go full on magic and sword/bow style? Berserkers are for you, and ironically, they are the ones "healing" the land and planting the new growth forests. Want to do shotguns and the like? Outlaws may be more your interest. Energy weapons? Clerics for sure. 

4. Skilling: you get 10 attribute points with each level, which is good because the skills you need require a LOT of attribute points to unlock. These skills can only be learned from specific teachers as well. So find those teachers. Also, the game requires a LOT of elex in order to even learn these skills. So expect a lot of grinding to get elex. Basically loot everything, do as many quests as possible, and carefully plan what skills you really want so you don't waste elex on something that isn't toward your goal. You will have to plan out your skills because Elex isn't all that easy to find, especially in the beginning of hte game. It gets a bit easier to locate once you have the skills to actually survive. 

5. Story: I don't care about the protagonist's story at all. Just as an FYI. But the story of the factions and the world in general is far more interesting than Drax's story. So some folks may like his story, and some may prefer the stories of other people in the world. Hit and miss I guess.

So overall? 

Fun gameplay, combat could use some work, strategy needed for determining skills, and lots of interesting lore and people to meet.

I'd say get this game on a sale. Just don't expect it to be fallout with magic. It's it's own little niche of cyberpunk/steampunk-magic hybrid really.

Right, so. On the surface, this game seems like it'll be fun. Post-apoc combining fantasy and scifi elements sounds like a good time, right?

Done well, it would be. Elex, sadly... does not do it well. Combat is janky with some very obvious and unsettling quirks. Using a fully automatic laser weapon, you can hit an enemy multiple times but only one hit seems to count. Instead of chewing through an enemy, you're just holding still as it comes up to pounce you and rip your throat out. 

Worse still, XP does not scale for tougher enemy variants. Your starter enemies, with Runt prefixes on their names, count the same as the normal ones. This might be by design, but a harder enemy should be worth more, right? Different enemies can net you more XP, but you cannot easily level through combat. The ONLY easy way to level, in fact, is through quests. Which, well... will often have you traipsing through areas with tougher enemies that will, again, happily rip your throat out. You'll spend most of your time running away, early on.

I wanted to like this game. I really did. And for a while it was fun. At first, it was janky, and there's a learning curve. Then I got to know it, and could play for hours. Hell, I DID play for hours. But... the more I play, the less I want to. Lesson learned. My advice? Avoid it until/unless they fix it.

This game has been sitting on my wishlist since it first appeared on Steam and during the 2018 Fall Sale I decided to take the dive. I was apprehensive due to the reviews criticizing the clunky camera and combat system... that said, I am a huge Souls fan, a huge fan of open world games and have a ton of RPG experience under my belt and figured I will overcome!

I absolutely LOVE this game! It portrays a hostile post apocalyptic wilderness and it feels like it... you can't aimlessly wander around with no regard for what you might run into, you must plan your expeditions and prepare accordingly. The combat at first will feel exactly like critics mention, but no, you do not need exploits, you merely need to adapt and overcome.

The ravenous dodo birds and demon dogs gave me a hard time initially, until I discovered and properly adjusted my combat style to theirs. Whacking dodos with quick attacks are pointless, use your strong attacks and chain-combo them properly evading at just the right moment. I went from downing half my healing supplies for a single enemy to barely needing any if I keep my wits about and concentrate on my opponents.

I leveled up, not my in-game character, but my game-play ability... The very same level 7 character that used to jet-pack onto rocky outcrops to deal with dodos and devil dogs at range, now efficiently hunts raptor packs alone, with an axe!

If you want the deep dive continue reading... (TLDR)

The setting and story-telling

I am also very surprised at how well Medieval Fantasy, Scrapyard Western and Hi-Tech Sci-Fi is blended in this game. Prior to Elex I would have cautioned that such a concept is overly ambitious, but my doubts are put to rest. As a player I identify with the protagonist, I have the same questions with regards to the world and events which is neatly portrayed in the story telling. I find the lore intriguing and the overall setting fascinating. Choices and conversation have very profound impact on the play through, for example a potential companion can either be recruited to your cause or killed as a rival...

Voice and Animation

I don't care much for AAA Holywood style voice acting or motion captured animations. I thoroughly enjoy indie games such as Balrum, Stardew Valley, FLT and the like. Great gameplay and story telling trumps bells-and-whistles, but they sure can complement an experience. Elex has very average voice acting, nothing phenomenal such as BioWare games, but certainly not as cringe-worthy as Guild Wars 2. The combat system and animations are not as fluid as Souls, but it succeeds at what it sets out to do...

Overall Look and Feel (Graphics and Controls)

The game is good looking in my opinion and much less demanding than a number of other titles that do not even manage the level of fidelity. I love the brightness adjustment required when moving between overly bright and dark areas. The UI menus are well organized, intuitive and fluid to use.

Combat System

I would describe it as a blend of the Kingdoms of Amalur and Souls combat systems. Timing based combos, stamina management, timed blocks, evades and parries, with death as a consequence of failure and elation a reward for success! This is most certainly not a button mashing combat system, nor a if you can combo you win combat system... You must adapt your attacks and sequences to each individual enemy.

Conclusion

Elex is a rare gem that manages to impress and surprise me! It is highly recommend...

I was very interested in this game for a long time and finally bought it
as an early christmasgift for myself. I was well aware of the type of game,
a game that would kill you and punch you in the face while doing it... for extra measure.

There is a Roadsign i come to think of when i play this game.
'Tresspassers will be shot, survivors will be shot again' - and you'll love getting shot.

I absolutely LOVE getting my face smashed in by this game, because it's the game's
way to telling me that i either screwed up and need to learn the proper way,
or come back when i've grown more muscle..

I recall spending almost 1 hour fighting my way up a tower that i had to turn off,
the majority of enemies were "my level", and it was still hard. I think i reloaded about
15 times before i even beat the guards outside the entrance... and there were 2 of them.

Everything in this game CONSTANTLY hits hard, and if you think you can go "godmode"
by putting on the endgame armor.. think again.
Elex will constantly challange you as a player, keep you on your guard and 
look around before you engage enemies - or a quick death can be around the corner.

The storyline is of "Bioware" quality, it's engaging and takes you all over the map,
puts you into contact with interesting NPCs and companions, amazing scenery
and downright deadly areas with poisonclouds, lava and radiation.. a wasteland.

Elex's Companions are amazing. Many people has complained about the lacking AI,
but i haven't seen any issues apart from the companions stopping to fight
if you haven't engaged the enemy in a while.
But the companions storylines themselves as well as their conversations
and reactions to your choices, makes any "issues" with the AI fade away,
you'll have too much fun.

I died SO much.. repeatedly, in the start of this game, but i realized it
was a learningcurve, i don't think i have every enjoyed reloading as much
in any other game - but then again.. i love Demon Sould on PS3.

I've read that alot of players finds the combat "clunky".. but it's not,
it just takes time and practice, and combat works just fine.


Elex also has a very cool questmechanic that i can't recall having seen
in any other game, and it's a mechanic that will make you think really hard
before you set out to complete quests for people.
In Elex, doing a quest for one NPC, might anger another NPC to the point of
them not talking to you or even outright trying to kill you, and that will
in turn take away any possible questlines from that NPC.

Here's an example. I was trying to build up my status with a faction,
and during my travels i came across a group of refugees that was looking for safety.
So i went back to the village and told a man about these refugees and he said
he would help so i gave him the location.   I later found out that he sent a group
of warriors to murder the refugees..  so i killed him as punishement for murdering innocents.

This caused all the questlines possible from this character to vanish... quiet obviously,
but it also caused the village chieftan to be angry with me..  but i had to avenge the refugees.

There is also another system in the game called "coldness" which reflects how much humanity
you have left in you. This will greatly impact your endgame options for
certain quest, so personally i'm trying to keep as much humanity as possible for my playthrough
by picking the "correct" conversation options.


The craftingsystem is simple and amazing, it makes you want to literally loot everything
that isn't chained down, because  you'll have use for it. Pretty flowers and junk,
it's all usefull at some point for you.
You can even make potions that gives you XP and attribute-points.. but at a cost of your soul.

Animals drops meat, meat can be eaten raw or fried, or even cooked with more ingredients to
give you a much much better dinner.

Da habe ich mich so drauf gefreut, und dann wurde ich doch enttäuscht. ELEX ist ein Mix aus Gothic und Arcania. Meine Güte, die Kritiker lobten dieses Game bis in den Himmel und Werbung wurde gemacht und, und, und.

Wie es in einem RPG eben so ist läuft man sich die Füße wund und versucht sich mit banalen Nebenquests ein wenig hochzuleveln.

Das ist ja alles gut und schön, aber das es so langsam von statten geht, war mir nicht bewusst. 
Man kann sich nicht die wichtigen Dinge, wie Schlösser knacken oder ein Heiltrank brauen, nein da braucht man erstmal einen Lehrer, der dir das beibringt. Und nein nicht einfach so, es kostet verschiedene Dinge und meist auch ne Stange Geld. Und das muss man sich vorab erstmal verdienen - stimmt Geld ist nicht gleich Geld, hier sind es Elexsplitter. Das ist die Währung.

Man kann sie natürlich auch klauen oder man findet sie in der freien Natur. Das meiste aber verdient man sich mit den Nebenquests. Und im Laufe des Spiels kommen immer wieder diese Quests, bei den man sich echt die Füße platt laufen muss. 
Es gibt natürlich auch ein Transportersystem, die man aber vorher finden muss, dann kann man sich zu einem nahe gelegenen Ort "beamen" lassen. Aber sowas gibt es ja in fast jedem RPG.

Mir macht es Laune wenn ich Gebäude durchsuchen kann, denn man findet dort immer was, das man für ein paar Elex- Splitter verkaufen kann.
Worauf ich auf das Inventar komme: man kann sammeln bis "der Arzt" kommt. Keine Beschränkungen! Das finde ich toll! Sogar für eine kaputte Lampe bekommt man was.

Das Kampfsystem ist wiederum schlecht: wenn man angegriffen wird, bleibt man solange an dem Feind "hängen" bis dieser tot ist, man kommt äußerst schlecht von ihm los und somit kann jeder andere dafür sorgen das ich ins Gras beisse. Das heißt das man nur Einzelgegner töten kann, aber nicht 2 oder 3 gleichzeitig oder im Wechsel. Und so ist es auch bei den Tieren.

Der Sound ist auch nicht besonders: Wenn man im Wald ist und man läuft über Holz, dann hört es sich eher nach einer hohlen Kiste an, und auf festen Untergrund, wie z.B. Strassen eher so, als hätte man Steppschuhe an. Auch das Gehen über Schotter wird nicht sonderlich berücksichtigt. Die Umgebungsgeräusche sind in der Regel immer gleich., und die Musikuntermalung habe ich ausgeschaltet, damit ich mich nur auf das Spiel konzentrieren kann und will.

Alles in Allem ein durchwachsenes Spiel, das erst nach vielen Stunden ein wenig Spaß bringt. Vor allem, wenn ein KI- Gefährte dazu kommt. Zur Zeit habe ich noch einen neugierigen Kleriker an meine Seite. Der mich wahrscheinlich solange begleitet, bis ich ihm verschiedene technische Gerätschaften bringe.

Ach ja, die Dialoge: die sind im Grunde immer gleich - wohin gehst Du, was machst Du, wer bist Du und natürlich... brauchst Du Hilfe...! Ein wenig einfallslos, auch bei meinem Kleriker - da frage ich ihn wie es so ausschaut bei ihm, und dann kommt immer die gleiche Antwort: da muss ich noch darüber nachdenken...! Außer es änderte sich was am Spielgeschehen. Dann kommt ein anderer Satz. Leider kann man ihm nicht danken, wenn er mir den "Kopf" gerettet hat oder ob er sich mal ein paar Stunden auf´s Ohr legen will. Das kann nur ich! Wie gesagt sehr einfallslos.

Der Kompass bzw. die Karte - leider stehen in der Karte nur gewisse wichtige Lehrer und natürlich auch den ein oder anderen Nebenquest, sonst nichts. Keine Städtenamen oder Dörfer oder sonst was. Auch nicht, wenn man es besuchte. 
Der Kompass gibt nur grob an wohin man muss, wenn man einen Marker auf der Karte gemacht hat oder es um einen wichtigen Quest geht. Und beim Kampf zeigt er den Feind an, aber keine Tiere, die auf einen losstürmen.

Bin aber Zwiegespalten mit diesem Spiel, zum Einen ist sogar das alte "Arcania" um Längen besser, was das Kampfsystem betrifft, aber nur der 1. Teil und zum Anderen finde ich das Inventarsystem hier wesentlich besser, da man nichts irgendwo in eine Kiste wegsperren muss.

Die verschiedenen Charaktere sind leider austauschbar, keine ist irgendwie anders oder angenehmer.
Am Besten bleibt man allein und versohlt den Feinden den Hintern..., aber lieber eine kleine Hilfe, als keine.

Daher eher einen schwachen Daumen hoch.

I don't usually take time to write reviews but this game deserves one. I picked it up recently because it was on sale and it looked interesting. I am still working my way through it but it is very much worth what I paid. The world is really interesting and the gameplay is challenging. If you like games like Fallout, Skyrim with a little bit of Dark Souls mixed in this is for you.

All in all, a good proof of concept that Gothic 3 could have worked.
It really does feel like Gothic 3, right down to the empty feeling you start to feel when you're quickly running out of meaningful things to do in the game.

I also think it kinda goes to show that PB games are at their best when they are tightly and carefully made over a smaller land mass. I don't think the PB philosophy works in a huge open world. People have tried to compare it to Fallout 4, and in my mind it kind of does achieve that nebulous feeling of lethargy and detachment Fallout 4 inevitably provides, just without the lame base building BS. 

Ever since Risen 2 hit with its awkward controls and ditched the elegant Risen 1 mouse input, I've been cold on PB games, but this just shows me they're determined not to bring back the Risen 1/Gothic 2 feel any time soon. PB games now entirely rely on stat grinds, not careful quest design made to help you experience the world, not careful timing or precision in combat. The abysmal melee combat in Elex just carries on the tradition of burying memories of fighting off hordes of orcs in the valley of mines, or memories of perfectly flank-dodging tough human enemies in Risen 1 and taking them out with nothing but a stick. 

My issue with how this game controls is this: you constantly feel like you're in control of a RC shopping cart, with no way of simply moving in the direction you want without the character drunkenly swerving around the place like he's recovering from last night's bender. The Witcher 3 managed an alternate movement scheme that fixed most of these complaints with that game, so why not here? As it stands, you can only backpedal or strafe if you've locked onto an enemy, or if you're blocking, meaning there's no elegance to the dodging or attacking in relation to the camera position/character facing. It's a big clumsy mess that depends upon having the highest numbers, and it even has some of the issues that ArcaniA has. Yup. Said it. From Risen 2 through to Elex, PB has been making the same control blunders as that one ArcaniA game nobody likes.

Add to that the severe bugs and glitches present in the game, as well as it's completely inorganic quest design compared to the prime Gothic-era games, and the fact that PB has entirely stopped working on it to create a sequel, meant the overall experience wasn't worth the effort for me. The ending was just a sequel hook that granted me no closure for anything. It left me tired, disillusioned and disappointed. The issue isn't in the difficulty at all, as it's very easy to bring the game down to its knees with a few fireballs, but rather the constant awkwardness of the... everything on display eventually sets in, and even when you're having a relatively successful session where you make tons of progress, you'll probably still be cussing the game out for its inadequecies. 

It doesn't feel like a PB game to me. I'm slightly warmer on it now that I've managed to work out how the quest progression is supposed to go, now that I know you don't have to go through 75% of your playtime without faction powers, but it still feels like a celebration of all the Gothic/Risen series' worst aspects combined into one, so unless people tell me Elex 2 is a grandstanding and excellent product, I ain't buying it. I think I'll stick with with the jankfests that were actually good. The ones which you gained an appreciation for before the end. This gave me the same dull buzz from start to finish.

Начну со смешанных пунктов:
[h1]1. Сеттинг [/h1]
 + Достаточно интересный и проработанный мир со своим лором
 - ...полный штампов и "отсылок" к другим сеттингам (Fallout/Gothic/Command&Conquer/Mass Effect).
[h1]2. "Дух" игры[/h1]
 + Пираньи во многом смогли приблизиться к атмосфере своей "золотой" Gothic 2
 - ...однако местами сходства с предыдущими играми чересчур явное (схожие квесты, те же имена персонажей).
[h1]3. Боевая система[/h1]
 + В игре представлено достаточно много видов различного вооружения, кроме того, фракции различаются не только текстурами брони, но и возможными подходами к бою
 - ...однако сама боевая система оставляет желать лучшего (особенно стрельба, ухх), чаще всего все сводится к "закликиванию" противника.
[h1]4. Сюжет[/h1]
 + Встречаются достаточно интересные квесты (например, у спутников)
 - ...однако, большинство квестов вполне рядовые, да и баги часто мешают насладиться квестами (например, квест Рэя).

[h1]Однозначные плюсы:[/h1]
1. Саундтрек: пожалуй, из всех игр Пираний саундтрек Elex мне запомнился чуть ли не больше всех (что, вообще, довольно странно).
2. Картинка: может, и не пример топовой графики 2017 года, но большую часть времени все смотрится приятно.
3. Заполненная карта: за два полных прохождения забраться в места, не рассчитанные на доступность, получалось буквально пару раз, все остальное явно было сделано с расчетом на то, что вы туда залетите (или упадете).

[h1]Однозначные минусы:[/h1]
1. Противоречивость сюжета: неоднократно создается впечатление, что одну и ту же сюжетную линию писало несколько человек, не советовавшихся друг с другом. Пример: [spoiler]квесты с воссоединением семьи, где Джакс взывает к брату, говоря об их происхождении, но узнает он оь этом лишь в ходе следующего по сюжетной линии квеста[/spoiler].
2. Длинные вымученные кинематографические вставки aka видения.
3. Жуткая неотзывчивость управления: срабатывающие через раз быстрые сохранения, не прожимающаяся вовремя атака, сюда же – пропадающие эликсиры из-за врагов, сбивающих анимацию.

В общем, игра нравится скорее вопреки, чем благодаря. Ждем вторую часть с исправленными недочетами.

Weiterhin wird auch jeder der an den zuvor genannten Spielen Freude hatte, auch seine Freude an Elex haben.

"Мы строили-строили и, наконец, построили!" (с)
Удивляюсь я упорству и педантичности Пираний: аж с 2001-го (с первой "Готики") года они доводили до ума и шлифовали свои идеи и механики. Но вот мы получили ту "Готику", которую заслужили. Игра не лишена своих недостатков, но и плюсов у неё довольно много.
Плюсы и минусы.
Плюсы
1) Интересный сеттинг. Конечно, попытки соеденить сай-фай и фэнтези уже бывали (и не раз). На вскидку, могу сразу вспомнить недоброй память "ВНебеКузню". Но в Elex, на мой взгляд, всё сочлось наиболее удачно, да ещё и с примесью постапакалиптики.
2) Интересные квесты. Вспомним игры от Беседки: часть побочных квестов - интересна, часть - не очень, основной квест - скучен и линеен. В Elex же интересен и основной квест и почти все побочные. Да и сюжетные твисты в наличии.
3) Запоминающиеся НеПиСи. Почти все NPC в игре это личности со своим характером, поведением, реакциями и заскоками.
4) Челендж. Игра не прощает ошибок. Да-да: как какая-нибудь соусница. Конечно, ошибки в прокачке можно исправит, но, в процессе исправления, придётся страдать.
Минусы.
1) Сложность. Челендж - челенджем, но, на первых парах, почти любой моб может ваншотнуть. Поэтому, наши лучшие друзья - лук, джетпак и F5.
2) Гиде циферки? "Холодность" (местный аналог кармы) и её изменения не имеют числовых показателей. Обидно. Мне, как человеку выросшему на Arcanum'е и KOTOR'е должно быть ясно как именно изменилась моя карма. А уж при учёте, что прокачивающие элексовое питьё тоже влияет на карму.
3) Кривоватости-шероховатости. Получили урон или контроль во время натягивания лука? Убирайте лук и доставайте по новой. Решили, что вырвались из зоны агра моба (раньше-то с такими же мобами получалось)? Идите нафиг - именно этот молох имеет безграничную зону агра.

I have been a fan of Piranha Byte games since the first release of Gothic. I have played every game they made and knew fully well, what to expect. That's why I think ELEX is a great game, but has flaws. 
The animations are clunky and sometimes weird, combat is a mess and the graphics cannot keep up with modern standards. The difficulty for first time players is frustratingly high as well, because you have to figure out the combat system and the way that enemies attack. As this stays true for a large portion of the game you will need a high pain tolerance for dying and loading that last save you did 20 minutes ago. 
But the way they create their worlds is just amazing. There are so many details, so many little things to find and so much to explore out there. You can litterally run to the end of the world and find a hidden outpost, tower or just a skeleton watching the sunset with a last beer in his hand. If you take your time to explore you can learn a lot about the world and everything that happened. The story setting is well made and even though it may seems strange at first to have a mix of fantasy, mad max and sci-fi, it works. Each of the factions is well explained, has it's specific history and the way they see the world differs drastically. 

Altogether ELEX is a good game and I'd defininately recommend it for people, that have played the Gothic series or like exploring a vast world. If this is you first time playing a Piranha Bytes game you might have a hard time because of the difficulty, but if you stick with it a wonderful game awaits you.

The game has a ton of potential but it suffers from extremely bad AI, hero movement, hit boxes, invisible walls and nonsensicle combat. These things completely ruin the entire experiance for me. If they fixed these glaring issues everyone talks about, the game could be great and worth the money, but currently stay away. They are apparently not going to fix it, and have moved on to "Elex 2 production.

Your companion will at times just watch you die in battle and not attack the enemy, at all, sometimes even run from you and the enemy. Or just walk directly in front of and behind you, preventing your movement and aim.

The enemy will hit you when visually it should not, and this will result in your death.

The enemy will randomly wheather your blows, that normally stop its attack, and this will kill you.

NPC' humans pretty much all have the same two faces and voices, minus main' storyline people.

The enemy can kill you through objects and walls, including other enemies.

Your hits will miss when visually they should not.

Your movement is clunky and has slow response.

You cannot melee something if you are one foot above it, say standing on a pebble.

Movements of enemies are predicable, giving you the ability to memorize its limited animations and just exploit that. Their way of getting around that is to give almost all enemies a ranged /AOE attack, and a super fast frame skipping lunge attack that can hit through walls. which in my opinion was extremely lazy.

If you are on top of a rock and dodge an enemy attack by rolling, you will not leave that rock, you will roll into an invisible wall and get smashed by the enemy. Rolling only works when you are on flat ground, not cars, walls, big rocks or anything of that sort. Its really strange and should have been coded better. 

Almost everything you do in this game has an input delay

Almost everything an enemy does is instant, including them switching from a sword to a gun and shooting you in one frame.

Look up youtube videos for examples and read other negative reviews, we all pretty much talk about the same things.

But for all the bad, the game can still be interesting, just play it on easy mode, and spam elex potion use. I personally have not finished the game because its too cringy for me in its current state, but the world and storyline are cool.

Elex is not an easy game to enjoy. The amazing, unique, beautiful world is what kept me coming back to it after 40 hours short interval playing over the course of nearly a year.  Once I hit that 41 hour mark, it instilled within me a certain addictive charm. It was at this point the sharp learning curve began to flatten, and the mechanics of the game started to make sense in its own weird way.

I can’t understate how interesting and incredible the world design is. I wish there were an option to add fog/shading on the map overlay so that you know what areas you haven’t discovered. It was near the end game that I found by my own random exploration several incredibly detailed lost towns/villages with their own sidestories on how they met their demise.  The story/quest-building team clearly had a difficult time keeping up with the world builders.  That’s not to say that there isn’t enough story - there is plenty of story. The world is still a behemoth in comparison.

I played primarily melee, one handed. Once I learned my choice companion was invincible and would not get angry at me for using them as bait (they get knocked out after a time), I realized early level combat was less about tactics and more about pot shots/escape while the enemies were distracted by my companion.  I also (after reaching level 35) found many areas with low-level enemies that I wish I’d known about at the beginning of the game, but was too scared to explore then because pretty much everything else can kill you in the blink of an eye.

The factions element is more cosmetic than I expected. I put off joining a faction until as late as possible, only to find out I could still do quests for the other factions anyway, but was just barred from their perks/armor appearance.  Having the better armor earlier in the game would have helped as well (though, not by much).

The gameplay is difficult to compliment. Combat is clunky. Quests are interestingly designed, but don’t seem fully fleshed out. Ranged weapons only serve to p*** enemies off (so don’t use them unless you’re on higher ground where you can’t be reached). You have a jetpack to aid in exploration, but it feels like an afterthought after [imagining]too many game testers expressed frustration at having to find paths/climb their way to an objective[/imagining]. Finding the sunglasses in the beginning is almost required (they highlight inventory-able objects in the world). By the time the game was over, I had a plethora of weapons that I had not used, and had no reason to.

My final thought about Elex is that it is definitely worth playing through a second time, now that I can start from the beginning understanding how the game actually works and how to play it better.  It is very hostile to new players and will not hold your hand at any step of the way (aside from giving you map checkpoints to follow).  There is a lot of nuance that I’m sure I missed the first time around; in fact, playing it a second time will probably be more gratifying and enjoyable than the first.  I promise I will when I have time…

Inutile girarci intorno, Gothic ha cambiato abito, epoca e personaggi, ma alla fine si arriva alla stessa conclusione.
Il progetto è interessante, l'idea di una civiltà che ricomincia quasi da capo dopo una catastrofe planetaria, mentre la trama del protagonista si svolge e si scopre sulla base delle scelte effettuate durante il gaming, scelte che possono influenzare enormemente le fasi future di gioco.
L'unico vero neo, il sistema di combattimento. Alle volte frustrante nella sua "ottusità" e gli aiuti proposti, come il bersaglio agganciato, spesso si rivelano ancora più dannosi; in combinata anche la telecamera fissa in terza persona, rende pressochè impossibile evitare di ritrovarsi accerchiati durante gli scontri di gruppo.
La difficoltà è mediamente molto più alta di qualsiasi altro concorrente del genere, rendendovi carne da macello per i primi 10-15 livelli, ma più che un contro è un "fastidio" che porta ad ingegnarsi sul come riuscire ad eliminare mobs alrimenti imbattibili.
Il resto è un enorme scenario da esplorare e scoprire, risolvendo quest e missioni secondarie o anche semplicemente esplorandolo in libertà, alla scoperta delle mille storie sepolte sotto le ceneri di una passato distrutto.
Lo consiglio, anche se in più di un'occasione il mouse ed il pad ne hanno fatte le spese...

Maybe the story will be great, but....as my impression of the game after 1 hour is so bad....I refuse to play it further. I very disappointed from this 2017 title, for different reasons.

1. ... a little thing, but still annoying :
Vsync in this game works only with exclusive fullscreen.
Even if I use a ini-setting to set the maximum framerate to a lower number, the game ignores it. 
This behavior might be ok for games pre 2010 , but not for relatively new one

2. The graphics are, sorry, a little but ugly? At least not what I expected from a game released in 2017. Cause I don't care what engine is used nor on what predecessors the game is based.
If there is a game tagged to be from 2017 with a regular price of 50 Euro, I simply expect something that graphics and animations don't look like old titles 5-6 years before. I'm ok with simply graphics in a old game....but this here is not retro, it's lazy.
And yes, I maxed out all the settings. Even  the maximum texture resolution seems to be to low. And a game that uses dialog-sequence with close-ups, should at least use some higher textures for the faces and clothing. The colors are way to strong....ok something that I could have noticed in the screenshot before. The animations are looking like donkey kong (yes yes I'm way to harsh here...cause I'm so disappointed)

3. The worst...and the main killer. The clunky, bad controls. Simply horrible....nothing to say more on that....

Maybe I would be happy with this game as a fan boy of the publisher, unfortunately I just care about my experience and not the brand.
