Игра понравилась, но порой ловил себя на мысли, что хвалю не реальную игру, а ту которой она могла бы быть. Потому что несмотря на огромный для маленькой студии объем работы, игра все равно осталась недоделанной.

Мир недоделан. Авторы нарисовали красивый ландшафт с разными климатическими зонами, а потом равномерно разбросали по нему руины из своего куцого набора моделек. Никакой системы в их расположении нет, огрызки асфальтовых дорог идут из ниоткуда в никуда, абстрактные развалины из кирпича торчат в лесах, горах и болотах без какого либо объяснения, как они туда попали и какую функцию выполняли. Понять как выглядел мир игры до катастрофы невозможно, а ведь для таких игр это очень важно. 
При этом даже в таком режиме авторы не смогли заполнить игровой мир целиком, поэтому значительную часть карты занимают непроходимые  горы-"заглушки" с радиацией. Откуда столько радиации объяснений нет, видимо на каком то этапе разработки Elex был постядерным.

Сюжетная часть недоделана. 

По традиции тебя в принудительном порядке заставляют вступить в одну из фракций. И... это не влияет ни на что абсолютно. После выполнения цепочки вступительных квестов и получения первого ранга фракции можно выйти за ворота и до конца игры вообще не вспоминать, что ты какой-то Берсерк, Изгой или Клирик. За всю игру и десятка раз не наберется, когда NPC обратят внимание на цвет твоей брони. Самое серьезное последствие вступления в Клирики за всю игру - Берсерки перестали наливать в своем баре. По остальному берсерковому городу ходишь спокойно.

Но что еще хуже - выбор фракции не влияет на геймплей. Стиль прохождения на 100% зависит от оружия в руках, а тут практически никаких ограничений игра не накладывает. Быть Паладином Берсерков(фракция магов, ненавидящих технологии) и палить из плазменной винтовки Клириков? Легко. Пользуйся чем хочешь, прокачивай тоже. Да, нельзя пользоваться магией других фракций и накладывать магический урон на их оружие ближнего боя. Но это играет чисто вспомогательную роль, можно спокойно обойтись.

Сами по себе фракции интересны, по их городам интересно ходить, их диалоги интересно слушать, а квесты выполнять. Ты втягиваешься, рассчитываешь на продолжительное сотрудничество и возможность повлиять на их будущее... И вдруг ты получаешь максимальный ранг фракции и тебя прямым текстом выставляют за дверь: "Квесты закончились, спасибо и пошел вон отсюда". Сюжетные линии фракций не сделаны даже на половину. 

Идешь по основному сюжету. Он тоже интересен, тоже хорошие диалоги. И тоже недоделан. История просто обрывается и вместо нормальной концовки предлагают ждать Elex 2.

Что еще не доделано? Геймплей, который адаптирован исключительно под ближний бой. Дальний бой прописан по остаточному принципу без какого-либо баланса. Любой огнестрел в первой половине игры мусор, а во второй превращается в "press RT to win". И это на тяжелом уровне сложности.
Бесполезные навыки взлома, которые никак не вляюют на квесты, а лишь засоряют инвентарь рандомным мусором из сундоков и сейфов.
Куча других навыков, что вообще непонятно зачем нужны. "Снижение штрафа за преступления" - нафига?


Однако то что авторы смогли доделать - сделано отлично. Нормальные персонажи с нормальными диалогами. Дополнительные квесты, которые грамотно вписаны в общий сюжет, имеют развилки, разные способы решения и последствия в будущем. Мир игры живой, разнообразный, его действительно интересно исследовать.

Так и думаешь, вот бы авторам больше денег и времени, какая получилась бы игра... Но потом впоминаешь времена, когда у авторов все это было, и они все пролюбили, выпустив Готику 3. Может большие игры не для них, и авторам лучше сосредоточится на камерных РПГшках масштаба одной долины/острова?  Все их лучшие игры были менно такими.
Die Geschichte finde ich recht Interessant und es gibt viel zu entdecken.

I have no idea how to feel about this game.

Everything is super fun, exploration, dialogues, lore, aesthetic... But the combat  is.... duuuuuude, I can't believe that someone made this mess, were they doing such a mess intentionally?

I don't mind that a ovegrown chicken kills you in one hit or that it takes one hundred hits to get  it killed. I agree that it can be part of the roleplay. But such hardcore mechanic mixed with regular RPG experience forces you to do ton of immersion breaking exploits. You companions are invincible and do at least some damage. Most of the time when I had to kill something, I just ordered compainon to stand on the highground so he could shoot the enemy while I was dancing down in circles, luring the enemy on me, so the companion could arrow him to death. Where's the fun in that? There's literally no other way of doing that, companions were essential in all my playthrough.

The AI, man, it's so bad. I had to kill a bandit who had a grenade launcher, one of his thugs had a grenade launcher too. They were spamming, shooting grenades to a wall in from of them (so it landed under their feet, damaging both of us, him lightly, me mortally), shooting grenades in the cluster of their own allies... Companion's AI is equally bad, sometimes it takes them seconds before they decide to attack the enemy.

It's not fun to run around the map just to find a quest that you're able to finish or exploit. Quests to retrieve something are not fun, you can just jetpack yourself to the thing, ignoring the enemies. Quests to kill something are next to impossible (if you cannot exploit them with your companion) and you just have to put them for later, when they get so easy that they're no fun either.

Hitbox of your character is messed up, you get hit even if the axe swings one meter behind you. Dodge move is assigned for double tapping movement keyes (you cannot disable that) but it's so sensitive that you dodge mostly when you dont want to dodge, depleting third of your stamina.

There's just so much wrong about this game... I really tried to like it, I enjoyed exploring the world but the broken combat balance and controls and target-locking just does not allow me to. I was so looking forward to the next Risen... Risen 2 was awfully bad, Elex looked promissing, but they messed up again.

EDIT: CCa 40 hours in the game, I acquired a rifle that could kill any average enemy with 3 hits and bosses with 10 at max, making the rest of the game incredibly easy. And... boring.

Если тебе нравилась Gothicа или, как минимум, Risen, то в это стоит поиграть. Игра не идеальна, нет, но затянуть на долго может. Попытаюсь назвать не только самые очевидные плюсы и минусы.
                                                                                   [h1] ПЛЮСЫ[/h1]

[olist]
    [*] Весьма неплохое сочетание постапокалипсиса, киберпанка и средневековья одновременно в одной игре.
    [*] Возможность иметь на постоянной основе спутника и их разнообразие. Каждый спутник отличается характером и своей историей.
    [*] Присутствие в игре других группировок, помимо основных фракций, на которые тоже можно поработать.
    [*] Огромный арсенал оружия и возможность его разобрать на запчасти или, наобарот, модернизировать.
    [*] Полное различие идеалогий 3-х главных фракций, каждая видит строение мира в дальнейшим по своему.
[/olist]
                                                                            [h1] МИНУСЫ[/h1]   
   [olist]
    [*] Неудобный инвентарь, слишком уж в нём много вкладок, разобраться сразу не получается. Что уж, я до сих пор в нём путаюсь иногда.
    [*] Система боя. Я бы назвал её больше непонятной, нежели неудобной, к ней стоит просто привыкнуть и всё, но в начале игры вопросы, конечно, возникать будут. 
    [*] Слабый персонаж на начальной стадии игры, приходится просто убегать от мобов. От этого спасает быстрое нахождение себе спутника, но количество опыта, за убийство монстров, конечно, оставляет желать лучшего.
    [*] Законы фракций, которые можно не исполнять. Яркий пример: в лагере Берсерков можно пользоваться реактивным ранцем и вам за это ничего не будет. Может быть я и докапался просто так, но раз уж разработчики придумали законы, можно было и подумать над мерой пресечения.
    [*] Анимация/ Различные баги. Тут уже много всего сказано, дополню лишь то, что меня больше всего раздражает отсутствие шлема(если он надет) во время диалогов.
    [*] Нету ответов на некоторые вопросы в начале игры. Что такое холодность и как она влияет на прохождение игры? Куда можно ещё пойти, кроме лагеря Берсерков?
[/olist]
                                                                                       [h1]Итог[/h1]
Подводя итог, скажу, что это игра не для всех и от неё надо научиться получать удовольствие, потому что первые 3-4 часа Вы будете разбираться с инвентарём, управлением и тд.  Многим она не понравилась, но если Вы играли в Ghotic или Risen и Вам они нравятся как и исследование огромного мира, а также Вы не гонитесь за мега-крутой графикой, то этой игре стоит дать шанс.

Should you buy this game?
- Wrong question, the real question is: Do you want to suffer?


The game starts with main character who has severe amnesia, you know nothing of the land, the people or the history. So you will feel completely lost in a seriously huge environment... If you start walking to any direction you will certainly encounter a monster that will kill you... just let that lovely anxiety kick in...

This is not hack&slash game, this is a scream and run game... hmm see that exotic looking spider? Let me try to hit it with bow&arrow see if I can kill it? ... few seconds later I try to turn around and run, but the spider uses the pointy leg to stab me in the back, ministunning me and holy shit that not only hurts my character, but it also hurts me as a gamer into my soul... Now this will repeat stab after stab until my character is dead and I start crying. Hideous beasts! No matter what level my character is, I always ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ NOPE away from those.

The salvation is people, early game only place safe is around people. Asking them about history of the land and completing quests inside the walls is a relaxing way to get into the game. Somehow the lore and history becomes addictive, you start to connect the dots that you thought are irrelevant and you start getting these eureka moments... you become lore junkie to get more of that sweet knowledge.

Mid to lategame once you are not completely riddled with crippling fear of monsters, you start to see how hideous or beautiful the game world is depending on your location... it is quite remarkable how blind tunneled vision survivor the anxiety gets me... once I can relax the games beauty just kicks in.

Like previous Piranha Bytes games, the world feels vibrant and it calls you to explore! If you love exploring in real life, you will certainly enjoy ELEX as well.


Still, the game is fustrating and difficult, every step feels heavy and sometimes all hope is lost. Yet you still want to take that next step. Which is why I started this review with question:

Do you want to suffer?

Tolles Rollenspiel der alten Schule. Der Anfang ist schön hart, man wird an jeder Ecke von noch so kleinen Viechern umgehauen, dafür ist es später umso befriedigender sie mit einem Treffer wegzupusten. Wirklich tolles Spielgefühl, wie damals in Gothic. Die Schuss- und Laserwaffen sind zu Beginn noch etwas seltsam, passen sich aber sehr gut ins Gesamtbild ein.
Auch die Spielwelt ist mit viel Liebe zum Detaill gestaltet wurden. Ich habe jeden Zettel und jeden Hinweis den ich finden durchgelesen, weil ich die Atmosphäre wirklich spannend und auch unverbraucht fand. Lediglich die Hauptstory traf nicht ganz meinen Geschmack, aber dafür gab es wirklich genügend Abwechslung. Was mir außerdem sehr gut gefallen hatte war, dass es zwar ab und an unterschiedliche Entscheidungsmöglichkeiten gibt, diese aber nicht zu drastisch ausfallen, dass ich das Gefühl gehabt hätte, ich würde etwas vom Spiel verpassen, wenn ich jetzt eine bestimmte Antwort gebe.
Ich hoffe es wird noch eine Erweiterung geben, ählich wie bei den Risenteilen damals.

TL;DR: Für Rollenspieler der alten Schule sehr zu empfehlen. Wer lieber an die Hand genommen werden möchte mit allerlei Tutorials und Minimonster, kriegt hier "volles Pfund aufs Maul".

Difficile de rentrer tout de suite dans le scénario, difficulté élevée, rigidité...

Ce jeu n'est pas fait pour ceux qui aiment tuer des animaux carnivores lvl 1 avec une dague rouillée et un slip. Pas non plus pour ceux qui cliquent sur accepter quête et attendent une flèche avec un "tuer XXX 0/20". 

Une fois dedans, wow ! Les quêtes vous surprendront (pourtant je suis un habitué du genre avec wasteland, torment, fallout, skyrim...) plus d'une fois, et on ressent une véritable évolution de son personnage sans pour autant finir par se dire "c'est bon je crains plus rien".

Dans Elex, on prévoit ses déplacements, on écoute, on fuit souvent... Une expérience géniale, boudée par les formatés aux AAA tout comme les RISEN que j'aime beaucoup également, mais moins qu'Elex !

[h1] Вкратце: [/h1]
[b] 1) [/b] первые 4 часа игра вызывает отвращение (анимации, боевая система, непонимание происходящего и много другое)
[b] 2) [/b] 5-15 часов, появился явный интерес
[b] 3) [/b] 15-50 часов, игра жутко нравится
[b] 4) [/b] 50+ часов, игра как игра, но бегать по миру весьма интересно

[h1] Минусы игры: [/h1]
[list]
[*] 1) Отсутствие графической оптимизации. Ведьмак 3 я прошёл на средних настройках, а здесь, чтобы нормально играть, пришлось всё снизить до минимума, притом несколько взрывов подряд (эффекты с большим количеством частиц) убивают весь FPS даже на минималках (фризы кратковременные, но бесячие)
[*] 2) Некоторые анимации запрещают 3д-модели персонажа выполнять конкретные действия. К примеру:
[list]
[*] 2.1) нельзя достать оружие в воздухе, только использовать
[*] 2.2) если вражеский персонаж пытается встать после взрыва гранатой, то пока проигрывается анимация, персонажа невозможно повторно откинуть гранатой (новый стан не засчитывается)
[*] 2.3) если вас ударили в момент перезарядки, то новая перезарядка не стартует автоматически, а у лука нет ручной перезарядки, т.е. приходится убирать оружие и снова доставать
[/list]
[*] 3) Вы не понимаете, что происходит в мире. Нету вводной миссии, или просто какого-то монолога за кадром.
[list]
[*] 3.1) Непонятно, что в этом мире есть, где какие земли, и кто все эти люди (у персонажа амнезия, и может это специальный ход авторов игры, но уже на старте Джакс может признаться, что он бывший альб, а я как игрок, даже понятия не имею, что это значит)
[*] 3.2) Что можно воровать, что можно покупать, как пользоваться инвентарём, что прокачивать, как прокачивать? Эти и многие другие вопросы обеспечены любому игроку в первые несколько часов игры! Именно это очень сильно оттолкнуло на старте :)
[*] 3.3) Что такое холодность, как и когда я влияю на симпатию компаньонов\спутников, холодность это общая симпатия? Где увидеть процент влияния? На более сложные вопросы игра редко отвечает и здесь помогает только Google.
[/list]
[*] 4) Чтобы вы не взяли в помещении фракции, все всегда вокруг реагируют, как на воровство, даже если предмет не помечен "взять запрещено". Т.е. вас никто не атакует, но все встают и возмущаются.
[*] 5) На 3-ем из 4-ёх уровней сложности вы можете убить... никого!... вообще никого из тех кто будет сопротивляться... Я выбрал направление стрелка и для того, чтобы начать уверенно бегать по миру понадобилось раздобыть стрелковое оружие хотя бы среднего урона и прокачать его два из трёх возможных раз. До этого меня кормили быстрые ноги и реактивный ранец.
[*] 6) Оружия много, но стрелок в одном из заданий может раздобыть лазерную винтовку, которая всего лишь совсем немного уступает топовому именному оружию. А за счёт очереди, так и в некоторых ситуациях может быть лучше... В общем, я всю игру прошёл на лазерной винтовке.
[/list]

[h1] Плюсы игры: [/h1]
[list]
[*] 1) Отдельные квесты. К примеру, очень крут секрет Фалька (все его личные квесты) и "Четыре дома" – в конце этих миссий я был приятно удивлён работе сценаристов.
[*] 2) Кат сцены очень атмосферны и просто шикарно смотрятся!
[*] 3) Каждый спутник местами шокирует своей историей, что весьма радует – сценаристы хорошо поработали

Well, the game is an average RPG, and I was well aware about that before having bought it at a discount. Other reviews call it a Gothic clone, and I cannot agree more. However, there are quite a few changes/upgrades that makes the game look "newish". And I say newish because not everything this game has to offer is "modern":-

[b]Firstly, a lot of the visuals are outdated.[/b] This does not make the game look ugly for a 2017 release, but it is fairly obvious that the project had to pass through some serious budget constraints. 

[b]Secondly, The gameplay is as clunky as it gets, with a few pleasant tweaks over the Gothic 3/Arcania formula.[/b] What makes things worse is how the enemy AI is buffed to make things unfair. They have unlimited stamina whereas you are as energetic as a morbidly obese person after 10 minutes of walking. In addition to this, most enemies have a lot of health to boot and strength to kill you in one hit, thereby making you quit the game every now and then. Such frustrating moments hamper the overall experience. Besides, the game is not meant to be a Dark Souls-esque RPG, is it?

[b]Thirdly, the quest handling/dialogue/minor RPG elements are uninspired.[/b] Quests are as basic as they can get, from meeting a person located at a distance, to fetch quests. Some are good, but they don't redeem the game in any way. Some effort is seen in the dialogue, though. Characters are given distinct personalities and you can easily end up liking/disliking them. I have read people complaining about excessive dialogue, but that is something I enjoy in an RPG. However the story progresses slowly and you don't feel like completing it (I am already getting bored).

To conclude, I would only recommend people to purchase this game if they want to complete their Piranha Byte collection, namely the Gothic loyalists. For others, try Gothic 3 and see if those kind of games appeal you. And then, come to this.

This game is an absolute masterpiece. A flawed masterpiece, perhaps, but a masterpiece nonetheless. I don't know if I've enjoyed a game this much since my first playthrough of the original Gothic. 

Like Gothic, however, this Piranha Bytes game takes some patience from the player until everything clicks, and for some, that "click" may never come. But for many of us, myself included, when everything gels, the game is all-consuming. I've played nothing else since I started the game, and after more than 100 hours, I finally finished. 

Without a doubt, this is the best PB game since the original Gothic. They've been trying to recreate that magic ever since, but with mixed success. The first Risen was decent, Risen 2 was so-so, and Risen 3? I've barely even played it. But Elex ... Elex is PB getting it right again. 

If you loved the original Gothic games, you will adore this. It has everything those games had and more ... a great levelling system, tons and tons of story arcs and branches, an abundance of places to explore, great creature design, a living world, a nice mix of magic and normal combat, a variety of factions to choose from, consequences for your actions, etc., etc. The sheer amount of detail in this game from a story perspective just absolutely amazed me. You can choose to enlist some help on your journey with a variety of AI partners, and each one has an incredibly detailed and interesting back story that you'll uncover along the way. The Ray story in particular was really fun, but they're all interesting. 

But the main story is also very smart, unique and interesting, much more like playing a great sci-fi novel than a typical game. What I also loved was the ability to take revenge on NPCs later in the game who took advantage of you early on. I loved that in the original Gothic games, and it was great to see that continue here. 

Like all PB games, though, this isn't without its flaws. The combat always gets criticized with PB games, and I can't say the combat system in this is great, but I truly enjoyed it overall. I used a melee style combined with ranged weapons and magic. My inventory consisted of swords, shields, bows, crossbows, shotguns, flame throwers, missile launchers, plasma rifles, grenades and more. How many other games give you access to all that? 

That's because the world of Elex is a great combination of the futuristic and the medieval, and the story explains that situation perfectly. 

But, the combat could've been a little more fluid I suppose. Still, to be able to have so much at your disposal was just tremendous ... creating enchanted flaming swords, for example, and use them on soldiers with plasma weapons ... a very unique gaming experience. 

Probably the biggest flaw in the game for me, though, was one that all PB games seem to have: sticking the landing. The game itself is just SO much fun, but the final showdown is usually anticlimactic, and that's definitely the case here. The final battle is just ridiculously easy. Also, some of the dialogue choices have very strange consequences that really don't make sense. For example, you might say something to an NPC that makes perfect sense to what you're trying to accomplish, and you'll get a message that your companion is angry at you for what you said/did, and that often makes no sense whatsoever. Not that it really matters in the context of the game itself, but it's a bit annoying at times. 

People complain that there's way too much dialogue in this, but as I said, it's like reading/playing a novel, and you can skip through the dialogue easily and quickly with the press of a button. 

But the world is so alive and beautiful and interesting, just as the first two Gothic games were. There are so many things to uncover way beyond the main storyline that exploration is an absolute must. There were so many great side stories in this game, and very few typical fetch quests. It was very much like Witcher 3 in that respect, and unlike many past PB games, the voice acting was generally really good in Elex. 

Speaking of Witcher 3, that's another of my all-time favorite series, and it's clearly more polished than PB games. That said ... I enjoyed playing Elex more than Witcher 3. The Witcher had far fewer options, with only four magic spells you could use throughout the game and a couple swords. The story was incredible and the quests beautifully designed, and the graphics were better, too, but ... I still had a lot more fun with Elex.

I bow before the sheer creativity, love and passion PB put into this game. It's really meant a lot to me and given me hours of enjoyment and stress relief, and for that, I truly thank them. Makes me disgusted to see all the negative reviews on this, but  .... they simply don't make games much like this anymore, and most people are just too impatient to let a game like this suck them in. And that sucks. 

Hopefully there are enough of us out there to warrant an Elex 2. I can't wait. Thank you, PB!

I played the 21.4hrs you see here on the first couple days that ELEX was released and have not picked it up since to finish. I usually feel bad about not finishing a game but with ELEX I can't seem to even force myself to complete it. Let me start by saying that ELEX isn't a terrible game, it's just... boring? Though that aside, there is one glaring issue that annoyed me to no end, the factions.

There exist three factions in this game, a group of hippies gone Viking on saving the planet living in the forest, a group of dashing rogues who use grenade launchers, the staple of any true rogue of course, living in the desert and finally the classic religious order of paladins that live in a volcano. On paper you've got some interesting shit going on but there's a problem. Leveled zones. You start out in the forest area with the Vikings who shun technology, the forest is also the lowest level area, so if say you didn't want to join the Vikings because you (like me) heard of a religious order of paladins using technological marvels and robots to fight, you decide to join them, you're shit out of luck. The Clerics are in a high level zone so if you wanted to play the game organically, you'd need to exhaust the viking area then move on to the next area and so forth before getting to the Clerics. I never tried to reach the rogues so I don't know if that's harder or easier, but essentially from the get go you're stuck with being a Viking and I feel many people will become a Viking without really understanding what that means, this is the kind of game that would do well with a world that levels with you like imagine Skyrim, you make a mage character but the mages college in winterhold is in a level 50 zone but the companions don't require a level, you can only join one faction so who do you join? Well only crazy people like me will jetpack their way past enemies at the start of the game to join the Clerics, get the laser weapons and suddenly, you're unstoppable and the game is no longer a challenge. Plasma guns have an ability that knocks enemies back so Melee fights although taking forever because all your enemies are 4 or 5 times your level are easy. 

Maybe I'm just weird but if I hear about cool factions, I want to be able to join them regardless of what level I am, why should my level determine the fun I can have?

Just going to make this clear, this is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up review, but it's still a review. I don't dislike or hate this game, that is why I am on both sides. Either look at other reviews or you can have a look at mine. Also, I haven't played this game for a few months, but I do remember a lot about the game, and planning on playing more soon. Thanks for reading. Also, read the very last part if you want to see what I just think about the game.

The game is fun, combative, and stressful. It takes time to learn and play strategic, to avoid hostiles that can kick your ass in seconds. ELEX in my opinion, really good game, fun, and interative, but doesn't have a replayablity, which I am fine with. The campaign can take over 50+ hours to complete, I farmed a lot to become the best bad ass in the game, and it was fairly easy to do so. Not going to ruin the game or anything, but the Flamethrower, maxed out or not, is FAR too overpowered, and can literally kill anyone in a few hits or even a single hit. The gameplay is good, I enjoy using the jetpack to get around certain spots and take down enemies with ease, weapons are fair, except the flamethrower and the War Bow, jesus christ are those two weapons far too overpowerd. War Bow does literally 140 damage, and the Flamethrower is around 110-120 damage, and that's enough to one or two shot someone. Moving onto the movement, it's not that entirely bad. 

The campaign is... something. I wouldn't say it's a good type of campaign where you can get really into. But did I enjoy it? Difficult to say, due to at the beginning of the campaign, it was irritating to even play it. Reason I say that is because you have to do a bunch of shit for the Warlord to be able to move onto the rest of the campaign, and that'll take around ten to twenty hours of your time if you keep on dying or just want to get a hold on yourself. But the funny thing is, you don't HAVE to do his missions, but the game suggests you should. The reason you don't have to is because you have to go find Ray, a guy who salavaged your body and took your armor and such, and that will lead you onto further campaign missions. The reason the game suggests you to help out the Berserkers is because you can get a fairly good amount of Elex and EXP so you can take out hostiles throughout the game with more ease. But I wouldn't suggest you join the Berserkers unless your very interested into Medieval stuff. 

Now lets move onto the factions. The factions actually represent a lot of the game, showing of the medieval times, the modern time, and the futuristic time. In my opinion, I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ LOVE the Clerics, mainly because of their armor, their weaponery, along with their base. I haven't done all the factions, due to I don't want to replay the game two more times to just try out the other factions even though I know they all do the same shit but a bit of different side missions/missions. But currently, I do know the Clerics are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ overpowered with their flame thrower. If you main Clerics and just use the flamethrower, you are bound to die very little, and become the most powerful living being alive. The factions seem unbalanced, but I'm not entirely sure. I do know the Berserkers have the strongest weapon in the game, aka the War Bow. I know very little of the Outlaws, but I do know they live in the desert and aren't that interesting, except their armor. For the Berserkers, they are pretty much the beginning faction. Also, you can't leave factions once you join them. Moving on, their the medieval guys, the guys who use magic, swords, and bows. Are they fun to play with? Kind of. Swords are for beginners, never saw anything that does over 90+ damage, never tried out the magic, and bows, well, I already explained them. But that pretty much covers what the factions are, but let's move onto side missions and missions..

So, for missions, there's a lot. The campaign is extremely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ long, but fun. The side missions though, holy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ shit. There's at least around like, 20-40 side quests that I could find, which were mainly in the main bases for the factions. I've explored the entire map, and mainly killing stuff than finding side missions. It's quite hard to find side missions that aren't in the main faction cities. So, if you plan on doing all the main missions first and then side missions, then expect very little time. Doing the side missions will take at least five-ten hours, while the campaign can take over 50. 

Now for customization.. there's none. You can't customize your character's look, and instead with going with a silent protagonist, which would have been a great idea, they stuck with a dude's voice who sounds like he's smoked for his entire life and has little to no emotion or tone in his voice. For armor in this game, there's barely any. The main shit you can get is from joining a faction, which is fairly enjoyable doing so. I feel like they could have done a better job doing this instead of just making a shitty voice actor do this part.

Now here's what I think the game stands at:

7.7/10. Main reason is because it has great ideas, great process for entering the game, makes it difficult, the view is just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ gorgious, I'd give that a 9/10, same with the wind and way animations and other shit worked out, and makes it great from a gamer's perspective. 
Bad things about this was, no customization, very little to no armor, weird processes in joining factions, making you have to go farm for money to boost your rank up in a faction, have to go farm for EXP for hours to be able to fight certain enemies, makes you think you have to join a faction first to be able to continue the game, very little kind of enemies, and how there aren't any mods you can use for this, or even a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ multiplayer. I feel like this game would be fun if you could play with your friends rather than yourself. Reason I state that is because it'd seem interesting if you could have a server full of 100 players roam around, in same the faction or different, and doing war plans. I believe a multiplayer would have made the game far more improved and entertaining than a campaign that you wouldn't want to restart for the love of your life.

But yeah, that's my bad review on this difficult to say good game. Anyways, have a nice day.

Технологически игра выглядит очень старой (не в графике дело). Ощущение, что ее сделали 10 лет назад (или того больше), а продали год назад как новейшую игру с наворотами (именно наа это я рассчитывал). В игре нет ничего интересного, кроме пожалуй сюжета (и то под вопросом), полный дисбаланс, убогая боевка, странная прокачка. От врагов приходится убегать, иначе смерть (в начале игры)... а в конце игры - зачем мне все возможности, которые у меня будут, если это конец игры? Почему я должен выполнять задания, загоняющие меня черт знает куда, когда по карте живым пройти не могу? Пользоваться хитростями из руководств - как обхитрить недостатки игры и как не использовать те или иные навыки (потому что они не нужны), с нахождением секретного оружия, а иначе не пройти игру? Мне это не интересно. Игра должна вести игрока, постепенно раскрывая возможности и быть интересной и понятной! В этой игре этого нет. Я не могу порекомендовать эту игру своим друзьям. Наверно 10 лет назад я в нее еще и поковырялся бы, но сейчас... лучше уж поиграть в старый добрый Скайрим. Но пройти ее придется ради принципа((( ... и меня стошнит, меня уже тошнит от нее.

Вот и пройдена игра и игра оказалась отвратительной. Ни один аспект игры не был сделан нормально. Сюжет это пожалуй единственное что в игре есть, но и он вызывает уйму вопросов (по сути все умерли, это очевидно но всё же приходится додумывать самому). С остальным же всё куда хуже. Баланса в игре нет абсолютно. 80% предметов и функций использовать в игре нет никакого смысла. Вступление в группировку по сути ничего не решает, более того даже ничего дельного не открывает. С самого начала игры вас воспринимают как сильного ниндзю, почему так не понятно, но задания в начале даже хуже чем в конце. Диалоги в игре просто беспощадны, из кучи вариантов что не выбирай всё равно приходишь к одному, лишь иногда есть пара вариантов. К тому же большинство строчек настолько невнятны, что нажимать их приходится через силу. Поступать по своему игра совсем не позволяет, даже когда есть очевидные решения, всё равно игра заменяет их на поножовщину. Прокачка просто отвратительна, тут даже говорить ничего не надо кто дойдёт до крафта банок сам это осознает (кстати это единственный крафт каким вы будете заниматься, весь остальной крафт просто бесполезен)
   Из обещанного, вы можете сами выбрать свою судьбу (враньё) как не выбирал диалоги всё равно даже концовка была не такая как в диалогах, не говоря уже об остальном. Большой мир (враньё) совсем не большой, даже если телепорты не использовать. Несколько группировок со своим мнением и интересами (враньё) все 3 группировки это воры, убийцы и чёкнутые люди. Каждая вызывает отвращение и ничем не отличается от остальных.
   В общем отвратительная игра, оставляет ужасный осадок и во время игры и после её завершения.

100 heures de jeu, j'arrive à la fin d'Elex... j'étais mitigé lors de son achat (en promo 50%) vu les tests peu élogieux ... et je ne regrette vraiment pas cet achat. Ce jeu est excellent, certes la progression est très lente et difficile, mais pas insurmontable comme injustement critiqué à sa sortie, 
La carte est vaste, la liberté vraiment là, plein de missions, des choix cornéliens, des dialogues qui changent vraiment le cours du jeu.
Alors, certes, on peut toujours trouver quelques défauts, mais ce jeu mérite vraiment d'être dans votre liste de jeux si vous aimez les RPGs / action.
Si vous voulez progresser vite, et tuer tout le monde au bout de 15 minutes, si vous cliquez comme un forcené pour rosser du monstre  à la pelle, passez votre chemin, vous n'irez pas loin.
Les tests ont critiqué le patchwork scénaristique (futur apocalyptique, chevaliers, magie, hors la loi, etc..) mais finalement tout est bien ficelé, et tout devient de plus en plus cohérent jusqu'à la fin du jeu...
techniquement : j'ai eu quelques crash, mais je pense que c'est ma machine qui vieillit un peu.
petit + le système de sauvegarde est très bien fait...

Elex est un jeu intéressant par son exploration et ses décors. 

Par contre la jouabilité est vraiment désagréable surtout lors des combats. 

Le personnage a deux de tension ; les combats sont hachés, il n’y a aucun plaisir à faire des combats tellement cela manque de fluidité (esquive qui ne part pas même avec notre jauge d’endurance pleine, parade qui ne fonctionne pas toujours, précision trop aléatoire)  

Les raccourcis clavier ne sont pas changeable ce qui accentue le manque de fluidité.

Niestety Elex mnie rozczarował i zawiódł. Nigdy nie grałem w grę, która ma tak denerwujący, frustrujący, MEGA drewniany system walki i interakcji ze światem. Co za kretyn to projektował? Co za debil to zatwierdził? Coś takiego nie powinno mieć miejsca w naszych czasach. Nawet ich starsze produkcje jak Gothic, nie były tak złe pod względem sterowania i poruszania się bohaterem. Nie wiem jak ludzie grali w to na konsoli. Zapewne nie raz rzucili padem, albo co bardziej prawdopodobne - sami skoczyli z mostu, trzymając tą grę w ręku. 

Kolejna sprawa to dialogi. Każdy NPC z którym dane jest nam rozmawiać, zalewa nas nudnym potokiem paplaniny. Nawet ważne dla przebiegu historii kwestie sprowadzają się do "lania wody" i ględzenia niczym stara baba na bazarze. Sztampowe, nieciekawe, nudne, aż cięzko słuchać. Co tu jednak oczekiwać, wszystkie postacie to kukły bez charakteru i osobowości. Zlepek skryptów udających towarzyszy, czy ważnych osób dla świata. Zero zycia. Równierz aktorzy podkładający głos się nie popisali i dołożyli tutaj swoje kilka groszy...

Rozwój postaci zaprojektowany totalnie bez pomysłu. Większość umiejętnosci jest w ogóle nieprzydatna. Szkolenie się w walce wręcz mija się z celem, gdyż system walki to jedno wielkie gówno. Jedynie bronie dystansowe mają tutaj jakieś szanse na powodzenie, chociaż strzelanie pozostawia również wiele do życzenia. Pociski lecą gdzie chcą, jak chcą i którędy chcą. Na szczeście bronie dystansowe posiadają amunicję z obrażeniami obszarowymi, wtedy nieważne gdzie trafi - przeciwnik oberwie.

Do minusów należy zaliczyć ponadto:
- Pracę kamery, która wielokrotnie blokowała się podczas rozmów, lub w ciasnych pomieszczeniach lądowała po prostu w ścianie na czas dialogu z NPC
- Sztuczną inteligencje. 
- Minimapę, która jest najgorszą minimapą jaką kiedykolwiek widziałem
- Liczne bugi
- Przesadzony, wręcz nienormalny poziom trudności. Chociaż przy takim drewnianym sterowaniu, to jak może nie być trudno?

Jednak mimo wszystko spędziłem w tej grze blisko 90h i dotrwałem z dziką satysfakcją do napisów końcowych. Ludzie z Piranha Bytes umieją robić coś, czego większość twórców nie. Chodzi mi tutaj o niesamowity klimat gry, który mimo tych wszystkich wad, nie pozwala oderwać się od monitora. Rzuca sie "polską łacina" i gra się dalej, fascynujące przeżycie! Ma się dość tej gry, a równocześnie chce się brnąć dalej, eksplorować duży otwarty świat, zwiedzac ciekawie zaprojektowane lokacje i poznać dalsze losy tej dość ciekawej historii. Dobra gra na przetestowanie naszej cierpliwości, samozapracia i silnej woli...

[h1] DISCLAIMER: This is a first impressions review, and NOT a full review [/h1]

[quote] PLEASE NOTE: I recommended this game with some exceptions, overall if the game did not live up to just a tiny expectation, I would not have recommended it at all, so please read the review carefully if you are thinking of buying/playing this game [/quote]

ELEX is a game developed by Piranha Bytes and published by THQ Nordic

Piranha Bytes is one of the worst/'best' game company I've ever had the audacity to play their games. Playing the Gothic and Rise series of games on GOG, I've had very mixed feelings about the level of quality the developer 'develops' its games on

Let's start with the positives, the game has a interesting story, nothing unique but interesting. The world has some beautiful moments, but that's all I can say in regards to positives with ELEX

However, the game is littered with odd bugs and glitches, a horrible combat system, really sub-par voice acting, textures and graphical hitches that made the world look really out of place

But, alongside the Gothic series and to a lesser extent the Rise series, ELEX and Piranha Bytes' games are oddly unique and enjoyable, this is not one of those games I would play from start to finish, but it has a lot of content to keep you invested throughout, even with 10 hours of gameplay invested, I still haven't discovered the world ELEX has to offer

ELEX is a mixed bag, but if you like these types of games that are 'so bad it's good' type of games with clunky and odd mechanics, then you will certainly enjoy ELEX

Even with low expectations.... this game still managed to dissapoint me...

In my opinion its an absolute chaos in terms of game balance, the difficulty is all over the place. Soon you bump into high level enemies left right and center, no matter what you do. The enemies are either too difficult or way too easy to fight.

The level system is a joke, spending attribute points is actually counter productive as they do little to nothing, so you just sit on them until you know what talents and weapons you want to use. At this point you probably realice that you start to sit on talent points, since the requirements grow ridiculous quickly and you cant spent them on anything...

This game appeals to a nieche type of players. If you enjoy classic roleplaying, do not play this game. even if you are hungry for a new RPG and have no alternatives, I do not reccomend this game. Combat and leveling are extremly bad.

The rest of the game, to say something positive, is at least decent. But in my opinion that doesnt justify the buy...

Man sollte Elex nicht mit anderen Spielen (schon gar nicht mit neueren) vergleichen. Dieses Spiel hat große Stärken und große Schwächen, weshalb ich vielen anderen Reviews zustimme:

[list]
 [*]Ja, die Grafik ist nicht die von Witcher 3, dennoch sind die verschiedenen Gebiete schön inszeniert und erstrebenswert zu erkunden.
 [*]Ja, das Kampfsystem ist absoluter Schrott. Beim ersten Spielstand bin ich Psi-Magier der Kleriker, weil ich keine Lust hatte mich mit Kämpfen rumzuschlagen, und selbst da bekommt man bei eigentlich jedem Gegner die Krise.

Es gibt Nebenmissionen, deren Ausgang die eigene Sichtweise auf die Welt in Elex komplett verändern. Auch die Story der Hauptmissionen ist spannend zu spielen, weil es selbst nach 40 Stunden Spielzeit Dinge gibt, die ein neues Licht auf die Ereignisse werfen.
Was man unbedingt erwähnen sollte ist, dass jede einzelne Handlung einen riesen Einfluss auf den Ausgang anderer Quests haben kann bzw. wird. In Elex ist vor allem so ziemlich jeder NPC sterblich, jedoch bedeutet es direkt den Weltuntergang, wenn jemand stirbt oder getötet wird.

Was ich damit sagen will ist, dass die ganze Geschichte um Elex eine Gesamtheit besitzt, die in heutigen Spielen nur noch sehr selten zu finden ist; eine Eigenschaft, die ich seit Morrowind irgendwie vermisst habe. Dazu zählen aber natürlich auch gewissen Eigenarten des Spiels.
Zusammengefasst ist Elex einfach ein neues Spiel der alten Schule.

This will be the hardest review to write in my history. I've not yet decided, if I'll recommend this game or not, so let's dive in.

There is one sentence that perfectly summarizes ELEX. [b] Less is more. [/b]

[u]World[/u] – It's enormous. Honestly, it's one of the biggest open world RPG I've played. It consists of four biomes. But this doesn't come with a cost. It's dull. Not at first, but the more you play and explore, the more you get frustrated by the same red brick buildings. The dullness is the result of how big the world is because PB is capable of creating beautiful locations. For example Domed City – It's plain beautiful with its castle walls and futuristic shield. To be honest, I was a bit afraid of fantasy and sci-fi mix, but it works quite well. It's nowhere near to Horizon: Zero Dawn, which feels a bit more natural. I'm going to reference HZD a few times because the games are quite in common. In ELEX I feel like the world is real. You can see people's daily routines; you can hear them talk; you can even hear them talk about your quest for example. You can even get a quest out of this dialogue! Not many games can put that in their resume.

[u]Story[/u] – This part Piranha Bytes always gets right. Story and lore is, in my opinion, the main reason, why to play this game. It is exciting to uncover all mysteries; it just consumes you. There are very few games, which ties me to the edge of my chair. But I have one complaint. The bits and pieces of the lore are all over the place and not properly structured. A major part of lore is found in notes, but you lose the context. It's something that Horizon Zero Dawn also did better. What HZD didn't do better and in what PB games always excel is the flexibility of completing quests. It is pure joy. You get a quest, and I can guarantee you there are at least three possible solutions to your quest. Do you have to steal a sword? Great. You can decline the quest; you can agree to the quest and then stole it. Now you can give it back to the quest giver, or you can give it back to the owner.  This decisions also make a difference in your world and relations to NPC. It is even Mass Effect level. But, what is unquestionably not Mass Effect level are companions. They have the potential to be interesting, but they do not have enough space. There are no interactions between them.

[u]Combat[/u] – Well, we're slowly getting to the worse parts of the game. Combat. Piranha Bytes and their clunky combat. It's essentially a mark of their games. Combat in ELEX is, on the other hand, a step back because combat in first Risen was excellent despite the clunkiness. In ELEX, there are a lot of issues. Miserably dumb AI, bad hitbox, small distance to show monster's hitpoints and name – and that's just the small stuff. The real problem lies in stamina. It's the biggest pain in the ass mechanic. If your stamina is depleted, you can do nothing, literally nothing. For melee characters, the fight looks like this: You equip your range weapon, fire one shot to the enemy to lure him, switch to melee weapon, dodge or block charge attack, deplete your stamina with combos and then... Then you're just walking in circles – because you can't run – hoping you won't get one-shotted by monsters. Your other choice is to use jet-pack, which also has a meter bar. But don't count on it, because due to clunkiness and slow responses, you won't always get off from the ground. You sometimes just jump. 
There are also special strong attacks. A heavy attack, which does more damage, but you get interrupted in most cases because it takes too long to perform. And there is a special attack, which can be only executed if your combo yet-another meter is high enough. But there is the same problem, it takes ages. And with unpredictable enemies (and allies) it's near impossible to use this technique effectively. Combat is easily the most frustrating part of this game. I've played on Ultra on my first and only playthrough, and I died [b]a lot[/b]. You also will die a lot. It could've been ok if it was your mistake, but often, you die because of the poorly implemented combat system. And since bad implementations are your enemy, it also can be taken advantage of. I killed many monsters just due to a bug, where they got stuck in a texture. Also fight against multiple enemies at once is abysmal. Even with target lock off, if you kill one enemy during your melee combo, you cannot continue the combo to another target next to the original. You just swing your sword in the same direction, while the big chicken will tear you apart. I also hate another part of combat. Stun-lock. Again, it's your friend, because if you cannot stun-lock your enemy, you'll die. Unfortunately the same goes for the enemy. If they respawn with knockback weapon, you cannot do anything, you just get stun-locked to death. And ranged combat? Projectiles are ridiculously slow; you get recoil for your guns and enemies can hit you almost everytime no matter what.

[u]Gameplay[/u] – Oh boy. There are so, so many little annoying things, that just doesn't make sense. PB should follow the [i]less is more[/i] rule here. Let's start my biggest issue, nothing is explained. And the few things, that are explained, are explained badly. Attributes are just enablers for skills and equipment. Skills are in few examples straight up useless. Weapons can be modified to nine elements. Nine! And is there some explanation of what the damage types do? Is there some bestiary with weakness? Of course not. Have fun reading Reddit, where there are guys, who spent enormous time testing and observing. Piranha Bytes doesn't want you to chase for numbers, I actually get that. But for ♥♥♥♥'s sake, you have healing potion which heals for 40 HP, for 80 HP, and for 120 HP. Good, and how many HP do you have? Which potion should you use? There is no stat for that. Or for stamina, or mental energy. Or basically anything. I absolutely hate this decision. 
Another example of bad mechanics is gems. You can find small gems which add negligible stats or upgrade them. Well, the thing is, if you want to upgrade gem to the max, you have to search through the whole map. There aren't enough gems. You cannot buy them; you cannot create them; you cannot find bigger gems, only the small ones. Why then even bother with this mechanic? 
Do you remember, how I said that less is more? Well, there is over twenty types of ammo. There are arrows, special arrows, other special arrows, same for bolts, spears, projectiles, shotgun shells, grenades, rockets, plasma cells, energy cells, fuel. There is so much. But you cannot utilize them due to one simple thing. Interface. Holy moly I've never been so much desperate in a game because of a bad interface. You find several types of Alb spells; you have several kinds of potions, food, chems, weapons (melee/ranged/heavy/magic), Clerics got another dozen of spells (over ten), two weapons each with three magic spells. And what you got? Quick bar with ten slots with no way to bind more via alt/shift/ctrl modifications. The game offers you so much, but due to game design, you're just unable to use it. ELEX is – I think – the first game, where weapons are not faction specific. That's great on paper, but again, try to use them in combat.
And Quests. Please, just show via color code if I am able to complete this quest or if I get stomped to the ground. It gets tired to quick safe before quest, get teleported to the location, spend five minutes trying and then give up and load.

[u]Graphics[/u] – ELEX is missing Risen atmosphere. Nights aren't dark enough, there are hundreds of characters, but only like five faces. Overall not much to say. I get that PB is a studio with 30 people but this game costs like AAA titles.

ELEX is nor good or bad Piranha Bytes game, but in the end, I cannot recommend it. PB fans will get it anyway – and they should, but the rest will be better off to try Risen series first.
Достойное продолжение серии игр Gothic и Risen в 2017 году.

I wish there was some kind of "Situational Yes" option instead of just yes or no, because this game requires quite a bit of patience to stick through.

The setting is really unique and interesting. Characters and societies are, like in most PB games, very believable and human; not everyone is of the same mind and ever faction in the game has people who are just there for security or money as opposed to being True Believers in the cause. Conversations and quests are a little robotic but not unbearable.

The combat system is deeply, DEEPLY frustrating, and the main reason why I say it can be hard to stay interested in the game. As with Gothic and other PB games, combat is very good for single combat, but the moment you have to fight more than one enemy the bullshit begins. It's very hard, but possible to hit multiple enemies in a swing, which obviously makes fighting groups hard if you're alone. Companions are incredibly fragile and die permanently so it's not much of a relief if you have them. The stamina sucks- your normal attacks don't do much damage so you need to build up a combo meter and execute special attacks. The problem with this is that usually uses almost all of your stamina, and then you don't have any left to dodge enemy attacks until it regenerates. Enemy attacks interrupt your actions and yours (hypothetically) interrupt theirs. I say hypothetically because, very frustratingly, enemies will occasionally just shrug it off and hit you anyway through your attacks, essentially just doing free damage and preventing you from fighting them, and possibly even stunlocking you to death. Human enemies will block your swings and then hit you back faster than you can react. Basically everything swings faster than you do, so you have to spam attack them, use your combo, then use your jetpack to try to evade their return. If you go too far away, most enemies have some kind of ranged attack (guns or... vomit) which they have perfect accuracy with all the time. 

I've rambled on long enough, but I think I've given you a picture of how ♥♥♥♥♥♥ this game's combat system is. It's just not fun, and I haven't even named all the bullshit ways it screws you over. You win combat by finding gimmicks and exploits in the system and using them, no other way. But if you can be patient with it, the game's pretty enjoyable.

Stubborn Piranha Bytes brought us yet another renamed Gothic with everything we love and hate about their games.

Terrible combat system combined with unpredictable and unavoidable enemy attack patterns will ensure that enemy encounters will always be as frustrating as possible, and extremely high difficulty at the beginning will again ensure that only hardcore Piranha Bytes fans will endure long enough to discover the beauty hidden behind all the unpolished aspects, which are PB games tradermarks since first Gothic.

Those patient and tolerable enough will be rewarded with great worldbuilding, exploration, hundreds of unique quests, robust RPG systems, story impacting decision-making and this time even quite good (althought not very original) story in unique fantasy/scifi setting, where you start your journy with axe and bow in your hands and end up with chainsword and plasma guns, jumping on enemies from the skies thanks to the jetpack like an assault space marine from Warhammer 40k universe.

If you are not a "production values" gamer and want to play some hardcore oldschool RPG, you should give ELEX a shot. Piranha Bytes games never had (and probably never will have) user friendly gameplay, but their games are much more addictive than any other higher budget RPG I ever played.

I  ended up really liking this game. As most negitive reviews have stated the first 10 hrs is not that great. But once you get passed that the game become a lot of fun. You do get that fealing that you are getting stronger. In the beginning your run away from every thing, later you see a large troll with a skull by their name and you run towards it after 5 or 10 min or dancing the troll falls. I like the combat system for a shield and weapon mix. I found that my play style ends up being very similar to dark souls. In fact a lot of the strategy I use in dark souls worked in Elex. Block, kite around the back, attack a few times and then roll away to create some breathing room and get some stamina back.

For me the combat system was one of the best for shield and weapon. I like how you can stack attacks to create a combo. I think some people have a problem because they wait for the weapon to hit before clicking for the next attack, but what that does is do 2 single attacks beacause you need to press the attack button before it hits to create the combo chain. Which I like, I can press shield bash,strike and then shield bash then block quickly and then you see the combo animation play out. While the combo is play out I can think of defence or what my next attacks will be. Dodging will interupt a combo.  I also like how your attacks build moment which increases your damage by quite a large value. Which just adds another layer to the combat, if you want to maxize damage. 

To me it make for a more plan your attack and then execute it, then move. Rather than just spamming attack.  The jet pack is something every open world game needs.

I really hope their next game keeps the combat system and has swords / axe and shield. I have played other games made by PB but this is the best for combat.

I went in expecting something akin to Skyrim or Fallout, which this isn't. There are obvious pros and cons with the game, but overall, I really enjoy it. It started out fairly rough and I almost gave up on the game, but something kept drawing me back. Now, I can play it for hour on end. If you like a game that has a heavy amount of exploration and decisions to make, then I recommend this. However, don't be surprised if this game doesn't hold your hand. Monsters don't level out the further from the start point; sometimes the best thing to do is bug out from a fight. When you do level up, check out guides of which skills to acquire immediately, as this may be the crux of whether you can get shards (in-game currency) in a timely manner. 

Two other unique abilities: you have a rechargeable jetpack and an unlimited inventory. Pick up everything.

Updated review: I experienced game burnout and haven't played in some time. I still recommend the game, but just know that it can get a bit old after awhile.

[h1]ELEX  - одна из самых обманчивых игр, в которые я играл[/h1]
На волне общего восхищения  приобрел сие творение, но игра этого восхищения не достойна.
На первый взгляд все смотрится довольно оптимистично: приятная картинка, интересный сеттинг, проверенные временем разработчики. Однако, всё это не более чем красивая обертка.
[b]Разберем по пунктам:[/b]
[list]
    [*] Геймплей. Он тут, скажем так, средний. Ни боевка, ни система прокачки особо не выделяются, но нельзя сказать, что они откровенно плохи. Ваши навыки влияют не только на возможности персонажа в бою или крафте, но и позволяют вам иметь дополнительные ответы в диалогах с неигровыми персонажами.     [*] Сюжет. Он довольно банален и мал. One area I don't think reviewers give this game enough credit for is the vast amount of choice & consequence built into the quests.  You can literally lock out entire questlines by certain choices, meaning multiple playthroughs are a must if you want to experience 'everything'.  Most NPCs seem to remember your choices as well, adding depth.

Bottom line: old school RPG, choices matter, replayability is high with this one (multiple factions, quests).

I'm putting summary here as probably most ppl won't feel like reading my long review. 

In sum the game is worth giving it a try imo, especially if you pick it up on sale (paid around 20$). Have in mind you will have to invest a few hours to learn (probably the harsh way) how this game works and how to deal with it. If you look for casual and easy game experience this game isn't for you.

The game has it's issues, but if you get pass them it can be a great experience. If you played Gothic/Risen series you more or less know what to expect. The major difference is the difficulty people are so negatively talking about. If you try to do the same stuff as you do in all others game and what you used to do in gothic, then yes, you gonna get your butt kicked. But if you forget about it, start using your brain and notice what the game tries to tell you from the start - you will be fine. In at least a few first couple of hours you are not really supposed to fight. That’s something completely different than we all are used to in games of this kind. The usual story about a guy who lost his strength looks a bit different here.  You actually are going to be very weak for at least a few first hours of gameplay and will have to rely only on your cunning. You can sneak, steal, run - whatever works. From my experience: after a few hours and a few gained levels I decided to go and try my luck again in combat. And i got my ass kicked again by a basic monster. Was frustrating, but then i found out i can travel to other capital cities, do more quests, loot more stuff, get stronger without fighting. After a while you will be able to kill/beat anything and it's much more satisfying than easily gained power.

About the story and technical stuff.
* It's not Witcher 3 story wise, but it's ok. Usual stuff. Do quests, join a faction, explore the world, save the world. If you look for a deep story you won't find it here, but for me it was enough to have fun.
* Interesting moral system. You are not being judged by good or evil standards. You are being judged by having/expressing emotions or not. You can be emotional or cold as a machine. And this statistic impacts some dialog options. I haven't finished the game yet, but I'm pretty sure it has an impact also on the ending. 
* Combat system. It's ok. But you need time to level up and train your character. Unlock new combat moves and possibilities. Upgrade your weapons etc.
* Levelling system. This one is quite interesting. In addition to traditional "gather xp -> level up -> get 1 skill point and 10 stat points", you can also improve your character by acquiring wealth. I would even say you should improve this way or you might have a hard time progressing. Stealing, exploring, hunting, questing - whatever works for you. You can brew potions which give you stat/skill points and help you get out of "being  too weak to fight" stage. Resources needed to make them can be bought or harvested from wildlife if your skill is high enough.  The possible downside is when you drink them, your cold statistic increases and you become less human. Downside unless you plan to play as a cold person. If you don't it is totally possible to drink them and remain 100% human. All you need to do is to stay emotional in your interactions with NPCs. Imo it’s a very good idea. Finally you can spend all this stuff you gather to improve your character. Every hard earned elexit shard counts.

Probably the worst Piranha Bytes game to date. While Gothic 3 failed due to numerous bugs, which were eventually fixed by the community, Elex fails in design decisions already. And this time around PB cannot blame Jowood for their failure.

On the plus sides: 
+ as usual, I find PB worlds quite believables and interesting to explore
+ Good graphics, interesting environments, cool looking mobs
+ Tons of quests, voice acting, NPCs
+ Vertical exploration
+ Story - I found the main theme really interesting and with a lot of potential, as you can see from the thumbs down, it is a wasted potential

And then the long list of things where the game fails miserably:
- PB somehow decided it would be fun when you're a weakling for like half of the game, meaning you won't be doing much combat until like 20h into the game
- The "Gothic formula" still applies here and it hasn't aged well
- Exploration - first you explore areas with your pants full since pretty much everything can tear you apart, when you can finally mount an offence, you don't want to explore the same stuff for the second time
- Combat is probably the worst I have ever experienced. The only difficulty here comes from clunky controls and terrible stagger mechanics
- Dialogues - already the very first monologue and dialog in the game makes you think the dialogues were written bz a 5 years old
- IU design - whoever designed it deserves to be forced to scroll through his own UI for eternity as a punishment
- Quests - the very first quests force you to go to areas where you will get torn apart in seconds or... just jetpack your way through
- Vertical exploration - back door to complete seemingly impossible quests at low levels
- Loot - most of the stuff you get early on you cannot use, when you are able to start using it, turns out it's useless (most legendary artifacts), tiered weapons don't really fit the "Gothic" universe
- Pretty much everything that is not listed as a plus above is bad, clunky, boring or simply unifnished

Though I have completed the game, it was a chore to play and I am glad it is over. As a die-hard Gothic fan I will be awaiting Elex 2 with anticipation. Hopefully PB will take community criticism seriously this time around instead of trying to fullfil their wet dream of a huge and interesting game world that they can never seem to be able to make right.

But that is the only good part about this game.

The battle is really clunky and the beginning of the game is really frustrating. You are basically surrounded by enemy that is far higher level than you. That itself is fine, but exp in this game is very slow. And similar like other Gothic games all weapon is locked by stats requirement. All armor is locked as well. You are surrounded by weapon that you cant use until 10 level later and you are surrounded by enemy that is like 20 level higher. It is close to impossible trying to kill high level enemy with low level weapon as you will need hundreds of arrow. Imagine how frustrating that is. You feel like a goblin surrounded by death knight each time. 

After you reach higher level, you will only realise that many weapon is totally broken and some weapon is just useless. Plasma rifle for example can just stun lock enemy till they are dead and the ammo is not hard to find as well. The enemy AI is very dumb, most of the enemy you can just fly to higher ground and shoot till they die even for range enemy it applied as well.

There is many glitch or game mechanics in the game that can be abused as well. Stealing in this game will give you ten times more money than selling a legendary sword. Exp, attribute point is infinite after you reach a certain point.

If you are Gothic game fans, this game might be worth considering as the game mechanics are similar. Otherwise I can only recommend this game if it is on sales

Loved this game.

I thought it was really clever to have three different factions that could almost be described as, Skyrim; Fallout; Mass Effect.  There are a lot of subtle touches I enjoyed in the quest system, particularly that once you've completed a quest, the quest giver will usually have additional dialogue/rewards when you return to them, and that other characters will react to you differently upon completion of quests.

The difficulty can seem punishing at first, but as you gain skills, it becomes very managable.

In terms of bugs, they've been overstated.  I only encountered one quest-breaking bug when an NPC clipped through the ground.

The ability to see dialogue in the mission tree was useful as well.

If you enjoy Euro-janky games like STALKER and The Witcher (original), this game should be right up your alley.  And even if you don't, ELEX feels quite polished and intuitive with a modern sense of game design.

Am liebsten hätte ich einen Daumen zur Seite vergeben. Für die Leute, die schon Piranha Bytes Spiele gespielt haben, ist dieses Spiel im Grunde wie die Vorgänger Risen und Gothic, mit wenigen kleineren Änderungen. Wenn euch auch die neueren Piranha Bytes Spiele gefallen haben, werdet Ihr auch Elex mögen.

Elex macht einige Sachen wirklich gut, aber leider auch ein paar Sachen schlecht:

1. Die handgemachte Welt ist richtig gut. Es macht einen riesen Spaß alles zu Erkunden. Man findet immer wieder spannende einzigartige Dinge. Dieser Teil des Spiels kann sich wirklich sehen lassen. Das Jetpack gibt einem dabei zusätzliche Optionen und ist eine richtige Bereicherung.

2. Die Fortschrittskurve ist nahezu Perfekt. Während man am Anfang gegen die meisten Gegner chancenlos ist und jeder Kampf eine richtige Herausforderung, merkt man das ganze Spiel über, wie man immer besser wird. Am Ende ist man schließlich eine schwer zu stoppende ein Mann Armee. Es ist sehr befriedigend, wenn man merkt, wie Gegner, die am Anfang noch ein unüberwindbares Hinderniss darstellen immer schneller vor einem in die Knie gehen.

3. Der Waffenmix aus verschiedensten Nah- und Fernkampfwaffen funktioniert erstaunlich gut. 

Leider hat Elex aber auch ein paar Macken, die das Spiel teilweise frustrierend machen:

1. Die Steuerung in den Kämpfen: Es passiert leider regelmäßig, dass der Charakter rollt, obwohl man keinen entsprechenden Befehl beabsichtigt hat. Es ist sehr ärgerlich, wenn man aufeinmal auf den Gegner zurollt, dadurch seine kostbare Ausdauer verliert und sofort vom Gegner halb tot geprügelt wird. Leider passieren unbeabsichtigte Rolle extrem häufig (Alle 1 bis 2 Minuten).

2. Standardmäßig ist ein Autofokus aktiviert. Dieser macht Kämpfe gegen mehr als einen Gegner zur Qual. Man kann ihn zwar auststellen, dies geht aber im Menü zum Schwierigkeitsgrad. Nach etw 15 Stunden, war ich so genervt, dass ich das über Google rausgefunden habe. Gute Menüführung sieht anders aus.

3. Höhenunterschiede versauen Kämpfe auf die verschiedensten Arten: Befindet sich ein Gegner etwas niedriger, als der Spieler, kann es passieren, dass man einfach über den Gegner drüber schlägt. Da solche Angriffe den Gegner nicht staggern erhält man dadurch ordentlich Schaden. Das sieht nicht nur lächerlich aus, sondern macht auch keinen Spaß. Das andere Problem ist die Mechanik, mit der verhindert werden soll, dass man einfach mit seinem Jetpack eine unerreichbare Position aufsucht und von dort alle Gegner ohne Gegenwehr abschießt. 80 % der Gegner verfügen über einen Fernangriff. Dieser ist in der Regel gefährlicher als der Nahkampfangriff, weil er den Charakter Niederschlägt, Autohittet oder mit Statuseffekten belegt.
Das Problem ist aber, dass Gegner diese Angriffe auch benutzen, wenn sie sich irgendwie festbuggen oder irgendwo runtergedrängt werden. Es kann also passieren, dass ein Hornwolf, den man im Nahkampf bei vernünftiger Spielweise in den Griff bekommt einen Batzen Blut spuckt. Dieser schlägt einen dann sofort Nieder und lässt einen Bluten, wodurch man über Zeit sein halbes Leben verliert. So zu sterben ist sehr frustrierend, weil man so etwas nicht verlässlich verhindern kann.

Die Story ist mittelmäßig und dient eher als Ausrede verschiedenste Quests zu erledigen und Feinde zu besiegen. Das ist nicht unbedingt schlimm, weil das Spiel dafür andere Stärken hat.

Insgesamt sollte man sich vor dem Kauf überlegen, ob einem die Stärken genügen, um die Schwächen auszugleichen. Das Erkunden und die lange Spielzeit sind aufjedenfall gute Kaufargumente. Man muss aber mit dem Kampfsystem leben können und braucht eine gewisse Frustrationstoleranz.

I decided, at around four hours into the game, that I would definitely write up a review of this title, but held off on a review until I had completed the game atleast once. 
 
 On the technical side, this game is an utter mess. The rendering will often have trouble keeping up with the movie scenes and changes from one place to the next. The opening scenes I had rendered in, even after adjusting settings and re-loading everything, it was like the game engine just couldn't handle what was asked of it. 
 
 The storyline in this game goes from pretty decent to utter trash in waves. Some of the story will be well flushed out, then you will fall face first into a plot hole that later will become a plot chasm, where it feels like they either did not translate everything accurately. Somewhere in the middle of the game there is a complete change in how your character was injured and then changed to be injured in another way. The immersion is pretty bad at this point. There are plot twists and a couple very lazily forced in moments. the romance options throughout the game are shallow and nearly un-needed at all. Then you will find a quest line or sidequest that is awesome and well brought forth. The endings have a terrible cliffhanger type of "Wait till you see Elex 2! Coming out in 20XX", which was not set up well.
 
 I set the game for the hardest settings expecting this to be a hell of a fight, which it was. The combat is only difficult for a few reasons though. often you will be fighting the game mechanics themselves. Camera and lock on functions will leave you open from even the slightest angle of attack and the parry mechanics are rarely synched with the incoming attacks. Ranged weapons are heavily weighted in favor of anything else and magic becomes so overpowering that you will wonder why you even bother carrying a mellee weapon at all. Traveling the path of a mellee warrior (Which I did on my playthrough) makes the game go from very hard to unimaginably frustrating. I actually give the game props for this, it would be a mix between tests of patience, dodging and putting thorough thought in how to deal with enemies. it eliminated the old fashioned "Run in and slam everything with your face" tactics that most games devolve to at end game. I've put in about 14 hours into the game so far, definitely enough to get a feel for the story and the gameplay.  I see a lot of reviews mentioning the combat system and the difficulty, so I thought I'd write a bit about that.

This is not a typical hack-and-slash game that holds your hand and gives you easy mobs and quests to solve out of the gate.  It hands you a set of tools and some open-ended quests and lets you figure out how you're going to finish them.  The first few hours of the game I had nothing but a metal pipe to beat enemies with (which was practically useless), so I found other ways to gain XP and money and used the jetpack to make my way around without directly fighting.  Eventually, I found a companion and they were able to tank one or two enemies at a time while I snuck in some flanking attacks.  Sometimes that wouldn't work, and I'd have to distract one or two of the monsters while my companion killed them off individually.  Some of the beginning quests I've had to avoid altogether, for now, because they deal with enemies way beyond my current level.

I've been playing the Witcher games, and while I don't think it's fair to compare the graphics to Witcher 3 (because Witcher 3 is so far above the bar), the look of ELEX is more akin to Witcher 2, a game that is 7 years old.  Most of the time, NPCs' arms will be clipping through their weapons and armor while they gesture, and their faces barely emote at all.  Speaking of emoting, while storywise it makes sense for Jax's voice to sound off (a side effect of Elex), even the Beserkers, who do not take Elex and are supposed to be the "emotional" faction, sound like they're straight from a B movie.  To me, it's more hilariously bad than grating.

The story and the factions so far have been engrossing, it just takes a while to get used to the fact that in some instances the dialogue isn't as open as the rest of the game.  Exploring the world and figuring out which side to take in conflicts (if you participate at all) has been what makes this game really fun.  

If you can get it while it's on sale, I'd recommend it.

It really does deserve its mixed rating, but I'm coming down on the positive side anyways. I had a mostly good time with this game. Elex is a beautiful, fascinating, and complex world to explore underneath some very mediocre, buggy systems and UI design. You'll know very quickly if you're going to like it, because all the annoyances are right up front and the game plays the same way throughout. If you're not getting sucked in before the refund window ends, opt out immediately. Even if you can stomach the dreck I wouldn't expect to get more than one playthrough out of this. The ending 'choice' is predetermined based on your character's disposition and the unique faction content is pretty sparse. There are a lot of ways individual quests can play out but not enough for me to want to go back for more. 

It's a tragedy that this never got the year or two of the finishing touches it desperately needs, because it feels a lot like an early access game with a fantastic core concept abandoned in beta. Definitely a sale game.
