[h1]前言：[/h1]

首先表明我的评测观点：好评，我个人强烈推荐游玩。

重点推荐游玩的人群：喜欢上古卷轴，辐射，巫师，质量效应等开放世界类RPG游戏的玩家；对科幻，奇幻，废土末世，西方中世纪等题材感兴趣的玩家；喜欢真实硬核设定RPG的玩家；[strike]喜欢黑魂，仁王，血源等受苦系战斗的抖M玩家以及被一些公式化开放世界游戏荼毒已久非常想换换口味的玩家（滑稽）[/strike]

建议观望的人群：喜欢线性流程RPG，不喜欢开放世界RPG的玩家；极其看重操作体验的玩家；选择困难症玩家；完美主义玩家；[strike]经常被路边小怪虐死（游戏初期的常态）之后容易冲动暴怒砸键盘摔手柄锤显示屏的玩家（滑稽）[/strike]

[h1]正文：[/h1]

截止我写下这篇评测时，ELEX这款游戏我已玩了70多个小时，游戏里显示游玩时长是50多个小时，我是通常难度通关的，选择牧师阵营，最终打出好结局，坏结局我还没有尝试，剧情暂时没做加入土匪和狂战士的后续主线任务，并且可能有部分支线的遗漏，但基本可以说对游戏各种机制十分了解和熟悉了，我玩得有些肝痛，先喝些护肝茶，以后再战（滑稽）。下面我从多个方面对本游戏做一个尽量全面的评测，也是对自己这段游戏历程的一个总结。篇幅或许有些长，我将各个方面小标题用了蓝字（留言板用分割线隔开），如果时间有限或者没有耐心全部看完的玩家，只选择自己对这游戏感兴趣的方面阅读即可。

[h1]本地化方面：[/h1]

像这种以剧情驱动的开放世界类RPG游戏，本地化的翻译质量可以说是十分重要了。本作的简体中文汉化质量我是比较满意的。有些评测说汉化完全是机翻的，我不敢苟同。因为汉化文本中的不少中文词汇完全不是机翻能翻译出来的。我的感受是人工翻译至少占百分之95以上，剩下不到百分之5可能是机翻（我估计是文本量有些大，翻译的老哥有些绝望了哈哈），中间包含少许错别字，但完全不影响整体游玩体验和剧情代入的沉浸感，特别好评给女土匪同伴娜斯蒂的大量骂人骚话的翻译，很有国骂连珠炮的感觉。

[h1]剧情方面：[/h1]

在尽量不涉及剧透的情况下，我这里只谈一下故事背景和游戏阵营。

故事是发生在一个叫玛格兰的大陆上，一颗彗星撞击了大陆，导致大陆的地形气候发生了巨变，大量建筑遭到破坏，大量人员和动物或者死亡或者受到辐射而变成了变种生物，随着彗星而来的还有一种奇特的物质，ELEX，中文译为“奥能”，一般以蓝色结晶体矿物的形式大量存在并分布于整个大陆，整个游戏自始至终都是围绕着ELEX展开的，天灾的发生导致原有的世界政治、经济、军事体系全面崩溃，因此天灾发生前的世界被称为“旧世界”，纸钞和硬币也变为了“旧世界货币”，而在游戏中的现世，流通货币就是ELEX奥能的碎片，少数人员幸存下来开始繁衍生息，并被称为“自由人民”。随着时间的演变大陆的幸存者们逐渐形成了三大阵营，狂战士（Berserkers），牧师（Clerics），土匪（Outlaws）（有些像三国）。（这里提一下游戏中一个叫作“无尽虚空”的公司，这是一家在旧世界非常有实力的公司，即使是在新世界也可以随处可见其宣传和资料，可见其影响力之广，该公司的性质类似于《辐射》系列的避难所科技公司，在故事起源中起着很重要的作用）

三大阵营各自占据着一方领土，他们的共同点是都利用奥能的力量，但是方式各不相同，狂战士将其转化为法力从而修习各种强大的魔法力量，牧师将其用于研究科技，机器和灵能，甚至可以影响人的心智，土匪将其用于研制兴奋剂（类似于带有成瘾性的毒品）强化自身和改造各种武器。三大阵营的利益出发点和追求也不同，狂战士崇拜一种叫“世界之心”的巨大植物，想将世界改造成自然的生态世界的模样，认为科技发展是造成天灾的原因，因此在领地内禁止一切科技存在（玩家在狂战士领地打开类似BB小子的手戴装置查看界面时会被周围的狂战士各种吐槽，因为这装置本身也是一种科技产物），牧师信仰他们的神明--卡拉恩，并且认为科技发展是将重建美好世界的核心，土匪追求自由发展，完全对于改造世界使之变得更好没有任何兴趣，崇尚利益和实力高于一切，无视各种规章制度，喜欢搞各种争斗和破坏。

由于各自对奥能的利用方式和对待世界的观点截然不同，三方阵营连年互相发动战争，彼此实力均消耗严重，这时一个第四方的阵营---智械（Albs）横空出世，智械的人们均极度崇尚效率与逻辑，他们平时吸食纯正的奥能，这让他们渐渐丧失了人类的情绪和感性，自身拥有着更接近于机器的冷酷和理性。他们拥有着比牧师更加先进的科技实力，追求完全摒弃人类的七情六欲，从而实现“进化”。他们平时趁着三方争斗时一直在积蓄力量，冷眼旁观，隐忍不发，等待着合适的时机。

智械趁三方阵营打得彼此两败俱伤之际，大举出兵攻击三方阵营，并且趁着三方阵营措手不及被打得节节败退之际在三方阵营各自的领地伊丹、伊纳顿、塔瓦尔以及中立区域阿珀莎分别建立了叫做“转换站”的建筑物，转换站的用处是将人类，动物和各种物品扔进去产出奥能，在智械的历史发展中起初是供智械们吸食奥能，后来则主要是供智械的领袖“混合体”使用，混合体上台之后宣称自己已经预示了未来，只有将大陆上所有奥能归于自己运用，才能真正拯救这片大陆，少数反对混合体的智械们认为混合体是异端，将让智械族集体进化异化为他自身的进化，他们集体出走，切断了与混合体的联系，成为了“独立分子”，一面对抗着混合体率领的智械同胞，一面应付着仍然不信任他们的自由人民，混合体统领下的智械加大了对其余三方阵营的侵略和掠夺。三方阵营见势不妙，随即明面上不计前嫌，携手对抗智械，然而暗地里暗流汹涌，彼此的隔阂和争斗仍未断绝。但是这一联手也让智械与三方阵营的争斗陷入了僵持的局面。

在这一故事背景下，我们的主角，贾克斯，闪亮登场。他是智械军队最优秀的指挥官之一，而且他的弟弟卡拉西和父亲瓦德克都是智械族有名的指挥官，贾克斯做事冷静果敢，唯命是从，为智械族出色地完成了各项艰难任务，在对抗三大阵营的战争中也建立了不少功勋，深受混合体的信任和智械人民的爱戴，有一次他接受混合体的直接命令，乘坐飞船外出执行一项秘密任务，却在经过狂战士领地伊丹时被不明人员击落，飞船坠毁后虚弱的贾克斯逃了出来，没想到他的亲兄弟卡拉西已经带着一小队智械士兵出现了，智械族的规定是任务失败就要被处决以示警示，卡拉西开枪处决了贾克斯，贾克斯掉落悬崖，或许是智械强大的体质和力量救了他一命，让他两次死里逃生，他醒来后发现自己身上的智械护甲已经被扒去，而自己却不知为什么已经切断了与混合体的联系，脱离了他的控制（也就意味着可以产生情感），“我的护甲去哪里了？”“究竟是什么人击落了我的飞船？”“为什么卡拉西会恰好带人出现并将我处决？”“这背后究竟隐藏着怎样的阴谋？”，贾克斯带着满肚子的疑问在这片美丽而危险的广袤大陆上开始了自己探索历程，而你将作出选择，决定贾克斯是成为一个无情冷酷的智械？还是一个唤回情感的人类？是继续效忠于强大的混合体？还是加入自由人民与其共同对抗智械族？并且玩家在探索中会逐渐揭开真相，究竟贾克斯的秘密任务是什么？三大阵营和智械都有着怎样的历史？智械从何而来？贾克斯和卡拉西的两兄弟有着怎样不为人知的身世？混合体的真实身份是什么？混合体是在说谎还是真的预见了什么？一个精（Jian）彩（La）的（Ji）故事由此展开。

游戏主要包含四大阵营（势力，派系）。狂战士（Berserkers），牧师（Clerics），土匪（Outlaws），智械（Albs）。为了给大家一个大致的直观的印象，我这里简单粗暴的用一些知名的开放世界RPG游戏对各个阵营做一下类比。狂战士---《上古卷轴》，土匪---《辐射》，牧师，智械---《质量效应》。狂战士，牧师，土匪，这三个派系可以由玩家自由选择加入其中的一个，而一旦选择加入了其中一个，就不能再加入另外两个派系了。这三个派系每个都包含三个阶层，玩家刚加入时是最低的阶层，之后做一系列阵营任务，达到一定等级，捐献一定奥能碎片（游戏中的通用货币）之后就可以晋升到更高阶层，晋升可以让玩家拥有更多的阵营魔法武器，狂战士一共可以得到三种，分别是火焰魔拳，寒冰魔拳，毒素魔拳，牧师一共可以得到两种，分别是灵能投射器和灵能强化器，土匪比较惨，一个阵营魔法武器都没有。每一阵营都各自有一套自己专属的独特技能和专属的抗性加成，只有加入了对应的派系才能学习对应的一套专属技能。所以请尽量考虑好之后再加入。给大家一个小建议，由于做支线任务会给不少经验，比刷怪划算得多，而且不少支线完全不需要战斗，所以可先去做各派系支线任务，支线做完之后把各派系的主线任务推进到三大派系都同意你加入并让你自行决定的程度，之后分别存三个档，每个档对应加入一个派系，这样之后就可以不重复地读档游玩各个阵营的独立主线任务了。还要说明的三点，一是还有一个相对比较神秘和隐蔽的阵营叫做“利爪公会”，在大陆的各地都有它的成员，加入他们会有很多好处，游戏中可以留意一下，二是游戏中所有NPC都可以被杀死，但是某些重要NPC被杀死之后就会有红字显示“XXX的死会影响故事的走向”，会对剧情发展产生影响。三是主角对NPC做了什么，他们基本都会记得，所以如果主角欺骗了他们或做了不利于他们的事情，他们可能会秋后算账，报复主角。

[h1]场景设计方面：[/h1]

玛格兰大陆地域辽阔，包含五大区域，在各个区域均可见到的是旧世界的公路，桥梁，房屋等基础设施，智械在各大区域建立的转换站和大量的快速传送点。

阿珀莎（Abessa）：中立区域，主要包含：森林、河流、中立城市（牧师负责管理，各阵营共存）：穹顶城（The Domed City）。
伊丹（Edan）：狂战士的领地，主要包含：森林、河流、狂战士主城：格列特（Goliet）。
伊纳顿（Ignadon）：牧师的领地，主要包含：火山、岩浆河流、牧师主城：圣城（The Hort）。
塔瓦尔（Tavar）：土匪的领地，主要包含：沙漠、温室、土匪主城：要塞城（The Fort）。
萨克尔（Xacor）：智械的领地，主要包含：雪山、冰河、智械主城：冰宫（Ice Palace）。

每个区域的地形地貌都与各自的阵营势力，风土人情是契合的，不会让人有违和感。场景内各个地方几乎在学会熟练使用喷气背包之后都可以到达。部分区域中含有特殊的地带，可能会产生毒素，辐射，寒冰，火烧等效果（一些武器和敌人的攻击也会产生这四种属性伤害持续掉血的效果），进入后人物会持续掉血，掉血速率与自身相关抗性有关，这四维的抗性能力均可以选择自己加点，值得一提的是，在进入这些危险的特殊地带前可以选择配戴“防护面具”，这是一个头部装备，需要玩家自己购买，可以有效抵抗毒素和辐射的伤害。

需要注意，所有快速传送点都必须要实地亲自到达之后才会激活，在“生存”能力下有一个子能力叫“冒险家”，注意该能力只能帮你显示所有传送点的具体位置，但并没有激活，无法传送，地图上传送点图标会显示为灰色（激活后的传送点显示为青色），因为能力点很珍贵，故我个人不建议点这项能力，我更推荐使用如下网址的ELEX的动态世界地图，显示了所有的传送点位置，这可以有效降低跑图时的盲目感，点开各个板块还有该区域的具体情况，支线和物品位置等等，非常实用，建议截图发到手机里存着，平时游玩时可以用于随时参考。
https://game-maps.com/ELEX/ELEX-World-Map.asp

[h1]行动、战斗和装备方面：[/h1]

动作僵硬或许是这游戏为数不多的缺点之一。我全程用手柄玩得，初上手操作时会感到有些别扭，据说玩过这个制作组之前的《崛起》系列和《哥特王朝》系列会比较适应，好吧，我没玩过。我用手柄操作最大的感受是加速冲刺是真的蛋疼，必须要先推摇杆至某一方向再按住LS，而且很容易误操作导致冲不起来，手柄加速冲刺时也会使得冲刺前先慢跑几秒再冲起来，真是蜜汁前摇，不过我也已经习惯了。值得注意的是，手柄和键盘可以设置的快捷键数量分别是8个和10个，上面可以放置各种药剂，武器，一次性法术，三大阵营独有魔法武器等等，但是我仍感觉不够用，因为想要装备的东西太多了哈哈。

扒窃系统的设定类似于辐射和老滚的扒窃系统，不过更丰富有趣一些，在点出“扒窃”能力之后操作贾克斯蹲下进入潜行状态之后从背后接近NPC会显示扒窃按键，点击后会进入NPC物品栏，右上角的几秒钟时间倒计时会提示你还有多长时间可以下手，每次扒窃成功后NPC会提高一级警觉度，共有“毫无戒心”“注意”“警惕”三个等级，分别用绿黄红三种颜色来显示，到“警惕”程度时再下手基本就大概率会被发现了。被发现之后这个区域的所有NPC都会抄家伙来攻击你，这时就别犹豫了，直接读档吧。关于加点，扒窃能力点到1级其实就完全够用，被发现就直接读档就是了。晚上NPC睡觉时最容易下手，需要注意的是正常走进或者跑进NPC睡觉的房间，NPC会直接从床上跳起来赶走你，因此进房间之前就要注意换成潜行状态。话说我曾经在一晚上偷了格列特村镇里面所有人身上的碎片没被发现过（滑稽）。


人物战斗时有耐力值的设定，在左上角以绿色环形显示，冲刺，翻滚，格挡，轻重攻击都要消耗不等的耐力值，耐力值为空时需要等待回复，无法做出更多的动作。使用近战武器时屏幕下方会出现一个连击槽，轻重武器攻击会积累连击槽，打出各种连招combo，但是不同连招自身会产生时间不等的硬直让敌人有机可乘，战斗时还请注意。左手持盾时除了防御之外貌似可以使出盾反直接弹开敌人攻击，我近战玩得比较少，还不是很了解。战斗中怪物会出现各种硬直，有些情况是怪物自身的攻击招数导致的主动回复硬直，有些则是由玩家攻击导致的怪物被动受击硬直，玩家可以善加利用怪物硬直抓紧机会输出，

值得一提的是，ELEX的战斗难度是可以在游戏过程中自由调节的，且战斗被细分得很详尽，包括总体的战斗难度，敌人的战斗行为（即攻击欲望），玩家造成的伤害，敌人造成的伤害，耐力消耗，近程和远程攻击是否自动锁定敌人，连击能量槽的增长速度等等，这些选项的存在相当于制作组在游戏中直接内置了一个游戏战斗修改器，从而满足喜欢休闲战斗看风景和喜欢硬核战斗挑战自我的玩家的各种不同的需要。

武器包括以下几种类型，单手、双手、枪械、重型、魔法、弹药。
单手包含斧、剑、刀、锤、盾等武器，单手时可以选择左手持前四种武器，右手持盾；
双手包含双锤，武士剑，砍伐斧等武器；
枪械包含能量武器、远程武器、弓，其中能量武器又包含激光步枪和电浆步枪，分别使用电浆电池和能量电池作为弹药;远程武器又包含弩和霰弹枪，分别使用弩箭和霰弹枪弹药作为弹药；弓又包含耕作者之弓，猎弓，战弓等等，使用箭矢作为弹药。
重型包含火箭发射器，火焰喷射器和手榴弹等武器，前两者分别使用火箭弹和汽油作为弹药。
魔法包含各种智械族一次性法术（非常好用），如能量猛推，能量波，控制机器人，物品扫描，躯体护盾等等以及三大阵营各自独有的一系列能力。
弹药除了上述提及的普通弹药，每种武器还有许多特殊弹药，有些需要加入对应的阵营才能解锁相应的特殊弹药。

普通武器一般可以升到三级，每升一级要消耗一些碎片和材料，并在工作台进行升级，一些阵营专属的武器只能在加入这一阵营后使用该阵营专属的工作台进行升级。每种普通武器都有与之相对应的特殊强力武器，有着单独的名字，在武器图标右下角会有一个小五角星标识与普通武器区分开。特殊强力武器无法再升级，伤害比普通武器高许多，还有一些特殊的属性攻击加成。我现在找到的特殊强力武器如下，毒蛇之吻（单手剑），卡拉恩的壁垒（单手盾），炽焰（双手武士剑），幻影之弦（弓），救赎者（电浆步枪，也是我最爱的杀敌神器），执政官的力量（激光步枪），雷霆（霰弹枪），熔炉（火焰喷射器）。应该是没有收集全，如果有遗漏，也欢迎大神指出。

一些武器本身有镶孔，可让玩家自由镶嵌各种宝石上去，这就涉及另一套系统---宝石镶嵌系统。首先玩家需学习“宝石镶孔”能力才能合成和镶嵌宝石，游戏中一共有白红绿蓝黄五种宝石，分别对应五种不同的buff，每种宝石一共有三个层次，buff强度从低到高分别为小块X宝石，X宝石，大块X宝石，若干低级宝石可合成高一等的宝石，玩家一般直接获得的是小块X宝石，这些宝石一般是由玩家在各地四处搜刮而来。

如果实在不想战斗，除了一些必须要消灭怪物的支线任务可以不做或者以后厉害了再来做，游戏中的许多任务都是可以不战斗完成的，在野外玩家也可以加速跑路从而躲避大多数的遭遇战，说到战斗这里就要提到两种能力和两件神器了，两种能力分别是“第六感”和“动物之友”，“第六感”这一能力可以在小地图雷达上以红点形式直接显示出附近的敌人，方便玩家及时规避不必要的战斗，而“动物之友”则可以让较弱的野生变异生物不会主动去攻击玩家，可以规避多数的战斗。两件神器其中一件是我最爱的“高科技太阳镜”，我玩到通关时仍然戴着它，一是因为戴上它后自带“第六感”能力，二是因为戴上他后感觉贾克斯明显更酷帅更有型了，非常适合截图（滑稽）。另一件神器是“潜行者护符”，同样带有“第六感”能力并且还带有“迷彩伪装咒语”，这一咒语是狂战士族的法术，会使得不受第六感能力影响的强力生物反应一段时间后才会攻击玩家，便于玩家及时跑路，也非常好用。

因为我主要是走远程流的，远程武器相对近战打得比较安逸，掌握好翻滚时机，练练准度就好，这里我重点推荐的远程武器是电浆步枪，我觉得无论是近战流玩家，远程流玩家还是远近兼修的玩家都应该带一把电浆步枪，因为电浆步枪的特殊射击模式“电浆球”非常好用，电浆球如果打在敌人身上时会产生击退效果，能够直接强行打断敌人释放法术，喷毒液火球等远程攻击的出招前摇造成敌人短暂的硬直，如果打在小型敌人的脚下地面时，电浆球可以直接将敌人震倒在地，形成一个时间较长的倒地硬直（有一些强力敌人，我基本都是用电浆球打地面震倒，他起来之后再打他脚下再震倒的套路慢慢磨死的，滑稽），利用电浆步枪的电浆球射击造成的敌人受击硬直可以打出一些骚操作，比如一个任务要求我在塔瓦尔地区杀一只强力独眼巨人，这个家伙要是近战摸我两下我就直接死了，远程也会喷出高伤害的火球中三下就死（别问我为什么知道这些的），之后我利用当地大型岩柱较多的地形特点以及电浆球的击退效果（独眼巨人太高大，打他脚下地面震不倒他），把他一直打到岩柱下面，将他打得定在那里，他有远程喷火招数，但是永远放不出来，因为它的前摇永远被我的电浆球打断，最后我慢慢把他磨死了（滑稽）。

药剂也有多钟，恢复生命，法力（狂战士），精神能量（牧师），以及各种兴奋剂（土匪），在点出“化学家”能力后玩家就可以在工作台自行调制各种药剂了。一些特殊的永久增加耐力，生命等属性的秘药则需要很珍贵的材料才可以调制出来。

护甲主要是头部，身体，腿部，手部（戒指），颈部（护符）五种。前三种主要增加的是人物的护甲值，主要影响防御力。戒指用途是暂时buff基础属性，如力量，敏捷，最大生命，最大耐力等等。护符用途是暂时buff能力，如第六感，书呆子等等。在点出“金匠”能力后玩家就可以在工作台打造各种戒指与护身符了。

最后说明一点，以上提到的药剂，兴奋剂，戒指，护符等的制作都是要有相应配方的前提下才能做出来的，而有些配方可在商人处花碎片买到，有些则散落到各处需要玩家寻找。

This is a great game.  The story is particularly immersive and the quests are well-integrated to make an interesting plot.  Many people gave it  bad reviews because it is hard in the beginning and they had trouble mastering the combat system.  Personally, I did have trouble at first but liked the game mechanics once I learned them.  Yes, the game is hard in the beginning but it gets easy as you level up.  Easy games get boring quickly.  Elex is challenging because it requires combat tactics, making good use of terrain, and having a strategy for tough fights.  I really liked combining all these elements to win battles.

Did I mention the game is hard in the beginning?  I went through four phases:
1.  Don't leave town or your will get eaten (levels 1-7)
2.  Run to quest, run from big monsters (levels 8-14)
3.  Choose your battles wisely and you can handle most things (levels 15-24)
4.  I am the new deity in town and it is you that better run (levels 25-43)
I did almost every quest and explored almost every square meter of the world to level to 33 before doing the end game, and then got 10 more levels finishing the final chapters.  I did not drink a single xp drink to level either.

I did not run into any bugs with the game, the graphics were beautiful, the dialogs were good, and everything ran smoothly.  The only real problem I had was trying to swap weapons during combat which was slow and often resulted in death, so I quit trying to do that.  All styles of combat and role playing are balanced enough to be viable (as compared to Skyrim which had a magic system so broken you wondered if it was play-tested at all before release :).  The key to having a good experience is to learn to use your favorite style of combat in combination with terrain/positioning and of course develop your skills to do enough damage for the level of creatures you are fighting.  The combat system subtracts armor from weapon damage, so raising your armor and damage dramatically improves combat (a weak weapon does nothing if your opponent has too much armor, but add 10 damage and suddenly you are slicing the mob up).

Pros:
The game is hard/challenging, which forces you to do the content, enjoy the game, follow the story, and feel a sense of achievement as you progress.  You know you want that instead of an easy mode grind-fest.

Cons:
You will be tempted to pound your keyboard and shout expletives at the computer screen when you die so often.  If you give in to these temptations easily, factor the cost of a new keyboard into buying the game.  If you are prone to these kind of outbursts, factor the social costs of finding new roommates or a new family into playing the game.

The reviews of the game are mixed, but from what I read I had the impression that people were basically complaining the game was "too hard" for them.  That made me more interested in playing it because I usually find games too easy.  I was not disappointed with the game at all.  I also think the game is better than other games such as Dragon's Dogma, Fallout 3 and 4, Skyrim, etc.  It is a lot like Fallout New Vegas in terms of story, playability and technical quality, which is I consider to be another great game.

I bought the game at 60% off, and glad I did.  While it appears to be a pretty big world, it's still wrought with bugs, contains clunky combat and the stamina system is broken as it currently stands.  The enemies and beasts are not leveled, so you never know what you're going to run into.  I can't at this time recommend the game, however, this could be like some games that when you get to a certain level, enemies can be managed better in combat.  Right now at a blazing level 4, 2 swings of a sword and he can fight no more until the stamina regens.  So, get it when its on sale, don't pay full price, as there are generic bugs that should never be in the game at this price.

I would love to recommend this game but I just can't

I've played every gothic, arcania, risen game there is and Elex is just bad, really bad

This game could have been great, it had the potential to be, but it looks like during the development nobody has actually played it from beginning until the end

1) My biggest problem with it - It's hard. Not dark-souls-level-hard. This game is frustrating and simply unfair, It's hard because everything is mixed up. There is no low level zone, medium level zone and some kind of end game level zone. You start off and right away there are completely unkillable opponents all around you. Why is this a problem? Because this game will not let you explore. It's an open world game where you just can't see the world until you get really high level and equipment. You will struggle to find anything that you can do at low levels, everything and everyone will kill you for like the first 10 hours of the game. 

2) Graphics - It's a 2017 game but it looks more like ~2013

3) Horrible soundtrack and voice acting. Some sound effect are just comically bad, most of the characters feel like they were recorded by robots (not talking about the Albs which is kind of explained by the game story)

4) Awful combat system. Whoever thought this stamina-based combat is a good idea should think about changing a career field. You can swing your 1-handed sword 3 times and then you need to run around while your stamina regenerates. I'm not even kidding, you can't block, you can't dodge during that because it all requires more stamina

5) Unnecesarily large map because there's nothing interesting in it, just kill 2-3 monsters, loot 2 arrows and a small healing potion and then run away from the large monster you have absolutely no chance against. Repeat this a hundred times

Elex gets a little better after around 15 hours of playing but those first 15 hours you need to suffer are not worth it
Totally worth buying and playing. Git Good.

不推荐
fantastic story-telling!!!  RPG lover do not miss it.

Great story and world building let down horrible controls, combat balance issues and technical glitches.

Technical - Game crashes to desktop regularly if you run in exclusive fullscreen mode.  If you use windowed mode VSYNC and frame limiting don't work so your GPU goes into overdrive to render useless frames.

Controls - controls are generally unresponsive in a game with ARPG like combat.  The decision to have double tap direction key as dodge is especially painful in combat as you will dodge roll when you don't mean to and then not be able to dodge fast enough when you do.

Combat - I will admit that learning the combat system in this game will increase your playability immensely but not even Dark Souls is this painful to start with.  Beginning monsters will be able to kill you if you make a single mistake in combat and it is not possible to take on more than one creature at once without dying.  Your companion ends up doing most of the work in fights.  Speaking of which your companion's fight AI is horrible.  They have a ranged weapon (which is usually better than their melee) but won't use it unless you start attacking with a ranged weapon or they can't physically get to an enemy.   At least the companion pathfinding AI when travelling is decent.  They will actually follow you in lifts or using a jetpack unlike Fallout 4.

The game world and story is at least interesting with many quests making you choose between supporting different factions and sub-factions.  I have just gotten to the point where the pain of combat is no longer worth putting up with to continue the story.
Good

Just finished the Elex.  I rarely finish a game.  I either get bored or move on to something else.  But this game kept me going.  I enjoyed the gameplay, loot, and story.  Looking for a fun game that you are likely to see all the way to the end pick up Elex it will be enjoyed.

I would not recommend this to anyone who does not like Gothic/Risen games.
I probably would not recommend this to anyone who has not played Gothic/Risen but loves Skyrim or Fallout 3-4 and compares everything to those.
But I would recommend this to anyone who did like Gothic/Risen games, already replayed them 3 times, and now really wants something new but similar. This will satisfy the cravings adequately i guess.

ELEX is basically a Risen game that wants to be more like Fallout. I think compared to Gothic this doesn't quite have the same "soul", but i think that soul's been dying slowly througout the Risen series so it's not that much of a shock i guess. A certain warm and fuzzy charm is missing.
But despite that it still offers a large world that will take a long time to explore, several large settlements, lots of quests, various weapons and a bit of magic. Plus you get a jetpack, can't go wrong with that.
The difficulty is a bit off, a lot of enemies near beginning areas take too long to kill and do a lot of damage, and beginner quests sometimes take you straight to them. That was annoying.
The story/dialogs are a bit lame at times and don't make sense.

If Gothic is a 9 and Risen is an 8, I think i'd give this a 6.5/10. Why am i recommending it then? Well, if i could give a neutral rating - i would, but i can't. And if i give it a negative review - it will move the game that much closer to "mostly negative reviews" and that's simply not fair. I've played games much worse than this one with much better average reviews.

The negative reviews are somewhat justified. I spent about 30 hours of game play running away from everything and setting up my companion to do all the fighting. Then suddenly I had the skill points to actually get some useful armor and a decent ranged weapon. A bow and arrow is only good for attracting the target. A flame thrower has some useful damage power although it still takes a while to bring down a monster.

Joinging one of the factions early will definitely fasttrack your ability to fight and win loot, etc. However, I've been much more successful with range weapons and taking a companion who melees and fires range weapons. Upgrade to 'better' companions as they becme available.

All of the 'good' stuff requires not only one but two high levels of skill (eg. 55 strength, 40 constitution) before you can wear or use it. Get better companions as you go and they'll help you level up. Their kill is your kill but you almost always have to start the fight first. Melee combat is very difficult until you get to the higher levels.

Story line is not bad, interesting missions and tasks, good (but not stellar) graphics ... it's worth paying a discounted price $25 to $30. Thought and effort has gone into the design of this game but it don't think near enough time went into game balance. This is a problem with many games. Everyone wants to be creative (programmer, artists, etc) and no one wants to actually make the game challenging but enjoyable by doing the necessary play testing and balancing.

Many comments appear to be from players who like the 'tank' roll. Unfortunately, that strategy will be difficult (as they've learned) to pull off. It may be better to choose a faction early so you can upgrade more quickly. I found a 'soldier's amulet' and some kind of ring that together increased my strength, combat and something else, which pushed my character over the hump so that I could start using something more than a rusty axe and bow/arrow. The game is quite fun now. The game is worth the effort if you give it some decent play time. It's never crashed once, which is a big point for me. Graphic are not bad. Story line is good, voice acting is decent. Elex may not be worth full price but anytime it's on sale you should definitely get it.

I played Gothic 1-3 and Riven 1, the last of which was horrible (the platformer gameplay at the end ruined it for me). Elex is a better game, which presents you with an open world which you can explore, no matter if you follow quests or not. 

The point, at which many fail, is combat. You need only read some of the reviews to get the picture. Melee requires timing and a certain knowledge of your opponents moves, which you get only by experience. Ranged combat demands a certain amount of aiming, and is tricky when the opponents a) move, and b) shoot back. But it is certainly close combat where many have serious trouble. And of course, all of them expected to beat the game easily at it's hardest mode ;)
Anyway, since you are required to fight to get through the game, combat is what will make or break the game for you. If you can master it, you will have a blast, if not, you will be seriously disappointed. Especially later, when you get to see mass combat.

The story is nothing very original, but at least you don't have to stop a godlike being from destroying the world. Aside from the main quest are many minor ones, some of which are pretty good, and some are very difficult. All factions have a quest series to join them, and you can do all of them up to a certain point to check them out (and get the xp and loot). 
The factions play somewhat differently, once you have joined them, since you get access to different weapons and abilities. Still, there are lying some faction weapons around the world - some of which are very good - so members of another faction can have a go with them. You will certainly have the easiest time, if you join the Clerics, as their psionics and weapons are very powerful, and they get a special dialogue option with some NPCs. The Berserkers come in second in my opinion, and the Outlaws third. It doesn't help the Outlaws that I find most of them not sympatico, not even the companion from there. Once you have joined a faction, that decision is irreversible and locks you out of joining the other two.

You can find several companions, and one quest even sends you out to find some of them. They range from a berserker over a hover drone to a flamethrower-toting cleric of varying personality and usefulness. They are most useful during the first 20 levels and become more and more useless afterwards - they are kinda like training wheels until you can dot hings by yourself. The berserker at the start is a big help against the puny lizards, which will kill you, and become mere nuisances later.

The factions live in differently themed terrains, so the game presents you with several sets of landscape. There are the european hills and forests of the berserkers, the volcanic wasteland of the clerics, the Mad Max desert of the outlaws, and the icy mountains of the albs.

Crafting is in the game, and you can make several drugs and potions, which provide a one-time benefit (like healing potions), and there are a few that provide you with permanent bonuses to your stats and skills. You can improve the weapons of your own faction, too, but this is not of equal benefit to all factions. You can find first-class guns lying around, which are as good a tier 3 crafter laser rifle, but I found no melee weapons equal to a tier 3. And without looking up some internet guides you will miss a lot of stuff, since the world is big, and the loot is small. I came across a great gun at the top of a ruined tower, which you can reach only by jetpack. And I missed a lot of stuff in similarly locations. There are dark cellars under ancient buildings, and it is easy to overlook things in the reddish gloom of magnesium torches. And there are terrain hazards (e.g. poisonous clouds), which make exploring some areas so tricky, that most people won't bother.
And you are not required to go everywhere - you can easily skip 50% of the game world and still complete the game, so hunting for minor secrets is a thing, if you are into that.

The opposition can be classified into: 
- human NPCs, armed with the same stuff as you are
- reptilian beasts reminding of raptors in various sizes and shapes
- mutants, who have inbuilt weaponry
- robots in various sizes and firepower
You start out with whacking a small dino, go over "kill the 4 raptors over there" to "there is this horde of mutants in said building" and ending at a platoon of laser-toting albs supported by combat robots. The enemies do not directly scale with you, but at the start of each chapter is the world repopulated once, and with more difficult foes. Where you found cheap muties in chapter 1 might be some very tough ones in chapter 3. But they are not the same type leveled up, just different ones who are stronger - and you can find some of the strong enemies even in chapter 1, although not so many. So it is easier to play through the world in chapter 1 to level 25 and only then continue the main quest into chapter 2. If you are going for a speedrun (for what? I have to ask - after all you want to play the game, not rush it), you can get an underleveled character, and if you suck at combat, chapter 2 will break you.

I was running it under Win 10 with a Radeon 480 at the time and cannot complain. The game runs well and I didn't suffer a single crash. I came across a few bugs, but no game-breakers. They were on the scale of a named gun not properly reloading (had to holster it), some dialogue lines not making sense at the time, and falling through the arms of a metal mast I was trying to climb to the top.

I recommend the game to people with a little patience, who enjoyed Gothic  and the later Fallout games. 

You must be prepared that combat is not easy (Fallout is a breeze compared to it) as many have found out. It is never a bad idea to check out some videos about the actual gameplay, btw. At least some are informative, even if the majority is useless, unless you like someone chattering away instead of playing.

Let's start with the superficial, the begging comparison.  Yes, the theme of the world feels very much like Skyrim and Fallout 4 had a baby.  BUT, the basic theme is where any comparison ends.  Those games are so vastly different as to make any further comparison illogical.  However, since there is bound to be fan base crossover, I will be mentioning them later.

The main complaints most people have with Elex revolve around combat.  You will probably need to tweak difficulty to meet your needs,  There are several videos on YT specifically dedicated to this. With that said, you will NOT be able to march across the land with utmost confidence that you can win almost any encounter. NO matter how you tweak combat, there are enemies that will be more powerful than you.  Especially in the beginning, almost everything is more powerful than you. In this respect, Elex is far closer to old school RPG game design.  Your character will have to avoid certain areas until he is strong enough to survive. Unlike Skyrim and Fallout, areas are not dynamically leveled to the player.  If this is one of you major complaints about those games, by all means, venture into the world of Elex.  Also, as far as I know, there is no console/god mode toggle.  If you're a player who uses tgm and tcl a lot in Bethesda games, you will never survive Elex until you bend to the will of the world instead of vice versa. 

The second major complaint I see a lot of is with respect to dialogue.  There is, actually, not a whole lot to complain about.  The dialogue is fairly well written and acted overall.  I have yet to encounter any really flat lines, nor any overacted lines.  The dialogue trees and progressions are logical and allow for player choice.  There seems to be a (at least rudimentary) player reputation system.  And, NPC lines do changed substantially as you progress.  The only real quibble I have is that the NPCs don't interact with one another unless it's scripted, and there's very little to no idle chatter around cities as a result.

My major complaint is that there is no first person play.  This seriously detracts from immersion and visceral combat.  I feel like I'm a puppetmaster in combat, guiding my toon to victory. I do not feel like I'm battling the creature.  For some this may be an easy to overlook and subtle distinction.  To me, it isn't.  I don't like it when people look over my shoulder.  I like it even less when I'm forced to do it to myself.

From a PnP perspective, there is a full, attribute-based character development.  This is further complemented with learned skills dependent on the character's other stats.  This should please a lot of old schoolers and number crunchers. Complaints that the character's development are "all the same" or "cookie cutter" are patently ridiculous.  

However, superficially at least, those complaints do have some merit.  There is absolutely no superficial character customization.  You are Jax.  You are male.  You are an Alb (at least at the start).  You can not change this, and every player, in every play through, will start as the same exact Jax.

Elex is a redemption, of sorts, for the developer.  Albeit with far, far futuristic content, Elex is the spiritual successor to the Gothic series.  Gothic 1 & 2 were severely hampered by control issues, but kept pace with the best RPGs of their time.  Gothic 3, for me, was a masterpiece, on the scale of Skyrim, that never got the credit it deserved.  Mostly this was due to it being buggy to the very real point of being unplayable for most players even years after release.  The community patches really did stablize it, though, and made it playable through to the end.  Arcania, the fourth installment in the series was a linear abomination that was still better than Dragon Age 2. Arcania was very poorly received by Gothic fans, hence Elex is the redeemer.

The world is sparse of feature, that can not be denied.  There are no real "little stories" to find in settings sprinkled throughout the world as there are in Skyrim and Fallout.  However, where there are more detailed features, they are very well done, make sense in the surrounding, and support the story.  Vertical exploration is also strongly encouraged, although, unlike Fallout, vertical combat is under utilized in the environment.

One last thing about gameplay.  Experience.  There is not much to be learned when running around killing things willy-nilly.  This is heavily relied upon in the game.  If you do not do things, complete tasks, go on quests, if you just want to explore the world and swing your sword or fire your gun, you will not get very far in Elex. and it will not be enjoyable.

In short, Elex is a very good RPG in its own right.  As long as you go into it with the knowledge of what it is, and play it as the devs intended instead of trying to force your playstyle on the game, as long as you are willing to adapt to the game and not have it adapt to you, it's definitely worth picking up.

In closing, I am actually in awe at the dev team.  Pirahna Bytes has less than 30 employees and has not stopped churning out worthy RPG after worthy RPG at least every three years since Gothic 1.  These accomplishments are nothing short of remarkable.

В целом из сюжета игры понравился только первый акт, второй и третий акт мягко говоря натянуты... четвертый. ну там развязка, понятно. Зачем тянуть кота за одно место. Elex é um jogo de rpg old-school raiz. Repete as mesmas mecanicas da série Risen, que fazia uma mistureba de piratas, magos, voodo e armas de fogo. Aqui misturam um mundo pós apocaliptico estilo fallout, guerreiros de espada, magos, psionicos e mutantes.

Apesar de ser um jogo meio meia boca, double A (não tem as limitações de um indie, mas tb não tem o polimento de um AAA), ele tem um charme que é dificil de descrever. Acho que duas coisas me atraem nele: 1. é um jogo com muita seriedade pelas suas mecanicas, não fazendo concessões; 2. qualquer habilidade nova que vc adquira, faz uma grande diferença para o personagem.

Dizendo isso, posso afirmar que não é um game para todos, com vcs podem perceber pelas justas análises negativas. Talvez agrade mais jogadores mais maduros e que curtam uma experiencia mais lenta. Compre quando estiver em promoção.

Elex is a game I didn't enjoy, a game I didn't have any desire to finish. It feels like there's a lot of game here to be played, but that its also screaming at me to not play it.

First off, the world of the game is a mess. The world reminds me very much of the 2008 post-apocalyptic film Doomsday, in that it has no idea what flavor of post-apocalypse it wants to be, so it just throws them all in a blender, pours the resulting disjointed mess on a plate in front of you, and hopes you'll just pick around the parts you don't like. Even the game  wourld feels disjointed and cobbled together like the devs smashed together the maps from 3 or 4 different games and said "Here you go." I'm sure there's an in-universe explanation for this, but in my 20+ hours playing this game I either never came across it or it got lost in the tsunami of exposition the game slams you with at the begining.

The story: Its forgettable, by which I mean, I played this game 2 months ago and have already forgotten it. Something about you being kicked out of a cult of tech wizards, and because they kicked you out you have to get vengence? Whatever it was it didn't hold my interest very long. I also remember being very confused at multiple points as to who certain people were and where I could go to advance the story, without siding with the luddite faction whom I very quickly grew tired of.

The gameplay can be divided into melee and ranged combat, I think there's also magic, but I never used it, both the melee and the shooting suck for different reasons.

Melee combat: Slow, clunky and frustrating, I tried it with both a controller and mouse and keyboard. It didn't work well with either, it reminds me of the witcher's combat, but much slower and worse. Get a ranged weapon ASAP.

Shooting: After many hours of frustrating melee combat, and running away from any enemy who looked tougher than a small rodent, I made far enough to aquire some sort of energy rifle from a travelling merchant. This made the game much more playable, leading to me tossing my melee weapons and never returning to them, and should really be the default with melee weapons being an option for those who side with the luddite faction. Even so, the shooting is limp and unsatisfying, your bullets or enegry pellets or whatever do about as much damage as the melee weapons, which do about as much damage as slapping the enemy with a wet noodle, really their only saving grace is they let you keep your distance.

So here I sit in the game, not immersed in the world, not enjoying the combat, and not really knowing what's going on or what I'm supposed to be doing, partway through a quest, wondering why I am playing this game. In most games you're playing because you enjoy the gameplay or the story, but in Elex, I was enjoying neither. So, I exited out of the game and went off to play something else. I pondered returning to it many times, each time deciding that I didn't want to, culminating in me uninstalling the game and writing this reveiw. Don't waste your time with this one.

So - nach 74 Stunden Spielzeit ist ELEX für mich nun zuende gegangen und es hat mich viele Nächte verkürzten Schlaf gekostet. Also kurz gesagt: Für mich gehört es klar unter die TOP-3 der besten Piranha Bytes-Spiele!

Für mich eine ABSOLUTE SPIEL-EMPFEHLUNG! :-)

Hier kurz aufgedröselt, was mich begeistert hat, und wo noch potenzial für das nächste Spiel ist:


- Das Spiel hat einen sehr guten Schwierigkeitsgrad. Das ist wohl eines der wichtigsten Dinge, die  aus den ersten Gothic-Teilen wiederbelebt wurde. Ich habe auf "Normal" gespielt - das kam mir etwa wie Gothic 1 vor (mal abgesehen von den Unterschieden in der Steuerng). Risen 2 und Risen 3 waren mir in der Hinsicht zu glattgeschliffen.

- Die detaillierte und abwechslungsreiche Landschaft ist wie immer großartig! - Da muss man glaub ich nichts weiter darüber sagen ;-)

- Die Queststruktur ist wirklich interessant gestaltet. Mir gefällt der Schwerpunkt bei "Entscheidungen und Konsequenzen" wirklich gut!! Interessant wäre es, wenn man die Hauptkonsequenzen aus ELEX später dann in einen potenziellen Nachfolger übernehmen könnte! Ein kleiner Kritikpunkt: Im späteren Spielverlauf werden die Fraktionen im Spielgeschehen ein bisschen zu belanglos - auch im fortgeschrittenen Passus könnte es ruhig ein paar mehr Nebenquests geben, die die einzelnen Fraktionen mehr in die Storyentwicklung einbinden. Ohne zu spoilern (Spieler von Elex werden wissen, was ich meine): Es gibt eine Hauptquest rund um die Stadt Abessa. Wenn die für die Stadt "nicht so gut ausgeht",  interessiert das die Menschen in den anderen Lagern überhaupt nicht. Das war wirklich ein bisschen schade.

- Das "Universum" von Elex  ist so was von genial! Allein die ganzen interessanten Hintergründe über die alte Welt, über die Fähigkeiten des Elex, über die Konflikte zwischen den Menschen seit dem Einschlag des Meteors - das alles ist logsich aufgebaut, sehr verstrick und vor allem voller Erkenntnisse, auf die man selbst gar nicht gekommen wäre. Da waren die letzten Spiele schon ein Stück weit "abgekarteter".

- Das Kampfsystem ist für mich soweit in Ordnung. Mit dem Element "JetPack" sind die Kämpfe auf jeden Fall abwechslungsreicher und auch etwas strategischer..

Ob die Grafik nun veraltet ist oder nicht, spielt für mich nicht so die Rolle. Das ist für mich nur die Oberfläche. Was bringt mir ein Spiel mit perfekter Grafik, wenn es keinen Spaß macht? Das Spiel polarisiert sicher und das ist auch gut so. Und auch die Personen, die sehr negative Reviews geschrieben haben, haben in dem Spiel trotzdem meistens 40+ Stunden verbracht. Dann kann es ja doch nicht so schrecklich gewesen sein ;-)

I was on the edge about purchasing this game because of the mixed reviews. I liked the Risen series though so I figured that I would try this one out also since I enjoy post apocalyptic settings. So far I am enjoying this game very much. I'm just a few hours into it and still exploring around Goliet.

The quests to me are enjoyable and I've noticed that some of them have alternate ways of being completed even though the quest log doesn't say so. I'm hoping there will be more quests like this because it makes it feel more like a living world. 

Others have said that some of the quest objectives are near tough enemies. I had one where there was some kind of big winged creature near a plant I needed to retrieve. I knew it would be impossible to kill it so while it's back was to me, I grabbed the plant and ran away. I like the idea of not being able to win every fight but being able to accomplish a task in another way.

The combat is kind of clunky but it doesn't bother me too much because I got used to it in the Risen series. I have had a bit of trouble because I would forget about the stamina bar, dodge too much and then have no stamina to do anything else. Overall I don't think the combat is too bad personally.

There are a lot of generic npcs but all rpgs that I have played usually have generic npcs anyway so this doen't bother me too much. I prefer there to be a lot of wandering characters even if they do nothing because it feels more like a populated world instead of a whole town made up of a few npcs that aren't generic.

One thing that is a little hard for me to get used to so far though is when entering buildings during the day, the screen is very dark for a little while to simiulate your eyes adjusting. I think I'm starting to get used to it and I understand that ruins could be dangerous so you don't want to rush in blindly. I just wish it wasn't so much in town since I'm constantly going in and out of the houses that shouldn't have hostile creatures since it is in town.

Another thing that gets a little annoying is when I open my inventory or map around people in Goliet, they always make a comment about how technology is bad and I could get in trouble. I find myself trying to get away from everyone before opening my inventory but sometimes I forget and have to listen to them.

Overall I am really enjoying this game and very happy that I purchased it. It feels like a real immersive world so far and I've only just started. I really hope that the rest of the areas later on will be the same way as the beginning.

All I wanted was another Gothic adventure, obviously in another world. I only wanted to wash away the terrible taste Arcania had left in my mouth. Boy, I got burnt again. I just don't have the energy to describe any further. Let's just roll with a classical pros and cons list.

Pros:
+ Instant feeling of familiarity. Even though you are in an entirely different world, you'll feel at home among the Berserkers (Nords) of Goliet.

+ Factions with their own believable backgrounds.

(Even I wasn't expecting the list to be this short. I literally squeezed out all my symphathy for these 2 points).

Cons:
- Uninspired world. Although at the beginning you'll like the world, it quickly becomes an eyesore, a tiring dull landscape that isn't very exciting to be in. It's not because this is a post-apocalyptic world devoid of life. That surely isn't the problem. It might be the sheer lack of traces of the past civilization, the too rare sightings of buildings and roads. You'll decide for yourself if you go ahead and play. Rather than a once-live planet having been destroyed, it feels like humans were later sprinkled on to an alient planet that never actually had life on it before. The whole environment feels vacant and lifeless. Not post-apoc lifeless, just lifeless as it has possibly ever been.

- Extremely terrible enemy design and placement. The moment you start playing, you get matched against numerous monsters/thugs/factionados that you stand zero chance against. Everything one- or two-shots you. Almost all monsters have this attack animation where they lunge toward you like a harpoon. Somehow every single enemy has to have a projectile too. You can always run or jetpack your way out of trouble, but then the broken stupid mobs are everywhere. You can never get a break from running.

- A lot of artificial difficulty. Your progression is painful and initially mostly limited to finding yourself quests to do where you won't have to fight. But good luck facing some hellspawn demon while you are on your way to pick up some healing herbs, which was requested by one of the NPCs in your first town. And you thought that was going to be easy.

- Very very bad item design. There are tons of different weapon options. A whole lot of them require you to advance a good bit through the levels. You think you'll be ok with the axe and bow you get your hands on during your early strides toward that damnable town. Wrong! As the previous cons suggest, the damage you deal is quite pathetic. Your axe obviously can't even give a reaver wearing a shirt a tiny scratch. And don't even get me started on the trivial and unnecessary stamina system. After a while, you happen to get your hands on some ranged weapons. Just wait until you discover how your fireball-hurling weapon is also close to useless against enemies, taking like 5-6 painfully slow-loading shots at even the lowest-tier mutant rat/dog thingy. The frustration is real.

- I can see how everything will later snowball into a ridiculous experience, where, after tons of blood sweat and tears, you'll be the one to one-shot everything in your comfy indestructible armor. But where the hell is the fun in that when the big majority of your starting hours will all be about desperately avoiding combat and trying to have your follower deal with whatever encounter you just cannot skip. This is not primarily supposed to be an FPS, is it? It fails miserably both as an FPS and RPG anyway. Then again, an FPS would give you actual choices and incremental upgrades regardless of what weapon you choose to wield. 

In my latest Gothic experience (that would be the highly-shunned, yet actually very enjoyable Gothic 3), you started off your journey as a poor pleb. Yet you could grab a bow for safe encounters and still have a fun time hunting beasts and doing quests. Getting an upgrade on your bow only meant fewer arrows to be shot, unlike this pile of garbage where even a high-tech weapon is an utter joke even against the lowest of mobs. Difficulty was never ever artificial. Everything was dangerous, but still manageable. And interestingly enough, even your final fully developed mage/paladin self had to be careful not to get cornered in a tight spot and mangled into pieces by a shadow beast. 


I might later add more to the list. This is all I have in mind at the moment. I am exhausted and disappointed. I know this isn't Gothic, but it came with the anticipation that it would contain a fragment of the essence of it. It just isn't there though. Much of what made the former awesome is gone here. I only wish I hadn't waited for such a long time to finally install and play it. No refunds for me now!

Elex hat ein sehr spannendes Szenario, welches für Gothic oder Risen-Fans eine gewisse Frische neben den altbekannten herbringt. Der Einstieg in dem Spiel war schwer für mich, da Gameplay und das "Retro Gamedesign", es einen anfangs nicht leicht machen. Unter "Retro Gamedesign" definiere ich u. A. Quests die keinerlei Infos geben wie hart z. B. ein Gegner ist, da keine LVL-Anzeigen oder "Härtestufen" an den Gegnern zu sehen sind. Also muss man erstmal in den Kampf gehen und sich selber an verschiedenen Gegnern austesten, Außerdem muss man selber den Überblick anfangs bewahren. Welche Quests bringen mich weiter, was skille ich am besten, damit ich eine Chance gegen die "machbaren" Gegner habe.

Sobald man aber die anfänglichen Schwierigkeiten überwunden hat und langsam härtere Gegner bearbeiten kann (Charakter ca. Lvl 20) fängt das Spiel an Spass zu machen. Vor allem aufgrund der Story. Man will unbedingt weiter im Rank einer Fraktion steigen (z. B. für eine neue Rüstung) und in der Hauptstory vorankommen. 

Ich war gefangen im Bann des Spieles, wie Früher zu alten Gothic 1-2 Zeiten, es war ein tolles Erlebnis. Ich sehe Elex als eine Herausforderung, die ein Gefühl vermittelt, wie man vom Schwächling zum starken Helden heranreift, in dem man selber sein Köpfchen etwas anstrengen muss ohne 1000 Hilfen/ Tutorials/ Leitfäden wie in vielen AAA-Spielen.

Fazit:

+ epische Story, alle Dialoge sind synchronisiert (mit altbekannten dt. Gothic Synchronsprechern)
+ Grafik ist gut (für mein Empfinden ausreichend)
+/- Benutzeroberfläche etwas zu schlicht gehalten (z. B. Filteroptionen im Itemmenü wäre schön gewesen)

- Kampfsystem ist veraltet und manchmal frustrierend
- nichts für Casual Player, die keine Geduld haben (kein leichter Einstieg,), (notfalls hilft z.b. für einfachere Kämpfe einfach die Ausdauer zu deaktivieren)

So I'm writing my review on two considerations, read whitch serves you best:

[( I'VE PLAYED AND AM FAMILIAR TO GOTHIC AND/OR RISEN SERIES )]
If you like these games, welcome to Elex! It's pretty much the same, with a few perks:
- Great story, great characters, a lot of things to do!
- Lot of choices that matters
- Same gameplay as ever, working a little better than the other games but inevitably feels old comparing to the newest RPG games.
- JETPACK! Never again falling to death for nothing or having long walks around things or climbing cliffs feeling that you're cheating the level design xD

[( I'VE NEVER PLAYED GOTHIC OR RISEN )]
Be aware that this game is founded on quite old mechanics. If you like heavy action or elaborated combat RPG, like Dark Souls or The Witcher (my favorite), you'll probably want to steer clear from this game. It will feel clumky and broken.
However, if you like exploration, talking to NPCs, choices that matter, this game is really good and deserves a chance, considering the following:
- Don't be affraid to run from battles at the beginning... and it's a very long beginning at that. Find a companion as quick as possible and let him do all the dirty work.
- Loot everything. EVERYTHING! There's no weight or inventory limits...You'll need the money for... well.. everything, even upgrading your weapons or upgrading skills
- Take your time to know the settlements and camps. Things are hard to find at the minimap and world map, and can be very annoying, but its part of the mechanics to get to know things.
- Get to know and understand your character and factions. If you don't immerse on it, than the game doesn't offer very much really.

Das Spiel und die Story sind ja interessant. Ich spiele das Spiel jetzt ein paar Stunden. Aber dieses Kampfsystem ist so hölzern und schlecht, dass es einfach eines RPG unwürdig ist. 
Die Story und die Welt sind aber fesselnd genug um darüber hinwegzusehen. Nach einer gewissen Zeit hat man sich so langsam reingefummelt.
Ist mein erstes Piranha Bytes Spiel

Die verschiedenen Elemente wirken zum Teil wie schlechte Resteverwertung vorangegangener gescheiterter Projekte. Den "Entwicklern" gehört eigentlich das Handwerk gelegt. Leider gibt es keinen Schadenersatz!

ELEX hat bei mir seit langem wieder das "Gothic-Gefühl" aufkommen lassen. 
Seit Gothic 3 war ich auf der Suche nach einem würdigen Nachfolger und ich für meinen Teil habe ihn in ELEX gefunden.

Dabei hat ELEX viele, viele Schwächen. Es beginnt mit der hanebüchenen Einführung: Ex-Supersoldat wird zum kraftlosen Nichtskönner. Die alles-unterdrückende Rasse der Albs schafft es nicht mal jemanden zu erschießen, der zwei Meter vor ihnen steht. Da fragt man sich doch: Wie konnten die Jungs bis jetzt überleben?

Das Inventar ist eine Sünde. Ich brauche nicht jedes Item als dreh- und zoombares 3D-Objekt aber ich hätte gerne eine Sortierfunktion und ich würde gerne Items von einander unterscheiden können, ohne jedes Mal den Text lesen zu müssen.

Allgemein wird in ELEX viel zu wenig erklärt. Was der eine als erfrischend empfinden wird, ist für mich persönlich einfach nur anstrengend. Wenn ich alle zwei Schritte auf eine grobe Karte schauen muss und mich Monster fressen, weil ich mich verlaufen habe, dann frustet mich das nur. Die Albs haben Gleiter und Konverter und schaffen es nicht, so etwas wie GPS oder ähnliches in die Zukunft zu retten?  

Meine Figur ist ein Arsch. Gut, so ist er angelegt aber selbst wenn man ihn "freundlich" spielt und seine Emotionen erweckt ist er niemand, mit dem ich mich identifizieren kann. Vielleicht bin ich im Spiel noch nicht weit genug aber wenn er seinen Begleitern ein unfreundliches "Mitkommen" entgegen schnauzt, würde ich ihn an deren Stelle schon stehen lassen. 
Dass ich ihn nicht anpassen kann, bin ich von Gothic gewohnt (es stört mich dennoch) aber wenn es um Emotionen oder Emotionslos geht, dann möchte ich das meiner Figur auch anmerken. Da wäre eine deutliche Veränderung in den Dialogen wünschenswert gewesen. Das Klischee vom harten, ungehobelten und rauhbeinigen Arsch passt nicht wirklich zu jemandem, der seine Menschlichkeit erkundet. (Oder zu einem der sich in den Dienst einer Gottheit stellt) 

Die Fraktionen sind mir zu oberflächlich. Keine versucht mich wirklich, für ihre Sache zu gewinnen. Selbst die Kleriker tun nicht wirklich viel dafür, ihren Glauben zu verbreiten. Ich soll mich euch anschliessen? Okay! Ich hab' zwar keine Ahnung, was ihr wirklich glaubt und ihr wollt mich auch nicht wirklich konvertieren aber ihr habt coole Waffen.  

Die einzige Fraktion, die ich auf Anhieb sympathisch fand, ist ausgerechnet die eine, der man nicht beitreten kann. (So weit ich es zumindest weiß)

Und so geht es weiter. Die Kämpfe, die wenigen Erklärungen, die Kollisionsabfrage, das Verhalten der Begleiter, der undurchsichtige und oft unglaubwürdige Kosmos, in den die Spielwelt eingebettet ist... Und trotz alledem ist ELEX kein schlechtes Spiel. Es macht Spaß, die Welt zu erkunden, die Fraktionen kennenzulernen und -ganz Gothic-typisch- in eine Welt geworfen zu werden, in der man sich fragt: Wie seid ihr nur ohne mich ausgekommen?

Die Sprecher sind wie gewohnt zwischen professionell und "atmosphärisch" angesiedelt und es sind nicht wenige Sprecher dabei, die es schaffen, einige der Schwächen der Spielwelt wieder aufzufangen.  

Auch wenn ich nach nun ca. 35 Stunden viele Frustmomente zu verbuchen habe und auch wenn man oft Rätselraten muss, was nun genau was bewirkt und auch wenn die Fraktionen alle irgendwie nicht genügend ausgearbeitet scheinen, habe ich doch viel Spaß mit ELEX. Jeder, der Gothic mag, sollte ELEX eine Chance geben.
   
Ich hoffe sehr, dass Piranha Bytes mit einem Nachfolger aufwartet und dass der die vielen Schwächen von ELEX ausmerzt. Dann hätte es das Potential zu einem richtigen Kracher.

Saw a good bit of negativety so I waited for a sale, and after ~13hrs at this point, i have to say I'm enjoying the game.

My first Piranha Bytes game but their 'flavor'/'style' of game I'm enjoying. It starts off almost unreasonably difficult for combat, but this leads to changing how you play depending on how strong you are, in the beginning you kind of sneak around, exploring, trying to avoid combat to finish quests, then later you get a companion and start getting stronger and change your playstyle to be more confrontational. 

No inventory limit that I've hit and not a super annoying gigantic loot list all over the place so way easier to acquire things without constantly finding your home chest or something.

Have to pay attention in combat but it's not super complex or a mindless hack 'n slash either. It's a relaxed combat system, and considering how hard some of the mobs are to kill with your current gear/weapons it keeps combat fairly fresh as you're not just grinding enemies constantly. 

World is built well, it feels fun and interesting. I saw some complaints about the environment changing so rapidly but if you actually pay attention to the story even slightly it makes a lot of sense and was essnetially done this way on purpose. Think competing environment crafting by the factions. 

Overall I'm enjoying this experience more than Fallout 4 actually, surprises me to realize that but it's true.

Keeping in mind that I'm level 4 currently, the following two additions would greatly enhance gameplay

1.  Quests with level indicators
     I've wasted time on several quests only to find that I am too undergeared and / or leveled which ends in a fast death.  There is a skull next to mobs' health bars that serve as a warning, so at least there's that.  I've also circumvented close deaths by running in, grabbing a quest item, and running / flying out of the area.  The good old fashioned EverQuest (EQ) style of training a mob to a tougher NPC also bore fruit.  :D
2.  Stealth indicator
     It's a game of chance from what I can tell as there's no visual aid to show whether you're seen or not.  In other games that hasn't been an issue because there's line of sight, but these guys seem to be able to see through walls as there's no line of sight, yet I'm being yelled at or taunted for failing to be sneaky

Setting those aside, the game is fun.  It's as though Skyrim, Fallout, and Assassin's Creed (what little I was able to play without getting motion sickness), came together into one game.  Camera speed was having an Assassin's Creed affect on me, but I found a setting to slow it down and I'm no longer getting woozy.

Fighting is clunky, very much like starting an Elder Scrolls character. (Morrowind comes to mind - the original, not the MMORPG).  Most things chew through me quickly and my gear is definitely in need of upgrading.  That's going to take time, though, as 10 attribute points are awarded at each level, but skills take a staggering number of points across several attributes to train.  At level 4 I've only been able to train 2 skills, lockpick and hack.  Gear also requires stacked points in attributes, and without knowing what gear is going to require because it hasn't been acquired, yet, pre-planning point distribution is a guessing game.  Recipes fall into the same trouble.  Sure, you could read guides and whatnot, but I prefer to jump right in and play rather than scouring the internet for hours looking for opinions and suggestions.

Advice:  Find and talk to the trainers before spending attribute points.  It's too late for me now, but that would have been good advice when I started.

I'm enjoying it, though.  It's remniscent of playing EQ when there were 72 person raids and NPCs didn't have breadcrumbs leading to them.  The map shows useful information, but NPCs themselves don't have a big "click me" sign on them.  I can see kids who started with games like WoW dislliking this game for the lack of spoonfeeding and the need to "hug the wall" to bypass mobs that will one-shot your character.  

Oh!  Lockpicking is fun!  There's potential for a thought process being required to getting goodies from locked containers.  It's a little like Oblivion, but there's another game that's much closer and it's bugging me that I can't think of the name!

It would have been nice to be able to choose a female character, but in the meantime I suppose I'll learn how to pee on trees and spit while scratching my newfound man pieces.  :D

Si te gusta Skyrim y su ambientación y pelea de espadas, si te gusta la ambientación de una civilización post apocalíptica en el desierto, si te gusta la ambientación futuristica de una utopía, si te gusta la ambientación de una civilización avanzada en la nieve. [u]因为很喜欢类似老滚5风格的非线性开放世界RPG类游戏，看到游戏宣传图片和视频跟老滚5很类似，趁着打折，66%off的时候入手了这个游戏，然而并非如此，玩了大概10多个小时，简单谈谈对游戏的看法：[/u]
[h1] 1.画质 7/10[/h1]

[quote] 首先谈谈画质，本作画质方面谈不上出色，但也不是很差，只能说勉强超过一些及格线，有沙漠，有绿洲，有火山，有雪地，从远处看还不错，但走进看，细节纹理就不那么到位了，例如雪景，ELEX里面给人的感觉就是瓢泼似的，差点都看不到路，给人的感觉很粗糙，跟老滚5比起来少了一些细腻。[/quote]

[h1] 2.操作 7/10[/h1]

[quote] 其次谈谈游戏的操作，本作完全支持手柄，手柄键位跟ACT游戏类似，L摇杆控制方向，R摇杆控制镜头，X起跳，RT攻击，A互动捡包，但有些设定比较奇怪，必须收回武器才能捡包。[/quote]

[h1] 3.战斗 5/10[/h1]

[quote] 战斗系统很糟糕，打击手感差不说，主要是怪物太强，主角太弱，即使玩最低难度，我目前玩到12级了，只要出了城，碰到野怪被打到2-3下直接躺，高级点的一下直接秒，就算怪太强也不算什么，关键是很多技能施放的判定很玄学，例如盾牌格挡，根本没什么用，你按了LT格挡，怪物猛冲过来，该倒还是倒，该掉血还是掉血，还有技能一旦施放下去很难收回，比如你按了攻击键3下，它一定会打3下出去，中间你按格挡没用，必须要等3下打完出去才会执行格挡，而你跟怪对A，都是你吃亏的多，所以跟怪对A的时候要很小心地施放攻击，要不就是被秒。	[/quote]

[h1] 4.玩法 6/10	[/h1]

[quote] 本作的玩法也是很糟糕，RPG游戏的特色-技能、装备等玩法在本作之中体现得很混乱，角色每升一级获得10点属性点，可以在力量、体力、敏捷、智力、狡诈上分配，问题来了，武器的装备、技能的学习要受力量、体力等属性的点数的限制，一把普通的单手斧要50多的力量和40多的体力，也就是说可能要升到20多级才能拿上。而升级所需的经验大部分来源于任务，打怪给的经验少得可怜，任务跑图又远，任务给的经验也少，可能做几个任务都升不了一级。技能的学习也是，很多有用的技能要求属性点很高，还有学技能要找技能师，每种技能都有专门的技能师对应，而且没有任务也没有提示你去找谁学，玩到现在我还没找到制造技能找谁学。[/quote]

[h1] 5.剧情 4/10	[/h1]

[quote]剧情对话很长，而且每个剧情要跑很远，基本上要做一个任务可能要从地图的东边跑到西边，再从北边跑到南边，坑爹的是一般任务点距离传送点都很远，而且路上一堆比你厉害得多的怪，又没有马匹和载具的设定，能不能走到任务点都是个问题，玩起来给人的感觉就是跑步一小时，战斗一分钟，而且战斗的结果大部分是主角被怪两三下秒，然后不断重新读档的多。[/quote]

[h1] 6.综合6/10	[/h1]

[quote] 综合起来我觉得10分本作能打6分，已经不能再多了，我能撑下去玩这么久的理由可能是我一直想着“制造技能没学到，也许做完这个任务我就能学到制造了”，可惜玩到现在我还是不知道去哪学制造技能，别看我玩了10多个小时，大部分时间都是在跑任务的路上，然后就是死了重新读档重新打的过程，作为一个RPG游戏，我认为只有个RPG的模式，老滚5之后，再难有稍微出色点的末世风格非线性沙盒RPG。好评仅为中文，体现开发商重视中国市场，希望继续加油！	[/quote]

To be honest, I was hezitent to buy this game for some reason but after playing it for a while, its actually a good game. It takes the world Horizon Zero Dawn and throws in midevil themes and environments. There is much to do in this game and I found the quests, including the sides quests to be fun as well as deep. Example: guard asks for a drink while he's on duty (do you risk getting him drunk and putting all lives at risk just to win his friendship or do you refuse and lower your status with your allies). All quests contribute to your allied status which helps lower prices, makes people friendlier, unlockes hidden side quests, ect. The game also uses a Mass Effect style good/evil bar which will not only unlock new speech options (this culminates with charisma passive skill) but will also contribute to your allied status. The combat is a little restrictive and clunky but it is fun and challenging. However, the game does have a few negative marks. characters in cutscenes have pixle edges (mainly on armor), NPC's can randomly walk into camera focuse during a conversation blocking your view of the characters talking, as I said before the combat is clunky and restrictive, and the facial animations are odd as well as out of sinc with how the person is talking. Despite the flaws this game has, I truely like this game.

Pros:
1. Very interesting setting, blend of futuristic/post-apocalyptic/fantasy
2. Decent enough graphics/models
3. The NPCs are very diverse in aesthetic/voice/personality
Thats about it

Cons: 
The Cons are so heavy that they cant possibly be reduced to a simplified list. Bear with me.

1. The protagonist, "Jax", is the most unlikable person I've seen in any video game. Not even just as far as protagonists go. As far as any character at all goes. He is the biggest edgelord in the entire game. Not even the villains are as rude/snide/edgy/pessimistic and annoying to talk to as he is. This is the kind of guy that would bark at a small teenage cashier for dropping one of the pennies when getting his change back. The game actually gives you dialogue options and ALL of them are the worst possible dialogue options imaginable. He is just the biggest idiot and the most insufferable person to be around. I want to take control of every NPC he interacts with just to have them punch him in his stupid face every time he opens his mouth, killing him instantly, which brings us to our next Con...

2. Jax is also somehow the most feeble character in the game. This is one of those games where fighting monsters gives you... maybe 2 experience when you need 8000 to level up. No matter how large or strong the monster is. You have to spend literal hours in town talking and talking and talking to gain any worthwhile experience. Then when you do level up, it was hardly worth it as Jax is pitifully weak. Even after 12 hours of playing and leveling up, Jax gets basically one shot by LITERALLY any other enemy NPC. Every fight is PUNISHINGLY difficult for Jax because he is just so incredibly weak and frail. And it's not like it's a one hit kill game. Jax may as well be holding a pillow instead of a sword and even when he shoots an actual gun, he somehow makes the bullets depressingly slow and weak. 

3. Apparently the point of the game is to avoid fighting, basically at all... There is literally no reward for grinding or fighting random enemies when travelling around. No joke. The random enemies yield no loot or experience. When you DO have to fight for a quest, it basically revolves around finding a way to cheese every single encounter. Or doing measly poke damage, running for your life, drinking mass amounts of potions, running back, rinsing and reapeating. It is horrendously designed. I can't stress enough just how pathetic of a fighter Jax is for someone who talks like he's a god and everyone around are just peons beneath him. 



Basically what I'm saying is... the game is not worth it, even on sale. It's just a horribly bad game. DO NOT be lured in by the action packed cinematic trailer. The setting and aesthetic is very very cool but ultimately not worth it as the actual gameplay is a slog of mediocrity.

Its a bad skyrim clone but I like it.  
If you've never played Skyrim, buy Skyrim, if you've never played Fallout IV get Fallout IV (same applies for New Vegas and III). If you've played all of them then consider getting ELEX. The story itself is kinda funky, it attempts to wedge together the worlds of Elder Scrolls (Fantasy and Magic) and FallOut (Outlaws and a post-apocalyptic world) into some sort of cohesive story and only fails a bit. It kinda works. I personally quite like how it makes you dislike every single faction in the game and struggle to choose between them. I think the lore choices made around the Beserkers and Clerics were interesting and well considered. 

The execution is okay up till a certain point but there are obvious issues with the polish. Obviously a developer's favorite deadline is "never" but this went out a little earlier than it should have. All of the women effectively have the same face (mostly just different hairstyles) they all have _precisely_ the same boobs. There aren't enough voice actors and some of the voice lines are obviously placeholders with accents completely changing (this is rare though) or my favorite:  

Me (talking to merchant): "What have you got?"
Merchant: "sure thing!"

later areas got much less love than earlier ones and generally there are a lot of rehashes of baddies where in a full game cycle they would have made each area more unique. The pacing of the mechanics is completely ♥♥♥♥♥♥ ("too hard, too hard" into "too easy, too easy") and there are skills and talents that just seem pointless or too weak to be value considering how attribute points scale/ Likely these issues would have been bashed into shape given more extensive play-testing. 
That said, its a decent stab at the genre and to be honest, that's all a lot of us are looking for. Its hard to make a game this big and beat Skyrim/Fallout at the same time and if you're bored waiting for the next Elder Scrolls then give this a spin.  

The same issues apply that plague Skyrim plague ELEX : somewhat clunky combat, hilariously underwhelming "end fights" of like 10 men going to siege a city, poor combat mechanics when there are lots of people fighting, plot-holes in the simplifications of the world-building (if life is cheap where are all the babies?, how do these people eat?), weird bugs and a general fatigue in the grinding.   

On the plus side compared to the titans in the field the jetpack concept is very neat and lets you explore the map even when "too weak". There's a lot of fun to be had trying to run away from terrifying baddies that you haven't a hope of facing.

If Skyrim is 9/10 then this is probably somewhere between 4-7/10 depending how harshly you score. Its worth a punt.

PROS

Beautiful open world
Good voice acting
Very challenging combat mechanic
(challenges actually make you feel like you earned something.)

CONS

You have no choice for the protagonist, Jax is integral to the storyline, ... this can be both good and bad.
You need to turn off the default settings for "target lock" and "dodge" for best results.
Steep learning curve will turn off casual gamers

Having said that, I'd like to educate you about some of the "negative" reviews, 
simply because so many of them are poorly thought out or just completely misinformed.

[i]"... combat is buggy as hell"[/i]
I didn't encounter this problem, so, ... No, the combat mechanic works very well once you understand how it works.

[i]"... will only sometimes accept your input"[/i]

A flat out misrepresentation of how the combat system actually works. Actions are Stamina based and each click of the mouse button creates a 'queue' of actions to be performed by the character. This enables you to create a "chain of attacks" that can force the enemy back for extra damage. During combat you can insert 'heavy attacks' and 'special attacks' based on you Stamina level. Throughout the game you are given opportunities to increase your Stamina level which in turn will increase your ability to deal damage. 

[i]"... quests are grinding wastes of time that feel half hearted at best, and mosty filler"[/i]
Nope, all quests reward you with experience points and sometimes a unique weapon or item. The more quests you finish, the more experience you gain, the stronger your character becomes. 

There are no "filler" quests, but there are some 'side quests' designed to provide story background and help you gain experience. 

Many of the quests are intertwined and the decisions you make will actually change the way the story unfolds, how can that be "half-hearted"?

I found it was best to learn how to play before claiming "it's broken" and to actually apply some thought to some of the quest descision points and dialogs. 

Other criticisms are the voice acting and animations. 
[i]"I think the devs recorded themselves instead of using real actors."[/i]
Nope, they were professional voice actors. For some there was an issue with "lip syncing" but on my end it was not noticable.

The animations are really well done considering that the game comes from an Indie developer working on their own game engine.

I am only 4 hours in right now and will update this review as I go along, but this game is definitely a diamond in the rough.  Definitely reminds me of Two Worlds/Risen/Gothic series.  The voice acting is not nearly as bad as people made it out to be in the steam reviews.  The graphics are beautiful.  The game has native 3440x1440!!  Sounds are great.

Story so far is very interesting.  It has a touch of The Last of Us, Horizon Dawn Zero, STALKER, and Dragon Age with some very interesting factions and characters so far.

The combat is indeed clunky, but I am used to Risen and Gothic so it's not terrible.  It's certainly not smooth like Skyrim or Witcher, but I knew this going into it and even on the hardest difficulty I am managing to make progress slowly.  The game punishes you for going outside unprepared, which I like.

I would say for $20, give the game a chance.  Go in with an open mind and you will likely enjoy this diamond in the rough.

Find ich klasse. Wer sich mit den alten Gothic Teilen anfreunden konnte und vieleicht sogar die Risen Teile mag ist Elex quasi ein Muss. Mit der Steuerung hatte ich soweit keine Probleme, auch wenn die Viecher vorallem anfangs sehr stark sind ist es problemlos spielbar. Man sollte halt Abstand halten also ziemlich gleich wie Gothic und Gothic 2 etc.. 

Die Story ist jedenfalls sehr interessant aufgebaut auch wenn man komplett planlos hineingeworfen wird, und sich Quest für Quest mehr Fragen als Antworten bilden. Das Menü hat man recht schnell heraus und scheint komplizierter als es ist.

Der große Nachteil meiner Meinung nach sind die Fraktionen: um Vorann zu kommen sollte man alsbald einer Fraktion beitreten nur braucht man Ziemlich lange bis man weiß was welche genau für Sachen kann und da jede etwas unterschiedliche Skillst benötigen man ziemlich Abhängig wirkt was aber eigentlich schlussendlich egal ist.
Nachteil daraus ergibt sich (für Spieler wie mich, die soziemlich jede Quest machen bis man aufgenommen wird und sich trozdem umentscheiden) dass man wenig bis keine Waffen und Rüstungen findet und man so sehr "verletzlich" ist, und ziemlich abhängig von Begleiter. Und wenn man mal eine Waffe findet ist die anforderung an Attribute ein ziemlich großer Sprung, so dass ich auch nach dem Ende! einige noch nicht halten konnte.

Zum Optischen: Die Grafik ist nichts Ausergewöhnliches trozem sehr gut und Vermittelt die dargestellten eindrücke der Spiele welt auch gut. (Man muss sich etwas mit der Geschichte auseinandersetzen um zu Verstehen warum die Regionen anders aussehen.) Waffendetails und Rüstungen sind liebevoll gestalltet. Die "Hauptstädte" passen optisch zu den Idealen jeweiliger Fraktionen. Und die Viecher sehen allesamt gefährlich und unheimlich aus. 
Einziges manko meinerseite: NPCs, vorallem die weiblichen sehen alle wie Zwillingsschwestern aus, wem das nicht stört sollte eigentlich kein Problem haben.

Im Großen und Ganzen ist ELEX empfehlenswert, vorallem! für alle diejenigen die von Tag 1 'Gothic' Fans sind (vorallem diejenigen unter euch die Gothic 1&2+Die Nacht des Raben mindestens 3 mal durchspielten um jede Fraktion zu probieren) und den Ehrgeiz von Piranha Bytes mit 'Risen' weiterverfolgten. Es ist ein gutes liebevolles Spiel, mit viel humor und unterhaltung, "dramatischen Wendungen" und einem Story verlauf der zum Teil selbst beeinflussbar ist. 

Geschichtlich ist eine Fortsetzung fraglich, jedoch warte ich gespannt darauf.

9/10 Insgesamt, weil sie mit Gothic 2 Die Nacht des Raben SEHR viel vorgelegt haben und noch einiges können ;)

[h1] Причины отрицательного отзыва [/h1] 
[b]Первая причина из-за кривой боевки:[/b]
Она оооочень кривая, видел тут комментарий, где автор сравнивал ее с дарксоулс - нифига подобного, кривее придумать было нельзя, перекат на двойной клик W-W либо D-D и т.д.(я сначала по привычке "перекатов" пытался жать Space :D), не совсем удобно, это учитывая, что могло бы быть терпимо, но все портит выносливость. (Но её потом можно будет нарастить)
Играл я на высоком уровне сложности, и разобрался в системе управления - есть блоки, перекаты, слабый-сильный удар (с возможностью комбо удара), нужно знать тайминги монстров.
Как говорится, у тебя может быть идеальная реакция, но зачем она тебе, если тебе максимум хватит на 2-3 удара и откат, а дальше придется бегать или летать от противника 2-3 секунды и восстанавливать эту выносливость - ничего похожего на "танец" (это из еще одного положительного отзыва) я не увидел. Просто "затягивание" боя и игры в следствии. Ибо для того чтобы убить монстра, нужно нанести ему овер-дофи*а ударов, а ему достаточно дать тебе около 3-4, если не меньше.("Баланс?" - и еще учитывайте, что придется постоянно зыркать на "выносливость")

[b]Вторая причина связана с локализацией:[/b]
Игра с русскими субтитрами и английской озвучкой, но диалоги посторонних НПС (ситуация - встретились двое нпс на улице и разговаривают) не переведены и соотвественно не отражаются на экране (игра "послушай речь и пойми о чем они говорят" - а вдруг мне это интересно? может хочу погрузится в этот мир послушать "городские сплетни"?). Это я заметил еще в самом начале своего прохождения в городе берсерков - и не нужно говорить "учи английский", я бы лучше тогда немецкий выучил, чтобы играть в игру на оригинале, возможно когда-нибудь так и сделаю.

[h1] Плюсы [/h1]
Она пропитана тем самым духом предыдущих игр. Много диалогов, разные подходы к квестам (т.е. большое количество вариантов прохождения) - это огромный плюс. 
Я сам обожаю исследовать и за первые полтора часа игры, нашел пару нычек с неплохими вещичками - игра поддалкивает игрока на изучение мира, что очень хорошо.
+ Реактивный ранец и возможность карабкаться на какие-нибудь выступы, тоже сделано весьма качественно.

[h1] Графика [/h1]
Её я даже выделю в отдельный пункт :)
Да, анимация местами подкачивает, а модели персонажей, как я заметил, похожи друг на друга. Но тем не менее она просто красивая, и ничего тут не поделаешь. Ламповые, тёплые локации, мне не нужно было много времени, чтобы увидеть, что они сделаны с душой, великолепное освещение, шикарные водоёмы и пейзажи в целом.
Еще понравился переход с улицы в темные помещения, "глаз привыкает", когда заходишь становится гораздо светлее (р-реализм)  :3

[h1] К итогам [/h1]
Может кому-то игра понравится, и он (или она) сможет закрыть глаза на недостатки, о которых писал выше, я попытался и не смог, увы... именно поэтому обзор отрицательный
Я еще побегаю и поисследую мир, но я уже понимаю, что, конечно, эта игра, как и все предыдущие, будет иметь одну, если не две трети составляющей - сражения с монстрами (и даже с несколькими за раз), и готовлюсь огребать пол-игры пока не вкачаюсь в дальний бой, ведь там потом еще гранаты появятся (ближний из-за "затянутости" я не рассматриваю) 

Не смотря на то, что это в основном отрицательный обзор, советую попробовать, если вам понравится, то я буду лишь рад за вас :D
Ибо я уверен, что в этой игре можно найти много интересностей и получить наслаждение и от сюжета, и от побочных квестов, и от исследования локаций

This game is so close to being good, but at least one of the developers is just bad at game design. It's so close to being a great game, but then there are so many so utterly pedantic, stupid and idiotic game design decisions which just make it a really frustrating "game".

The balance is wrong, the early quests will send you to areas with enemies that one shot you from afar, the levelling system is rubbish, the distribution of enemies is seemingly arbitrary and wrong (there is literally an unkillable enemy if you go 10 yards from the prescribed starting path in the first 10 minutes), you're constantly forced to backtrack on areas because one little bit of it you weren't high enough level for.

And as for the combat. Think Darksouls, but without any of the skill or satisfaction. Just bullshit. It's just pathetically bad, whoever programmed it should honestly never work on a game again.

After several hours you will find yourself shooting at someone at someone close to the starting area and it will not even take off a sliver of their health. They will then run at you and one-shot you.

It's just mind boggling, unnecessarily, bad.

The world is great, the atmosphere is great, just marred by truly awful gameplay.

Don't buy it, honestly, you'll read "git gud" or "you can get good" or "everything's good apart from the combat". But it's nonsense. 

It's just a badly balanced game. You will die a lot, and every single one of those deaths will feel like it was just bullshit.

Nach zwei Schlägen mit der Waffe habe ich keine Ausdauer mehr, um die sagenumwobenen Combos durchzuführen. 
Hatte mich gefreut, als ich ein Legendäres Schwert gefunden habe, wofür ich jedoch noch mehr als 30 Attributspunkte zu wenig hatte. Die Mutanten die nicht einen Totenkopf als Symbol hatten konnten mich trotzdem regelmäßig zerlegen.. Wollte die Hauptquest weitermachen, doch ich mache dennoch keinen Schaden an den zwei Typen, die mich unfreundlich empfangen. Eine Granate, einen Flächen- und vier Einzelzauber, diverse Heiltränke aber ich hatte in 20 Anläufen einen, bei dem ich es geschafft hatte EINEN der zwei tot zu kriegen. Jedoch nicht geschafft, trotz "Easy" ...

Ich hab kein Problem mit Herausforderungen, ich hab kein Problem damit, wenn man nachdenken muss, sich Pläne überlegen muss und improvisieren soll. Aber zugegeben, ich kann euch nur das empfehlen: Kauft es euch nur, wenn es reduziert ist. Ob es den Preis wert ist, müsst ihr entscheiden, meiner Ansicht nach verdient es nicht den Hype, der veranstaltet wurde.
