If you’ve ever been on a date with someone who seems very interesting and pleasant, but suddenly goes on tirades about lizard people or how the Illuminati faked the moon landing, you have some understanding of my love-hate relationship with ELEX. It’s a sprawling, ambitious, Euro-style RPG in the tradition of series like The Witcher and Gothic, and there’s plenty to admire peppered across its more than 50 hours of adventuring. But while it spends about half its time making me want to sing its praises, it spends the other half making me want to pull every single hair out of my scalp.

The seamless open world is built on a strong foundation of detailed lore that feels unlike anything the genre has thrown at us before. There are dazzling sci-fi elements like super soldiers and radioactive mutants, but also a clan of woodsy wizards who shun all technology. There are exciting influences from Fallout and Mad Max, with sand-blown, post-apocalyptic ruins and gangs of mercenaries in biker leathers, but also a medieval-ish religious order that worships the god of machines. Somehow, it all fits together in a way that feels interconnected and believable. The sheer uniqueness always left me wanting to dig deeper and learn more.

The early part of the main quest involves aligning with one of the three main factions, and while each has a very distinct aesthetic, values they expect you to uphold, and a unique set of quests, they unfortunately don’t play as differently as I expected. I quickly found that trying to treat ELEX like a shooter, or make a go of things as a pure magic user, isn’t terribly viable. Ammo and mana potions are too scarce, and going all-in on ranged makes it very hard to defend yourself against most monsters. Melee weaponry almost always ended up being my main combat tool, and a lot of the supposedly exclusive abilities for each faction are mirrored in the other two. For example, many of the buffs available through Berserker magic have almost direct analogs in the psychic powers of the Clerics and the stimulant consumables that can be manufactured by the Outlaws. So in practice, they’re the same abilities shuffled to different parts of the skill tree.

The story is definitely the strongest pillar holding up ELEX. The twists are unexpected and memorable. The characters are endearing, with multi-layered and engaging backstories. Duras, a stoic warrior and your first companion, has a checkered past that presents many interesting questions as you pick through it. Nasty, an outlaw who seems like a stereotypical, curse-flinging, edge girl femme fatale has a meaningful arc of growth that sheds light on her behaviors in a believable way. There are enough potential variations in the ending that I almost want to play it again to see more of them. And it’s all accompanied by almost shockingly high-quality voice acting.

Yet for an RPG that puts so much emphasis on player choice, there really aren’t a lot of opportunities to solve problems by means other than combat. I built my character to take the fullest advantage of speech-based personality skills, as I often do. Disappointingly, I could count on one hand the number of times I was actually able to use these skills to change the outcome of a quest. Putting so much emphasis on combat isn’t necessarily a bad thing, but the fact that I was given the option to dump points into skills that will almost never come up in a meaningful way feels like I fell into a trap set for idealistic fools who thought they could solve problems with diplomacy.

The biggest problem with ELEX is that it’s buggy to the point I almost wasn’t able to finish it. Broken event triggers, horrible party member AI, and missing or misplaced map markers that make quest targets impossible to find call to mind the worst of Fallout: New Vegas or Vampire the Masquerade: Bloodlines at the time of their respective releases. At one point I had to chase down and speak to every named NPC in a large town - most of which do not stay in one place for long - due to having no indication of which one had the quest that would let me advance the story. In another case, I spent almost an hour jetpacking around looking for a way into a locked structure because that’s where the quest marker told me to go, and I was never tipped off that it unlocks through another quest I hadn’t completed yet. I’m not the kind of RPG player who needs everything spelled out for me with GPS directions on every quest. But the reason great games like Morrowind got away with less hand-holding was the fact that you could read books, talk to guards, or otherwise get clues from the environment on where you needed to go. ELEX offers none of that, so a lot of quests aren’t so much involved treasure hunts as they are a guessing game mixed with hide-and-seek.

Maybe developer Piranha Bytes will fix it in a few months with some extensive patches. It certainly has the ingredients to be a come-from-behind success story like New Vegas or Bloodlines (though fixing the latter was largely a fan effort). But at the moment, I just can’t recommend anyone spend money on the technical disaster area that is ELEX.

Even when everything is working as intended, the combat balance often feels absurd. Games like Dark Souls are punishing, but never feel unfair. Certain quests in ELEX, on the other hand, made me feel like I had to break or circumvent its core systems to win. Some required me to snipe a couple enemies from a large group with fireballs at a distance, run several hundred yards to a shack with a bed, take a quick nap to regain my health and mana, and return to repeat this process four or five times. That’s a tedious way to fight. One boss took me almost two hours to slay because I had to keep trying until I got lucky enough not to trigger his unblockable, nearly undodgeable rock-throw attack (which he could somehow hit me with even when I was standing directly behind him) too many times.

On top of the poor encounter design, moment-to-moment combat is irritating because of things like imprecise hitboxes and animation timings, especially on area attacks. Enemy damage scales up way too quickly in comparison to yours throughout the middle levels, forcing frequent grinding detours to catch up. Too often, I felt that I was fighting poor design choices rather than monsters.

The designers also seem stubbornly phobic of many quality-of-life features that became standard in the genre for a reason. Things like having to constantly buy potions from vendors to heal yourself while also dealing with the constraints of a stingy, gear-focused economy are throwbacks to the bad old days when your survivability was based on the size of your wallet. It’s hard to believe a lot of balance testing and tuning was done on loot drops, monster stats, and player abilities. The math involved all comes across as arbitrary rather than carefully thought-out, from the fact that the endgame armor costs more than I made in 30 levels of exploring and questing to the aggravating reality that damage from hard-to-avoid ranged attacks is so high, fights with more than three foes at once are almost always suicide, even at higher levels.

There are lots of little moments that made me go, “How did this make it into the release version?” One prominent example is the fact that there’s a long, unskippable conversation right before the highly difficult final boss fight, and you can’t save after it - so you’re forced to mash B to get through a bunch of dialogue on every single attempt. It’s one thing to make me earn my victory – it’s another to punish my defeats with an annoying inconvenience every time, especially on a fight designed to take several attempts to complete.

First, the combat is bad. Not the amusing kind of bad, the aggrivatingly absolutely aweful kind of bad. The beginning of the game has emphasis on melee combat, and does a horrible job at actually telling the player how to operate melee weapons, only doing so after you are being attacked by something. The actual melee attacks do extremely low damage, take too long to execute, and seem to lag a second behind the actual attack command. On top of that, the roll is useless because half the enemies in the game dash three yards to hack into you when you attempt to avoid an attack. The block/parrying outright does not work most of the time, and you run out of stamina extremely fast with little indication of such. This is basically a game trying to execute dark souls combat in the worst unintuitive way possible that only serves to be extremely aggrivating and frusterating. As for the ranges combat, you point at something and shoot. Not much more to say on that. On top of that, the movement overall is sluggish and slow.

What about the story? Well you are immediately introducted to the entire backstory of this work upon clicking the new game, which I understand may be good to give people context, but I can't muster interest in the world if I have yet to see much of it. You character is non-customizable for people who care about that. He is a generic gravely-voiced short brown haired guy like in every video game, enough so that I cannot even remember his name. He is also shot by his own people less than 5 minutes into the game with no context whatsoever. This far into the game, and nothing has made me care about this world.

It’s hard to make a defensive case for ELEX and the developers have pretty much ruined any attempt when charging 50$ for it. The game is in a rough technical state and no matter how much you are willing to ignore that for the sake of immersion and nostalgia, the problems will eventually get to you. ELEX is haunted at every step by a limited production budget that forced a small team of developers to cut many corners in order to deliver the grand vision for their game. However,ELEX follows in the footsteps of Gothic 2 like no other game that I played, providing a true RPG experience in an actually well designed open world. It has many problems, but that won’t stop me from eagerly waiting for the sequel the same way I waited for Gothic 3, hopefully not with the same end result. It’s understandable to avoid a full price purchase. But if you are a fan of the genre, give it time, wait for the patches (maybe an EE?!) and the price cuts, because it would be a shame to skip on this game altogether.

Pros:
+ Captivating story
+ A complex system of choices and consequences
+ Cool companions
+ Excellent world design
+ Great sense of progression
+ Plenty of quality content
+ Gothic nostalgia

Cons:
– Outdated graphics
– Questionable voice acting
– Clunky animations and controls
– Ugly and lackluster UI
– Some lazy oversights
– Plenty of bugs
– Quite pricey for all its problems

Сюжет: Он повествует нам о командоре альбов Джаксе, во время задания его глайдер сбили, а собратьям было порученно немедленно казнить его. К чуду, мы выжили.
И тут начинается игра. Разработчики не врали, и уже после первой встречи с NPC вы можете идти куда душа пожелает, но, к сожалению, делать, что душа пожелает уже не получится. 
Я не играл раньше ни в одну из игр пираний, это была для меня первой. Сюжет односторонний и не без дыр, особенно финальное сражение за судьбу Магалана, и в этом учавствует армия двух фракций которая суммарно насчитывает 12 человек. Хотелось бы 2 часть, учитывая, что игра заканчивается на самом интересном (только чтобы узнать сюжет, ибо в остальном эта игра паршива).
Местность: Ну тут все чудеса света на любой глаз: И снег, и лава, и леса, и пустыня, и даже современность (фабрики/заводы/дома). Исследовать приятно, но из-за живности атмосфера убивается. 
Бои: топорная система закликай врага убита напрочь добавлением выносливости. В игре жуткий дисбаланс который не позволяет драться добрую треть игры, и это будет самая унылая часть. Я смог убивать нормально лишь после 15 часов игры, но даже к эндгейму 2-4 врага уже вызывают проблему в которой действует тактика Ударил-кувырок, притом прокатиться надо вокруг всех врагов, ибо некоторые имеют пушки, а это всегда дополнительная боль (особенно если у них тяжелое орудие)
В игре есть оружия ближнего боя (двухручные/одноручные), стрелковые (луки/пушки/лазерные пушки), гранаты, ну и что-то там по магии.

This game is a type of bad that slowly erodes your will to see the game through. It starts off a bit wonkey, but drops just enough universe and lore building that makes you want to see the better part of the game (ie. "It must get better after THIS mechanic is introduced!). Elex is a game of loose ends, actually scratch that. Elex is a game that covers the continuation or conclusion of any leads in dirt, and then entices you to dig just a little further in so you can see if anything makes sense. Throughout the game every npc and upgrade tree leads you to believe that the powers you will get from joining a faction will unlock an insanely powerful skill tree that would allow you to armwrestle a robot with your mind, on fire, while god himself looks on with jelousy keen enough to cut the planet in half. What you recieve however, is little better than a new type of weapon with stand-in graphics. For myself, this came in at hour 12 after I had explored and grinded my way through landscapes that change from climate to climate like a pokemon or legend of zelda game. It was a killing blow, to know that the game was not going to get better, or more fun to play in any capacity. the worst part is that it took me way past the refundable time played for me to see what this game truely was. By the end of my playing, all i was left with was wasted time, money, and an insufferable headache whenever i see this title in my library.

Complimenti a Piranha Bytes! Ho trovato Elex un gioco molto complesso, in modo sorprendentemente positivo. La storia mi è piaciuta perché piena di dettagli ed è stata creata in modo tale che tu possa divertirti, esplorarando Megalan, incontrando numerosi personaggi  e creature diverse in modalità free roaming ma con importanti conseguenze sulla storia principale. L'evoluzione del protagonista è avvincente e molto particolare, occorre pianificare e investire del tempo per decidere quali abilità coltivare, ma non eccessivamente! Ho trovato intrigante il sistema delle scelte e le conseguenze, non l'ho trovato pensante o troppo vincolante. Megalan è un vasto mondo dove puoi incontrare alleati potenti che possono diventare nemici se le tue scelte non sono in linea con la loro filosofia. I personaggi possiedono un carattere e una storia molto dettagliati, ognuno ha le sue paure, aspirazioni, tabou. Ho incontrato qualche bug qua e là, come nemici che saltano in aria e spariscono all'orizzonte o creature che si bloccano in qualche parete, ma nulla che ostacolasse la giocabilità, anzi hanno fornito qualche nota di ilarità al contesto di gioco. Il sistema di combattimento è valido e occorre fare attenzione ai nemici che incontri, il gioco ti offre la possibilità di uccidere un troll ma allo stesso tempo un piccolo ritter può esserti fatale se non pianifichi i combattimenti: una bella sfida! L'ambientazione è fatta molto bene e la transizione tra i diversi territori controllati dalle fazioni è gestita bene con paesaggi suggestivi e dettagliati. Le fazioni hanno una loro storia che non reputo sia scontata. Se si presta attenzione ai documenti e agli indizi sparsi tra le rovine di Megalan si scoprono interessanti dettagli sulla storia del pianeta che arricchiscono il contesto.
Consiglio vivamente questo gioco, da godersi con il giusto stato mentale.

通关了，这是一款我开场几个小时以后就想怒删的坑爹游戏，途中也有开挂直接升满级满装备的想法，当然最后是没开（讲道理后期改过一次钱出衣服，Elex太难收集了），也是幸运我没开挂，得以在6个小时以后终于开始有游戏体验了。
首先是故事，这个故事通篇下来还是很饱满的，虽然人物说话通常都是站桩（导致我前面的对话疯狂跳过），但是里面的世界观，小细节，某些梗都很有意思，绝对值得深入品尝。特别到后面，明显能感觉到主角越来越有血有肉（可能是代入感问题），甚至还从没有情感到谈个恋爱，这些都很棒，剧情绝对是很有诚意的，非常期待后续剧情。
然后是战斗，不喜欢这游戏，包括IGN能给出4.9分，确实是因为战斗系统的问题，这游戏的战斗系统实在是让人难受，伤害就更难受了，我一开始不要命开了困难难度，前几个小时都是跑路，随便一只小怪秒杀互相循环，也差点让我有了怒删的冲动，其实到后面技能武器防御（死得慢）上去了，战斗也就相对轻松了，武器什么的还是很华丽的。
说 一下这个游戏没啥毛病的地方，风景，建筑，这些都很好，在沙漠旁边有个海，然后旁边有个超大的铁架建筑物（就是码头边那种），在一个风和日丽的中午，看见这种的景象是让人觉得很奇妙的，武器的设计也很棒，我承认前期就是想拿到光武才坚持下来的，最后也满足了。
写在最后，这是一款好游戏，如果你有兴趣去了解一个关于彗星撞地球几百年以后却还在打仗的世界的话，请选择这款游戏吧，虽然战斗系统很垃圾，但是你会战斗了以后你会发现风景才是大佬，剧情才是大佬，战斗只要不影响你过剧情就行了，世界观也是非常特别的，你想想一个未来科技的指挥官掉到原始森林以后被某原始部落的人收留了（里面又能找到枪），然后又穿山越岭到了另一座冰（火）山加入另一的高科技的组织，这一切听上去多穿越啊！可偏偏它就发生在同一世界观下，因为末日后人们的信仰问题导致这种两极分化的组织又让这一切显得很合理，这不是很棒啊，虽然有缺陷，也是美的，期待续作，但是应该不会开二周目了，前期太想死，无限捡垃圾也不够钱花，这我觉得不行。

ELEX is an amazing game that, through questionable design decisions, makes you work a little to love it. My first time through, I absolutely LOVED the world design. It was lush and colorful with some variety as you went further out and absolutely filled to the brim with danger and adventure. However, the combat turned me right off. Yes, you will get stun locked. Yes, ranged weapons blow. You won't be able to feel powerful until level 20 or so when you've had a chance to beef up your stats. The game expects you to explore and do quests in order to level up and make money, and although it tries to give you some guidance via the main quest, there was never any urgency and so it always felt like I was missing something.

So I lost interest and gave up.

Then I did a second playthrough and noticed that there was a dodge. What? A dodge? You have to double tap a direction key to dodge. I immediately saw the problem with this, but I found the magical options: a button for dodging, which I set to mouse 4, and another switch for turning off double-tap dodging. Then I discovered a second magic trick: comboing. It turns out that if you hit until you can special and do it as a combo, you do something like 300% - 500% damage. These things were game changers. Once you get used to dodging around big enemies and comboing them, the games transforms from some kind of masochistic die fest to a truly tactical RPG.

The other big complaint I shared with professional reviews was the main character. However, as you learn more about the world and the character himself, you find that everything is accounted for in the story. There aren't non-pasty Albs. There aren't fun, quirky Albs. Albs looking and acting like each other is integral to the story. Jax going through emotional confusion became one of the more compelling subplots of the game.

I love walking around with a hammer and an energy rifle hunting trolls and drinking health pots. This game is magical.

[h1]Кто вы такие и что вы сделали с Piranha Bytes? [/h1]

15 лет. 15 долгих лет студия Piranha Bytes делала RPG. Специфические, глупые, однотипные, вновь и вновь наступающие на грабли тотального непонимания того, как нужно делать игры. За эти годы всех издателей, с которыми им довелось работать, постигла нелёгкая судьба: Phenomedia и JoWooD Entertainment отошли в мир иной, а Deep Silver была выкуплена THQ Nordic. Мир вокруг менялся, а разработчики будто бы и не осознавали этого. Казалось, всё так и останется неизменным, но время берёт своё. Часть команды скоропостижно скончалась, другая же предпочла отделиться и попытаться создать что-нибудь новое. Оставшимся предстояло решить, что делать дальше. Разработчики решили не изобретать велосипед, как это было с Risen, а обратились к опыту прошлого, воспользовавшись им, чтобы достичь новой вершины на реактивной тяге. Поприветствуйте ELEX – первую игру Piranha Bytes, за которую им не должно быть стыдно.

ELEX привлекает внимание в первую очередь своим миром. Магалан. Мир, переживший столкновение с кометой. Миллионы погибших, утрата прежних технологий и привычного образа жизни, а вместе с этим новая надежда – элекс. Принесённый кометой минерал стал главной целью для оставшихся в живых группировок: для берсерков это источник их магии и способ восстановить уничтоженную кометой природу; у клириков он служит источником энергии для их могущественных технологий; лишённые эмоций альбы видят в элексе путь в становлении расы на новую ступень эволюции; изгои же находят в минерале сильнейший наркотик. Все группировки видят друг в друге врага, а потому и жизнь на Магалане спокойной не назовёшь, даже если не брать в расчёт орды опаснейших мутантов, заполонивших пустоши в поисках все того же элекса. Для игр комбинация фентези и высоких технологий ещё не успела стать избитой. Особенно в таком глупом и притягательном виде, когда воины в тяжёлых доспехах мечами дубасят огромных боевых роботов. Впрочем, невесть откуда взявшиеся в стенах студии творцы вложили в свою работу столько сил, что любые сомнения в правдоподобности происходящего постепенно сходят на нет, а на все вопросы, возникающие относительно спорных моментов мира игры, будут даны удовлетворительные ответы. Узнать подробности о прошлом Магалана можно через разбросанные по всему миру записи и аудиодневники, написанные так интересно, что именно они служат главной мотивацией к исследованию огромного, но при этом проработанного и красивого мира. Впервые за всё время игрок примерит на себя роль не очередного безымянного героя с размытым прошлом, а вполне чётко прописанного персонажа — Джакса, подробнее о личности которого можно будет постепенно узнать по ходу игры через флешбеки. В ходе выполнения очередного задания глайдер командора альбов Джакса оказывается сбит, а сам он приговаривается к казни прямо на месте, однако чудом остаётся в живых. Без оружия, без брони и без толики былой силы. Зато с неожиданно пробудившимися эмоциями. Джаксу предстоит осознать себя, принять сторону в конфликте и найти способ отомстить альбам.

А поможет ему в этом команда разношёрстных спутников, у каждого свои цели и причины путешествовать с Джаксом, узнать о которых можно лишь завоевав их доверие, а то и любовь. Piranha Bytes вводят систему последствий – каждое действие игрока повлияет как на отношение к нему персонажа, так и на более глобальные вещи, включая основной сюжет. Никогда не знаешь, на что повлияет твоё решение в, казалось бы, маловажном квесте. Сначала, конечно, кажется, что постоянные уведомления о том, что персонаж что-то запомнит – это пшик уровня игр Telltale, но разработчики до последнего держат планку, не забывая о принятых игроком решениях. Вместе с этим получила развитие и система кармы из Risen 3. В ELEX на её место пришла холодность, обозначающая то, насколько Джакс подвержен эмоциям. Это расширяет возможности взаимодействия с холодностью, не разделяя поступки на чёрное и белое, как это обычно происходит с системами кармы.

Ролевая система стала более привычной: достигаешь нового уровня и получаешь 10 очков характеристик, распределяемые на свое усмотрение, и 1 очко навыка, которое можно потратить у учителя на один из множества навыков игры, если уровень характеристик позволяет. А на начальных этапах игры достаточно тяжело набрать достаточное количество уровней для прокачки всего необходимого, не прибегая к использованию элексовых зелий, повышающих вашу холодность. Также следует отметить, что прокачка навыка в ветке повышает её уровень, который в свою очередь влияет на особые фразы в диалогах, дающие различные бонусы.
Боевая система сильно преобразилась и бесспорно является лучшей среди всех игр студии. В целом, всё стандартно: обычный и сильный удары, блок и парирование. Однако ряд новшеств полностью меняет ее восприятие. Во-первых, появилась шкала выносливости, влияющая на возможность атаковать. Да, прямо как в Forsaken Gods. Только здесь это куда продуманнее, а потому избавляет игрока от необходимости постоянно бегать и ждать, пока выносливость восстановится. Ещё расход выносливости можно отключить в настройках, вернувшись к старому-доброму закликиванию. А во-вторых, появилась шкала комбо, заполняя которую можно провести особую атаку, эффект которой зависит от оружия в руке. Дальнобойное оружие просто пестрит разнообразием. Если с луками и арбалетами всё понятно, то остальные следует рассмотреть поподробнее. Пушки подразделяются на легкие и тяжёлые, а те в свою очередь классифицируются по типам используемых патронов. Причём у каждой пушки по несколько режимов стрельбы. Оружие ещё улучшать можно, придавая ему новые свойства. Добавьте к этому широкую систему магии и главную фишку игры – джетпак. С его помощью можно не только оказаться где угодно, благо, что мир стал многоуровневым и располагает к этому, но и атаковать самыми разными способами, вроде использования ускорения для усиления удара по врагу. Бестиарий, кстати, огромен, а большая часть врагов не являются простым рескином, а потому имеют свою собственную модель поведения и атаки. Игра даже возвращается к опыту первой Gothic и руководствуется, малым количеством врагов, но большой опасностью от них исходящей.

ELEX – прекрасная игра, сделанная с невероятным старанием и вниманием к мелочам. Абсолютно каждое дополнительное задание реализовано качественно и вызывает неподдельный интерес. Ещё ни в одной игре студии не было столько свободы во всех смыслах этого слова. Огромный шаг вперёд для Piranha Bytes, который незаслуженно холодно встретили фанаты. Вам правда стоит ознакомиться с игрой, даже если вы не особо любите игры студии. Спустя 15 лет они наконец-то смогли.

I've finally completed the main storyline, so what  I can say:
This is 100% Piranha Bytes 2017 game. This is Gothic 2,5 with guns. But there are some features that are different:
1) The game is divided into chapters and, logically, you travelling around the world, unveiling the main story line. But you also can forget about the main story and just go challenge the world, fulfilling the side quests and fighting mobs, this is what I did. So, chapter one took for me around 50 hours, when 2+3+4 around 10 hours at best (I idled about 10 hours, so the whole game took around 60-65 hours).
2) The idea for the game is good: classic 3 factions to choose from, each with its' own vision how to use the power of Elex, now they differ from each other more than classic people and orcs. The main character now can show emotions and, at the end of the game, become soulless machine, stay reasonable or become freaking emo. And your temper will influence at the key points of the main quest. The idea is good, but sometimes it seems that being logic is being cruel and being emotinal is being kind, though, there are several moments when you threaten to NPC and become more emotional. Nevertheless, I assume that this maybe the very idea of the developers, because, I, for example, remained neutral at the end, just like in real life, so there must be something in it.
3) Jetpack. You can shoot and fly. Though, almost every mob can shoot too.
Other things are done for Piranha fans:
1) At the very beginning you are a maggot. I think, untill 20-25 level you are a maggot. You just complete the quest, fast and furious, trying to fight only weak mobs and running away in panic when you see someone of average power, or, god bless, a boss. But then... From level 25 and up to 35-40 you bring hand of God to this world and this is cool. You can literaly see your progress. Creatures are different, by the way, their behaviour, type of attack vary, making it interesting to play.
2) Skillpoints, teachers etc...
3) Really interesting story and lots of good side-quests, especially ones of your companions.
4) Buggy bugs. Not so many of them, though, they won't break your main storyline but somethimes they happen. 
So, the conclusion.
Guys who are older than 25 who played Gothic 1-3 and Risen 1 for hours - this is for us. Younger guys who started their RPG way from Skyrim or later... Well, I think you should try - it will convert your vision of what good game may be.

If you're not familiar with games like Gothic and Risen then this game's mechanics, quests and story will seem different from other games. ELEX is generally speaking a mix of ideas from all previous Piranha Bytes games. It has the combat and enemy level scaling from Gothic I, progression from Risen 2, magic from Risen 1 etc.
Here are some issues with the game:
- early game difficulty and mid/late game balance. For newcomers early game will be very difficult and because the game doesn't have a tutorial chapter (except killing two rats at the beginning) the game is supposed to be learned by the player's mistakes. This will scare away many players, but once you understand the mechanics the game is pretty easy even on ultra (which just like difficulty in all Bethesda games just changes the numbers related to combat).
- broken economy. The only PB game that had more or less balanced  economy was Risen 1, ELEX took the worst ideas from all games as such the only way to make money in the game is to learn trophies up to 3rd level but after that the player will be flowing in money. Stores also are restocked very fast, even faster than Skyrim/Fallout, but as opposed to those games traders have infinite money on them so you can sell as much as you want and traders buy everything (there are no separated armor/food/clutter traders). In previous games crafting was also a reliable way to make money especially in Gothic 1/2, in this game crafting is similar to Pillars of Eternity: upgrading/creating something requires money as well which looks like you're paying someone to make/upgrade something, as such only things that will be constantly crafted in the game are potions, while jewelry and weapons will be upgraded few times per game because upgraded/created items cost a lot less than money "invested" in it, so there is no way to profit from crafting.
- "mmo rpg". In Gothic 1/2 and Risen 1 enemies/monsters re-spawned based on chapters and it was pretty hard to max your character because there was a limit of xp/attribute plants per chapter, in ELEX all this was thrown away, now plants respawn behind your back (except attribute plants) and once you kill all monsters in a location it will be "refilled" with more high level monsters shortly (this is not tied to chapter/level) and with the fact that farming elex (which is can be used to increase attributes) is extremely easy the game feels a lot more like a mmo RPG/Skyrim than a "hardcore RPG".
- {many more issues}

The main issue with this game is Piranha Bytes lack of direction. Their games have a small but consistent fan base (Gothic 2 is still actively modded), yet in ELEX they wanted to add the hardcore elements from previous games to appeal to fans with infinite/easy leveling from mmo to appeal to more casual/console players and the end result is a Skyrim/Gothic/Risen game that didn't please anyone: fans see it as too easy/too "skyrim-like" while casual players see it as too hard/unintuitive. As such to have fun with the game just see it as a sandbox like Skyrim/Fallout 4 and care as less as possible about balance and economy and only playing with this attitude I would recommend the game.

Futuristic Sequel to Gothic, here comes Elex.

Elex places you in a world where a comet brought something with it : Elex, a powerful material that can be used to do almost anything. You play Jax, an alb commander, who was sent on a solo mission and betrayed by his kind. You awaken free of the taking of Elex that made you an Alb and start your quest to understand what happened, survive and decide the fate of the world.

As all Gothic games, you start off as a really squishy and weak. That's the charm of these games, you know where you came from and look at basic enemies remembering that they used to two-shot you... now they are two-shot or one-shot themselves.

Elex is a very nice game that has good graphics, the only flaw I find is that there are not enough models for faces. It feels like every woman in the game has the same face.

Combat system is pretty basic and deadly : You have hit points, stamina points and mana points.
Mana points will only allow you to use the powers of the faction you joined, and those powers can turn the game from hard to medium or easy. There are fights you just can't win without these.
Stamina points indicates how tired you are, if you're out of stamina you can't block blows and you can't strike. Blocking, Attacking in melee and Running consumes stamina.
Hit points... I don't need to explain that if you run out of these you're dead ? Do I ?

There are many weapons in the game, melee and ranged, many powers to unlock.
You learn skills a trainers scatered in cities, for fees that sometimes aren't cheap.

You'll have to decide wether you're kind or mean a lot of times because it's a RPG.
PNJ remembers you actions and this has an effect on how the game unfolds.

If you played and liked the Gothics I strongly advise you buy and play this game.
If you dislike games that punishes you even when you're doing the quest, don't play this game.
You are not meant to fight all the enemies, learn to attack from a high point, drain their attention, be stealthy or just plainly run from them if they are too strong. They will be too strong for you for many hours. This games forces you to use your brain in a lot of tricky situations and that's why I like it a lot.

TL;DR: It's a rough piece of ore, but it's worth your time and money, especially if you've played the first two Gothic games, and the first Risen and liked them. If you're on the fence, buy it when it goes on sale -- I bought it during this year's Steam Summer Sale.

So, my two cents:

First: yes, there are a few bugs still, there are problems with, LOD pop-in, and clipping objects,  monsters, etc. and some animations could be better -- those are distracting, but not a deal breaker for me.

Second: the graphics are nice but definitely not top of the line, considering that the game does require a decent amount of processing power. Some of that can be ameliorated (and improved dramatically in some cases) by tweaking the ConfigDefault.xml file located in the folder \%(insert_your_path)%\Elex\data\ini\ [b][i]without[/i][/b] incurring in a computing penalty if you do it right.

Third: some of the controls are a bit clunky, and there is some lag in the response -- I believe the latter is by design, not by oversight.

Fourth: some dialogue lines are either badly translated, or are plain wrong because they may be specific to certain actions which may have already occurred, not occurred, or simply nonsense, or reused in not the best way when they are short replies; and in some very rare cases voiced by a completely different actor, and though very rare and depend on which choice of line you use, they stand out.

Given that, I [b]LOVE[/b] the game. It's complex, it's got a big world to explore, I love the story line thus far (I'm not done with it yet, but I'm having fun just exploring and I've already spent close to 200 hours). Yes, it's hard at first -- it's meant to be that way, like the other Piranha Bytes games.

So, it's a definite YES for me  It's worth full price if you ask me, but as I said, if you're unsure, get it on sale. In [b][i]my opinion[/i][/b] it's worth it.

ELEX is a game of many flaws, but the game excels at some aspects which more than makes up for the deficiencies.

[h1]Lore and Open World[/h1]
In my opinion, the strongest aspect of ELEX is the world design and setting.  The game world is a post-apocalyptic world, where a modern-ish human civilization was wiped out by a Comet impact.  Besides destruction, the Comet also introduces the resource "ELEX" to the world, which is slowly integrated into the survivors.  This results in technological leaps in robotics and weaponry; the discovery of ELEX-powered magic; and mind altering stimulants.  You end up with a mish-mash of multiple settings; Sci-fi, Fantasy, and Fallout-like; interleaved in a sensible and believable manner.

The world itself, including the land and the people, is split into areas that correspond with each of these settings:
[list]
  [*] The Sci-fi faction calls itself the Clerics.  They have hold a single metallic-looking city situated near the Comet impact site, which has transformed into a volcanic crater.
  [*] The magical faction is called the Berserkers.  They hold lush (mutated) greenery and forests, and live in primitive wooden houses.
  [*] The Fallout-like faction is called the Outlaws, and they live in a desert, with shelters built out of salvaged sheet metal.
  [*] Finally, the antagonists of the story, called the Albs, live in frozen wastelands in the north.
[/list]
As an open world game, the explorable landmass is not terribly large, but the entire map appears to be hand-crafted.  As you wander (or more likely, run wildly from city to city, avoiding monsters), you'll find ruins of the pre-Comet world that help build up a rough history of the world.  Not everything is relevant of course.  In the ruins, you may find hints of pre-Comet panic to reach shelters... or the skeletons of people gathered around a table to play a board game.

[h1]Questing and Roleplay[/h1]
Another strong aspect of ELEX is the roleplaying.  The character you play (no customization) is relatively nondescript, but this personality is explained in the story (and conveniently allows the player to project themselves into the game).  At the very start of the story, the protagonist Jax is betrayed by his own kind, the Albs, and left for dead.  The Albs are technologically-advanced survivors that have taken up consuming "ELEX" directly, as it appears to grant them strength, endurance, and focus in exchange for their emotions (and skin pigments).  Jax somehow survives, but finds himself drained of ELEX, weakened and bewildered by newfound emotions.

Instead of exploring morality in a generic good-vs-evil conflict, ELEX is more focused on survival while dealing with the dissonance of emotion vs logic.  In the beginning of the game, your character feels weak and is objectively so.  The weakest of hostile animals can make short work of the protagonist and you have little recourse to become stronger.  Mechanically, dying to a rat or mutated chicken might not be "fun", but it makes sense and forces you to struggle to survive.  Before you recover from near death, fleeing from battle is advisable.  

[h1]Combat[/h1]
This brings me to one of the weakest aspects of the game: combat.  Ignoring the difficulty, the combat system is rather basic.  For melee combat, you have the choice of one-handed or two-handed weapons.  You may use a shield with one-handed weapons.  There are no special moves for either, just generic swings and optional heavy attacks.  Controls in melee are unresponsive and your character can become stun locked from any hits.  Due to that, it is inadvisable to fight in close quarters unless there is only a single enemy.

For ranged combat, you have the choice of guns, crossbows, bows, grenades, and rocket launchers.  Each class of ranged weapon has three different firing modes, but all except one have the accuracy of Star Wars drones.  For some reason, bows have the longest effective range; and they are the only weapon with a homing missile option.  This turns out to be very important, as the game does not easily let you manually compensate for enemy movement (i.e. aim ahead of the enemy).  In ranged combat, if the aim cursor is red, and the target is stationary (or moving towards you in a straight line), then your shot will hit.  Otherwise, it will miss.

Besides this awkwardness, you may also recruit a single follower to assist you in combat.  The follower will be unkillable, but can be "stunned" if he/she/it takes too much damage.  For the most part, followers make the combat easier, but the follower combat glitching may be distracting and immersion breaking.

[h1]Overall[/h1]
Because I found the combat unenjoyable, I mostly avoided it for the majority of the early game.  When I needed enemies out of the way, I would lure groups of monsters into each other, or into bandits (or into towns :D).  Watching bandits get smashed by a troll, or Alb soldiers get murdered by swamp spiders turned out to be fun in its own way.

Instead of fighting, it was more interesting to talk to NPCs, learn about the world, and explore freely.  The game is fully voiced (including the main character) and probably has hours of pure dialog.  I would highly recommend ELEX based on the strength of its setting and lore.

So I purchased this game after watching it and reading reviews for about a year. The most common complaint about this game is that it is hard in the beginning, I did not find this to be true. The bland combat system was only made difficult by the fact that even though I am using a controller all of the controls are given in keyboard and mouse format for the first  hour that I played. As annoying as that was I still found the combat fairly easy and it actually had no bearing on my choice to refund the game. What fueled that choice was the fact that I felt lied to by the screen shots and videos. When I purchased this game I thought that I was buying into a beautiful and immersive RPG experience and I was wrong. As soon as the first game scene started I realized I had made a mistake. The graphics in the cutscenes are just slightly more polished than the gameplay and the gameplay graphics are not all that much better than GOTHIC. If it was just the graphics, I could still probably drag myself through the game to finish out the story. 

Then came the voice acting. Monotone and bored, it sounded like they were reading the script for the first time. Only 2 hours in and I had to quit, and that is a shame because I was pretty excited about this game. It's not that it is a bad game, in fact it's very reminiscent of GOTHIC which I loved as a kid, but I just can't get immersed in it with the graphics that are nowhere near as pretty as the pictures and the poor voice acting on top of that.

Sorry das Spiel ist scheiße.
Ich hab ihm wirklich mehrmals die Chance gegeben, mich zu begeistern, aber die Begeisterung stellt sich nicht ein. Es kotzt einen einfach an.

1. Die Welt ist scheiße. Unnatürlich Anordnung von Bergen. Bäumen, Pflanzen, Kreaturen und Gebäuden. Es fühlt sich an, also laufe man durch eine willkürlich angeordnete Comicwelt.

2. Die Kämpfe sind nicht gebalancet. Die Steuerung ist scheiße. Mag sein, dass das im späterne Spielverlauf besser wird. Aber man ist einfach nicht in der Lage durch die "tolle" Welt zu laufen und die "Postapokalypse" zu erkunden. Weil dir just ein Gegner, eigentlich nur Gegner begegnen, die dir maßlos überlegen sind. Sogar die verkackten Hühner hauen einen Weg, wenn man sich ihnen allein stellt. Klar kann ich mit dem Jetpack ausweichen, klar kann ich mir auf einen Felsvorsprung setzen, wo der Gegner nicht hinkommt. Aber als dauer Gameplay....bullshit. Du kannst tatsächlich nur mit deinen Gefährten durch die Welt reisen. Die Gegner hauen bis deine Ausdauer weg is, mit dem Jetpack wegfliegen (Ausdauer aufladen) und hoffen, dass dein Gefährte ausreichend Schaden macht, was auch nicht immer der Fall ist. Es ist eine Freude 30 Minuten auf eine Echse einzuprügeln, fast alle Heiltränke zu trinken (die schweineteuer sind) und dann 20m zu laufen und wieder einem übermächtigen Gegner zu begegnen.  

3. Die Story ist die Ausgeburt aller Lamehaftigkeit.....gäääähn. Supergeile Mega-Held fällt den Abhang runter und ist plötzlich die größte Pussy ever, die sich hochleveln muss.....bullshit.

4. Die Dialoge hat irgend eine Pfeife gescripted. Absoluter nonsene und belangloses Geschwätz. Episch geil, wenn ich ausversehen in einen Dialog gehe, während ein Kampf losgeht. Mein Gefährte fechtet die Schlacht seines Lebens und ich muss mir gleichzeitig (gefangen im Dialog) anhören, dass irgend ein weinerlicher Lappen sein Bogen 100m entfernt hat liegen lassen und Angst hat, dass sein Meister sauer auf ihn ist (woraus ein Quest folgt, bei dem du auf Gegner triffst, die dich nur mit ihren Blicken kaputthauen)....sorry, da fehlt mir das Verständnis für. 

5. Du kannst nicht mal groß Zeug suchen und verticken. Blumen sammeln...toll. Da haust du mit allen Tricks einen top bewaffnenten Banditen um...was allein schon ein episches Wunder ist, und dann lässt er nicht mal seine Kanrre fallen.....Bullshit.

6. Der Jetpack ist eine nette Sache, in Quest aber eine riesen Einladung zu bescheißen. Da soll man bloß nicht auf den abgesperrten Müllplatz gehen.Man sollte verhandeln, oder schleichen. Skill verwenden. Die Wache ist auch ziemlich böse. Das Problem löst man mit dem Jetpack. Einfach über die Mauer fliegen, die Wache rafft nicht, dass man gerade an ihr vorbeigeflogen ist....super realistisch.

O jogo é bom, mas não chega a ser um épico...

Vou analisar os pontos que fazem um bom RPG: história, gameplay, liberdade de escolhas e construção do personagem.

História 7/10: A história é um pouco fora do convencional, as subplots são aceitáveis, mas não chegam a prender a atenção nem ser memoráveis. As quests do final do jogo prendem um pouco mais a atenção e o jogo se desenrola bem. O Boss final é pouco expressivo, e chega a ser fácil dado o nível de poder que você fica no final do jogo. Se no começo você foge até das moscas no final fica bem poderoso.

Gameplay 7/10: Como eu disse, no começo você é bem fraco, mas investindo para usar as armas adequadamente fica bem forte, o jogo não chega a ficar trivial, se não ficar experto mesmo no final do jogo os inimigos te matam, portanto o combate é desafiador mas não chega a ser fluido como um dark souls da vida. O mecanismo de Jet Pack é até interessante, mas acho que tira a imersão do jogo de andar no mundo, encontrar caminhos etc...

Escolhas 7/10: Achei que as escolhas do jogo tinham mais impacto, basicamente o jogo tem dois finais e depende do tanto de frieza ou emoção do personagem principal, é isso você vai modificando nas escolhas do jogo...ou seja ou você joga do mal ou do bem. Por ser tão limitado o sistema e as consequências serem tão poucas não acho que seja tão bom como o sistema do Fallout New Vegas, que as coisas que você faz tem resultado imediato, mas só pelo fato de ter um sistema de escolhas já faz desse RPG um bom jogo, digno de pelo menos dois Gameplays (três se você quiser jogar com todas as facções).

Construção de personagens 5/10:
Pra mim RPG bom teria que ter construção do rosto, escolha do sexo, formato do corpo...é isso não temos aqui. Além disso Jax o personagem principal parece um robô, pouco expressivo, sem nenhum atributo marcante, oque o torna um personagem principal fraco (ao contrário de the Witcher por exemplo). Apenas dois personagens são marcantes, a seguidora nasty e o seguidor Arx, são bem únicos e bem construídos, outro bom seguidor é o Falk, sempre comentando informações do mundo de elex por onde se passa. Parece que o jogo foi entregue rápido, e depois que você completa algumas missões com os seguidores eles deixam de ter importância na trama, são mal aproveitados.
As builds são basicamente as mesmas, o personagem usa arma de longo alcance, curto alcance e tem algumas magiazinhas, sendo que as magias dos clérigos são as mais poderosas, eu diria que torna o jogo trivial. Alias as magias são bem mal caracterizadas nesse jogo, como gosto de jogar de mago, não existe magia que seja como as de um Elder Scrolls 3 por exemplo...tudo muito parecido, as magias são como atirar com uma arma comum, os berserkers podem invocar um lobo, ou ativar áureas, mas tudo isso tem custo de mana e você tem que esperar recarregar pra usar denovo, coisa que detesto.

Resumindo 7/10: dou nota 07 para o jogo, ele é suportável, mas os elementos de RPG são medianos, como vivemos uma era de muita ganancia na indústria dos games, um jogo que tem sistema de escolhas, consequências e algum grau de construção de personagens já é algo fora do padrão. Só não espere nada memorável a longo prazo.

The game performs well in the realm of storytelling and faction advancement, but lacks consistency in every other category. Enemies are overpowered the whole game, and you are never really fully equipped to fight unless you spend hours scavenging for resources to craft a few healing potions "if you have the materials that is". 

The AI is very simple in how you are attacked, some attacks can be easily dodged, while others can essentially one shot you. 

There are only a handful of "good" ranged weapons and every other one pretty much will expend all your ammo only to take down 1 or 2 mobs before having to go back to melee attacks. Speaking of melee, you will constantly run out of stamina after taking a few swings, but you need to not take that last swing because you will need to dodge, I'm still confused on why the stamina pool is shared across all actions it's almost punishing the way it is designed.

The Berserker and Cleric factions have abilities that allow you to cast spell/psy powers in combat, these are very helpful and almost required in order to complete the game in any meaningful amount of time.

The game doesn't need multiple playthroughs as you can pretty much tell from one ending how things would be different if you were to chose any other faction. You basically pick a side, one of the other sides will forever hate you and will ultimately attack you at the end of the game. There are some side factions that supply very little to the narrative, so don't feel bad about them if you end up killing them.

All in all I cannot recommend the title in its current form, it is nearly impossible to beat without using cheats or spending more time that it's worth to beat the game legitimately. And if you do cheat, it doesn't really take away from the experience since the experience in itself is completely broken.

TL;DR - Pretty, but Faction choice is a lie, and the Voice director needed to be fired.

I loved the previews for Elex.  The in-game trailers were great to look at, the concept of a world combing tech, magic, etc was interesting, and the variety of abilities, gear, and weapons looked like it would provide some nice replay value for trying different paths.

Two things stacked up heavily to make me not recommend this game:

1) I have to admit, this may have been bad interpretation on my part, but the advertising on this game made me think you had free choice between the three main factions:  Berserkers, Outlaws, and Clerics.  And from there you would progress the main story with side stories matching the faction you chose (once again, replay value).  That's not the case at all.  You are forced into siding with the Berserkers because the Outlaws and Clerics are in drastically higher level zones.  In order to join them, you have to avoid the main story and actually progressing anything productive in the game to do enough side missions or just farming just to be able to survive long enough to reach one of those other factions.  Definitely not the "Pick your Faction" style theme that has been present in every other game in history that has used it.

2) The Voice Acting is AWFUL.  Not early Resident Evil levels of awful, but for a game of this level from this studio, at this time in gaming, it is inexcusable.  The main character will give vastly different deliveries in a single bit of monologue from sentence to sentence.  The most apparent example of this is during the tutorial zone where you come across a wrecked drone.  It's like they recorded the separate sentences on completely different days and the Voice Actor completely forgot his tone, motivation, and what was going on in the story, and the director did nothing to correct him.  It wrecked the immersion less than 5 minutes into actual gameplay.  There are even some moments where you select a dialogue option, and the person responding's voice completely changes.  Like they forgot they needed that one extra to say that line so they grabbed the line from another character entirely and hoped we wouldn't notice.

This game is not typical in that your character in the begining pretty much can't fight anything,  it takes a good deal of time doing quests, and running away from monsters before you can. That's turned some people off, but if you go into it knowing that, and prepared for it you wll likely enjoy the game too. Another thing to watch out for is even when you can take on weaker creatures stronger one are mixed in the same area, those strong one's can easily one  shot you. There are no low level areas, just lower level mobs and high level one mixed together. You can kill a high level mob early if your willing to die a lot,  save and reload until you learn the fight down. Under those conditions I could Kill trolls at level 7,  when I made a single mistake I'd die. I looked at it like a Dark Souls game where dying was part of the learning process how to beat a tough mob. The only problem with that was when I became higher level all the mobs were way too easy.

The one thing I wished I understood better was how little drinking Elex pots raised my cold level. I barley drank any until the final mission afriad my cold level would get too high however, near the end I needed to raise my cold level for a netrual ending. I wound up needing to drink around 200 Elex pots to get my cold level where I wanted. Had I know they effected my cold level so little I would have drank many more  early game when I could have realy used the attribute and skill points. I was already OP at that point in the game so it was an anoyance.

Elex is an extremely solid RPG.... If you give it the chance. Combat is not the strongsuit of Elex but it never has been for any of PB's games. The world building, dialogue, and interactions within quests are stellar and are what makes Elex a solid title in my opinion. Overall I recommend this game once it goes on sale. Give it around 10 hours and decide what you think of the game. The beginning could have been better but it does make sense as to why it's so hard in the beginning because your character is stripped of his powers and given nothing but crappy clothes and an even crappier weapon. The RPG aspects are what make this game great. Not the action aspects. I thoroughly enjoy playing Elex and hope you find the same enjoyment out of it as I do.

Edit: Also the game has gotten much better since release and many of the bugs and issues have been addressed.

Błedy tak strukturalne że nawet amator zrobiłby to lepiej...   przykład: trafiamy do wiochy berserkerów (kto wymyslił tę nazwę ??) w której zakazany jest jakikolwiek nowoczesny sprzet (pod karą wygnania/śmierci) po czym cały czas latamy za pomocą jetpacka (razem z towarzyszem berserkerem!!!) i uzywamy mapy z czegoś w rodzaju pip boya a berserkerzy - zobligowani swym prawem do karania nawet śmiercią odszczepienców uzywających techniki ograniczają sie do 'nie powinienes tak robić'...     a że mapę w tym badziewiu musisz ogladać czesto żeby sie w tych dziurach i dołach połapać (szczególnie  w rozrzuconej bez ładu i składu wiosce berserkerów) wiec non stop słyszysz narzekania, ostrzeżenia i pogrózki - które zresztą zlewasz sikiem prostym bo nie mają absolutnie żadnych konsekwencji (poza wkur...zaniem słuchającego tej kakofonii gracza)...  debil by nie wymyslił tego głupiej.

Brzydki i nieprzyjazny gameplayowo swiat. Wszędzie jakieś górki i góry przez które nic nie mozna dojrzeć, miszmasz pierdyliarda styli (od 'średniowiecza' po 'kosmos', od raptorów po mechy od łuków po plazmaguny) a wszystko to wpakowane do jednego wora kompletnie beż zadnego sensu i logiki - w tej grze drewniana strzała ma podobną moc co pocisk plazmowy... 
 
Dretwy bohater i jeszcze bardziej dretwi NPC - dialogi są bezsensownie rozwodnione jakimiś kretynskimi szczególami nt. swiata które mozna usłyszeć po kilkanaście razy z róznych ust, często nie mają kompletnie sensu i choc rzadko mi to jakoś wyjątkowo przeszkadza tak tutaj to jakiś kuriozum - dziesiątki linii dialogowych z których nic nie wynika, wybór odpowiedzi to totalna loteria bo nie wiadomo z czym wiązę sie taki a nie inny wybór - jednym słowem żenująca tandetnie to wypada na tle innych produkcji

Toporny i mozolny system levelowania/rozwijania postaci - najpierw znajdz w tym bajzlu trenerów, potem pograj kilkanascie godzin! żeby móc rozwinąć max dwie lub trzy umiejętnosci (bo wczesnije masz za mało expa) - super - pierwsze kilkanascie godzin to symulator paroba bładzącego od jednego niewykonywalnego zadania do drugiego (bo wiekszosc polega na zabiciu czegoś/kogoś wraz zlicznym towarzychem) oraz zbierającego rosliny i wycinającego kitę przed 90% stworzeń na mapie (bo dla byle szmatławca jesteś na 2-3 strzały a kazdy inny załatwia cie na raz...)

Elex ist wieder mal ein typisches Piranha Bytes Game im Stile von Gothic 2 und deswegen auch unheimlich fesselnd und ausgefeilt. Ich verstehe die schlechten Reviews nicht. Kein Spiel hat mich mehr so gefesselt seit langer Zeit. 
Es ist schwer und fordernd, so wie ein RPG es auch sein sollte um einen bei der Stange zu halten und gerade deswegen freut mann sich um so mehr ueber Fortschritte. Ausserdem ist die Welt sehr stimmig und mit viel Tiefe und Liebe zum Detail entworfen. Genauso wie die einzelnen Gemeinschaften und NPCs. Durch all diese Aspekte wird die Elex Welt zu einer RPG-Welt in die mann wieder richtig eintauchen kann. Auch die Charakter und Faehigkeitenentwicklung ist ausfuehrlich und so gehalten, dass mann immer wieder ein kleines Stueckchen besser wird und sich so ueber seine Erfolge sehr freuen kann.
Wer wert auf die Sachen legt die ein gutes Rollenspiel wirklich ausmachen sollte Elex unbedingt spielen. In Zeiten wo fast alle Entwickler nur noch Wert auf Grafik und andere oberflaechliche "Werte" eines Spieles setzen bleibt die Authentizitaet und Stimmigkeit der Geschichte und Welt leider oft auf der Strecke. Nicht so bei Elex!

Как РПГ игра однозначно удалась, захватывающий сюжет, отличные квесты и диалоги. Мораль, выбор и юмор все в наличие. Удачная реализация симуляции жизни НПС и их повседневное поведение, но в тоже время в бою враги совершенно ужасны, как роботы с мгновенной реакцией, сменой оружия, целей и прочими прелестями. Вообще боевка совершенно ужасная, пожалуй худшая на моей памяти. 
Баланс как таковой отсутсвует, столько смертей и загрузок ни в 1 игре у меня не было, хорошо хоть есть быстрая загрузка и работает очень быстро как и сохранение. Стреляющее оружие совершенно одинаковое и лук и бластер ведут себя совершенно идентично, скорость полета снарядов тоже у всех видов оружия похоже одинаковая и ее очень легко оценить на глаз, в этой игре и от стрелы, и от пули, и от лазерного луча вполне можно уклониться. С попаданием тоже имеются проблемы, снаряды частенько пролетают сквозь врагов. 
Не мало проблем доставляет отсутствие элементарного фонарика. В мире где есть ракетные ранцы, роботы и плазменные винтовки, вместо него предлагаются магнивые факелы, от которых толку чуть.
С технической стороны игра недалекой ушла от Fallout New Vegas, текстуры размытые и очень низкого разрешения, в моделях тоже полигонов не хватает, но радует, приличная дальность прорисовки и хорошая частота кадров на максимальных настройках

This game rewards the type of player that likes to do a lot of exploring and adventuring. The enemies do not scale to your lvl or to certain zones, there are strong enemies everywhere that can 1 shot you, so if you keep dying over and over again do not get discouraged! Just simply go around them or run away until you get better gear or lvl up a couple times. With that being said make sure to use liberal use of the quicksaves! You will have to reload saves A LOT because you WILL die a lot. Like everyone else says...there are some things that are janky about this game but if you can play through them you will find a really good and deep RPG.

PROS
-huge map
-lots of loot
-lots of missions and stuff to do
-really cool sci fi/fantasy setting
-rewarding and sense of accomplishment when you complete missions/kill big enemies
-although clunky and janky at times, the combat is actually fairly deep and dark soulsish

CONS
-Reuse of certain character models and building models
-Voice acting/dialogue lines can be downright silly at times
-graphical clipping
-sound effects and music are sometimes off and do not sound right

But IMO the PROS outweigh the CONS in this game. If you play it and AT LEAST get to the first town or shortly after, you will see that this is a gem of an RPG that is fun and nice to play!

Пишу спустя полгода после прохождения, ибо на тот момент я был в восторге полнейшем (проходил сразу на харде).
Лично для меня в игре есть 3 камня которыми хочется кинуть в разработчиков:
  1)Главный квест. Под конец он настолько однообразен, когда вычищаешь одни и те же здания, с однотипной планировкой, и т.д. Будто оттягивают концовку, и банально тратят ваше же время повторение одного и того же раз за разом. 
  2)Открытый мир. Нет, то что он открытый это априори хорошо, но! хоть с первого уровня (условно) можно пробежать куда угодно фактически, между самыми стремными монстрами и бандитами и т.д. можно топить по полной в любую сторону и ты прорвешься, да есть и опасные враги вроде роботов от которых не так легко скрыться (но опять таки реально), но таких мест не много,  благодаря джетпаку это сделать еще проще, прыг на скалу и все (или со скалы). Хотя безусловно не полутать ящики или не собрать квестовые вещи, но все же, интерес исследования новых территорий притупляется, зачем ковырять или расчищать дорогу, когда я могу сквозь нее пробежать (претензия по поводу траты времени по прохождению основного квеста и трата времени на расчистку локаций, это совсем разное), да и опыта с мобов раз-два и обчелся. Да и мобы увы однообразны, их всего несколько видов. Да становятся сильнее, меняется внешний вид немного и тд, но поведение и атаки одни и те же, и независимо от локации ты сможешь пробежать где угодно зная эти модели поведения. Хотя есть места где особо не побегаешь, но такой процент мал.
  3)Заполненность. Ребята в сфере левел дизайна очень толковые, красивые локации, довольно большая куча разных мест, где можно полазить, очень интересные сооружения: гигантские лестницы, заводы, пещеры, заброшенные здания, деревеньки и т.д. все очень грамотно, прям одно удовольствие на 5 с плюсищем. Но мир довольно пуст на события, во всех этих чудеснейших постройках тусуют преимущественно агрессивные мобы, не задрипанных раненых сторожил, ни каких то там беженцев или переселенцев, никого дружелюбного чтобы нам рассказать, что тут было, что есть или что будет, все куда мы прибегаем, везде нам пытаются навалять люлей, и наградой нам будет дай бог какая-нибудь шмотка или отрывок какой-нибудь записки. А ведь все настолько отлично отрисовано и проработано, что хочется бегая по этим локациям (пусть и кишащими мобами) чувствовать не только, что ты просто пробегаешь очередной склад/завод/пристань как локацию наотье.. а как то понимать, что это не нагромождение моделек домов в определенной тематике, а что есть какой то лор, что мир не пуст, что есть интерес пробежать туда или сюда, понимать историю мира чуть лучше, чтобы было желание с каждым новым прохождением открывать какие то новые места, а не тупо проходить за альтернативную фраку, где можно пробежаться тупо по квестам и забить на все остальное, потому что чего то "нового" в этих локациях не найдется увы. 
  Но в общем и целом, игра замечательная, все остальное на хорошем уровне, боевка со своей спецификой, виды оружия и т.д., интересный сюжет, альтернативы в квестах, быт фракций и тд. все присутствует. Пожалуй самым ярко выраженным моментом будет, конечно же совмещение фентезийного, "современного" и футурестичного. И все кажется нелогичным и парадоксальным, тем не менее смотрится весьма гармонично.

Ich bin kein Gothic Spieler, habe diesbezüglich also keinen Vergleich. 
Jedoch hab ich inzwischen sehr viele Spielstunden und muss sagen das ELEX mit abstand das Beste RPG ist das ich anfassen konnte. Es ist herausfordernd, es hat eine intuitiv gestaltete Welt mit vielen einzigartigen Charakteren und das Kampfsystem ist nach einiger Eingewöhnungszeit auch mehr als gut genug. Sowieso ist das Kampfsystem anfangs eher zu vernachlässigen da man sich eher durch Botengänge und andere reine Dialog-Quests auflevelt. So zumindest meine Erfahrung.

Generell hat die gesamte Landschaft und die Stimmung, das Spiel einen gewissen Charm, der sich extrem schwer zu beschreiben lässt. Ich verleugne nichtmal das vieles (Wenn auch nur am Anfang wenn man versucht sich durch zu starke Gegner durchzuschlagen) frustrierend ist, und es stellenweise dann doch wirklich stark fehlplatzierte Grafiken gibt: Als Gesamtpaket bietet ELEX das, was jedes Spiel hergeben sollte: Ein Spiel mit einer Identität, von dem man die Stärken aber auch Schwächen als Spieler mehr miterlebt. 
Wer also ein RPG spielen möchte, das Identität statt Perfektion hat, ist mit ELEX sehr gut beraten!

ELEX to kolejna gra od studia Piranha Bytes, które stworzyło takie tytuły Gothic, czy Risen, które szczerze polecam. Rzeczą, o której warto wspomnieć jest to, że PB stworzyło grę, która gameplayem przypomina swoje poprzednie twory, więc jeżeli grało się w ich poprzednie tytuły i czuło się z tego przyjemność, to gra jest jak najbardziej warta kupienia, jeżeli jednak NIE grało się wcześniej w ich produkcje, to może nie spodobać się niektórym graczom toporność, na początkowym stadium rozgrywki.

Grafika w ELEXie jest jak najbardziej poprawna, nie powinno się oczekiwać jakichś efekciarskich wytryskó, bo jednak Piranha to małe studio i nie może sobie pozwolić na wiele, ale to, co gra nam oferuje jest ładne i przyjemne dla oka. Wygląd świata pod względem klimatu jednak, to kompletnie inna sprawa. Gra łączy w sobie klimaty fantasy, sci-fi oraz post apo, co skutkuje takimi dziwnymi scenariuszami walki kolesia w zbroi płytowej z człowiekiem uzbrojonym w karabin plazmowy. Niektórym może się to nie podobać, mi jednak przypadło to do gustu, chociaż trudno te rzeczy uzasadnić logicznie.

Jeżeli chodzi o fabułę, to historia jest całkiem niezła, zwłaszcza, kiedy zaczyna się rozwijać. Szczerze polecam najpierw zająć się wszystkimi zadaniami pobocznymi, a na koniec zająć się fabułą, bo historia jest głównym daniem gry, według mnie. Bywały momenty, keidy byłem naprawdę wciągnięty w opowieść gry. Niestety zachwycenie historią potrafią czasami odebrać drewniane przerywniki filmowe, które są dosyć średnie i ludzie, którzy robią animacje w SFM tworzą je płynniej i lepiej, ale cutscenek w tej grze nie jest aż tak dużo, więc nie należy się ich za bardzo czepiać.

Walka, czyli chyba najbardziej irytująca mechanika w całej grze. Twórcy zdają się łączyć schematy z Wiedźmina 3 oraz Dark Souls, chociaż nie wychodzi im to za dobrze, przez zniszczone hitboxy oraz niewyraźne sygnalizowanie ataków przez przeciwników. Na początku gry polecam znaleźć sobie porządne wyposarzenie oraz towarzysza, bo walczenie z chociaż odrobinę lepszym przeciwnikiem od początkowego, jest prawdziwą mordęgą i dopiero w środku gry jesteśmy w stanie przyzwyczaić się do walki i daje się radę pokonać trudniejszego przeciwnika. Ta toporność jednak bardzo przyjemną rzecz, której nie widać by było, gdyby nie ten mało sprawiedliwy poziom trudnośći.

Chodzi mi tutaj o system progresu. Przez całą grę mamy za zadanie dołączyć do jednej z trzech frakcji, a następnie zdobywać w nich coraz wyższe stanowiska i nie było by pewnie w tym nic satysfakcjonującego, prócz lepszego wyglądu uzbrojenia, gdyby nie właśnie system walki. Z coraz lepszym ekwipunkiem, którego nie da się tak łatwo zdobyć, walka z adwersażami staje się przyjemniejsza i łatwiejsza, a brak skalowania poziomu przeciwników, pokazuję naszą drogę, przez którą przez całą grę przeszliśmy z poziomu frajera z rurką PCV do elitarnego wojownika z płonącym mieczem.

Kupiłem ELEXa i nie żałuję wydanych pieniędzy, oraz polecam ten tytół również wam. Należy przebaczyć tej grze kilka jej wad, a wtedy otrzymujemy ciekawą historię z ciekawym światem oraz świetnymi elementami RPG. I chociaż mało osób będzie chciało zapłacić za produkt pełną cenę, to zachęcam przynajmniej do kupna gry w promocjach, bo jednak pieniądze przydadzą się studiu Piranha Bytes, które będzie mogło je przeznaczyć na Gothica 4.

В своём обзоре [b]AshKing[/b] восторженно говорил, что мол эта лучшая игра от Пираний, а остальные говорили, это игра средненькая, на [b]6-6.5[/b] из [b]10[/b]. 
По иронии и то и то - правда. 

В игре хороший сюжет и не такой уж плохой сеттнг, Пираньи внезапно смогли более-менее органично запихнуть бластеры, луки и пиломечи в одну вселенную и на одну планету, но хромает постановка и подача, нету нужной музыки, нет правильного кадра или ударения в голосе при переломном моменте.   

Как РПГ Элекс хорош: много квестов с разным выбором, который потом влияет на другие квесты и их решения. Но порой выбора нет вовсе, там, где казалось бы он должен быть по умолчанию.

По традиции три фракции - [b]Клирики[/b] (почему именно "Клирики" неясно, то  ли косяки перевода, то ли ещё что, Клирики в данном случае никого не лечат и даже наоборот), которые слепо и фанатично верят в бога Калаана и при этом нереально развитые учёные, которые каким то образом после катастрофы скакнули в 3к17 год. Вера в бога и наука - вещи несовместимые (учёные устали это повторять), но только не в Элексе.
 [b]Берсерки[/b], которые презирают элекс и технологии, поэтому они берут элекс, слегка его изменяют и продукт на выходе благозвучно называют "маной", лол. Гоняют с топорами и луками как то смогли нагнуть клириков в великой войне.
[b]Изгои[/b], истинные либертарианцы и МэдМаксы из бункера 76, ни во что не верят, вместо магии и элекса наркота. [spoiler]Живут на атомной бомбе.[/spoiler] Такие дела.

Можно брать спутников,[spoiler]что бы всё как в Скайриме и Фоле[/spoiler], которые приятно удивляют и у большинства очень интересные квесты.
 
Нужно привыкнуть к дубовой боёвке, странному построению городов, вникнуть в происходящее - только тогда начинаеш получать удовольствие от игры. И чем больше играешь, тем больше погружаешься.
 Боёка, как по мне, ещё хуже чем в Готане, нпс можно убивать связкой отбежал-сделал сильный удар на любом уровне, было бы терпение. "Реактивный удар" работает через раз.

Странная прокачка - тебе в начале твердят, как плохо есть элекс, как это опасно и вредно, а по факту игра про то, что ты будешь хлестать элексовое питьё как чумачечий, которое повышает холодность (и характеристики), но настолько незначительно, что можно смело закидываться хоть всем элексом Эдана.  

В игре есть крафт, но он практически ненужен: вы не скрафтите колец или амулетов лучше тех, что найёте и так. Апгрейд оружия с помощью камней? Только, может быть, к концу игры, когда насобираете этих маленьких камней 16шт, что бы скрафтить один большой, от которого ещё может и будет какой то толк.

Отельно стоит упомянуть инвентарь и вообще весь интерфейс игры - он ужасен. К примеру, миникарта показывает только точки - врагов, направлени до цели, но не дороги, местность, торговцев, учителей.

Loved this game, 65 hrs to complete main missions, but I'll still do a bit more exploring.
A lot of the other reviews are true though, the first 10-15 hrs are a struggle, I almost quit a couple of times, but after watching some youtube for tips and locations for useful gear and weapons, things improved quickly and the next 50 hrs were a blast.
This game has some beautiful places to explore, some great characters to interact with, some awesome creatures to kill (or get chased by, depending on your level) and was a great adventure with a satisfying story and conclusion.
Yes the controls feel clunky compared to Nioh or Horizon zero dawn, but once you get the hang of them you stop noticing- like skyrim or early fallout games. 
Yes the voice acting for the main character is a bit stiff at first, but that is his character and it does improve as he loosens up and gains emotion (if that is the path you choose).
A lot of the early complaints have been patched out, like stamina use can be switched off completely and difficulty can be turned right down, as of july 2018 I didn't notice a lot of what people had complained about in earlier reviews.

It is an interesting choice that the developer decided to make every enemy a fixed level in the game, the only way to fight them is to improve your gear and strength and skills, which forces you to play as a massively underpowered character for many hours initially. It does make you really appreciate it when you start killing the creatures that have hounded you for so long though, and when you can easily obliterate anything that gets in your way towards the end of the game it is very satisfying indeed. 
If you only get an hour or two to play games at a time, this game is going to be hard to push through the early stage to get to the good stuff though.

Exploration in this game is outstanding, with interesting places to explore all over the map, and plenty of variation and clever building designs that make you really look everywhere, and the loot is actually useful.
Great creature design, characters, story, world, I found this game just as engrossing as skyrim, the witcher series, fallout series etc, it just takes some dedication to get into.
Definitely recommended to serious gamers, maybe a tough sell to casual gamers or newcomers.

For Keyboard/Mouse Layout, here are the basics:
1. Your Dodge key should also be your Jump key.
2. Your Lock-On default should be tab
3. Whether your weapon is sheathed or not, it should not effect your ability to interact with items or objects. What, If I have my rifle out, I can't see/touch that box? Really?
4. I should not have to point my cursor at exactly what I'm specifically going to use to climb. If I'm standing by a wall, looking up at a ledge, the margin of error there on whether or not I want to climb is quite low. Bigger target area.
5. E is Interact. You don't need a separate key for climb, open, Use Item, etc... 1 key. Not super hard.

These are basic ergonomic decisions that many amazing games have employed. It's the basics.

Piranha Byte ist für das etwas eigenwillige Gamedesign bekannt, insbesondere dafür, das es diese ultra-harten Level-Unterschiede hat, die den Protagonisten zufällig in Gebiete bringt die ihn sofort töten, ohne Chance auf...ja..auf irgend etwas. Viele treue Fans sehen dies als Tradition, Wiedererkennung usw. an und bei diesen Fans möchte ich mich schon einmal im Voraus entschuldigen.
Ich halte es für katastrophales Gamedesign und einen unintuitiven Haufen Programmmüll.

Startgebiet, verlasse das Tutorial, treffe den ersten NPC.
Ignoriere ihn weil er mir absolut unsympathisch ist. 
Gehe nach links, erstes Monster, One-Hit, tot.
Neu laden. 
Gehe nach rechts, erstes Monster, One-Hit, tot.
Neu laden.
Gehe geradeaus, erstes Monster, One-Hit, tot.
Neu laden.
Laufe straight durch, nutze Jetpack, sehe viele Menschen. Komme bis auf Spuckreichweite ran, keine feindliche Reaktion, gut, werden Freunde sein. Komme auf Axt-Reichweite ran, sind Banditen, One-Hit, tot.
Neu laden.
Selbes Spiel, ignoriere Menschen, finde neue Waffe, möchte ausrüsten....60 Stärke und 40 Konstitution als Voraussetzung. Ich habe 10 und 10. Laufe weiter, Teleporter, laufe weiter, Monster umgehen. Komme zu einem Konverter, Zwischensequenz mit Alben. Habe zufällig genug XP für den ersten Stufenaufstieg bekommen, irgendeine Meldung poppt auf als die Zwischensequenz vorbei ist (Die sich nicht überspringen lässt), ich kann mich nicht bewegen und werde zerkloppt. 
Neu laden.

Und so ging es halt immer weiter. Mittlerweile bin ich Stufe 10. Bei Quests gibt es die Möglichkeit Fachwissen vorzuweisen, wenn man Punkte in Kampf, Überleben oder Persönlichkeit hat. Um in Persönlichkeit genug Punkte reinzubuttern damit es sich lohnt, muss man aber viel locker auf 40 oder 50 steigern. Tut man dies zu Beginn, hat man keine Chance weil die Attributvoraussetzungen für Waffen so extrem hoch ist. Tut man dies nicht, entgehen einem viele coole Gesprächsoptionen. Aufheben kann man nicht, denn Quests sind fundamental wichtig zum Leveln. Monster töten bringt nichts, bzw. nicht annährend genug für den Aufwand. 
Achja, hat man mal nen menschlichen schweren Gegner besiegt und plündert ihn....gibt es natürlich NICHT seine Ausrüstung. Warum auch? Wäre ja "zu einfach" so an Waffen oder Rüstungen zu kommen. Nein, wer einen menschlichen Gegner tötet bekommt i.d.R. Klopapier, einen kleinen Heiltrank (Für den Kampf hat man dann 20 verbraten), 50 Splitter und ein unbefriedigendes Gefühl, so als wäre deine Freundin mittem beim Blowjob geben, kurz bevor du kommst...eingeschlafen.

Ich fände es nicht einmal schlimm wenn es diese Levelgrenzen gibt, so dass in einigen Gebieten stärke Gegner hausen die man erst später bekämpfen kann. Problem: Spieler weiß es nicht, es wird nirgendwo angezeigt. Tatsächlich kann eine machbare Kreatur keine 20m von einem unmöglichen ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ entfernt sein.
Und wer zur Hölle hat sich eigentlich den Protagonisten ausgedacht?
Ich bin der übelste ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, der Töter, Schlächter oder was weiß ich von sonstetwas....und....ich...bin....gerade einmal verfickt stark genug für ne beschissene Eisenstange? Habt ihr sie noch alle? Lasst mich doch wenigstens ein No-Name sein, unwürdige Spreu die vom Weizen getrennt wurde oder denkt euch den unkreativen Mist mit Gedächnisverlust oder so aus. Aber alles was mir passiert ist, ist das ich auf Entzug von einem Stoff bin, welcher mir magische Kräfte und emotionale Kälte gibt aber nicht meine Intelligenz, Wissen oder Stärke beeinflusst.
Also: Warum?

Das Inventar ist unintuitiver Müll, der Kampf unintuitiver Müll, die alternativen Lösungswege sind kaum vorhanden und wenn dann schlecht umgesetzt. 
An sich wären wenigstens die Quests ziemlich geil, es gibt da richtig gute Ansätze...aber die Umsetzung ist Müll.
Soziale Interaktion? Müll
Begleiter? Müll, mann kan ihnen nichts anständiges Befehlen, angreifen tun sie teilweise nur wenn man Schaden genommen hat, aber wenn man Schaden nimmt ist man oftmals schon tot.

Das Spiel hat KEINE Lernkurve, das Spiel ist KEINE Herausforderung. Eine Herausforderung wäre ein Spiel, wenn es so gvestaltet ist das ein Spieler über logisches nachdenken, Schläue, Geschicklichkeit und Beharrlichkeit weiterkommt.
Das bietet dieses Spiel nicht, bzw. auf die falsche Art und Weise.
Die einzige relevante Beharrlichkeit ist die, wie lange der Spieler bereit ist sich von dem Spiel ficken zu lassen, bis er es entnervt in die nächste Ecke pfeffert (Was ich nicht machen will, da Steam-Version^^).
Das Spiel ist somit keine Herausforderung sondern eine Qual.

Nun bin ich vielleicht leicht masochistisch veranlagt oder so frustriert über das rausgeschmissene Geld und die verhunzte sehr gute Idee und Spielwelt, dass ich das Spiel trotzdem weiterspielen werde. Vielleicht ist das natürlicher Bestandteil der Piranha Byte Fans und treuen Spieler, das sie allesamt masochistische Idioten sind...und ich bin es auch?
Keine Ahnung, aber ich kann dieses Spiel nicht empfehlen, selbst wenn ich mich jetzt aus Prinzip durchquälen werde.
