D'entrée de jeu, je tiens à signaler que ce pouce bleu tient davantage d'une satisfaction subjective que d'une notation véritablement objective d'ELEX, dernier nés des studios Piranha Bytes. 

Le nom du studio est important, notamment pour ceux hésitant à se lancer dans ce RPG : rappelons que Piranha Bytes est père des licences Gothic et Risen. Pour les non connaisseurs, leur système de jeu de rôle se positionne à l'extrême opposée de ce que pourrait programmer Bethesda avec le level scaling, où les ennemis s'adapteront constamment à votre niveau : ici, n'espèrez pas triompher d'un dragon dès les premières heures de jeu : vous vous contenterez de quelques rats puants et bestioles faiblardes avant d'atteindre un premier village. Le système de combat vous propose d'alterner entre des attaques à distance ou au corps à corps, ces dernières se décomposant en attaques normales, puissantes agrémentées d'une éventuelle attaque spéciale. 

N'y allons pas par quatre chemins : le combat dans ELEX est médiocre, voire très médiocre. N'achetez pas ce produit si vous souhaitez retrouver les lices d'un Dark souls, ou le côté épique de certains affrontements dans Skyrim. Sans être complètement raté, certains ajouts comme la dite attaque spéciale sont clairement inutiles. Ajoutez-y à cela un système de caméra bancal ainsi qu'une IA ennemie aux fraises, vous vous retrouverez à faire des roulades sur le toit d'une tente pour échapper à une texture tenace pendant qu'un ennemi déchargera sa 20ème roquette sur un lustre malchanceux. De plus, la hitbox est mal maitrisée : certains coups esquivés d'une arme à deux mains (heureusement assez rares, mais pénibles dans un tel jeu) vous occasionneront quand même des dégâts, alors que l'esquive de l'impact d'une roquette sous vos pantoufles vous lèveront quelques cheveux sur la tête, tout au plus. 

Vous vous sentez quand même confiants dans la maitrise de la roulade en excellent joueur PvP de Dark Souls, et souhaitez tenter l'affrontement d'ennemis plus balèzes que vous? Investissez dans un abonnement dans un donjon sadomasochiste, un fouet, voire les deux car ça équivaudra au même : ELEX, comme dit précédemment, conserve sa difficulté aberrante, notamment lors de votre première dizaine d'heures de jeu. Le moindre coup de patte d'une créature vous enlève tellement de points de vie que votre survie dépendra surtout d'un facteur : la fuite. Non, vous ne serez pas considérés comme "lâches" en vous cachant dans les fourrés pour éviter quelques raptors : Piranha Bytes nous a habitué, depuis le temps, à cette difficulté hallucinante, voire douloureuse. De plus, il s'y ajoute l'ultime frustration de voir que les combats sont très durement récompensés : vous n'obtiendrez que quelques pauvres points d'expérience alors que vous venez de terrasser une atrocité de la nature, et les loots après triomphe contre certains mobs spéciaux vous feront parfois frôler la crise de nerfs (après avoir terrassé un bandit affreusement dangereux, non seulement je ne pouvais pas récupérer son arme lourde, mais j'ai découvert que son coffre fort contenait une ... barre céréalée. Comme quoi, même les méchants dans ELEX ont droit à leur instant Nutella ...). 

Pour gagner cette expérience tant convoitée, ELEX vous dirige droit dans le système de quêtes du jeu. Là encore attention, même une quête récupérée dans le premier village peut vous envoyer droit vers un ennemi impossible à déloger (cela me rappelle la fois où un idiot m'a demandé de chercher le gourdin qu'il avait perdu ... sous les pieds d'un mecha armé comme un Star Destroyer, bref). Néanmoins, l'expérience s'avèrera être au rendez-vous, et vous monterez vite vos premiers niveaux. Au système classique de montée de vos aptitudes (force, dextérité, intelligence, etc.), vous devrez également choisir entre différentes aptitudes pouvant relever des domaines du combat, de la ruse ou encore de la survie. L'équipement ramassé dépendra du nombre de points investis dans vos aptitudes. Malheureusement, ELEX vous octroie une nouvelle frustration lorsque vous constaterez le montant très élévé des prérequis pour équiper un équipement décent. A titre de comparaison, j'ai pu seulement récemment m'équiper d'une arme relativement efficace en toute circonstance (soit, quand même, au bout de 15h de jeu). 

A ce stade de la lecture, vous devez vous demander (et vous aurez raison) pourquoi diable ce fou a-t-il octroyé un pouce bleu à ELEX vu tous ces défauts? Dans un premier temps, si les animations des personnages restent moyennes, les graphismes sont tout de même plutôt jolis, même s'ils n'atteignent pas la beauté d'exploration d'un Witcher 3. Vous passerez néanmoins de beaux moments à parcourir la grande map du jeu, d'autant qu'explorer est souvent récompensé par des objets utiles disséminés dans des endroits insolites. Pourquoi insolites? Puisque l'une des features d'ELEX est de disposer d'un jetpack vous permettant de vous élever dans les airs pour atteindre des endroits classiquement inaccessibles dans les autres jeux du genre. En outre, la construction du décor très verticale permet de bien profiter de cette feature. 

De plus, l'univers d'ELEX peut sembler assez rocambolesque dans un premier temps : ancien commandant de la faction des Albes, votre vaisseau est abattu en cours de mission et vous êtes laissés pour mort par un allié. Vous croiserez alors le chemin de trois factions : les Berserkers honnissant la technologie contrairement aux Clercs, ainsi que les Hors la Loi. Me voilà donc dans un village Madmaxien en plein désert équipéé d'une armure de cuir nordique, de lunettes de soleil derniers cris et portant sur mon dos un fusil énergétique plasma. Devant l'aspect peut être burlesque de cette situation, force est cependant de constater un bel effort des développeurs à appuyer tout au long du jeu la cohérence de cet univers. 

Le verdict actuel? Objectivement, ELEX vous occurera beaucoup de frustrations du fait de sa difficulté parfois insoutenable et de défauts de gameplay ne mettant, notamment, pas la part belle aux combats. Cependant, ELEX reste un RPG plaisant et intéressant à parcourir sous l'unique condition d'accepter ce système de jeu si particulier : vous ne progresserez que TRES lentement avant de pouvoir, ENFIN, sentir le début d'une satisfaction de jeu en commençant à dompter cet univers si hostile. A conseiller uniquement aux joueur(se)s averti(e)s.

There's a screen freezing bug that has been politely ignored by the developer.

Each time I go to troubleshoot it, I find information about tweeking some settings, opening some files with an editor, and doing something really basic, like manually inputting the screen resolution.  The game will work for about an hour, and then the game crashes again.  Also more good news: Your previous saves will be unusable since they use the crash mode settings. 

In addition to the technical problems, Elex also is terrible even when it is working properly.  The combat is horrible, and made up of a bunch of canned animations.  The graphics look like something off the X-Box 360, and there's at least one monster that is a free engine asset.  The voice actors all suck, the animations are a joke, and the AI behavior was programmed beyond the developers competence.

If you are really hurting for a Gothic style RPG and are tempted to buy Elex, I would advise you to gnaw your own arms off instead.

As I played my ~40 hours of ELEX I went through a wide range of emotions. Combat is hard, like...really hard. Painstakingly brutal, especially at the beginning.

Your first 10-20 hours will consist of running away from essentially every hostile NPC. until level 15-20, 90% of mobs will have a skull next to them (also impossible to see from non-aggro range) which signifies that they will 1-3 shot you, and you will need a few hundred hits to kill. Most required combat for quests consisted of me either running the quest mobs into guard NPC's or jet-packing on top of a building and letting my companion (who will respawn non-stop 90% of the time) slowly whittle it down for 5-15 minutes.

You'll notice here that Melee seems heavily underpowered compared to ranged, mainly because fighting more than one mob will essentially result in your death. It gets bearable as you progress for certain fights (provided you learn how to time your blows and block 99% of the time) but the real power exists in joining a faction. 

Around level 15-20, you'll have done enough quests that you can join a faction. Once you gain some faction abilities the game will start to feel "almost" playable(it only took you 20 hours to get here!). You'll have one or two weapons/abilities that do the large majority of your damage, and running out of ammo/energy/mana for them mid-combat will probably result in death.

At this stage, your actions will start to have far-reaching consequences, and people will have no problem making sure you know it. Expect to get regularly attacked for being a d*ck and for your companions to not have constant "Theme" you can stick to to keep gaining favor with them. 

At level 25-30+ You'll probably be nearing endgame, and it started to become less "fun" for me because my entire survival consisted of my black hole thrower that is tremendously overpowered and keeping my psi(mana) bar full enough to keep using it. It still doesn't take much for mobs to kill you even with top-tier armor from your faction, full armor skills, full health skills, ect. so most of your time is still spent jetpacking out of melee range while shooting mobs that (hopefully) don't have ranged attacks.

Overall though, this game is what you want it to be. Graphics/voice work are pretty nice, I like it because it was traumatizingly hard and the storyline/side quests were decently entertaining. With sidequests you could probably run through ~80/90 hours in a single playthrough, and more if you wanted to join other factions. As much as I liked playing the game one time through, I really couldn't imagine re-rolling two more times to join the other factions/choose different outcomes because of the mind-numbingly difficult intro for 10+ hours of trying to run away from everything and dying alot. Don't come into it thinking it will be like Skyrim/The Witcher and you won't be let down, providing the game doesn't force you to punch a hole in your monitor first.

As someone who played all Gothic games and the Risen titles (except for part 2) I was already familiar with the gameplay. Everyone who played any of those will feel at home in Elex. IMO Elex is the one most refined and the one which combinates the best of all its predecessors. The gameworld is huge and seamless and downright amazing. It looks beautiful and has different biomes (forest, desert, snow...) and I had a blast exploring it. Factions differ a lot and each hold unique quests for you if you join them. 

The game is very challenging in the beginning since EVERYTHING will kick your *** but it adds greatly to the feel of surviving in a harsh world and. You can also use this to your advantage and lure enemies into one another. Later in the game you will get much stronger and will be able to explore everything without having to fear every sound you hear that might come from a beast. 

The only thing that bums the fun a bit is the combat system. Apart from feeling clunky it gets very chaotic in group fights and encourages looking for cheap tactics and exploiting AI behaviour. It is fine for duels though, once you get used to it.

Overall a definite recommondation if you don't mind getting your *** kicked at the start.

I'm sorry, I really wanted to like this game but after 19 hours of gameplay I realised it's just not happening. The world is nicely rendered and the story is OK. The character you play with is rather dull but that wouldn't be a deal breaker for me. What totally ruined it for me was the very slow character development and progression combined with the fact that you really can't do battle with most of the creatures in the world (probably until you develop your fighting skills). But to do so, you need to do quests which are tiresome and you'll need to avoid lots of enemies on your way just to not get killed.

The quests themselves are not that interesting and fighting gives very little XP (beating a troll took about half an hour and rewarded 200 XP :-) - I probably should've beaten him later as I developed my character, but I just wanted some action and got tired of running away from any battle). After almost 20 hours of gameplay I felt that I'd not developed my character enough to feel any progress and that the hours put into this game would have been better spent doing something else.

I guess that if you're into a game that gives you lots of dialogue choices that affect the quests and story it's fine. If on the other hand you don't want an interactive storybook but an action RPG game then ELEX disappoints .. a lot.

“两大”游戏论坛就很好笑了，只知道游侠和3大妈并且在里面下载盗版很得意吗，老核心a9vg逛过吗
您要说这个画面好的话，建议先搞清楚什么是dx9时代的技术和dx11时代的技术；以及既然逛论坛不妨多看看其他大作最高特效截图。（看您只知道说“分辨率”三个字，我猜你想说的是“画面不只是看画面技术”）我理解了，你所说的画面好也许是美工或者场景设计。不好意思，我没耐心看到后面的美工，因为一开场的人物建模精度毁三观，地表贴图连凹凸贴图都没有，整个画面全局近乎于没有的环境光遮蔽，以及那可怜的不知道什么样的抗锯齿；看到这条评论的朋友可以点开楼下那位他发的链接，里面有他自己截的图，可以说真实性比steam商店页面里面那几个PS出来的好不少；我开最高特效基本就是那个样。
我当然知道，谈画面的时候不能只谈及技术，还要考虑到美术风格，整体的色彩协调性，等等。。。但是当你的画面技术不足以支撑起你的这些艺术设计的时候，就会起到反效果。老滚5发售以来，打完各种mod以后的画面，收到一致好评，但是放到今天那个画面就是不合格的画面，因为他引擎使用dx9，很明显的能看出来充满贴图感的假。这个游戏也是一样的问题。
作为一个小众游戏，本来玩家们是可以很宽容的，只要他有出彩的地方，就足以收到我们的好评。我想这游戏出彩的地方一定有，比如您评测里提及的任务设置，支线剧情；但是您看，不是我一个人，相当多第一次知道这个工作室的玩家在这个游戏下面打出了差评，给好评的大多数都是玩过工作室前系列作品的，您有没有想过为什么？
而且给差评的理由惊人的一致，大部分就是喷画面或者手感；说明这个游戏的画面和手感，我不说那么难听吧，就说距离同时代游戏差距相当大，这个绝对是事实。而为什么我们只试玩了开头几分钟的画面和手感就下了结论并且果断差评？您可以说我过于急躁，那总不至于那么多玩家都急躁都傻逼都不懂得慢慢挖掘吧？其实很简单，就是因为我们对这个游戏有期待，而且也有画面和手感上的期待，结果进了游戏却发现完全不是想象的那么回事。期待谁给的？就是你们这些粉丝无脑的吹。试想一下，如果你们粉丝一开始就客观公正的告诉我们这些路人，这个游戏画面和手感差，但是新接触的朋友不要急，后面会很精彩。。。。我想会有很多人留下来多尝试一会儿然后改一个好评。像你这样，上来素质三连“这游戏画面比GTA5好，操作差个鬼，你不会玩”你觉得有益吗？作为一个粉丝是不合格的，只会让我们这些路人更讨厌这个游戏。
我也在很多好评下面点赞了，他们说的就比较客观公正。但是你这样的无脑吹态度的粉丝每多吹一句不切实际的，就会毁了这个工作室以及那些正常粉丝的一百倍的努力。

The graphics are very good, nothing groundbreaking but the game certain is visually pleasing to look at. The scenery is beautiful and you can tell that the team meticulously put a lot of time into detail. I remember being in Goliat and seeing some ballistas next to an overlook that Im pretty sure are just there for artistic effect, but it looks like an actual defense point, with large bolts mounted next to the ballistas. I was pleased with all the detail in Goliat and look forward to finding more cities and exploring their beauty.

Now the gameplay isn't as great. It feels very slow and at some times clunky. I often find myself encountering mobs that 1 hit me on normal difficulty when Im going to do the starter quests from Goliat. Frustrating, but something thatwill air out as I gain levels and better equipment I'm sure. 

Finding things is kind of hard, especially in a city as large as Goliat. There are no signs that point you to where a certain vendor might be(to my knowledge), and you can easily get lost looking for these people in the city. Finding quests is also a bit difficult, as the game doesn't seem to have any desire pointing you in the direction of anything that isn't a major quest line. There isn't really any UI tips for a person who might have a side quest for you so you have to find these things on your own.

The story is good, your actions have real consequences and feel important. 

Kind of a sidenote but the voice acting for the main character feels a bit flat thus far. He has a low grizzly voice but it comes across as lacking presence or involvement in what was going on. It was for the most part the same monotone level throughout, and was quite frustrating at times.

In short this game was one of high ambition and even higher potential, let down by either a lack of funding, QA, or time; hell probably all 3.  It has creative characters, an immersive world, well done attribute and skill system, and a good core combat system.  I tried really hard to like this game, looked over so many little issues because of how god damned good it COULD have been.

There are a whole host of issues I have found.  The combat is awkward, the stamina bar decays and generates quickly, but the delay means that its a lot of move in/back out. meanwhile enemies hit you quite hard, so you spend a LOT of time running away to drink potions.
The stat system works well, though the requirements to use any of the gear or pick up any skills means you spend WAY too long running around with the starting axe and bow, which are largely ineffective.

The turning point was when i spent 6 hours trying to join one particular faction, and could not figure out how.  Turned out i had to offer the guard a bribe, which he would reject, but then let me in anyway.  Once I was in I was tasked with bringing down a drug dealer.  This random dealer 3 shotted me, yet could take 30 hits from me without flinching, no matter where the difficulty was.  Additionally my companion would not attack him under any circumstances, nor would the host of guards that were around. 
The only other option was to agree to work with him, and frame someone else.  When i took this option and returned to the quest giver, it never gave me the option to betray the dealer.  It was either become a drug dealer, or die.

Пираньи сделали смелый шаг, объеденить магию и технологии. Получилось ли уних это? Каждый решит для себя сам но если взглянуть в целом то все весьма неплоха. Хардкорная боевка, интересные квесты, не такие уж и нудные диалоги. Фракции представленны достаточно интересно и сами по себе уникальны. Немного нехватает игре того шарма что был у Готики или Готики 2 (с длс) но игра определенно достойна внимания.

Сюжет: Закручен вокруг предательства, противостояния фракций и странной субстанции под названием "элекс" Сказать чтоб он сильно чем то удивлял нельзя, однако для бывалых игроков сейчас любой сюжет любой из вышедших рпг не кажется чемто космическим и шедевральным. Но куда более важно не то какой сюжет а как он приподноситься. Лично для меня он гдето на 8 из 10. 

Боевая система:  Сложная, особенно против некоторых врагов с кучей пушек для дальнего боя. Но и в ближнем бою не легче. Враги не самые умные и как и в готике против всех их можно легко найти лазейки и с легкостью с ними раправляться. Однако даже с учетом лазеек играть отнюдь не проста. 
Слегка хромают увороты и уклонения. Их можно было бы сделать лучше и удобнее, потому все зачастую сводиться к блоку или дальнему бою.

Мир: Красивый. Очень красивый! Пираньи имея небольшой штат работников смогли сделать невероятно красивый мир. Жаркая пустыния с изгоями, разаренные и вызженные земли клериков, густые леса и болота берсерков. Все сделано потрясающе. Весьма отмосферно выгледят заброшенные постройки, разбитые автомобили и заправки, все что могло бы напоминать о том какой был мир игры до калапса выглядит соответствующи. В некоторых местах даже необходимо носить защитную маску и пользоваться антидотами что бы не умереть от радиации или газа. Для любителей атмосферности в руиных старого мира можо найти аудио записи с рассказами событий до котострофы, старые радио передачи, доклады солдат, последние мысли людей. Море фана.

Главные Антогонисты: Конечно это не жнеци из масс эффекта или какой нибудь злодей из серии TES однако они посвоему уникальны со своей историей и своими тараканами в голове.

Чего нехватает: Чуть больше жизни в игру было бы неплоха добавить. Путников на дорогах почти нет (совсем нет, только бродячие торговци), люди сидят в лагерях или за стенами городов не вылазия за их приделы, самые сильные враги зачастую оказываются почти не убиваемые а на высоких уровнях слишком легко контряться или их слишком проста бывает завести в тупик когда они не могут сделать почти ничего главному герою (например убивать их с высоты не получая урона) это тоже нужно исправить. Сложность прокачки - шмот в начале игры требует слишком много очков характеристик и почти пол игры ты бегаешь в ужасно убогом шмоте. Здесь требуется некий... баланс статов персонажа и статов необходимых на оружии. Однако есть несколько стволов которые на вполне раннем уровне характеристик уже можно считать имбалансным для сражения с мобоами.

Это не готика! - Игра сделана тойже студией что и легендарная серия готика, но это не готика. Это даже не ее продолжение. Совсем новый проэкт лишь немного напоминающий по механики игры той серии=) например Ризен или Готику. Не стоит сравниавать эту игру с ними. Разве что в некоторых элементах геймплея. Относиться к ней как к игре с похожими механиками но совсем новой. Будет куда правельнее. 
Пираньи сделали отличную игру. Неординарное сочитание магии и технологий хоть и кажутся дикостью но в мире игры они достаточно сбалансированны и не одна не сельнее другой.

Ich hab Gothic 1 bis 3 und Risen durchgezockt, bei Risen 2 wieder aufgehört, da es einfach nicht meinen Geschmack getroffen hat. Daher flog ELEX auch ein wenig unter meinem Radar, so dass ich es erst vor einigen Tagen gekauft habe. 

Ich hab mir die Beschreibung und die paar Videos angeguckt, und dachte mir, das Game von PB mit neuem Setting kann ich ohne große Erwartungen ausprobieren. Immerhin gefallen mir postapokalyptische Welten, wenn sie nicht komplett aus Wüste bestehen, ganz gut (Metro 2033, Stalker) Zum Anderen haben mich auch die Berserker (WIKINGER IN EINEM SCI FI SETTING WTF?) angelockt, Grund steht in der Klammer. 

Wie auch immer, der Anfang ist getan, den ersten Berserker getroffen und es werden munter Viecher gekloppt... und es stellt sich das typische Gothicgefühl ein:

VOLLES PFUND AUFS MAUL, wenn man nicht aufpasst. Die schwächsten Monster killen einen, wenn man arrogant davon ausgeht, alles zerkloppen zu können. Auch später, wenn die Rüstung dicker ist und das Schwert/Gewehr stärker, können dich Standardmonster ordentlich zerkloppen. Gott, ich liebe es!

Da geht es auch zum ersten "Manko", das Kampfsystem: Es ist an sich eigentlich nicht schlecht, jedoch ab und zu manchmal etwas hakelig, vielleicht liegt es aber auch an meiner Grobmotorigkeit. Des Weiteren kommt erschwerend hinzu, dass Stärke oder Geschicklichkeit nicht mit dem Schaden skaliert, sondern bloß die Vorraussetzung für die Waffe darstellt. Das ist in in PiranhaBytes Games normalerweise nicht so ,ist aber eine willkommene Abwechslung. 
Letztendlich lernt man aber mit den Feinden umzugehen. 

Der zweite Punkt, der für mich wichtig war, ist die Atmosphäre, und auch zu diesem Punkt kann ich sagen, macht Elex es wunderbar! 

Die Dialoge in den Städten sind wundervoll kantig und die Gespräche mit anderen NPC'S stellen sich zudem als interessant heraus. Damit meine ich, dass ich am Ende eines Gespräches durchaus amüsiert, verwirrt oder überrascht/erschrocken war.
 
Das  Gleiche gilt auch für die Quests, die zur Atmosphäre beitragen, die sind nämlich mit Wendungen versehen, die einen den Kinnlade herunterfallen lassen (Arx, WTF?) 

Ach ja, und die Umgebung... Aye! Wunderschön, wie ich finde! Und damit meine ich jedes Areal; Tavar, die Wüste; Edan, das Waldland; Ignadon, das Feuerland und zu guter Letzt Xarcor, das Eisland! Was man dort vorfindet , also Ruinen und Landschaftsgestaltung passt zum Setting. In der Nähe von Häusern und anderen ehemaligen Behausungen der Menschen finden sich Mutanten, im Rest Monster. Es liegen überall alte Sachen und Wracks von Fahrzeugen. 
Zum anderen sich Bunkeranlagen, die zum Teil betretbar sind, vorzufinden. Dort ist es ähnlich wie in Metro 2033 auch eher dunkel :D 

Nachdem ganzen Geplapper fehlt noch die Story... und auch zu der kann ich sagen, dass diese mir gefällt! 
Ein gefallener Commander der Albs wird zum freien Menschen und lenkt die Geschicke gegen oder für diese, denn die Entscheidungen, die man im Laufe des Games trifft, haben Relevanz für das Ende.

Wird man wieder zur Bestie von Xarcor? Oder ist man Menschenliebhaber geworden? Deine Entscheidung! 
Der Eispalast wartet auf dich! 

Zum Ende, wenn ich das mit anderer Popkultur vergleichen darf, sag ich , dass es 'ne schöne Mischung aus Metro 2033, Mass Effect, Mad Max und letztendlich Gothic. 
So hat man mit Albs die logischen und eiskalten Maschinenhybridenverehrer, die in die Länder der freien Menschen einfallen und das Elex wollen (lol, Konverter); mit den Kleriker ähnlich technikgeile Fanatiker, die einen merkwürdigen Glauben führen; die Berserker als technikfeindliche und mächtige Wikinger mit Magie und die egozentrischen Outlaws mit ihren Stims ( Drogen ) und der Gleichgültigkeit für das Schicksal der Menschheit.

Elex, like previous PB games, has a rough start, peppered with plenty of wtf moments, and the two hours before refund are not enough to even get the slightest idea of what the game is about, so i guess reviews could be helpful.

Elex is not a game that will try to please you, or to attract you to play it, or to make you feel good....actually the game feels more like its telling the player to "go away" during the first couple hours. Reminds me strongly of Misery mod.
No gorgeous nekid dames in the intro like Witcher, no spectacular dragon attacks, nope...in Elex you start as an ex commander, now a hobo freshly off drugs that is chased by his former buddies and has to do with only his shaky hands and a "glorious" iron bar as a weapon.

As if this was not enough, there is no conventional start area that is easy, in order to let players accomodate, nope, the start area in Elex is almost just as dangerous as the rest of the world. The only reason to call it a start area, is the fact that you start the game there.

So you follow your presumed savior to the nearest settling and....thats about the only direction you will get. Here you will have to look around, speak to people to get an idea about whats going on, start understanding a bit of the world around you and of course get the mandatory quests.

The quests do have a destination marker, but they dont have a level requirement or any indication that they might be too difficult for your present level....up to you to figure out what you can do and how.

As soon as you get out of the first settlement, all mobs will be able to kill you in a few hits.
See that little insect in the corner? It can SQUASH you! RUN! HIDE!
Ok thats an exageration because once you figure how the combat works, you can easily kill some mobs in one successful combo with the iron bar, others will take a bit more effort, while others will be impossible and must be avoided. 

Leveling up will do nothing for you other than give you 10 attribute points to spend.
Spending the attribute points to increase the different attributes like str dex, int, will do nothing for you other than allow you to learn certain skills and use better weapons.
Weapons and skills dont have level requirements, they have attribute requirements.

Figuring out what you can fight and how to fight and what to avoid and how to get around certain hurdles, was a lot of fun for me, but its easy to see how many players will get very frustrated by the harsh starting difficulty.

There are things to figure out, and your life will be very hard until you do.
Like for example the extreme importance of better weapons (player skillz alone wont get you very far without good weps). 
You dont have to buy any equipment, exploring will get you all you need and more.

One of the most unusual features of this game, comes in the form of elex potions, and abusing them can make the game become too easy too soon.

Elex is one of the games with the most powerful ranged combat ive seen. Some say its overpowered, maybe so, but ammo costs money and money is very important in this game, so everything comes at a price.

The story kept me intrigued and interested (and thats rare for me), and the choice and consequence system was very satisfying.

PB strongest point has always been creating beautiful, realistic and organic feeling environments. In this respect they have no equal and easily wipe the floor with everything else, including the big titles. 
Exploring is really good and worthwhile, again i find it much better than the big titles in this respect, only comparable to Stalker. 

There are quirks: 
-your combos can push the mob into rocks and walls and you cant hit them there, but they can hit you and if they get stuck, the AI will consider it cant reach you and start shooting fireballs in your face. This one is easy to avoid, i always chose the combat area and the angle of my attacks so i dont push the enemies towards stuff they can get stuck into.
-its an open world with various terrain, so some mobs will be higher or lower than you on some slope, and you cant hit them, but again if they get stuck they will start shooting fireballs.... again a quirk that can easily be avoided, just dont start fights on slopes....
-when fighting multiple enemies they have the bad habit of attacking all at once, so taking them on without at least the jetpack skill is gonna turn the combat into a clusterf*ck leading quickly to the reload screen. The good news is that with some effort, care, or simple run around tactics you can "pull" them out and deal with them individually.


Despite the quirks, for me, and apparently for several others, Elex was easily game of the year and even of the decade, it was the most fun ive had in a game since Stalker.
For others it was an irritating pile of jank.

Elex is great, but its definitely not for everyone. 
While Witcher and Skyrim and Fallout were designed to please as many players as possible, Elex was not, and my review was aimed to prevent players wasting their money on something they might hate.

[h1]Elex, ein Rückblick nach 138h und 2 Durchläufen[/h1]

[u]Pro:[/u]
- Weltgröße
- Handlungsvielfalt und Skillung
- Folgehandlungen und Charakterentwicklung
- typische Gothicschwierigkeit :D
- Respawnende Monster
- läuft stabil (auch keine selbstverständlichkeit heutzutage) ^^
- machbare Achievments

[u]Contra:[/u]
- Kampfsystem, vor allem am Anfang
- Falsch spawnende, damit unerreichbare Gegenstände (in Felsen etc.)
- Falsch spawnende, damit unerreichbare Monster (in Felsen etc. ,meißt aber unwichtig)
- Inventar und Menüführung, teilweise UI-Fehler

[b][u]Begründung[/u][/b]

Wer Gothic kennt, weiß was man erwartet, jedoch wie mir scheint hat über dieses Game jedoch nicht einmal ein Betatester drübergeschaut. Also nach 5 Minuten hatte ich 1/4 A4 Seite Verbessungsvorschläge... (Verkaufsversion)

[u]1. Schwierigkeitsgrad und Kampfsystem[/u]

Also das Kampfsystem regt am Anfang einfach nur auf, man muss um überhaupt sichtbar Schaden zu machen einen Komboabschluss machen, allerdings erweist sich dieser mit dem vorhandenen Ausdauerbalken als äußerst schwierig, da man nach bereits nach einem Dodge am anfang nicht mehr genug Ausdauer hat um eine minimal Kombo durchzuziehen.

Damit heißt es, anfangs Gegner versuchen auszumoven mit WASD, Problematisch jedoch bei Hornwölfen die fangen gerne sogar Leute in Ausweichanimationen ab, kurzum ohne Begleiter könnt ihr dieses Game am anfang vergessen, also schnellstmöglich einen angeln.

Eine weitere Sache die mich ganz schön gernervt hat, jeder Gegner bis auf 2-3 Monster oder so können Fernkampfattacken, manchmal noch mit Flächenschaden, die sind teilweise so präzise und schnell ausgeführt, dass sie euch in einem Jetpackansturm noch treffen.

Ansonsten besteht die Hauptschwierigkeit in diesem Game ausschließlich im Kampfsystem, Schadens- und der Charakterentwicklung, entwickelt ihr euch Falsch oder zu spät Kampfbezogen, wegen Chats etc. kann es sein, dass ihr euch das Game selbst schon schwerer macht als es ist.

Mit jeder besseren Waffe wird es leichter, dazu später noch mehr in meiner Tipstüte.

[u]2. Charakterentwicklung und Vielfalt[/u]

Die Charakterentwicklung ist hier das A und O, man merkt dies spätestens mit der ersten besseren Waffe.
Ergo sollte man wie in vielen Gothicgames, viele Anfangslevelups durch Quasselquests in sicheren Gebieten erledigen und Monstern auch wegen etwaigen Bonusexp-Skills oder Tierausschlachten erst einmal umgehen.

Dieses Spiel ist Gothictypisch 0 Einsteigerfreundlich, daher müsst ihr um so mehr schauen wo ihr machbare EXP herbekommt. Die Vielfalt an Taletenten und falschen Tooltips verwirrt massiv.

[u]3. Falsche (eher unvollständige/fehlende) Tooltips[/u]

Wenn ihr mal ins Charakterfenster schaut seht ihr, Stärke erhöht das... , Geschicklichkeit das ... und so weiter.
Jedoch ist dies im übertragenen Sinne gemeint, Stärke erhöht hier nicht wie in Gothic auch direkt den Schaden sondern ermöglicht euch bessere Nahkampftalente zu erlernen und Waffen zu benutzen, wenn man dies beachtet und gezielt auf gewisse Waffen hinskillt ist dieses Spiel eigl. gar nicht so schwer.

Weitere UI Fehler kommen bei einem sehr niedrigen Kältewert nahe 0, normaleweise steht da nix jedoch kann es passieren, dass plötzlich rein emotional da steht und ihr denkt wtf nun 79 Kälte oder was ? Nicht panisch werden einfach kurz gegenprüfen paar Elextränke reinpfeifen oder Spiel neustarten, dann steht expressiv also 1-10 und alles wieder gut.

[u]4. Falsch platzierte bzw. gespawnte Gegenstände und Monster[/u]

Dies fällt zumeißt nur mit entsprechenden Brillen auf, Gegner auf Map sehen oder Gegenstände werden Hervorgehoben.
Solche Fehler sind sehr ärgerlich und wären bei einem Testdurchlauf eines gutes Betatesters auf jedenfall aufgefallen.
*hust* würde mich da anbieten *hust* :p
Gegenstände liegen plötzlich unter dem Boden oder hinter Ziegelsteinwänden, (hier z.B. im Verbotenen Tal bei den Aggro Berserkern), Gegner vor allem Ecke Xarcor buggen in Felsen und spucken euch mit ihren AoE Attacken an, während ihr sie eigentlich nur mit dem AoE des Flammenwerfers oder Raketenwerfers schaden könnt.

Das mit den Gegnern ist mir erst mit weiteren Fortschritt (ab Akt 2.) aufgefallen denke die sind einfach falsch gespawnt.

[u]5. Kältewert[/u]

Hier nur eine beiläufige Erwähnung, dieser nimmt eigentlich nur Auswirkung auf die Haupthandlung und dient sonst nur zum erreichen einiger Achievments, die einen anderen Handlungsabschluss forcieren.
Die Bonustalente bewirken kaum was, vielleicht 10% Schaden oder sowas. (steht ja nicht da...)

[h1]Arcu's Tipstüte[/h1]

[u]1. How TO Achievments[/u]

Wer ein Achievmentjäger ist, kann dieses Game mit einen erweiterten Spieldurchlauf mit allen Erfolgen abschließen, ist aber sehr schwer zu erreichen, da ihr viele Punkte und Geld zurückhalten müsst und wahrscheinlich erst mit lvl 28-30 die Fraktion wählt.
Hierbei gilt noch zu beachten, dass man auf minimale Kälte geht, da für ein steigenen Kältewert nur Elex konsumieren müsst, jedoch anders herum geht dies nicht.
Weiteres Problem minimaler Kältewert heißt, oft emotionale Entscheidung zu treffen und diese sind gerade am anfang naja nicht SOOO gern gesehen aber man kommt auch hiermit durch, ansonsten gilt beim Weg der Achievments vieeel Geld sparen für Elextränke.

[u]2. Schaden, Charakterentwicklung und Skillung[/u]

Der Schaden berechnet sich in Elex ungefähr so, Rüstung vs. Schaden, das Problem hierbei, es verfügen auch viele Monster und Mutaten über Rüstungen ergo ihr werdet eigentlich dazu genötigt, zügig ordentliche Waffen zu equippen.
Wenn ihr relativ ausführlich und tiefgründig zockt, liegt euer maximales Charakterlevel so zwischen 40-45.

Nun denken einige alles klar, mit lvl 7 oder 8 hab ich den bekomme 1 Statpoint mehr pro Level Talent und das wären dann ca 30 extra stats, theoretisch gut überlegt - praktisch schwachsinn, aber man weiß es anfangs nicht besser.

Euer Level gibt euch vielleicht 50-60% der nötigen Attributspunkte, den Rest holt ihr euch durch Elextränke auch bei minimalen Kältedurchlauf, können bis zu 80+ locker konsumiert werden, das wären min. 160 Statpoints. (16 Level)
Wem Achievments nicht wichtig sooo wichtig sind, damit der Kältwert egal kann auch noch mehr konsumieren, für manche Achievments wie "Erlerne alle Kampftalente" Notwenidig, dann zieht ihr euch über 300 Elextränke rein und habt damit über 60 Level gratis bekommen.

Wie nun an viel Reines Elex kommen, entweder finden und kaufen oder looten durch den 3ten Punkt in Tierausschlachten, glaub Tiertrophäen entnehmen oder so heißt der, damit lootet ihr bei jedem Mutanten reines Elex je größer je mehr.

[u]3. Waffen und Skillungstip[/u]

So traurig es klingt, aber die Berserker und Outlaws haben mit ihrer Waffenkonstallationen die sinnvollste Statverteilung für Fern- und Nahkampf, folgendes lässt sich Kombinieren, daher müsst ihr euch entscheiden.

Schwerter und Bögen, Schrotfinten und alle großen Waffen
(Stärke/Geschicklichkeit) mit einer Ausnahme auch 1 Lasergewehr

Äxte, Knüppel, Stäbe und Schilde (Stärke/Konstitution)

Laser und Plasmagewehre (Geschicklichkeit/Intelligenz)

Also mein Tip, besorgt euch ein Zweihandschwert und einen Bogen, könnt auch ein gutes bereits finden in Edan, das Ignis Artifex, hier ergeben sich nun 2 Konstellationen, Rare Waffen haben oft andere Stats.

Ignis Artifex (65 Agi, 44 Str) und Kriegsbogen (53/34) (Kriegsbogen aufwertbar)
Zweihandschwert III (69 Str, 61 Agi) und Geistersehne (70 Str, 30 Agi) später Todesstrahl (83/59)

Anfangs geht auch ein Einhänder und ein entsprechenden Bogen, Schrotflinten kann ich nicht entfehlen, da hier nur Stumpf die Rohschadenswerte in die Berechnung eingehen und diese weniger Reichweite haben.

[u]4. How TO Win, schwachsinnige Gruppenanfangskämpfe[/u]

Hier ist mein bester Tip besorgt euch mit Taschendiebstahl etc. Handgranaten bei den Outlaws.

Disclaimer: I love most things that Piranha Bytes create, specially Gothic 1/2/3 and Risen.

I'm only 20-odd hours into this game but it's a work of art. Truly amazing. Initially I thought... a jet-pack!? What the... Then very quickly I realised it's a stroke of genius. It really opens up the world without making it too open. Graphics are amazing in places, lighting and ambience is spot on.

Reading several negative reviews regarding difficulty, I mean it's hard but that's not a negative. Lower the difficulty, find a new strategy, find a new quest, go exploring and get better/stronger. It's not too difficult.

Some negatives: bad grammar and spelling in places, perhaps translation issues? Some dialog options force you into choosing things you don't want, no alternatives provided. Maybe adding some options here would be nice.
Face models are overused, or is this a limited gene pool type deal? Other than that, no major problems so far. Stable and runs quite well. 

Bravo devs, you've created a true open-world RPG with depth and character.

Edit: GeraltofRivia made a good point in his comment: the character sheet needs some work. Also, I feel a little disappointed with the music. The music isn't bad, but nothing _really_ stands out. For example, Kai Rosenkranz's score on Gothic 3 had a beautiful, strong, thematic score that didn't get in the way of the game-play. Maybe the Gothic 3 world lends itself to more thematic music though...

Final edit: Finished. It's a great world. Loads of really nice exploring. However, there are real negatives. The story is underwhelming and unoriginal, the scant parts of lore we do get are fairly lacklustre. The lore could be far deeper. I'd love to have read more in game, even rubbish lore is fun. The dialog is weak, the same thing is constantly repeated, specially at the end. Also, save some voice actor time and don't voice Jax's character. That's me, I don't want to hear "him".

TL;DR: Great world, loads of exploring. Doesn't have the story and depth to make it a great game. Fans of open-world RPGs will love it and certainly worth a play-through. A few minor tweaks would have put this game up there with the best of them.

可以说 这是个好游戏 但要注意几点
每次开游戏都要开关一次垂直同步（记得点应用）来把游戏自带的锁30帧bug？关掉
这游戏通常武器伤害越高玩起来越流畅 假如你的近战武器伤害超过30 就能苟活 超过50 就相对稳了 要是超过70 并且那拿着伤害超60的激光枪 那就没有任何野怪是你打不过的
但要是伤害不足30 就要被各种野怪虐得死去活来 这时就会产生一种这是个垃圾游戏的想法
画质可以说是有些粗糙 部分细腻 水面质量可能是为了致敬哥特王朝 做得跟10年前一个样
喷射背包除了便于到达各种隐秘场所 方便从高处降落外 还开创了一种新的战斗闪躲和落跑方式

这游戏越晚后钱越重要 战利品技能尽快点满 到时打个野怪都会掉钱和高级素材 多余素材拿去卖 
只有选了派系才能买到中级和高级护甲 不选就只能穿着最低级的那些 这我感觉是一大缺点 顶级护甲全套至少要3万 讨价还价技能只能减少售价不能提高卖东西价格 技能点满也就打个9折
另外这游戏有些陷阱技能 点了必后悔 [spoiler]我就不嗦了[/spoiler]

这游戏感觉跟辐射还是有些像的 可以概括为近战版辐射吧 至少在制作组出了崛起2 3俩无聊游戏以后 终于做出了像哥特王朝的东西

Ich bin seit Gothic ein Fan von Pyranha Bytes. Sie verstehen es, eine raue Spielwelt zu erschaffen, in der man nicht jedem trauen darf, in der Characktere ihre eigenen Probleme/Beweggründe haben und sich diesen - mit oder ohne dir - stellen. First time writing a review, and the only reason I've decided to write one - is that Elex is extremely underestimated. There are 3 parts in the review: 1st - general note, 2nd - for non PB/Gothic fans, 3rd - for PB fans.

1st part. General note:

Rating is strongly affected by the initial wave of reviews, in which broken quests and bugs were reported. After that, within a couple of months, several patches fixed most of the problems and increased overall game quality. Devs did a great work with patching, which does not happen often according to today's standards (and also according to previous PB games).  Difficulty settings were also improved for those who are scared of "damage sponges". So do not be confused with negative reviews.

I've spent about 100 hours in-game in the last 2 months and I've only met several small bugs that were solved by save-reload. No major bugs or broken quests.

2nd part. For those who are looking for a nice RPG (and is not a hardcore fan of PB games):

Elex is a well made, I would even say "high quality" (considering today's standards) rpg game. The world is big, interesting and consistent. There are no or almost no "stupid farming" quests. All fighting styles are playable, though if you play on the max difficulty - you will find yourself using melee a lot. 

The story is OK, it is not a masterpiece but how often do you see masterpiece stories in RPG's? It is not Whitcher level, but the story is interesting and somewhat nonlinear. Be wary of your actions and cold level, though, since it will determine the ending (similar to Deus Ex). Also there are some quests with a hidden timer (ignoring the quest for a long time affects the result), which I really like.

Balance is fine (compared to other PB games), and, most importantly, - you can use custom difficulty settings. For those who are not familiar with PB - I would not recommend highest difficulty settings, otherwise, you will have to spend about 10 hours leveling with non-fighting quests until you are able to fight even rats comfortably.

The big problem is the description of character characteristics, skills, and the cold level.  It may be (and it will be) misleading, so you may have to google for it. I can kind of guess the idea of devs hiding the actual numbers and meaning of the skills, but when you play on ultra difficulty without consuming elex (each skill point counts) - it becomes quite annoying. Skills design is also a bit questionable - a lot of usless skills in the game.

Overall it is a good, solid RPG game.

3rd part. For PB fans:

It is not Gothic. It is not even Risen. From my point of view, in many ways, it might be a higher quality (do not burn a hole in your chair please) game than any of games previously made by PB. Initially, I thought of not playing it for 6-12 months, waiting for community patches. But I was able to enjoy without major issues it just 1-2 months after release. This is unusual for PB and it is great.

However, it is not gothic. Not even Risen. Gothic 1&2 were hilarious games full of fun. I am still waiting for new Gothic 2 mods to play it again. Even bugs in those games were fun. Risen 3 main character had a very charming personality, small guys and parrot spell were amazing. It was fun playing. This particular feeling is (in my opinion) much weaker in Elex. There are some jokes and nice characters, but overall it feels more bland compared to those games.

Another thing that is missing is attention to "fractions". Basically - it does not really matter which fraction you decided to join. There is not much "fraction dependent" content and fraction skills are not as diverse as they were in G2 for example.

On the other hand, in Elex I saw a lot of things I was enjoying in Gothic, so I would definitely recommend it to any PB fan.

tldr: Takes some time to get into, but afterwards Elex gets really addictive like all the other PB games. Smaller issues and the combat system make a 8/10 for me on this title. 

Beginning with Gothic I in 2001 I've used to spend thousands of hours on the games of Piranha Bytes - so there was no way to leave Elex out. I was sceptical in the first place for the setting, but every step you go
you see and feel (!) it's a classic PB game. For I started recently I can't say much about the story, but here are some pros, neutrals and cons on Elex I've gathered througout the first bunch of hours:

+ The setting is interesting and immersive - I worried about the entanglement of SciFi and classic PB game, but in fact it's well done
+ The world looks beautiful and tempts you to go off the road where many little secrets are hidden
+ The story is good and the talkings with NPCs are awesome, like always. PB finally got their narrative skills increased for the first part and the second part has always been one of their best tasks. I can't rate the english translation for I play Elex on german, but PB usually does a good job on that one.

* Once you go off the road at the beginning you get killed quite often. For this is normal on PB games it's still a bit frustrating at the beginning.
* The whole UI was mainly build for consoles. This is something which troubles me since Risen II, but you get used to it over time.

- The combat system lets Elex lose a lot of points on the pro side. Sorry for that PB, but the combat system is still as worse as it has been since Gothic I. The Risen I combat system was nice, but this one is just.. meh
- Same applies for the controls and the character movement in general. 
- Dropped weapons cannot be looted. I was really disappointed after taking a lot of time to kill a bandit which could one-hit me just to get my hands on his chainsaw-sword or his ranged weapon but in fact I've got a beer and some elexit. Awesome!

Not many points on that list, but for my not so many hours of playtime it should be sufficient. Elex is a really nice game with the lacks of all the previous titles - a classic PB game but still worth the money.

tldr: Der Einstieg braucht etwas Zeit, aber danach ist Elex genau so suchtgefährdent wie alle anderen PB Spele. Kleine handwerkliche Unsauberheiten, sowie das Kampfsystem lassen mich für diesen Titel nur 8/10 vergeben. 

Tausende Spielstunden habe ich bereits in die PB Spiele seit dem Release von Gothic I im Jahr 2001 gesteckt - also gab es keinen Weg Elex auszulassen. Anfägnlich war ich skeptisch was das Setting angeht, aber bei jedem Schritt sieht und fühlt (!) man, dass es sich um ein PB Spiel handelt.
Da ich erst vor kurzem gestartet habe kann ich nicht viel über die Geschcihte sagen, aber hier sind ein paar positive, neutrale und negative Punkte, welche mir in meinen ersten Stunden aufgefallen sind:

+ Das Setting ist interessant und immersiv - die Verknüpfung von SciFi und klassischen PB Spielen betrachtete ich anfangs skeptisch, aber die Verbindung ist sehr gut gemacht.
+ Die Welt sieht bezaubernd aus and verführt dazu abseits der Wege zu suchen, wo sich viele kleine Geheimnisse finden lassen. 
+ Die Geschichte ist gut und die Gespräche mit den NPCs sind genial, wie immer. Bezüglich des erstgenanntem konnten PB endlich ihre narrativen Fähigkeiten verbessern und letzteres war schon immer eine Stärke von PB gewesen. - Das Kampfsystem lässt Elex eine Menge Punkte verlieren. Tut mir leid PB, aber das Kampfsystem ist genau so schlecht wie seit Gothic I. Das Kampfsystem von Risen I war klasse, aber das aktuelle ist einfach nur.. naja

- Fallengelassene Waffen können nicht geplündert werden. This game is great. However, you need to know what to expect:

1) Major technical issues. Often my guns will shoot right through an enemy's model. The controls will feel sticky and movement sluggish.

2) Difficult beginning. Well, difficult may be stretching it. The game doesn't make you a superhero. You have to work to get there. If you start out and get an axe and think you can kill stuff, you're screwed. My first 5-6 hours was doing jobs around the first town, involving myself in story, making choices, etc. all while clawing for the bit of money and experience I could get. It wasn't until I joined the clerics, got a flamethrower, etc. that I was starting to reliably kill things.

3) You're looking at a Skyrim-esque game in that you're released onto a major world. Unlike Skyrim, however, you don't have mod support, but you do have a more fulfilling and rewarding base game expereince. Skyrim is great as a template, but the base game suffers from a lot of technical issues and bad writing. This game is a bit better than that, but it isn't as mod friendly.

If you understand this and enjoy the idea of working your way into greatness rather than starting at it, then this will be a great and rewarding experience for you. You can make mistakes in this game, you can screw up your character. Read things, research stuff, and be smart about leveling.

I want to love this game, but it's trying hard to make me hate it.

Pros:
- The overall storyline is great, and the visuals are gorgeous.
- The world feels enormous and diverse, and exploration is a treat.
- The different factions you can join and branching moral choices are a great touch.

Cons:
- Combat and movement are a clunky, infuriating mess.
- No sense of balance at all. Your life as a melee will be endless misery. Ranged characters can breeze through the game.
- Melee in general is somehow even more one-dimensional than Skyrim. Combat is "left click on something until it stops hitting you."
- Hitboxes are awful. If something is an inch above or below you, your giant 2-hander is probably going to pass right through it.
- Mob AI is dumb as rocks, and your companions will spend more time getting stuck on trees or attacking the air than they will connecting blows.
- To make up for the terrible AI, every creature in the game starts shooting fireballs if they can't figure out how to path to you.
- The skill system is bland and feels unfinished.
- Stats are meaningless, other than being a bizarre way to gatekeep gear. You can pick up one of the best swords in the game just outside the starting town, and it'll sit in your inventory until your stats are high enough to use it 40 hours later.
- There's very little incentive to fight anything unless forced to do so by the story. Dozens of hours into the game, you're still one-shottable by most mobs you come across. Also, quests give 800exp, and mobs give 10-50exp. Given that, plus the awful combat, the best play is to just run past everything.

Somewhere underneath the monotonous, clunky gameplay is a great game. If you loved their other flawed titles (Gothic etc), you'll enjoy this one as well. Otherwise, pick up Witcher 3 if you need to scratch your openworld/fantasy/rpg itch.

ELEX - 10 hours in.

Imagine a world that you've read about before (The Shannara Chronicles). Then imagine factions you've seen in games before (The Berserkers: Skyrim, the Clerics: Mass Effect, the Outlaws: Fallout) and throw in a dallop of old RPG nostalgic gameplay, and what you end up with is ELEX: an amalgamation of familiar RPG elements with enough flavour to keep things interesting while hiding the fact that it does not do anything new and is not really all that great.

Don't get me wrong, I'm enjoying myself in the world of Elex. The design is good, even if the angular graphics look a bit outdated and you feel like you're controlling a brick rather than a person. It's another fantasy RPG, so you can't possibly expect too much originality. The bridge between fantasy and science-fiction has been done to death in many older games, prominently the Might and Magic series, and the jewel that was Arcanum in its time. ELEX seems to take an Arcanumesque approach to the technology vs magic plot, although while in Arcanum this was an analog slider, in ELEX it's a binary faction choice. Or trinary, I guess, if you count "scrap-tech" Outlaws a technological genre on its own.


The actual problem ELEX has is that it hasn't learned something many other games have learned about appealing to the general public. People who start out in a game don't want to listen to a thousand conversations and gradually figure out how the world works. They want to grab a sword and stick it into the nearest goblin. ELEX thus presents itself as a game out of time; where in order to progress, patience and attention are required rather than quantifiable statistical progress. 

After all what passes for skill these days is the reaction-speed oriented button pressing that is the staple of the online community as presented to us by multiplay FPS combat, counter-combat mechanics, for those who still dare touch them: quick-time events and of course MMORPG PvP. Against this contextual behemoth, the rhythm-based, almost ponderous mechanics of ELEX and low early character combat ability seems unwieldy, maybe even unappealing.

I can't even blame them, on the pendulum of this context ELEX swings squarely the other way. I've gained 6 levels so far but my combat ability has only increased marginally. I'm chugging down consumables every battle just to stay alive, and it's not even the highest difficulty setting. Moreso than staying alive however is the pathetic amount of damage my character inflicts upon opponents. I love stories, I don't mind running errands for xp, but at some point fleeing from nearly every monster in the game becomes tedious, and a quest where you killed the ugly beastie feels more completed than a quest where you ran around it to grab the item you needed.


As for what the game is actually about, you play as Jax, a guy who is so generic the plot has to explain why he's so wooden: the use of ELEX dulls emotion. Incidentally, ELEX came to Earth via meteor, a few hundred years ago it slammed into the planet, disrupted life as we know it, and brought the ELEX substance which powers technology and magic equally. From this four factions arose, the Clerics and their derivatives the Albs (who are very powerful), who focus on using ELEX to power machinery or using ELEX for machinery and magic respectively, the Berserkers who are a gigantic misnomer as they consist of magic-wielding hippie-vikings who seek to restore nature to the world by transforming ELEX into Mana and using it to power magic and plants all the while insisting this is "natural", and the Outlaws, a loose collection of misfits who loot, scavenge and steal what they can, thus relying on more "mechanical" and gunpowder level technology rather than electronic devices.

Jax himself is an Alb, or rather, was an Alb. During the introduction scene you are selected for a Mission Most Important, so apparently you're special, and extraordinarily capable. Next thing you know your plane gets shot down over hippie-country by obviously not bows and arrows, your mission is declared a failure and some other Alb is right there to kill you for failing. Not suspicious AT ALL. Next thing you know you fall off a cliff, somebody steals your Alb armour in your coma, and you are left as a complete and utter loser who can barely swing a weapon because apparently anything you ever could do was related to the ELEX which is no longer in your body. It's probably not the worst origin story ever but I'm hard-pressed to think of a worse example.

You quickly run into a friendly dude who invites you over to Berserker Village, all the while clearly making sure that it's your choice whether or not you go. This seems like freedom of choice, except you suck so excessively at combat your alternative is fleeing everything till you reach another settlement and hoping there's completable quests there too. I sensibly went along to Berserker village, thinking I might as well fling some magic, 'cause I love magic. Except, I don't apparently love magic when it's the schtick of tyrannical hippies who exile or kill everyone who likes technology. It did not help that there are a bunch of faction-based skills and the Cleric ones just sounded so much cooler. "One Man Army"? Yes please. Good compensation for my current suckage, assuming I ever get powerful enough to travel from hippie-ville.


In the end, ELEX is an RPG in the sense of an adventure game, far more than a combat game. Combat obviously plays an important role but after 10 hours I'm only barely capable at fighting what's in the wild, and 80% of it still kills me quickly. Designwise it's okay, 'cause I can still achieve goals for quests by running and talking and progress that way, but it can't dismiss the fact that slaying a few monsters along the way is infinitely more satisfying than having to avoid them all. I suspect ELEX is all about the story, but the story is already so full of cliches that I'm not expecting much there either.

Simultaneously there's so much detail in certain parts of ELEX, like how a village has about 12 significant NPCs, all of whom will have their own opinion of your actions. I don't know if this actually *does* anything mechanically, but I'm the kind of person who wonders what the hell I just did wrong that I got a message that this NPC disapproves of what I just said. It's details like that that get me invested in a world, no matter that the character I'm playing looks like a Jason Statham clone without any social skills. It feels like someone poured love and effort into creating this place (flaws included), and I feel like the ELEX world affects me, or rather, my character.

I just wish I could affect it back. With my axe.

44 hours of play and I enjoyed the first 20-30 hrs, but now it has become boring and repetative. 
The game seems to have many bugs. 
You are given a task or quest but it doesn't always appear in your quest list or show on the map so you are screwed. You can complete a quest given by someone important with the hopes you will progress in the game, but nothing happens. 
I've spent most of my 40 hours trying to join the Beserkers, one of the main factions in the game, and I've completed many quests given by people, but the war lord of the Berserkers never allows me to join and there is no mention of any quest I've done. Others have complained about this particular bug and it really defeats the whole object of the game. Why do a quest when there is no advancement after completion.
Also the combat is the worst I've seen in many years, if you are fighting alongside a companion you will almost always end up fighting them because the game has an automatic target system, so the nearest person to you becomes the enemy regardless. In other situations you can be slashing away at fresh air because it's so hard to get your character to turn while fighting.
So in short the game looks good and you will probably enjoy the first few hours until you encounter the various bugs, after which you will slowly grind to a halt.

TLDR: They tried to make something similar to Gothic and they failed.

Long version:
Combat. The person who designed dodge mechanic should have some special "worst idea" award. It's insane. For example, I need to strafe left a little bit, then a little bit more, so i tap couple times A and woosh i make roll to the left. It might be fine if it wouldn't require my stamina. Couldn't you make something like SHIFT+A or SHIFT+D for rolls? It's irratating like hell since it's working outside of combat too! Imagine you using jetpack, jumping on tiny platforms and trying to manuver by hitting A and D keys. And of course character will try to f...ing roll.

Bugs are still there. Sometimes when i got hit in aim mode, i can't reactivate aim mode. I need to remove my weapon, then draw it again and only after that my right mouse button starts working properly toggling aim. There was a moment when i wasn't been able to even remove weapon after combat. At least quick save\load helped me there.

The jetpack is the next thing. Who the f..k thought that it's bright idea to make limited fuel that recharges over time? So there is a lot(actually not a lot) of "secret" places where you need to get using jet pack and i ended up doing 1 jump, alt+tab read some news, another jump, read twitter, another jump... Can't you just reset it on landing outside of combat? Make some "overheat" mechanic that cooldowns really fast once you landed and that's all! That blue/red bar... why? Red bar isn't even working everytime. Sometimes i landed safely with empty bar. Sometimes i can't activate my jet when i am falling even if there is some fuel in red bar. 

Traders. They got limited amount, but all you need is just reopen shop to get stock refilled. Don't even end conversation. Just ask for trade again. WAT?! WHY?!

The world. Starting very promising with berserks village. And in the middle i got feeling that they run out of money or something like that. There are places with bugge texture positioning like one of the outpust of clerics, where some walls are just floating in the air. There are working lights in one of the pre-metheor houses (hey, who hired stalker dev?). There are fire barrels and torches everywhere with nobody who could light them!

Light. I like that tiny idea that your eyes need some time to get used to dark and i don't like NO FLASHLIGHTS when i see things like working radio, energy weapons, actual lights (at least in cleric and outlaws towns).

Story. I haven't finished yey, but it looks plain. Hey, you were betrayed go get your revenge. dot.

Dialogs. That voice change of some npc during exact same conversation sometimes makes me really pissed off. They will show you all the lines but don't even highlight unavailable (or use red color). So you would know that you can't choose some line only by clicking on it. Hello? It's almost 2018 here.

Now the things i like. 
The bow from berserks village that they sell even to someone not in berserk faction, because it's OP and can kill even robots (wat? rly?). 
The tiny dialogs between npcs after some quests. At least they tried to show that world is a living thing.

Overall, it's not THAT bad, but only with 50% discount and if you have a lot of free money. 

P.S. oh and devs should have a yellow star with text "we tried" cut from cardboard by some kid.

Играю только от тотального ногеймса.

Commençons par les moins :
- interface nulle, aucune ergonomie (craft, cuisine, inventaire). Totalement à revoir. On sent le relent ergo pour "consoleux"
- les notes/livres trouvés dans le monde auraient pu être intéressants s'ils étaient écrits et non décrits. Ecrits, ils auraient pu donner des infos sur le background du monde...
- un monde avec un autre nom, mais qui ressemble au nôtre une fois l'apocalypse passée par là
- une sensation de déja vu et "d'édulcorant"...
- jeu très dur pour les novices, mais qui raviront les amateurs de Gothic/Risen
- le jetpack qu'on utilise trop (?) finalement pour se sortir d'affaire trop facilement ?
- dials sans queue ni tête des fois (dû au monde ouvert)(difficile à expliquer, genre un type nous parle d'un autre type comme si on le connaissait, hors jamais entendu avant, etc...)

Les +:
- c'est du Pyranha Bytes à l'ancienne
- un Gothic/Risen like sauce Post Apo
- un monde ouvert vaste
- certes niveau graphisme, ça fait un peu moche, même en tout extra, mais ça reste joli, du Pyrana Bytes quoi...
- environnements détaillés, avec plein de lieux à découvrir, de grottes cachées
- le jetpack qui paraissait fun au départ, s'avère crucial en début de jeu pour éviter de se faire OS par le premier gros rat mutant venu... Il permet également une vaste exploration en hauteur (falaises, montagnes), nous permet d'aller dans des trous profonds (et en ressortir)...
- on peut pas faire n'importe quoi dans les villes, maisons (voler, faire le c...) sous peine de se faire arrêter ou attaquer
- trouver du PQ partout. Oui c'est important le PQ en monde post apo... pour bien se torcher à l'ancienne... derrière un drageon (je vous laisse découvrir ce qu'est un drageon)
- certains dials 
- les easter eggs (je dirai pas lesquels, mais yen a des gros et des moins gros)
- le bestaire Pyranha Bytes (raptors, bécasses géantes) et d'autres... 
- des surprises dans les coins, en hauteur, dans les antres...

Au final :
On se laisse prendre à l'ambiance malgré les défauts... Reste à voir le scénar qui m'a l'air intéressant, et que je n'ai pas trop suivi... 
Les devs corrigent lesdits défauts, et c'est cool. A voir une fois définitivement patché. 
Je le recommande à tous. Surtout aux exigeants. Car il est hard le système de combat, si on essaie de pas trop utiliser le jetpack.

What a mess. If you really, REALLY like the Gothic games, I suppose you can enjoy this, but overall it's just terrible.

Pros:
-Jet packing around is fun
-Weapons and armor are overall pretty cool.
-The animal/mutant/robot designs are also pretty cool
-Nice mix of fantasy and Sci-fi elements

Cons:
-No level scaling. INB4 "Don't stray off the main path!" or "but that's how games should be!", the skull marked enemies (aka the "♥♥♥♥ your SHlT with one hit" enemies) are placed in the main path, the side paths, and anywhere else you can think of. Takes about ~15 levels or so before you can really fight anything. Get used to running away as fast as you can, you previously ultra badass murder machine you!

-Combat sucks. enemies are easily kited, either through standing at range, firing a single shot then letting your companion go to town on them for 5 shots, then hit the enemy once to get the companion to fight again. Rinse and repeat as desired. Melee? Hope you like shitty hitboxes that don't work well if you're on different elevations. (instead of attacking at a downwards angle like you're looking, the attacks are made as if you're standing on even ground, meaning you either swing above the enemy, or into the ground below them if you or the enemy are on any half decent dirt mound.

-Hitboxes suck. See above about melee, and any sort of AoE attack able to hit through thin walls or roofs. Mostly just enemies can do this though, good luck trying to do the same thing.
-The characters are boring. Your main character is an emotionless killing machine (intended), but his story for revenge is boring. Every character around you has a boring story, and directly contradict their faction sometimes (i.e. the berzerker companions have no problem using that high tech jetpack they abhore. Nice.)

Conclusion:
The game just makes you ask yourself "why am I playing this? It doesn't get any better. It hasn't gotten any more interesting since I unlocked those kinda nifty mana/energy/psi powers which are basically treated as guns instead of the spells they were obviously designed around."

Pass on this, get a real RPG like Divinty: Original Sin (1 or 2), any of the fallout games (3, New vegas, or even 4. Or the original Turn based ones if you don't mind going into a non third/first person game.), The Witcher series, or just about any other game.

Once you get past the crappy combat, lackluster environments, and boring storyline, this game is one great big steaming pile of "meh".  

The first 10 hours or so are spent running from everything as you try to level up by completing non-combat "courier" quests.  The fan bois will tell you how realistic this is and they're right.  It's also frustrating and you know how we all play video games to be frustrated, right?  

After enough slogging, you'll finally get the attribute points you need to use that weapon that you've had in your inventory for the past three days.  Now you can kill some stuff (after numerous one-shot deaths and game reloads) and be rewarded with a low XP gain and worthless junk to sell.  Say, didn't that enemy have a super cool looking green sword?  Nowhere to be found.  Yay for realism!

After more slogging, you will be able to use some powerful weapons and armor.  Then the game becomes a snooze fest.  Even the toughest enemies are defeated with just a few ranged shots or well placed melee swings.  It's a race to the finish as you breeze through enemies and checkbox the quests.

Now it's time to decide upon the final dialogue choice you want to use.  Oh wait!  You can't use the one that you want because it's blocked by this "Cold" system that's never explained.  I guess you just have to accept the end that you're given.  So.  Much.  Fun!

The actual end of the game was really good.  Right-click.  Uninstall.  Delete all content.  Win!

If you choose to ignore my advice and buy the game anyway, then I suggest that you do two things:
- Disable the auto-focus.  It keeps you facing an opponent, which helps you hit them, but prevents you from being able to move effectively in combat.  This is especially frustrating with multiple enemies.
- Map the Reload key to your favorite button.  You'll be using it a lot for the first half of the game.

Normal people would ask for directions to a place not just wander around for minutes on end looking for something simple like a tavern, especially when the tavern itself doesn't even have a sign indicating it might be an establishment. The controls are very clunky and unresponsive. Graphics are decent, but I'm glad I didn't pay full price. There are many other games out there for equal price that are much better. I didn't make it very far in the game before I decided to call it quits. Playing the game gave me no real enjoyment and that is the point of a game, entertainment. This game might be for more hardcore types looking for an exploration game, but at the start of this one, you can get killed by almost anyone or anything. Just wasn't a game for me.

Elex is a game about picking your battles. This game absolutly does not hold your hand. There is danger everywhere; you have to plan your movements and think more tactical. You have a jet-pack and a sprint key that are just as important as any weapon. You have limited resources and must weigh their use with every major encounter. I have lost many fights over and over, only to win when I took a different approach. Are there some headaches? Yes. Is there a very robust RPG system under the hood. Yes. You will be very weak starting out. You will want to lean on your companion for the early game. You will still have to be very carefull about where you step even when you are stronger. Its just a different game, where running away is always an option. You have to get used to sizing up and avoiding danger, and only picking fights you are confident in winning. This game is going in my top 15 favorite RPGs ever, and I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a great mix of fantasy and sci-fi in a unique RPG.

Buy this game, who does not like a post-apocalyptic high fantasy sci-fi with warring sword-wielding beserkers fighting cleric mechs.

You are not a superhero, chosen by the divine, or prophesied about. You are a nobody with a  jetpack and a rusty pipe. The game is rough, you will die. Get better and pick your fights.

Combat is interesting as it goes off how well you can fill the combo meter as opposed to traditional "per hit" damage; if you don't learn how to chain attacks the enemy is not going down anytime fast. Of course, it would be wrong if I did not say it is a challenge in of itself to adjust to the clunky controls. It can be done, but it's not going to be enjoyed along the way.

The story is fantastic, I can't say I've seen other games pull off such an interesting game world. Sadly the budget was not there, so some of the textures look off and the sound's get strange. 

If you don't mind a little lack of polish and fighting difficult controls, this is by far one of the most memorable games I have ever played. 

TL;dr I loved it, once I got good.

PB I want my money back.  You can't just say it's hard get over it.  You actually have to make something that people want to spend their precious hours doing.  Being everyone's errand b*** is not my idea of a good time.  Ever.

I thought this would be a great review video for my channel. I though I would have at least four or five good videos that came out of this game. I gave this game a chance, expecting it to turn into countless hours of play. This may have been the worst $33.49 that I have ever spent in my life. 

The visuals are atrocious. Outdated software. Almost looks like its running on Unreal 3. This was released at the fall of this year; it looks like it was developed 6 years ago. Disgusted. I have no other word than disgusted.

The soundtrack is actually pretty cool. The music is catchy. Was very impressed with the score. Found myself singing it to myself without even meaning to. Pretty neat.

I can't even begin to scratch the surface of how painful the dialogue is because I'm pretty sure it gave me some form of an as of now yet unknown terminal disease. I thought Bungie struggled with finding voice actors, but jeez, did this take the cake and eat it in a single bite. I've never heard voices more stereotypical and lifeless than the ones I heard in this game, reading their lines from a que card as if it were a spelling test in elementary school. Absolutely atrocious.

I couldn't tell you a single thing about the narrative because all of the other problems had me so off put and off focus. I couldn't even FORCE myself to get into this. I play games seriously; I run my own Youtube and Twitch channel. Like, this is what I do. But this was so bad, I literally couldn't even force myself to bear it any longer. However, if one is able to look past all that, I can imagine that the narrative is probably very entrancing. The use of magic and advanced technology creates a diverse and unique game world and atmosphere. I just didn't have it in me to push myself to get that far. 

The combat system felt a bit wonky at first, but once you figured it out it did actually turn out to be pretty fun. Slow combat really makes you think twice before smashing something with your fists, for sure. It featured a outdated yet somehow still sort of fresh combat UI, and as much as I wanted to completely hate it, I wasn't able to dislike it as much as I figured I would. Don't get me wrong, its still weird. But the werid factor lessens over time. Give it a few minutes and you'll catch right on, assuming you can get past the terrible visuals and putrid dialogue. 

In all honesty, I should be writing a review for this. I literally played it for about 20 minutes. But the fact of the matter is that while the issues the game has can be overlooked by certain types of players, they are issues that never should've existed in the first place. The game world was colorful and inviting, and it felt warm and ripe with adventure. But a game with issues like these needs a strong opening, and the first five to ten minutes of opening cutscenes were nothing short of a joke. Poorly acted, all hand crafted; not that there's anything wrong with that. But when you pour this much money into a title, you need proper motion tracking to animate character movement. There's a reason people don't hand animate character mesh models anymore. And that's because it looks absolutely terrible. 

With that, I bid this game farewell from my hard drive. Pardon me while I go cry over the time I lost playing this game that I will never get back.

Je crois que j'ai jamais vu un jeu aussi dur de ma vie.

Le jeux au départ se voulait amusant et avait une atmosphère intéressante. C'est là que vient la déception, les premiers ennemis sont simples vous faisant croire que le jeux sera facile si on monte de niveaux correctement.

Arrivés dans le premier village, les quêtes ça manque pas mais si vous croyez vraiment que vous allez en réussir beaucoup vous vous ratez... La plupart des quêtes vous demande d'aller tuer certains ennemis. Étant dans le village du départ, on croirait que c'est simple, et bah non ! La difficulté impressionante du jeu vous fera cracher du sang tellement vous crierez à l'injustice. Le gameplay vous propose une mécanique un peu similaire à la dark souls (esquive et frappe) mais c'est encoree un autre piège, certaines esquivent vous feront tombés dans la portée de l'ennemi, l'esquive n'est qu'un gros piège vous faisant mourire pour la plupart du temps. En 3 heures de jeux pour la plupart me laissent encore voir la possibilité de gagner face à un ennemi. La possibilité de pouvoir le vaincre après un petit moment de combat et de roulade bien placés... Et bah dans ce jeux c'est pas possible, la roulade coute tellement en endurance qu'on a plus la possibilité d'attaquer.

Parlons des dialogues... Les dialogues sont vraiments mous, la plupart des personnages me prennent pour un con la plupart du temps. Il y a des possibilités de dialogues, je me suis dis "Cool mes choix ont une importance dans le scénario" sauf que pour rire j'ai répondu un truc qui fallait pas (Ca semblait même pas comme une attaque je ne faisais que répondre à une question) je me retrouve avec un mec qui me poursuit pour me tuer... Dans le premier village... Qui est censé vous protéger !

Au bout d'un certain moment, on récupère le jetpack, outil qui est devenu presque indispensable si vous voulez pas passer 1 heures à faire le tour de la carte pour retourner rendre votre quêtes qui se trouve juste 10 mètres plus bas au niveau du plateau... Et parlons de l'escalade... On a la possibilité de grimper mais j'en vois pas l'utilité. Si encore je pouvais grimper sur les murs comme dans "Zelda breath of the wild" en perdant un peu d'endurance à chaque fois je l'aurais trouvé utile. Mais grimper sur une étagère je vois pas en quoi c'est utile au gameplay.

Parlons des achats. Un des premiers alliés, on dira, me propose d'aller dans la première ville récuperer des armes et des armures pour me protéger. Je me rend donc au forgeron et aux vendeurs d'armes et c'est impressionnant comme tout est cher ! La seul excuse qui est donnés c'est qu'on doit grimper dans la hiérarchie... Mais c'est une excuse bidon pour nous faire perdre notre temps a tuer plusieurs monstres sur 1 quêtes HORRIBLEMENT dur... Autant vous dire qu'aller farm c'est impossible,

J'ai tenté d'aller farm des mobs dans la nature mais chacun d'entres eux me one shot dès que je m'approche un peu trop près. La seul arme qui semble être un tant soi peu efficace est un arc récupérer dans la zone de didacticiel... Les épées sont censés (dans la plupart des RPGs) faire plus de dégats qu'un arc... Bah là c'est l'inverse.

Je déconseillerai ce jeux car il est dur pour être dur. A l'instar de Dark Souls, qui ce dit être dur, on peut vaincre en ayant du skill ou en farmant les niveaux ou loots. Dans ce jeux, c'est quasi impossible
