Nach langer Zeit des Wartens, ist es nun soweit. Elex ist da! Als Fan der echten Gothic-Reihe bis Gothic 3, welcher auch Risen in allen Teilen durchlebt hat, war die Freude groß, dass es wieder weitergeht. Wie wird es sich aber anfühlen? Ist der Gothic Spirit wieder da und wie wird es sein, die moderne Komponente im Spiel? 

Nach dem Start war schnell klar, es fühlt sich tatsächlich an wie Gothic. Die gleiche Sychronstimme vom namenlosen Helden und das Einsammeln von Kräutern und Gegenständen, ging gleich wie von selbst los. Schön das man zunächst bei den Beserkern erste Eindrücke sammeln kann. Fast so wie früher, man hält unwillkürlich schon nach den Drachen Ausschau. 

Nur mit einem Rohr bewaffnet in den ersten Kampf. Die Ratte umzuhauen, ist fast schon ein Heldenkampf. Schön.
Man merkt noch den Pudding in den Beinen. Wie man als alter Gothic-Spieler weiß, braucht man zu Anfang eine Begleitung, sonst kann man den Rasen mit dem Gesicht pflegen. Viele kleine Aufräge zum Sammeln von Punkten
und Informationen schließen sich an.

Klar in den Regionen, die nicht für die Charakterstufe angepasst ist, gibt es schnell was auf die Nase, da hilft auch nicht der Begleiter, welcher dann auch schnell mal mit der Nase im Dreck liegt. Ein schöner Ansporn schnell aufzusteigen und nach geeigneter Rüstung zu schauen. Wie verteile ich die Punkte? Bleibe ich doof und werde stark wie Bolle oder habe ich Intelligenz bis zum Abwinken, kann aber keine Gabel anheben. Wer sich auskennt, der startet ein paar Probestunden, um dann neu anzufangen und seinen Charakter richtig zu leveln. Was ist richtig? Kommt darauf an, Bolle oder Gabel.  

Da liegen wieder Stunden an Spielspaß und Sammelwut vor einem. Tränke brauen, Waffen bauen und Monster jagen.
Und natürlich neu, dass man  auch fliegen darf und coole Waffen ausprobieren.  Die Techwelt ist aus meiner Sicht auch sehr interessant. Man ist gespannt, wie sich die Geschichte weiterentwickelt bzw. wohin man sie entwickelt wird, durch seine Entscheidungen.  

Der Kampfmodus ist leider nicht ganz so geschmeidig. Ich dachte mein Rechner hängt, aber nein, es war ein Effekt! Vielleicht kann man da noch etwas Nachjustieren. Hat es bei den anderen Teilen ja auch gegeben, wenn die Erinnerung mich nicht trügt.
 

Schön das es wieder weitergeht im Piranha-versum.

Great story. Lovely to look at. Great concept all around. Terrible balance issues damage and factions. Terrible AI companions and monsters. Berzerkers don't even have any knockdowns. Outlaws have knockdowns and Clerics have them.

Pro:
-The quest- and dialogue-system with Skillchecks
-Sometimes characters run to each other in order to pass information in a dialogue (which makes the world incredibly more vivid)
-There is "somewhat" of a reload animation for firearms (compared to Risen II and III that is a huge step forward, but it's basically just a little bit of flopping of one arm and a click)

Cons:
-The combat-system is not "oldschool-Gothic". I can't put a finger on it, but it feels way to mechanic and also the absolute necessity to just jump around like some sort of frog on cocaine is a bit tiresome.
-The balancing of Weapons... Bows having a longer range and damage than all the High-Tech-Firearms?
-The dialogues are overall not very good. It's mostly people insulting each other in an uninterested way.
-The textures vary in a quality... A lot.
-The Jetpack does not at all "feel" like a jetpack. It's more like some sort of one of those electro scooter for elder people: Slow.
-The inventory works as if there was no mouse, which is okay if you don't use the mouse in a game. If you do implement it: Go all the way. Also selling just a part of your 700-item-stack of scrap electronics is... a time consuming matter if you only want to sell about 200 of those.


Overall I can't recommend this game. I played every Gothic and every Risen so far and this feels more akin to Risen II or Risen III. Except from some Voiceactors and a Reference to the Lighthousekeeper from Gothic II there (in my opionion) are no more similarities to the "good old times". When PB released Risen I was really looking forward to the sequels to become a renewed Gothic series after Gothic III was only playable after the community put their time and effort in it. But unfortunately Risen took it's way down the drain. Elex is the current pinnacle of this development and I will have to think long and hard if I will buy their next product.

Everything I've ever loved and hated about the Gothic series, but with a post-apocalyptic vibe.

Laughably inconsistent English voice acting, typos and mistakes in the subtitles, clunky horribly punishing combat, quest dialogue that clearly missed out lines or are voiced by the wrong character... you get the idea.

Oh, but the world-building, the delightfully murky character and faction motivations despite their ostensibly clean and cliched public positions on ethics and politics. Every character you speak to has an agenda and their own take on right and wrong.

Most of all, for me, the signature of every Piranha Bytes game is the exploration... every square inch of map is utilized, there's things to find and discover around every turn... even if the discovery is "holy hell, I'd best not come back here for 30 levels... or at least get crafty with my sneaking and jetpacking..."

You're never entirely comfortable wandering the landscape, knowing that a wrong turn will put you in immediate and very real danger of dying, probably before you've even realised your mistake. There's very few game franchises that capture that feeling of danger, for most you're left with a feeling of "best be careful, I might accidentally step into a level-appropriate challenge before I'm quite ready and start at a tactical disadvantage". With ELEX (and the Gothic games) you won't have time to have thought past the first two words of that sentence before a troll one-shots your level-5 ass for carelessly stepping six yards off the safe path to pick some herbs for your potions.

That might seem unduely unfair, but if you can learn caution, to scout your surroundings carefully and to be crafty about evading combat, you'll find that there's a huge reward and enjoyment in just travelling around avoiding the fights you can't win... and figuring out how to still get your objectives done.

Don't get disheartened by unwinnable fights, there's very few unavoidable fights.

So I just finished ELEX and am finally ready to write about it. Pre Release I avoided everything that has been released to the public, as to not overhype this or get disappointed with the actual game. This left me with the feeling of not expecting too much of the game and boy did PB deliver.

As a former Gothic fan who has played each Title at least twice, I instantly felt an overwhelming amount of Nostalgia during the first 20 hours or so. The games are obviously not related in story, but it felt like I finally found the game that can extend the Gothic experience and be its rightful successor. And to be honest I did not expect that at all when I went ahead and spent my money on this.

If you are a former Gothic fan I feel like this game is a no brainer. It has similar little annyoing flaws like gothic, but overall it's just a unique experience no other game can offer. If you are not a Gothic fan however i'll try to clear things up a bit.

This Game is extremely hard at the start, stays rough in the midgame and - if you did everything right/efficient - becomes insanely easy in the last portion. Just don't expect to have an easy time figuring it all out. It is part of the game and that's what makes it so rewarding to me. The reason for this is mostly the completely open world that allowes you to encounter countless enemies way above your abilities right from the start. As the game progresses you will slowly be able to take down one kind of creature after another. They never scale with your level and the XP-reward for killing them stays the same. Since that you will feel a sort of character progression unlike most other games/rpg's i know of.
If you are up for a little challenge this game should interest you :P

----

The Good:

The Story seems rather strange at the start but after a while it takes it's course and I started to really enjoy it. The Ending was pretty good and there seem to be a few ways this could go. Though i gotta say it's nothing mind boggling or varies too much. Still ... your decisions in the game matter and so do the factions you choose. I'll need a few more replays to be sure though :P It's hard to tell after just one play through, since this game offers a huge amount of replayability. I am excited to see how they continue on in the successor that should be ELEX 2 and tie those strings back together.

The Combat System feels very clunky at the start and the lack of Stamina is painfully obvious. Other games like Risen, Witcher, Shadow of Mordor/War, etc. just toned everything down a notch and made it much easier ... also a lot less engaging and fun in my opinion. Once you understand the limits of your character and how to successfully fight others in this game it's no issue at all. The more you level up the more capable you will become. Personally I love that. You need to manage your Stamina and can't just mindlessly attack. Otherwise you wont be able to dodge and especially in the earlier stages of the game the enemies will crush you in an instant because of that.

The Variety and Factions. While it may sound absurd how a game can be whole and logical with 1 middle age faction and a radically opposite futuristic almost Mass Effect like faction, I can assure you they somehow made it work. It adds to the story and allows for very creative World Design. Everything has a reason and they did a good job explaining that to the player. It's all pretty logical and even the balancing (laser weapons vs magic) makes sense to me. I was highly unsure about it before i purchased the game, but having played it through it is one of the highlights. To me it is one of the reasons this game stands out so much, compared to the many others that are available.

The World is absolutely amazing and crazy detailed. It has been one of my favorite RPG Worlds to spend my time in and just explore. You can spend hours upon hours just roaming around and explore right from the start. Though you might need to avoid a lot of enemies on the way. Anyways, its absolutely beautiful! From the vegetated Jungle that is Edan, the desert in Tavar, to the magnificent Ignadon (especially at night). I can't wait for my second playthrough to become more familiar with the areas from the other factions.

The quests are great and a lot of fun. Most of them offer various ways to complete and it allowes you to be - or at least feel - smart about certain approaches. Absolutely missed that in many other modern RPG's.

The Replay factor is very high and i'll be sure to try out the other factions as well. This game offered 60 hours of content for a single playthrough and somehow i still haven't gotten enough of it. I just know there is so much I missed since I wasn't able to play any of the other faction quests and most of the Quests in the respective areas.

In 63 hours for my first play through i have not encountered a single gamebreaking bug or quest that can't be finished. It's sad, but in this day and age it is rather rare for a rpg game of this caliber to be seemingly flawless on release day.

----

The Bad:

The Skill Descriptions are horrendous. Very vague and they sometimes just don't tell you exactly what they will do. If you want stats like percentage increases and stuff like that you will have a hard time finding that. Hopefully the community will provide more details over time. Okay, ich gebs auf. Das war das letzte mal das ich ein Spiel von Piranha Bytes gekauft habe. 
Ich bin ein Gothic Fan erster Stunde, habe alles X mal durchgespielt und war dazumal schon mit der Unfertigen Gothic 3 Version zum Release auf die Fresse gefallen. Dann hatten wir in der Zwischen Zeit Risen 1-3 wo man ja hätte etwas lernen können...  

Ich war am Anfang ja echt Skeptisch was das Setting angeht, habe mich aber dazu gezwungen die ersten Stunden zu überstehen. Wenn man sich auf das Spiel einläst funktioniert das auch ganz gut,,, ABER, das Spiel reisst einen immer wieder durch Sachen aus dem Spielfluss die man mit etwas mehr Liebe und Zeit verhindern hätte können. Da wären Sinnfreie Dialoge, Dämliche Kameraführung, Schlimmstes Kampfsystem Ever, Fehlende Erklärungen zu Grundlegenden Sachen wie Menü und Inventar oder wie wechsle ich meine Munitionsart. 

Das ganze Artet irgendwann einfach nurnoch in Frust aus. Durch das dämliche Kampfsystem hat man fast keine Kontrolle und endet dann dabei jedesmal mit dem Jetpack hochzufliegen und Stamina zuregenerieren. Es wäre auch mal hilfreich hinweise zu geben wo man sich evt hinbegeben kann und wo man sich nicht aufhalten sollte mit einer bestimmten Stufe. Das ganze ist eigentlich nur Try and Error weil es jedes Monster in Verschiedenen Stufen gibt was man aber auch nur sieht wenn man Quasi schon im Kampf ist. 

Es bleibt zu hoffen das es demnächst mal eine überarbeitung geben wird. Aber ob die dann in so Grunglegende Spielmechaniken eigreifen wird ist denke ich fraglich.

Wer dem Spiel eine Chance gibt, eventuell eins der anderen Spiele von Piranha Bytes gespielt hat (keine Pflicht natürlich), und sich vollkommen auf die doch großartige Welt einlässt, wird so viel Spaß haben wie schon lange nicht mehr! 
Elex bietet eine in sich stimmige Welt mit tollen Aufgaben, faszinierenden Dialogen und sehr vielen Erkundungsmöglichkeiten. Ich kann mich nie richtig entscheiden, was ich machen soll und obwohl Elex zu Beginn nicht das einfachste Spiel ist, wird man mit Frustration, F5 spamming und vielen Lachern belohnt.
Wer hätte gedacht, dass Bogen + Jetpack so gut zusammenpassen würden.
Ich liebe das Spiel und kann es nur empfehlen. Und vergesst nicht: Steckt die scheiß Waffe weg!

- Can't fast forward through cinematics

The characters move like a console character (when you move down on the gearstick your character spins 180 degrees, and then finally moves). This is definitely reflective of console play not PC play. You can fast forward through cinematics and dialogue... right click. Solves all your problems.

Get into it you'll enjoy this game.

TL;DR: I can't recommend the game in its current state. I finished it out of spite, but it needs some serious patching and reworking of basic gameplay elements such as monster levels, stats, and melee combat. If you like Eurojank, you will probably enjoy this. If you don't, you will hate this. 

Eurojank. Eurojank is defined as a European game with janky controls that is usually pretty weird and illogical in several areas. Gothic 1/2 and Risen are some mainstream examples of Eurojank. Sometimes, Eurojank can be fun despite (or because of) its oddities. 

Elex is peak Eurojank. Very stupid story, ugly and inconsistent graphics, horrible game mechanics, unrewarding and extremely unbalanced encounters, zero hand-holding of any type, bad ui, terrible map, etc. The game should not have been released in its current state, but here it is anyways, in all its Eurojank glory. The devs simply don't care. They were subsidized by the EU and Germany, recieving multiple grants to create this game. Commercial success was not what they were after, clearly. This game exists because of a bureaucratic process, and it shows.

Combine all of that, and you've got a really unique experience. I feel compelled to play it and finish it simply because it is such an unfriendly insult of a game. It's like the guys who made this crapheap spit in my face and dared me to beat their turd. It's not even consistently fun. There are fun MOMENTS, but every time I jump in I am left bewildered by just how terrible everything is, and my sense of adventure and exploration, and stubborness compells me onward just to see if it can get any worse.

Expect to spend the first 8 hours doing bitchboy work (fetch quests, running around), before you acquire enough skills and gear to take on stuff your level comfortably. It will also take that long to figure out just how unfriendly the world is, and how all exploration is limited by how hard you can cheese the local SKULL-level mobs, which will 1 shot you if they catch you. 

After you get fed up and finally go get some decent weapons and armor, the game becomes piss easy. There is no progression. Once you put on a weapon that deals more than 60 damage or a melee weapon with energy damage, everything dies in a few hits. Everything can also be stunlocked infinitely, removing any potential challenge from high-health enemies. 

First half of the game: run away from stuff.

Last half: kill everything instantly.

Marking as 'not recommended', but that means 'Not Recommended Unless You Really Love Eurojank'.

This game isn't hard. It was simply not playtested, not balanced, and not scaled to present a consistent challenge. The initial difficulty is a product of failed game design, not a product of a decision making process. Despite all its problems, it still gave me nostalgia for the good old days of bizzarre european RPGs. Your milage may vary.

Es ist Gothic 2 im futuristischen, hübscheren Gewand mit all seinen Stärken und Schwächen, wobei es schon in Nuancen ein paar Verbesserungen und leider auch Verschlechterungen gibt. Das Kampfsystem ist genau so hakelig wie früher, so dass gerade am Anfang der Bogen für die Meisten Waffe der Wahl sein sollte. Nachwievor kann PB nachwievor selbst im Vergleich zu Fallout 4,  Skyrim oder Witcher 3 die schönsten Bergpfade, Täler, Sonnenauf- und -untergänge gestalten. Die Umgebungen sind wie das Szenario kreativ und sehr abwechslungsreich und laden zum Erkunden und Sammeln ein. Nachwievor gibt es Krönstöckel, Feuerkraut, usw. und einige neue Kräuter. Nachwievor ist die Grafik nicht up to date ist und es mangelt zuweilen an Diversität bei den Charaktermodellen und Objekten, dazu steife Animationen... Nachwievor ist die Vertonung der derben Spielsprache ein Genuss. Nachwievor gibt es diesen prüden konservativen  Charme und zuckende Brüste seit Gothic 3. Das Questdesign hat die ähnliche Qualität wie in Gothic 2 und die Anleihen sind offensichtlich. Nachwievor definieren Waffe und Rüstung die Stärke des Charakters. Attribute dienen nur als Vorraussetzungen. Nachwievor gibt es spannende Begleiter und Freunde. Nachwievor gibt es 3 Ränge bei den 3 Fraktionen und 3 unterschiedliche Rüstungen :) Ich empfinde das Jetpack als innovativ. Zu den Verschlechterungen gehört für mich aber der Sound und die Musik. Die Musik ist nicht schlecht, hat aber nicht mehr den epischen, orchestralen Anspruch und der Sound ist leider teilweise auf dem Niveau von 2000 stehen geblieben. Das Leiterkletterngeräusch ist einfach grässlich. PB hat einst mit ihrem In-Extremo-Auftritt eine unvergessliche Memo geschaffen. Warum nicht wieder eine Live-Band im Spiel (oder habe ich was verpasst)? Auch das Handwerk hat man für meinen Geschmack zu stark reduziert. Einst war PB hier führend bei der Darstellung der Arbeitsabläufe und Skyrim und Co haben fleißig kopiert. Insgesamt aber eine klar Kaufempfehlung eines Gothic-Veteranen. Der Suchtfaktor ist wieder enorm.

What started out as a clunky overly difficult mess quickly ended up as the best RPG i've ever played.

So this game is the Gothic/Risen take on Sci-Fi, much like Fallout 3 was the sci-fi version of Oblivion.

If you don't like the Gothic and/or Risen series, don't buy this game :)  It's a bit like a bad movie; if you like this particular flavor of bad movies, you'll probably like this one.  If you don't, you'll think its stupid, point out all the obvious problems, and write a bad review.

There is a story, but its not terribly intersting so far.  Classic 'you've been betrayed, go get your betrayers' kind of thing.  However, the world building is interesting.  I enjoy exploring this ruined "post apocalyptic" world and its fun to explore.

In typical Gothic/Risen fashion, combat is incredibly difficult and you will have your butt stomped repeatedly when you're starting out.  In part because it is incredibly easy to stumble into insanely powerful enemies right out the gate.  Game balance seems horrid... your rate of progression in skills is very slow, and yet everything takes a huge number of attribute points to do.  Leveling takes forever, and just getting enough skill points together to put on some basic armor and weapon takes an absurd amount of time.  I have a huge stock of weapons in my inventory that I doubt I will ever be able to use.

That all being said... I consider that pretty typical for a Gothic/Risen game.  Really, the name of the game is to figure out how to use the weird game glitches and quirks to your advantage.  Chief among them is your invunerable follower; get a companion, and he's invincible.  Sure, he might fall down now and again, but if you walk far enough away from him, he'll snap right back onto his feet and resume kicking more butt than you ever will be able to.

I will say that I really hate the stamina mechanic.  Its basically ensured I will never use melee combat in this game.  You run out of stamina, and you may as well sign your own death certificate.

I'll also say: jetpack.  Crazy fun and it makes the combat kinda interesting to use it as an evasion device, shooting arrows from the air.

Anyway, in summary: 

PRO's: big world to explore, interesting sights to see, interesting world and background, JETPACK!

Meh: Story is mediocre, a lot of your typical Gothic/Risen tropes (3 factions to pick from, you can only be in one; using invulnerable characters to defeat enemies; skills require trainers and are hard to advance)

CONS: Melee combat sucks out loud; this stamina thing is really a pain.  Incredibly hard right out the gate.

Would I recommend it?  If you like Gothic/Risen and you know what you're getting into, YES VERY YES.

If you don't like them, don't play this, you will find nothing to love here.

If you've never played them ........ if you like "bad movie" games and you're willing to be patient, maybe worth a try :)  Set low expectations and remember to run around in circles around your follower while he does all the killing if necessary.

По крайней мере схронов и всяких тайников здесь не меньше чем в "Ведьмаке" (почти все оружие, имеющееся в продаже, а то и лучше, здесь можно найти - не верьте игрожурнализдам, которых искать нычки отучили Bethesda со своим автолевеллингом предметов и знаки вопроса, тыкающие в схрон носом), но в случае с "Ведьмаком" про это не вспоминают. Может быть потому, что эти схроны милостиво обозначены на карте знаками вопроса, а здесь ты должен искать все сам?
- Некоторые говорят, что в ELEX нет вариативности. Да нет, ее ровно столько же сколько в "Ведьмаке 3". По крайней мере и там и здесь мы можем влиять на события весьма ограниченно и лишь в определенные моменты. Между прочим,(к вопросу о проработке мира) я заметил, что только в третьем "Ведьмаке", а так же в ELEX, NPC обещавший с кем-то поговорить, реально идет и разговаривает с целевым объектом.
- Как и в "Ведьмаке 3" мир ELEX не подвержен автолевеллингу, а значит в игре присутсвует то забытое с начала 2000-х годов ощущение опасности при походах вокруг городов. Ощущение того, что из любого похода в пещеру или вон в те разрушенные домики, можно не вернуться. Спасибо так расхваленным Скаримам и Обливионам за то, что убили это ощущение напрочь. Вот только если в "Ведьмаке" встреча с монстром обозначенным черепком весьма редка и в основном привязана к тем самым пресловутым знакам вопроса, то в ELEX этих монстров много, они повсеместно и даже простой мутант может убить уже вроде бы готового к встрече с ним персонажа.
- Вся прелесть игр от "Пираний", повторяемая из раза в раз беспроигрышная формула "из грязи в князи". Наш герой не ведьмак и не спаситель галактики по умолчанию. Как правило он голый, босый, без оружия и связей. Именно получение всего этого в процессе игры отличает творения "Пираний" от остальных РПГ, даже от любящих начинать с тюремного заключения Elder Scrools. В играх от Bethesda мир все-же вертится исключительно вокруг игрока. Миру от "Пираний", каким бы он ни был - "Готикой" или "Elex" на игрока плевать. Подсознательно, игра уже бросает вызов - вот ты никто "пойди и добейся".
- Природа. Несмотря на отдельные текстуры, пришедшие из 2001 года, если бы не было "Ведьмака 3", я бы назвал мир "ELEX" самым красивым на данный момент в РПГ. И никакие угловатые деревья с плохо зашейдеренной водой этого впечатления не портят. Почему? 
А потому что "Пиранья" это студия из примерно 25 человек, разрабатывающих игры на свои средства в небольшой студии. И это не идет ни в какое сравнение со студией из 200 сотрудников, сделавших "Ведьмака 3" на огромном бюджете. Если бы все это было у "Пираний"...
- И этот пункт я все-таки вынесу отдельно. А давно ли вы, уважаемые любители РПГ, находили в подвале каких-нибудь разрушенных домов оружие, на 5-7 уровней выше, чем имеющееся у персонажа? Вопрос риторический. Давно. Потому что все РПГ сейчас используют лишь две одноклеточные схемы лута: 
первая - вы НИКОГДА не найдете оружие или доспех выше уровнем, чем вам положен (автолевеллинг - привет Бетесда). Идея может и неплоха, но с таким подходом поиск сокровищ в локациях становится не нужен - следовательно убивается одна из самых важных составляющих РПГ и открытого мира - исследования.
вторая - вы ограничены уровнем локации (привет Биовары). Следовательно, на данной локации вы никогда не найдете что-то на порядок лучше того, что есть у вас.
Даже в хваленом третьем Ведьмаке, предметы в схронах подстраиваются под уровень Геральта (+- какие-то характеристики). Наверное, это в чем-то правильно. Но здесь, наконец-то перед нами игра, где в самом начале, проявив немного выдержки и смекалки можно получить оружие, которое будет служить вам верой и правдой через 30-40 часов игры. И вот благодаря этому локации "ELEX" хочется исследовать (хотя, конечно, в 90% случаев лут будет средненький).
В общем, кто пишет про лут и т.п. в негативном ключе - вы видимо родились недавно и не помните те времена, когда в "одной небезысвестной игре из серии TES" даэдрический доспех был не попсой, а был всего один в игре и тот на сюжетном NPC

Да, игру справедливо ругают за корявые анимации (где студия из 20 человек найдет motion capture), за топорную боевую систему (я тоже считаю, что выносливость вообще лишний параметр), за кривые хитбоксы и в целом не очень ровную коллизию. Зато в играх "Пираний" герой начиная с 2002 года таскает щит за спиной, в то время как Бетесда не способна научить этому своих героев до сих пор, заставляя всяких там Драконнорожденных ходить со щитом в руке в любой ситуации.

Так вот, реалии в том, что по совокупности субъективных недостатков, "ELEX" обвиняют в том же, в чем можно обвинить и третий "Ведьмак". Однако она отличается от него еще и самобытным, хоть и несколько непривычным и гротескным миром (персонаж в ковбойской шляпе, реднековской рубахе и с энергомечом и щитом выглядит настолько комично и несуразно, что это становится даже стильно и очень круто), куда большим количеством вызовов и свойственными только играм жанра "Пираньи снова сделали Готику" особенностями. 
Поэтому (опуская последние недоразумения от Bioware) я могу повторить: Если бы не "Ведьмак 3", то "ELEX" могла бы претендовать на звание лучшей РПГ последних лет. И для маленькой но гордой немецкой компании "Piranha Bytes" это может быть и достижение. А может быть и нет, потому что все равно, хотим мы того или нет, а игры в стиле "Готики" выпускает только она. Да, кривоватые. Да, отстающие от времени в графике. Но от этого отнюдь не худшие и отнюдь не менее интересные. А с тех пор, как откровенно слился основной соперник в виде "Bethesda", переключившийся на казуальщину Скурима и Обливиона, то, возможно и лучшие. Ведь как ни крути, а "Ведьмак" с которым я сравниваю ELEX явление тоже единичное. Над остальным РПГ миром ELEX возвышается весьма уверено, ибо хоть и не предлагает графоний типа "Крузиса", но свою принадлежность к жанру РПГ оправдывает на все 100%. Ведь вы покупая ELEX в РПГ пришли играть, да? А не в 3D-action.

I Went into this game after reading the big name reviewers slamming it for technical issues, and seeing many complaints about clunky controls on Steam.

The controls are nowhere near as bad as I had expected from the reviews. I have run into some minor issues, but nothing game breaking.

The world is immersive and interesting, full of danger, peril and excitement, and it has me thinking about what I am going to do next while I am not playing it.

After having put a decent amount of time into Elex I'm pretty sure that a medocre amount of more effort and a couple of months of polish would have taken this game a long way. There's a lot put into the world but there's a lot more that could have been put into the world. I think an honest price point would have been $30-$35 rather than 50. I find myself play because I feel like since I've put this much into it I might as well finish it... but there's just no decent way to find exp/quests ect.

Cons:
The translations look like they were done in google translate.

Questlines are difficult to find without trying to talk to everyone, and everyone moves around, with no journal system to remind you if you come back later what you were sopposed to do. Don't get me wrong, there's a quest book thing, but it might as well not really say anything just link to where you need to go.

I feel like there was a real attempt at making not joining a faction a thing but I honestly couldn't tell if it was or not. I ended up joining the berserkers after spending about 5 hours looking for one of the lasts quests and finally finding it some time later on accident. I felt accomplished until I was promoted after one quest. And then again after 3. It had taken some 10+ quests to get to that point so getting promoted so fast until I was literally met with a level cap restriction was fairly... sad actually.

Early game you spend 90% of your time running away from things. By the time I was done playing today I was running at things, feeling okay, and was running out of shit to fight in a world I'm pretty sure has no respawns of substance. 

Progress feels like you're sucking cement through a straw. There's lots of perks to pick from leveling up but they all come with an attribute restriction and there's no real way of knowing whether you're putting points in wisely or not. 

Voice acting was "okay" but rather frequently whoever voice acted many characters didn't voice act the SAME CHARACTER when it came to trade confirmation. I have to admit saying "What do you have to trade" and them responding "UNDERSTOOD" 3 times louder than their normal talking by someone else's voice was comical. You know the first ten times.

Mana doesn't regenerate unless you potion it or sleep. Which honestly would be fine if it felt like it was any good. It really doesn't. 

Honestly the biggest Con is the lack of information. Strength increases your damage with melee, but how much? Same with dex and ranged. Perk increases damage but doesn't tell you by how much until you put it in and THEN look at your weapon. Enchanting my weapon with poison adds... poison damage but how much? It literally tells me nothing. I understand not having quest markers above quest givers but it looks like they tried and then just gave up in the middle of polishing... anything.

Lack of polish is probably what this game should be called. I haven't played something this bad since X Rebirth and that got second worst game of the year when it came out. Still... I gave it a chance. People said it opened up and was better after around 15 hours so I put in the time and all I came out with was a gold nugget. It might be worth something polished to a shine and turned into a brick but all I'm left with is an awesome trailer for an early access title that'll never be finished.

The Pros:
Pretty oldschool. If this was ten or fifteen years ago this kind of of thing might be more acceptable but honestly we've moved passed this. Long gone are the days of no dungeon finders in MMOs, no aim assist in shooters, and no hand holding and shitty gameplay action RPGs. If you want to feel like you're playing Gothic, feel free, but that's really the only thing I can say positive about it. I realize this sounds like a negative. Some of you like that I think.

Exploration is okay until you run out of shit to find/fight.

Weapon balance. Everyone seems to have the same amount of power in their weapons. Plasma shoots around as fast as arrows just without the arc. So I don't think you really need to worry about who you join for the best weapons. They all seem pretty shitty in the long run.

Score : 3/10

Score for 2002 : 6/10

TL;DR

Leaves a bad first impression and in general is not fun compared to similiarly priced titles.  If you're a prior fan, I think this is worth your money.  If you're a veteran gamer that's brand new to this series/game, I would recommend buying it for $20 or less.

If I had to pick a couple words to summarize what playing this game feels like: "A chore"

Expanded Review:

Gameplay: 6/10

The action system is clever in the sense that it requires timing.  This isn't presented well to people that aren't familiar with the game/series however.  Despite this, most modern games have largely moved away from it and focused on full action oriented combat.  This games action system feels like a weird turnbased/realtime hybrid.

The minimap/map system seems to be a barebones implementation.  It lacks a lot of the visuals/legend that we're used to seeing from modern titles.  Using it is frustrating.

Quests can be somewhat difficult to find.  I chalk this up as a win in this case since this game seems to have gone for immersion  (a good effort for a small developer)

Visuals: 7/10

The game runs poorly in 4K but I'm sure it runs fine in 1080p.  It has some really bad textures that are obvious in cutscenes.  Cutscenes seem to be somewhat rare so I can overlook that.  Overall the visuals appear reminiscient of a 2014/2015 game.  For a small studio, it's a good effort.

Audio: 2/10

The voiceovers are terrible.  Uninspired, low quality.  The music is your typical fantasy style music and the audio system likes to play it a bit loudly (or not at all) at times.  Turn your music volume down to 40% and the experience will be much better.

Overall: 5/10

Recommended for fans of this studios work (You are probably used to any quirks/issues and can easily overlook this games problems)

Not Recommended for new players, until it's on sale for under $20.

There is SOOOooo much potential there, the game is just a hair away from being great...but it isn't. 

The game is set on the world of "not" Earth, in a future (or past, or present, who knows) where a giant comet smashed into "not" Earth. It left behind Tiberium...err... Elex, and destroyed the planet. Except, it didn't destroy the planet because you are in a VERY lush jungle terrain. You play the character of John Doe (Jax), a character defined by his making Cloud from Final Fantasy 7 look like a very well fleshed out character. You go through a cutscene where your told how awesome your guy really is and then he loses all his equipment and your left with a metal pipe to fight giant rats. You kill a bunch of rats and then get down to meet your first NPC that knocks you out only to protect you so that you can follow him to town, because he's a good guy that way. First, you have to talk to him, using many dialoge options that clearly show a distinct lack of writing or voice work, often wondering why the world is inhabited by so many bipolar people.

That, kinda describes the story. At no point do I find myself even 1% to caring about anyone, even my character. 

Enemies, where the combat is, show a mechanic where the game is close to being good... but isn't. I thought I could get used to the combat and work around it... but no. It's aweful. Think of dark souls, you LOCK ON to your target right? Not here, it tries to have Dark Souls esque combat mechanics, yet feels like trying to perform a ballet with a semi truck. Speaking of Semi Trucks, the core problem with combat is that turning is a chore. You have to perform a full U turn, no pivoting on your feet, just a giant U turn.... just like a Semi Truck. 

Now, you also have a stamina bar. Attacking, running or dodging diminishes it. So, attacking the enemies depletes your stamina bar and leaves you vulnerable, yet you do so little damage to bullet sponge enemies, that it takes forever to do anything and then the enemies can attack you straight out of your attack for 90% of your health (playing on max difficulty). There is a semblance of "fun" there, but it is marred by a rough outline of a system, rather than an actual system itself. Combat is VERY unrewarding, and even then the loot/xp usually don't justify the fight. 

Cutscenes aren't thought out either. Watching a cutscene where Joe Anybody, your character, the supersoldier clumsily "sneaks" up on your old allies like he's a Drunk bull in a china shop, leaves your trying to combat 2 of your old supersoldier buddies. Not a problem until the cutscene leaves you within footsteps of the enemy, leaving you no time to prepare, and the only "good" option is to run away and reset the fight... except you aren't a supersoldier, your a semi truck trying to make a 20 point turn, running in a Uturn that gets you hit. Don't worry, you can still escape...except they also have giant lazer rifles and one shot you.

The voice acting is AWEFUL! It's not Two Worlds aweful, but it's getting there. To be fair the the Voice actors... it doesn't matter, as the writing is so bad that it doesn't matter how good they are. You can polish a turd to shine, but it's still a turd kinda moment. 

This is all a shame though, because the world itself is actually quite interesting. A sci-fi/fantasy RPG where you get a jetpack in the first 5 minutes of the game makes for a very compelling idea, and the ruins of "not" Earth to explore seems like an easy victory. 3 factions to join with different ethos and no clear "these are the good guys/these are the bad guys" choice.

Overall, the game is a hair's width away from being great, but that hair's width is enough to make this a "do not buy" game. If you told me this was an Early Access game, I'd be all for it, but it isn't, it's a full price half baked game with SO much potential that it doesn't realize. Combat and movement are 2 of the most important mechanics to get right, since that's the majority of what you will be doing, and they fail at it. 3 hours in and at no point did I not feel like I was fighting the controls. The Voice acting/writing could be overlooked if it had compelling combat, but it doesn't which just leaves the voice acting and writing in an even worse position because that could have (but didn't) carried the game. 

A very begrudging "do not buy".

Очень много положительных отзывов, могут ввести в заблуждение человека, не знакомого с серией игр Готика. Если вы не играли в Готику1,2 - эта игра вам однозначно не понравится. Если вы играли в них, эта игра может понравится, но это далеко не факт, ведь в ней гораздо больше минусов чем в играх 15 летней давности. Стоит ли игра своих денег? Однозначно нет. Она стоит рублей 300 максимум. Покупать в стиме её стоит при скидке 80-90%. Иначе вы практически точно, после долгой игры придёте к выводу что вас обманули.

Плюсы игры:
+Ностальгия по Готике
+Интересный сеттинг
+Ощущение связанного мира, все события в мире создают единую картину (собственно черта Готикоподобной рпг)

Минусы:
-Устаревшая графика
-Огромное количество багов (как-будто играешь в альфа версию игры)
-Скучные диалоги (хуже чем в игре 15 летней давности)
-Отстутствуют харизматичные персонажи (опять же 15 лет назад их было навалом)
-Слабый сюжет (15 лет назад сюжетный твист захватывал дух)
-Баланс в игре позиционируется как сложный, на деле он просто отсутствует (в отличии от Готики). Вам достаточно найти правильный предмет который будет невыпускать из стана врага. При этом до нахождения такого предмета/заклинания - никакие танцы с бубном не помогут вам играть комфортно.
-Огромное количество неактивных предметов, абсурдность доходить до того что рядом могут стоять две колбы - одну из них вы можете взять в инвентарь, другая же просто декорация. В результате заходя в дом и видя там на столе кучу разнообразных предметов, вы понимаете что это декорции. По большому счету главный герой собирает мётлы, кружки и туалетную бумагу. (позор для рпг такого масштаба)

TL;DR Do not waste money on this game. I regret my purchase. You will too.
   Just read the rock,paper,shotgun article for a more thorough explaination. Put simply, this game is bad if they'd even released it as early access. The dialogue is bland and sounds like it was written by someone taking their first steps into writing, with a single-dimensional protagonist grunting and growling through simplistic "choices", often dictated to players by an obvious best-choice method based on skills accrude. 
   Movement can be a chore, especially navigating around cliffs and other perilous places. The default movement mechanic includes a double-tap wasd roll move akin to Darksouls. However, this is not changeable despite a keybind existing for this inconvenient "feature". This, combined with the games loose recognition of player location and movement, sums up to a frustrating and often slippery adventure. If it were not for the jetpack included at the beginning, this game would be DarkSouls' worst nightmare.
   So far, this game is not worth a buy and we haven't even discussed combat. During he first eight or so hours of the game, enemies feel like demi-gods and are generally unapproachable. Companions are eventually attainable, and are far stronger than you. Combat breaks down to an unfulfilling rotation of blocking, rolling, and ineffectively chipping away at basic monsters, while your less-than-capable companion doles out any meaninful contribution to the fight... or doesn't.
   This game looks and plays like its an early release. It needs substantial fixes on animations and movement all the way through their very concept of combat, story, and dialogue. This game feels more like an test of patience than an adventure. For a $50 game, I feel ripped off.

I am loving Elex.

I found the Gothics to be a bit 'wonky' and strange...... played Risen 1 and own but haven't played the next 2.....

To me, ELEX is above and beyond all these titles.  

I disagree strongly with many of the criticisms as being completely overblown and out of proportion.

The opening 10 hours are hard ONLY if you insist on fighting.  Imagine that: a game that asks you to actually roleplay a nobody and do quests until strong enough to fight.  It isn't hard to do so - you have a jetpack and the ability to run from the fights fairly easily.  In one early quest, I was to gather some herbs and there was a huge monster - I distracted the monster and collected the items - no problem.

I like the dialogue and the quests have many solutions.  People who criticize the quests must absolutely HATE every game but the Witcher 3 then ..... b/c these quests put to SHAME the quests of Skyrim and Fallout 4.  The quests in ELEX allow you to betray people, turn them in, help them.... people lie to you, double cross you..... many are excellent.

The lore of the game is good - with an original story far superior to many.  Again, people who say otherwise must absolutely HATE Skyrim and Fallout 4??? (I like Fallout series and Elder Scrolls and have thousands of hours in them but they are very one dimensional in their quests and factions)

The factions in the game are well developed and interact in a dark sci-fi gritty way.  

Overall, I am very very glad I bought ELEX.  I would be more than happy to rip it to shreds if it deserved it but it doesn't and I'm left a bit baffled by the harsh critics given by many players and so-callled professionals.  It is head and shoulders above the content in many triple-AAA games.

Are the graphics dated - yep.  But otherwise I love ELEX and was surprised b/c I almost didn't buy it given the reviews..... so glad I did.

If you liked Gothic or Gothic 2, you will love this game. Of course it does not have the best graphics, the best animations, or the best combat. But it has this special vibe that only Piranha Bytes games seem to be able to deliver.

It is a great RPG with an incredible atmosphere that is worth playing if you can accept that you are not taken by the hand through the whole game like in most other games of the genre. If you are a low level character and there is a large monster, you better run. The enemies do not scale with you as in other RPG's -- it's meant to be the way that you feel weak in the beginning. It is so incredibly rewarding when you come back to a monster that killed you a couple of hours ago with a single punch, and now after a few level ups you kill it in a long and tough battle. I love Piranha Bytes for creating such experiences.

If you are even slightly interested in the game, give it at least a try when there is a sale. It would be a shame if Piranha Bytes could not continue to create (admittedly rough) gems like this.

Nach 45 Stunden habe ich die Story 1x durchgespielt und habe bei weitem nicht alles entdeckt. Die Welt ist riesig und an allen Ecken und Enden gibt es etwas zu entdecken, sei es eine Nebenquest, eine neue Waffe oder ein anders Geheimnis. 
Die Welt fühlt sich Lebendig an und dies trotz ihrer Größe. 

Vom Beginn an bis zum Ende, versprüht Elex den typischen Piranha Bytes Charme. Leider gibt es auch einige Ecken und Kanten mit denen man sich erst einmal anfreunden muss, gerade für Anfänger ist dies nicht gerade leicht. Gothic und Risen Veteranen werden damit schneller umgehen können.

Zum einen der Schwierigkeitsgrad, welcher selbst auf "Leicht" noch mehr als fordernd ist. Man beißt regelmäßig ins Gras, weshalb ich die Taste "F5" als besten Begleiter im Spiel empfinde. Selbst als jemand der Gothic1-3 und Risen1-3 mehr als 1x durchgespielt hat ist Elex eine harte Nuss. Desweiteren, was bei PB Games aber auch seit G1 Standard ist, es gibt kein Quest-Feedback d.h. entscheidet man sich die falsche Quest zu machen, kann es durch aus sein dass man sich sehr schnell in einer Gruppe von noch zu schweren Gegnern wieder findet. Da hilft nur Try & Error oder das zu Rate  ziehen eines Guids oder einer Komplett Lösung.

Zum anderen das Kampfsystem, ist etwas hackelig am Anfang, bis man den Dreh heraus hat können schon ein paar Stunden vergehen. Denn auch hier verzeihen die Gegner kaum Fehler.

Ein Beispiel, Wir kämpfen mit einem Gegnern unserem Level entsprechend, war in Gothic und auch Riesen locker machbar, wir greifen an, der Gegner pariert, wir setzen nach, der Gegner pariert wieder, wir haben keine Ausdauer mehr können also weder angreifen noch ausweichen. Der Gegner ist dran, er setzt zum Schlag  an und trifft, zweiter Schlag, er trifft erneut, dritter und vierter Schlag ebenfalls. Ergebnis wir liegen Tot im Dreck und drücken "F9" für nen Quickload.

Die Kämpfe bleiben auch im späteren Spielverlauf fordernd, da einige Gegner sehr gerne in Gruppen unterwegs sind.

Und zu guter Letzt, man sollte ich gut überlegen, wo und wie man die ersten Skill- und Attributspunkte setzt. Denn umskillen geht nicht, dadurch kann man sich das Leben in Elex unnötig schwer machen (bis hin zu einem kompletten Neustart).

Und trotzdem ist Elex mehr als gelungen. An jeder Ecke gibt es etwas zu sehen, zu entdecken und zu bestaunen. Der typisch raubeinige Charme der Charaktere und die liebevoll gestaltete Welt von Magalan sind definitiv einen Besuch wert.

PRO
+ riesige Spielwelt
+ lebendige Welt 
+ 4 Skillbäume +1 je Fraktion
+ lädt zu mehrmaligem durchspielen ein
+ der typische Reibeisen Charme der Charaktere

CONTRA
- Elex ist selbst auf "Leicht" noch sehr fordernd
- das Kampfsystem ist gewöhnungsbedürftig
- die Grafik ist nicht mehr die aktuellste
Buy it for the wonderful, vibrant world-building and consequent exploration alone.

This is an exceptional game. It has a very good story, lots of in-depth lore that you won't be able to find unless you explore and characters that you will want to shoot in the face immediately as well as many characters that you will find enjoyable. 

It is nowhere near extremely difficult, even in the beginning it is doable, if not slightly more difficult. The environment is your friend, it is easy to get above most enemies, and they will be unable to fight you, this is a lifesaver. You can map your own controls but even then they are basic, not hard to understand or learn.

The best advice is to find a weapon you enjoy, and put everything towards the abilities that help that weapon. You will be able to kill any monster that way, albeit some may still take some time to kill.

The companions are very useful, however the AI behind them is not the best. They will not find Line-of-sight to attack, so if you have a companion with an explosive weapon, you will get knocked down continuously. It gets very old, that mechanic killed me more than the actual monsters.

Overall, this is an extremely good game and worth buying. I did pretty much everything in the game, before i even joined a faction, so you can explore and have fun without worrying about a faction at all. Then when i decided to actually join a faction, it was faction leveling missions and endgame.

Als Spieler der Gothic- und Risenreihe kann ich sagen, dass ELEX ein würdiger Nachfolger ist. Nach knapp 70 Std Spielzeit konnte ich (nahezu) alle Quests erledigen. Wer sich auf die Hauptstory fokusiert kann wohl auch nach etwa der hälfte Zeit den Abspann über den Bildschirm laufen haben.

Pros:

- Story ist gut und die verschiedenen Fraktionen fügen sich darin plausibel ein
- Stories der möglichen Gefährten/innen sind spannend und haben überraschende Wendungen
- Die Spielwelt ist abwechslungsreich und mit Liebe zum Detail erstellt 
- Jetpack macht nicht nur Spaß, sondern ist derade während der ersten Spielstunden unverzichtbar, um heftige Gegner erstmal zu umgehen
-  Die Vielzahl an Waffen ermöglicht jedem/r einen individuellen Stil  
- An der Werkbank/Lagerfeuer sind sehr viele Gegenstände herstellbar, die alle ihren Sinn haben 
- Jede der Fraktionen hat ihren (moralischen) Haken. Mit keiner der Entscheidungen zu einem Beitritt wird man uneingeschränkt glücklich, ist aber gezwungen eine Entscheidung zu treffen. Gut so!  

Neutral:

- Wer wie ich gerne alle Nebenquests abgrast, bekommt die eigentliche Story erst sehr spät mit. 
- Die Grafik hält mit aktuellen Titel, va bei der Gesichtsanimation, mit AAA Games nicht mit. Wer darauf Wert legt...

Cons:
 
- Balancing 1: Zum Einstieg ist das Kampfsystem echt happig. Im Lategame ist mit den richtigen (unique) Waffen kein Gegner mehr eine Herausforderung, sonder nur noch nervig... 
- Balancing 2: Giert man in der ersten Spielhälfte nach jedem Atribut- / Lernpunkt, sind in der zweiten Spielhälfte mit der Charakterspezalisierung mehr als genug vorhanden und man häuft sie an, ohne sie wirklich zu verwenden... 
- Ausbau des Lagers sehr dürftig - hier wär echt noch mehr gegangen. So ists leider überflüssig. 
- Die Tailer sind zu sehr polished. Man ist im Allerersten Eindruck erst einmal etwas enttäuscht. Hier wär weniger echt mehr gewesen. 

Fazit
Alles in Allem ein gelungenes, kurzweiliges Spiel, dass vor allem Fans von Gothic und Risen sicher deas ein oder andere Wochenende bzw Abend fesseln wird. Die mögliche Spielzeit ist für den Vollpreis mehr als ok.

Schade um ein tolles Spiel.

Dass die Grafik nicht besonders ist, wusste ich bereits und stört auch nicht wirklich.
Das Problem von Elex ist jedoch, dass es is vielen Belangen schlechter ist als das von mir so geliebte Gothic 2 & 3.
Seitdem wurden von den Entwicklern eher kleinere Verbesserungen beim Comfort durchgeführt, das ist nett, aber nicht wirklich von Bedeutung.  Auch das Jetpack halte ich für eine gute Idee und recht spaßig. Wobei man das Rüstungs- und Waffensystem leider völlig in den Sand gesetzt hat, was hätte man nicht alles mit einem halbwegs guten Crafting System erreichen können? Auch das wäre nicht so schlimm, immerhin gab es das in der Originalreihe auch nicht, denn wenigstens kann man soviel sammeln wie man will, theoretisch wäre ein Ansprechen des Jäger & Sammler Triebes nichts im Wege gestanden, leider finden wirk eine wirklich guten Gegenstände, bzw. ist die Decke schnell erreicht, wenn man den Legendären Blaster findet, kann man sich sozusagen zurücklehnen. Dies führt uns zum eigentlichen schwerwiegenden Problem des Spiels:


Egal ob ihr auf Level 1 oder 10 seit, es mach keinen Unterschied, die Monster killen euch in der Regel nach ein bis zwei Bissen.

Das Kampfsystem ist eine Katastrophe. Als Nahkämpfer hat man praktisch keine Chance, auch das System an sich ist eine Farce, und war in der Gothic Reihe wesentlich besser. Es hört dabei leider nicht auf, die Welt von Elex ist stimmig und schön gebaut, jedoch auch sehr kanntig. Das ist einfach nicht mehr zeitgemäß. 

Eine weitere Schwäche sind die Fraktionen und die Quests, war es etwa bei Gothic 2 nicht wahnsinnig spannend, wenn man die Aufträge der Lehrmeister erledigt hatte und endlich Bürger wurde, sprich in die Oberstadt durfte? Dies fehlt hier völlig. Kurz gesagt, mir sind die alle völlig egal. Die Albs sollen sie alle vernichten, man fühlt sich einfach nicht in das Spiel hinein. Ich entwickle keine  Lust Quests zu absolvieren, da auch diese nicht besonders interessant gestaltet sind, die einzelnen Charaktere merke ich mir kaum, alle sind mehr oder weniger austauschbar, ganz anders war dies noch bei Gothic mit Diego und Xardas.

Fazit: Ich würde das Spiel sehr gerne wirklich mögen, vielleicht wird es in einigen Monaten, nach zahlreichen Patches, auch meine Erwartungen erfüllen, bisher tut es dies jedoch nicht. Für mich ist das Spiel noch lange nicht fertig. Es macht zu vieles Falsch um sich an den Punkten die gelungen sind zu erfreuen. Daher unbedingt FINGER WEG! Schade um die 44 Euro.

Elex это в первые 15 часов много смертей буквально на ровном месте,нехватка опыта и денег, наглые напыщенные нпц (Берсерки). Которые считают вас мусором и куча не простых квестов на вступление во фракцию с подвохами и своими издевками. К примеру ( Отомстить за смерть берсерка "убить  5 альбов") Эти5 альбов с плазмоганами  увидив вас за 200 метров откроют огонь  и сложат вас  за пару залпов, если вы не начнете применять свою голову и смекалку. Можно натравить на них местную фауну в виде троля который быстро расправится с врагами, а вы с пригорка будете наблюдать как  выполняется задание.После вступления во фракцию игра кардинально меняется к вам начинают относиться,как к равному и в голосе некоторых нпц чувствуется сожаление за то как они разговаривали и относились к вам ранее. Это очень меня поразило,играю я за берсерков. Мое первое впечатление о них было таким: почти все вожди мудаки напыщенные, люди поголовно лживые твари и я уже собирался идти в клирики, но вступив понял, что сделал правильный выбор. Говорят чужаков никто не любит, а первое впечатление, не всегда верное. Вот и ELex в первые 30 минут  может быстро начкучить или утомить своей сложностью, неудобной боевкой или непосильной задачей, но если вы их преодолеете. Он погрузит вас в невероятный водоворот событий которые подарят вам массу приятных эмоций и впечатлений.

Wo man zu Beginn der Reise noch die Hundekacke am Schuh ist und von allem aufs Maul bekommt, so endet sie mit einem brutal starken Helden der alles und jeden in sekundenschnelle filetiert.
Gut, wenn man nicht so viel grindet wie ich das tat könnte das Endgame sicher noch etwas herausfordender sein. Aber ich hatte es absolut nicht eilig mit dem durchspielen, da die Welt von Elex mir so viel Abwechslung bot, dass ich mich ständig beim erkunden dieser verlor. Nach 60 Stunden Spielzeit (Zeit des Spielstandes) habe ich dann irgendwann die letzten wichtigen Dinge erledigt die nötig waren um die Story voranzutreiben und stellte mich dem Endboss. Der Kampf dauerte ungefähr so lange wie ein Kombo-Angriff... ich war schon so weit übers Ziel hinausgeschossen, dass sogar das vermeintlich stärkste Wesen sich anfühlte wie eine umherstreunende Pestratte.

Aber wo viel Licht ist, steht auch gerne mal ein riesiger Unhold und wirft einen grossen Schatten auf Magalan.
So ist die Technik alles andere als ausgereift und hinterlässt bei einigen Spielern gerade zu Beginn des Abenteuers Spuren aus Verzweiflung und Demotivation.

Seit jeher kränkelt es bei Piranha Bytes schon am Kampfsystem. Die Kämpfe fühlen sich so steif an wie der Held wenn er eine Leiter erklimmt. Manchmal funktioniert der Target Switch nicht und die Kamera steht auch nicht immer optimal. Ausserdem hat man das Gefühl, das blocken ineffizient ist und man dadurch fast schon komplett darauf aus ist jedem Angriff getimed  mit einer Seitwärtsrolle auszuweichen.
Das Kampfsystem hat seit Gothic 1 kaum Veränderungen durchgemacht und sollte eigentlich über die Jahrzehnte verfeinert und optimiert sein. Dem ist nur leider nicht so. Aber es ist auch nicht das pure Böse. Nach etwas Einfummelzeit hat sich jeder Gothic Veteran wieder mit der Steuerung vertraut gemacht. Hier werden eigentlich nur die Spieler bestraft, die zuvor nichts mit Gothic oder Risen am Hut hatten. Sollte man im nächsten Spiel vielleicht mal berücksichtigen.

Dafür macht die Grafik eigentlich fast immer einen grundsoliden Eindruck. Es gibt zwar die ein oder andere verwaschene Textur über die man stolpert aber das nimmt man hin wenn man mal seinen Blick in die Ferne schweifen lässt und das wunderschöne Panorama, welches einen offenbart wird, geniesst.

Alles in allem bin ich aber mehr als zufrieden mit dem Titel und ich habe meinen ersten Durchlauf genossen, trotz einiger Macken. Zum extrem hohen Wiederspielwert brauch ich hier glaub ich garnichts erzählen. Zuerst war ich ein emotionaler Eiswürfelspender der Kleriker. Ich fällte meine Entscheidungen stets rational. Ich möchte aber noch als warmherziger Berserker und als durchgeknallter Outlaw spielen. Tzz... jetzt hab ich ja doch noch was zum Wiederspielwert gesagt.

Das Spiel ist auf jeden Fall den Vollpreis wert und ich freue mich schon auf die Fortsetzung dieses postapokalyptischen SciFi-Fantasy RPG's.

Что можно сказать о ELEX? Типичная рпг от Пираний, эдакая готика в новой обёртке. Здесь есть конфликт фракций, тяжелые бои, которые за частую сводится к одной тактике(ударил и уклонился, выстрелил из лука\бластера\магией, убежал, повторить до победы) Типичный графон конца 2007 года только с подтянутым лицом, но убогой анимацией, что мне как поклоннику не критично. Главное в этой игре это сюжет. Во всех играх Пираний будьто Готика или Ризен сюжет это основа их игр, ну а потом делается все остальное, что как я уже написал сказывается на графике\анимации. 

Если кто не хочет читать вступление подытожим.

ПЛЮСЫ:

-Сильный сюжет.
-Обилие различных сильных врагов, что не оставят равнодушным таких же мазохистов как я, что будут дратся в ближнем бою.
-Большое обилие интересных квестов и загадок.
-Огромная карта мира с отдельными зонами.
-Возможность выбора типа прохождения.
-Фракции, коих в игре играбельные три штуки.

МИНУСЫ:

-Самый главный минус этой игре, это ее нет не графон, а боевая система и дикая сложность на старте игры в независимости от выбранного уровня сложности.
-Графон и Анимация которые пришли прямиком из 2007.
-Довольно примитивное отношение со спутниками и сами спутники. Которые по большей частью выступают в роли мясца, что отвлекает на себя врагов.
-Реиграбельность. Казалось бы в игре есть разные фракции которые фундаментально отличаются друг от друга. Но количество чисто фракционных квестов оставляет желать лучшего и ради которых нет смысла перепроходить всю игру заново.

Вывод.

Если вы фанат Пираний, то игра вам зайдет. Если вы по какой-то причине застряли в 2007 она вам тоже зайдет. Всем остальных она может не понравится, особенно отпугнет начальная сложность игры..

In no particular order.

Cons:
1. Animations
2. Floating Grass
3. Slow HDR
4. Random NPC Chatter
5. Generic Angsty Protagonist
6. UI
7. Some SFX (wooden-ladder-grab)
8. Some Particles (I'm looking at you water-mist)

Pros:
1. Fleshed-out World
2. Scale
3. Replayability
4. Outdoor Lighting
5. Score
6. Random NPC Chatter
7. Generic Angsty Protagonist
8. UI
9. Water waves
10. Jet-pack
11. Enjoyable

Pro-tip:
Turn Field Depth off.

TLDR:

Cons:
1. The animations are janky, clunky, transition poorly, and are pretty freaking rookie looking.
2. Some terrain is really spiky, and really shouldn't have grass on it. The bottom of the grass texture is often sticking out.
3. The HDR going from outdoors to indoors is very slow. You can't see anything for a few seconds. Can the character not squint?
4. The NPCs when gathered will try to string bits of conversation together to make a group conversation happen. Most of the time the things they say won't be related to what they are responding to.
5. The protagonist is as generic as they come.
6. The in-game HUD is either off or on full-time. No opacity control, or smart feature.
7. Some SFX sound like placeholders.
8. Some particles look like placeholders.

Pros:
1. The level of world building that went into the game is impressive. A lot of characters have really interesting motivations.
2. The world is big and the systems are deep. There are lots of customization options when it comes to equipment and abilities. Lots of things require planning, and the payoff feels usually pretty rewarding.
3. Due to the 3 faction system and the number of skill options, you could easily play the game several times with totally different results and experiences.
4. While the lighting may be annoying while going in and out of buildings, it looks amazing when out and about. I also appreciate that night time and environments with no light source are darker than the standard RPG experience. The falloff seems very natural.
5. The music is fantastic. While it should be turned down if you want to make out everything people are saying.
6. The NPCs can say some pretty cool things, and sometimes the random things they say actually work in conjunction to create a unique audio backdrop. Not just a looping background chatter track. How many games have you heard the exact same tavern crowd?
7. The tough guy videogame hero is so generic you can actually mold him to be what you want him to be.
8. I actually like the retro RPG menu UI with its stylized icons. It is just in desperate need of a filter/sort button.
9. By some magic water flows around some large objects placed in it. The waves look really cool.
10. You get a jet-pack. There are a lot of really tall structure to base jump off of. Much fun.
11. Feels like a proper RPG.

Pro-tip:
Always turn off Depth of Field [Field Depth] off. Unless of course you are doing screen-archery.

What a twist. ELEX is actually a very good RPG.

Most people can only see the tip of this game, such as graphics and animation (I honestly think the animation is fine outside of combat). But RPGs are more than that. ELEX is a very mechanically-deep RPG with very minimum hand-holding in a harsh world. Tackle quests however you want, be it with a persuasion, a bribe, or even a duel. Go anywhere, do everything, and be anything; it's game of complete freedom.

The combat might require some adjustments before you get it, but it's not that bad. Unlike in some other RPGs, the enemies don't scale according to the area they reside in. You can meet low-level enemies and higher level ones in the same area, so it's best to scout ahead and plan your move before encountering them. Sometimes, hiding and sneaking around the enemies is the only way to tackle a quest. You're not a superhuman, you're just a weakling in this game. Even after 25 hours in, the world is still dangerous with deadly enemies lurking in every corner. 

If you're a fan of RPGs and could stomach Bethesda janks, you shouldn't skip this one out. It's even more polished than Bethesda RPGs, in fact. Don't let the mainstream reviewers sway you, don't miss out on this hidden gem.

This game ellicits that same feeling of awe, wonder but also fear. Fear of not knowing the most efficient way to do things. Fear that every single battle could be the end. Fear that each decision could piss off the wrong person yet the conviction to allow you to make all those choices.

Sure its not as polished as Skyrim or Fallout in many ways - but it also has a much smaller dev team. Any small issues with animations or movement you very quickly grow used to and forget as the rich and detailed game world comes to life around you in every encounter you engage in. Every corner you take or hill you climb reveals more sprawling wonders ahead for you to bravely venture forth and explore.

This to me is a true RPG. You can get into your character and it feels like you are stepping out on this trecherous journey with all odds against you for the very first time in a long long time.

Thanks PB for a wonderfully nostalgic yet modern game.
Not for everyone - but if you have patience to learn the mechanics and excitement to adventure and explore then this is a good purchase and a company you should support.

Elex, a tragic love/hate merging of gameplay options that you wish were in other games along with some options you wish were taken from other games. 

That's not to say that i don't recommend this game, i certainly do. There's a big draw to the game if you can get past the occasional hiccup that you will come across.

The story starts off a bit odd, you are an alb; a group of people who use elex to infuse into their body to enhance themselves at the cost of all emotion. You are on a mission of which you are shot down on the way. Your brother happens to be there and is sent to execute you for failure. Upon waking you have been robbed and must fend for yourself.

This leads to your first npc encounter, a berserker for said neaby faction stonghold. I will start with the quest system, far from a fetch this or go kill questlines you are often sent to complete various tasks that will weave into branched outcomes. Most quests have two or more outcomes, a boy loses his bow and you can either return it to him or give it to his master to teach the boy a lesson. Each comes with their own reward, like a sword you are asked to steal, you can take it to the quest giver, or return it to the owner stating you found it to return it, money or reputation gain is your choices.

The story and lore of the world comes from the people you encounter. Each character is voice acted in the game which is hit or miss, mostly miss but it's not grating on the ears and more or less tolerable. Talking to people is also how you will find quests to complete. What looks like small talk can become a new thing to do. You companions also help drive the story, as you go through the world you will encounter people who will join your cause, an alb who broke free from elex but doesn't care about how to get the job done, the thief who stole your equipment at the beginning of the game who for some reason has a bounty on his head from old friends, or a berserker who deems her magic abilities so strong and uncontrollable that she exiled herself they all have their own questlines to flesh their characters out.

There is no hand holding in this game, the game gives very little direction and even further little help when it comes to surviving in the early levels. Most adventure RPG's give you some direction and you can handle most encounters early on, Elex does not. You will die, and you will die often until about level 15-20. Some of this has to do with the games combat. A lot say it's clunky, i don't believe so, it's slower than most games in this genre, however with over 30 hours played most enemies have patterns that you can adjust to and manage easily. Attacks are deliberate, you have to adjust to these attacks to overcome the challenges of the game.

The one thing that holds this back is hit detection. If you're going to fight, don't do it on steep inclines. Hit's aren't detected if the enemy is higher than you. Some instances will have you wondering if you even hit them, they blocked, or somehow evaded. None of this is game breaking though, you just have to put some more thought into fighting. There's also times where you will encounter multiple enemies leaving you to figure out ways to take them out or even cheese them. Your weapons include; one handed, one handed with shield, two handed weapons, bows, rifles, grenade launchers along with other heavy guns.

You have 5 stats you can put points into when you level: Strength, Constitution, Dexterity, Intellegence, and Cunning. These stats determine which weapons, armor, and abilities you can have or equip. You get 10 points per level to spend points and the cost goes up at certain thresholds. 1 point per level until 30 which it goes up to 2 per level until 60 then a whopping 5. What you can do and learn are heavily reliant on these and it takes a lot of time to get to where you are moving the needle on overcoming problems easier. 

You can join one of 3 factions in the game, and each faction will determine your baseline playstyle.

The first are the berserkers and the first group you can readily join as you start right near their stronghold. They are one with nature and are trying to repair the planet with world hearts, giant seeds that soak up Elex from the ground and replace it with mana. They abhor technology and anything that uses elex. Their weapons are mainly wood or steel like weapons and their ranged weapons are bows and crossbows. Their abilities are magic based and mostly enhance your character.

The second are the clerics, they are a religious sect that relies heavily on technology and heavy weapons. They have melee weapons that look more futuristic and they have plasma rifles and flame launchers. Their abilities are Psi in nature using elex fueled items.

The last group are the outlaws, these post apocalyptic looking individuals are just that, a nearly lawless group that convert elex into drugs. Their weapons are very apocalyptic in nature, chainswords and slug firing weapons. Their abilities have to do with taking stims and chems to enhance their character. The downside to these are a 50% reduction in exp earned, however the bonuses gained can outwheigh the losses, especially if you have exp increasing abilities.

While these groups have weapons specific to their region you can equip any weapon you have the stats for, however each group can only enhance the weapons specific to their region. 

Some have issues with the UI, i however don't really do. I can see how some feel a menu based UI would be terrible however being an older gamer it doesn't really bother me.

In Closing:

If you can look past some of the flaws of the game, there is a game that draws you in and once the progression starts gaining traction you will continue to want to see what the next upgrade does for you. I also can appreciate the steep requirements for weapons, armors and abilities which even further enhances that drive to get to the next level.

I recommend this game fully if you are able to dig into the whole of the game.

Oider, dat Game. Das ist das erste mal das ich eine Review verfasse.  Ich bin wirklich wütend und fassungslos.

Ich habe die Kommentare zu Elex gelesen und mich von den begeisterten Gothic Fans überzeugen lassen dieses Spiel zu kaufen. 50 Tacken, ich bereue es so hart. 

Was Spiele angeht bin ich echt tolerant, habe schon so einige miese Formate über mich ergehen lassen und konnte aufgrund einzelner Faktoren wie Atmosphäre über gewisse Mängel hinwegsehen. Aber dieses Spiel ist eine einzige Frechheit. Die Spieleentwickler bzw. die Dudes die da am Hebel sitzen sind ja dermaßen dreist geworden das ich darüber echt fassungslos bin. 

Hölzerne Charaktere schön und gut, das wäre alles kein Problem, aber bei den lowen Cinematics geht einfach jede Atmosphäre flöten. Wie kann es sein das meine Begleiter nur rumstehen und in der Luft rumkucken während ich 7 Hits kassiere. Das kann einmal passieren dann schaut man darüber hinweg aber man muss standardmäßig einen Treffer landen muss damit die Begleiter reagieren; Mensch was soll denn das??  Die Begleiter antworten abseits der Story/Quests grundsätzlich mit einem Wort was jedes mal ziemlich unpassend wirkt. Warum zuckt der Charakter nur kurz rum wenn man eine Druckwelle "zaubert" oder eigentlich nur den Knopf dafür drückt, folglich fliegen 5 Brösel durch die Luft und der Gegner nimmt 60% HP Schaden. Jungs das kann man doch nicht ernst meinen, die FX bei den Spells von Gothic 1 waren in kosmischen Ausmaßen geiler. Man summoned eine Drohne und das Ding erscheint ohne Effekt, ohne Ton, ohne wow. Der Sound an sich wirkt oft sowas von übersteuert und unangenehm repetetiv, zum kotzen. Man steigt auf ne Wurzel und es scheppert dermaßen das man das Headset ablegen möchte. Guter Sound ist subtil und fällt nicht auf, fügt sich ein. Sobald Töne auffällig werden läuft schon was schief. Wenn man die erste Siedlung, welche, wenn auch zu groß, absolut gelungen und atmosphärisch wirkt, dann ist es mir unbegreiflich wie man solche Stimmungskiller zu lassen kann. Es gibt eigentlich nur eine Schlussfolgerung: Das Studio hatte wie immer zu wenig Kapazitäten an Zeit und Geld und irgendein geldgeiles Vollarschloch meint dieses Projekt schön zum passenden Termin releasen zu müssen. 

Videospiele sind eine Form von Kunst. Wenn man die jüngsten und weniger jungen Ereignisse betrachtet wie, z.B. ganz aktuell Bethesda's faux pas, dieses Spiel, Gothic 3 + Risen Teile und die ganzen Lutscher von Blizzard mit WoW und Hearthstone dann dämmert doch durchaus das was man ganz lange nicht wahrhaben wollte: Die Branche hat sich vollends (!) in ein kapitalistisches, unehrliches und leidenschaftloses System entwickelt welches uns diese Form von Kunst raubt.


Ich möchte appellieren an die Szene, gründet DIY Studios, nehmt euch den Mut und erschafft Kunst in unserer geliebten Form! Leute zu finden ist einfacher als man denkt.

I have enjoyed this game so far. Typical PB burtality at the start. Same wonky animations. Lore seems indepth, and the story is interesting.

However, there are some severe issues it seems with the questing systems in the game engine. Quests don't complete out of your log. Some quests don't trigger (though going to the next area in the quest may force the quest into your log). Some dialog doesn't seem to read saved values properly where I completed one quest in a positive way (npcs lived), yet the npc I talked to clearly indicated I had killed the other npc.

I also must point out that as an rpg the lack of a stat screen is infuriating. A piece of armor gives you x amount of armor, but nowhere can you see the total. or resistances. or current xp or xp needed to level, or current mana or hp amounts. Despite this, hp and mana pots and armor all list values for these. Skills that increase these things don't tell you how much either. And attribute points only seem to serve as a requirement checkmark to wear certain gear or buy certain skills.

Also worth noting is that companions are currently useless as they don't help you fight unless they have been hit by a mob, or you have hit a mob. But they only will enage those mobs. So if mob a hits them, and you hit mob b you comanion will help you with both, but not mob c.

All in all if they correct the major issues with game breaking/altering bugs that exist within the questing system in the game I would be able to change my recomendation to a thumbs up.
Yes, it's lacking in polish, but speaking as someone who just doesn't pay full price for games, this one is worth it. No ragrets.

Фу игра тупая буна пчолы убевают и вобще игра плохо зделона тупо,  не смогла прайти Гундира и боивая сестема нипанятная тупая все миня убевают мало стомины и удары гирой ни наносит толька зачёк зилененький кокойто карочи я тупой казуал.
Вот так примерно видится мне львиная доля негативных обзоров: бестолковый человек вешает свои косяки на игру, разработчиков, боевую систему etc., а потому считаю, что руководствоваться ими - дело гиблое, ибо можно пропустить если и не самую, то одну из самых шикарных РПГ последнего времени и уж точно, на мой взгляд, самую рпгшную из всех. Игра не поразит вас графикой, но эту брешь вролне в состоянии заполнить красота и проработка мира, а уж о необычности, интересности и внимании к мелочам говорить нечего - продукт Пираний, как никак, так что это по умолчанию. Боевая система, о которой столько шума у детишек, выращенных на скайримах, может быть описана как своеобразная: она не идеальна, но довольно таки удобна и позволяет при должной сноровке расправляться с врагами, которые выше по уровню без особых страданий. Мобы, как это было принято в предыдущих играх студии, не подстраиваются под игрока, что добавляет реализма. Так же его добавляет тот факт, что большая часть НПС не тупы и не линейны: они хитрят и хотят использовать вас с выгодой для себя. Многие ваши действия будут иметь последствия, даже если кажутся незначительными, квесты зачастую переплетаются, что так же делает игру атмосферной и затягивающей. Какие то свои минусы игра, как и любая другая, конечно же, имеет. В основном они связаны с технической частью, что характерно для игр Piranha Bytes. Тем не менее, критических багов я не увидела и считаю, что плюсы очень сильно перевешивают минусы. В общем, игра вышла замечательной и стоит своих денег.

This game draws a lot of hate, which I don't understand as to it's core it's a decent explorathon.  Not to say the criticisms are all without merit, as the main characters are generic, the writing isn't anything approaching Shakespeare, and the combat is something that will either make you sit up for the challenge or withdraw at the clunkiness.

But then this is a Pirahna Bytes game, they of Gothic who make strange open worlds with combat that is 'different' and a quest system far, far more subverted than that of say Skyrim.

Quite often you will find the solution to a early quest before you find the quest, it doesn't hold you hand with quest markers, you need to go out and find them.  Quite often conversations will open or lock off quests, before you realise it.

Like Gothic 2 & 3 the game is buggy, and I can imagine so many gamers not liking the lack of polish around this game.  BUT there are also gamers like me who thinks a game can be enjoyable without having the Hollywood spit n polish. 

And like the other games they have made, exploring is great. A vast world full of junk to pick up, and answers to questions you may, or may not have been given. Also, jetpacks.

Every free open world game from this point on should have jetpacks.
